AvroExample mein sabse chhoti encoding (32 bytes). Schema changes field name se match hote hain, jo generated schemas ke liye sahi hai.Reader ko writer’s schema pata hona chahiye, isliye use store ya negotiate karna padta hai. Nullable fields ke liye union types chahiye.

Dataflow ke modes

Is chapter ki shuruaat mein humne kaha tha ki jab bhi tum data aise process ko bhejte ho jo tumhari memory share nahi karta, toh use bytes mein encode karna padta hai. Yeh tab hota hai jab tum data network par bhejte ho ya file mein likhte ho. Phir humne kaafi saari encodings dekhi, aur yeh bhi ki unhe compatible kaise rakhein. Compatibility asal mein data encode karne wale process aur decode karne wale process ke beech ka relationship hai.

Yeh baat thodi abstract hai, aur processes ke beech data kai tarike se flow ho sakta hai. Toh data kaun encode karta hai, aur kaun decode? Book teen common modes dekhti hai: databases ke through data, service calls ke through data, aur asynchronous message passing ke through data.

Databases ke through dataflow

Database mein jo process likhta hai woh data encode karta hai, aur jo process padhta hai woh decode karta hai. Ho sakta hai database ko sirf ek hi process use kar raha ho. Us case mein reader bas usi process ka ek baad ka version hota hai. Toh database mein kuch store karna ek tarah se apne future self ko message bhejne jaisa hai. Yahan backward compatibility clearly zaroori hai. Warna tumhara future self wahi cheez decode nahi kar paayega jo tumne pehle likhi thi.

Aam taur par database ko kai processes ek saath use karte hain. Woh alag-alag applications ya services ho sakti hain, ya ek hi service ki kai copies jo scalability ya fault tolerance ke liye parallel chal rahi hain. Badalte hue system mein kuch processes naya code chalate hain aur kuch purana. Jaise, ho sakta hai naya version rolling upgrade ke beech mein ho. Isliye newer code ki likhi hui value ko baad mein koi older version padh sakta hai jo abhi bhi chal raha hai. Matlab databases ke liye aksar forward compatibility bhi chahiye hoti hai.

Ek aur dikkat hai. Maan lo tumne record schema mein ek field add kiya, aur newer code us field ki value likhta hai. Baad mein older version ka code, jise us field ke baare mein pata hi nahi, woh record padhta hai, update karta hai, aur wapas likh deta hai. Yahan sahi behavior yeh hoga ki old code us naye field ko intact rakhe, bhale hi woh use samajh nahi paa raha.

Example

Book is dikkat ko teen steps mein samjhati hai, jo neeche figure mein dikhaye gaye hain.

  1. Newer app ek record likhta hai jisme naya field hai. Ab database mein woh field present hai.
  2. Older app wahi record padhta hai. Use naya field pata nahi, isliye us field ka uske liye koi matlab nahi.
  3. Older app apna model object wapas database mein save kar deta hai. Agar woh object naye field ke bina bana tha, toh field drop ho jaata hai, aur newer app ka data lost ho jaata hai.

Pehle discuss kiye gaye formats unknown fields ko rakhne ko support karte hain. Lekin kabhi-kabhi application level par dhyaan dena padta hai. Agar tum database value ko application mein model objects mein decode karte ho, aur baad mein un objects ko dobara encode karte ho, toh us translation mein unknown field kho sakta hai. Yeh solve karna mushkil nahi hai. Bas iske baare mein pata hona chahiye.

Alag-alag waqt par likhi gayi values

Database mein aam taur par koi bhi value kabhi bhi update ho sakti hai. Isliye ek hi database mein kuch values paanch millisecond pehle likhi hui ho sakti hain aur kuch paanch saal pehle. Jab tum server-side application ka naya version deploy karte ho, toh kuch minutes mein purane version ko naye se replace kar sakte ho. Database contents ke saath aisa nahi hota. Paanch saal purana data apni original encoding mein wahin rahega, jab tak kisi ne use explicitly dobara na likha ho. Book isse ek line mein kehti hai: data outlives code.

Data ko naye schema mein rewrite ya migrate karna possible hai, lekin bade dataset par yeh costly hai, isliye zyadatar databases ise jahan tak ho sake avoid karte hain. Zyadatar relational databases simple schema changes allow karte hain, jaise null default ke saath naya column add karna, aur existing data ko rewrite nahi karna padta. Jab koi purani row padhi jaati hai, toh disk par encoded data mein jo columns missing hain, unke liye database null bhar deta hai. LinkedIn ka document database Espresso storage ke liye Avro use karta hai, isliye woh Avro ke schema evolution rules use kar sakta hai. MySQL ko book exception batati hai: woh aksar poori table rewrite kar deta hai, jab ki strictly zaroori nahi hota, jaisa document model mein schema flexibility wale chapter mein bhi note kiya gaya tha.

Natija yeh hai ki schema evolution se poora database aisa dikhta hai jaise woh ek hi schema se encode hua ho. Andar storage mein shayad schema ke kai purane versions se encode kiye hue records ho sakte hain.

Archival storage

Tum kabhi-kabhi database ka snapshot lete ho, backup ke liye ya data warehouse mein load karne ke liye. Us case mein dump aam taur par latest schema se encode hota hai. Source database mein alag-alag daur ke schema versions ka mix ho sakta hai, lekin jab tum data copy kar hi rahe ho, toh copy ko consistent tarike se encode kar dena behtar hai.

Dump ek baar mein likha jaata hai aur baad mein badalta nahi, isliye Avro object container files jaisa format achha fit baithta hai. Tum data ko analytics-friendly, column-oriented format mein bhi encode kar sakte ho, jaise Parquet, jo book ne Chapter 3 mein column compression ki baat mein cover kiya tha. Archival storage mein data use karne ke baare mein Chapter 10 mein aur detail hai.

Services ke through dataflow: REST aur RPC

Jab processes ko network par communicate karna ho, toh isse arrange karne ke kuch tarike hain. Sabse common arrangement mein do roles hote hain: clients aur servers. Server network par ek API expose karta hai, aur clients us se connect hokar requests karte hain. Server jo API expose karta hai use service kehte hain.

Web isi tarah kaam karta hai. Clients, yani web browsers, HTML, CSS, JavaScript aur images download karne ke liye GET requests karte hain. Server ko data submit karne ke liye woh POST requests karte hain. Yahan API protocols aur formats ka ek standard set hai: HTTP, URLs, SSL/TLS aur HTML. Browsers, web servers aur website authors in standards par kaafi had tak agree karte hain, isliye koi bhi browser koi bhi website khol sakta hai, kam se kam theory mein.

Browsers hi akele client nahi hain. Phone ya desktop ka native app bhi server ko network requests kar sakta hai. Browser ke andar chalne wali JavaScript application XMLHttpRequest se khud HTTP requests kar sakti hai, jise Ajax kehte hain. Us case mein server ka response aam taur par HTML nahi hota jo insaan dekhe. Woh data hota hai, aksar JSON, jise client-side code process karta hai. HTTP transport ho sakta hai, lekin uske upar bani API har application ke liye specific hoti hai, isliye client aur server ko uski details par agree karna padta hai.

Ek server kisi doosri service ka client bhi ho sakta hai. Typical web application server database ka client hota hai. Yeh approach aksar bade application ko chhoti services mein todne ke liye use hoti hai, functionality ke area ke hisaab se. Jab ek service ko doosri se kuch chahiye hota hai, toh woh request karti hai. Is style ko traditionally service-oriented architecture (SOA) kaha jaata tha. Haal hi mein ise refine karke microservices naam se rebrand kar diya gaya hai.

Services kuch tarah se databases jaisi hoti hain. Dono clients ko data submit aur query karne dete hain. Lekin database Chapter 2 mein discuss ki gayi query languages mein arbitrary queries accept karta hai. Service ek application-specific API expose karti hai, jo sirf wahi inputs aur outputs accept karti hai jo service ki business logic ne pehle se tay kiye hon. Is restriction se ek had tak encapsulation milta hai. Service yeh fine-grained limits laga sakti hai ki clients kya kar sakte hain aur kya nahi.

Service-oriented ya microservices architecture ka ek key goal hai application ko badalna aur maintain karna aasaan banana, har service ko independently deployable aur evolvable bana kar. Har service ek team ki ownership mein honi chahiye, aur woh team doosri teams se coordinate kiye bina naye versions aksar release kar sake. Isliye tumhe expect karna chahiye ki servers aur clients ke purane aur naye versions ek saath chalte rahenge. Servers aur clients jo data encoding use karte hain, woh service ki API ke versions ke beech compatible honi chahiye. Aur yahi baat is poore chapter mein ho rahi thi.

Web services

Jab service se baat karne ke liye HTTP protocol use hota hai, toh us service ko web service kehte hain. Yeh naam thoda galat hai, kyunki web services sirf web par hi nahi, aur jagah bhi use hoti hain. Book teen common contexts batati hai:

  1. User ke device par chalne wali client application, jaise native phone app ya Ajax use karne wala JavaScript web app, HTTP par service ko requests karti hai. Yeh requests aam taur par public internet se guzarti hain.
  2. Ek service usi organization ki doosri service ko requests karti hai, aksar usi datacenter ke andar, service-oriented ya microservices architecture ke hisse ke roop mein. Is use ko support karne ke liye bane software ko kabhi-kabhi middleware kehte hain.
  3. Ek service kisi doosri organization ki service ko requests karti hai, aam taur par internet par. Is tarah alag-alag organizations ke backend systems data exchange karte hain. Isme online services ki public APIs aati hain, jaise credit card processing, aur OAuth, jo user data ka shared access allow karta hai.

Web services ke do popular approaches hain: REST aur SOAP. Book ke hisaab se philosophy mein yeh lagbhag ek doosre ke ulta hain, aur inke supporters aksar inke baare mein garma-garam behas karte hain.

REST koi protocol nahi hai. Yeh ek design philosophy hai jo HTTP ke principles par bani hai. Yeh simple data formats pasand karti hai, resources identify karne ke liye URLs use karti hai, aur cache control, authentication aur content type negotiate karne ke liye HTTP features use karti hai. REST SOAP ke muqable popular hota ja raha hai, kam se kam organizations ke beech services connect karne ke liye, aur ise aksar microservices ke saath jodha jaata hai. Jo API in principles par design ho use RESTful kehte hain.

SOAP network API requests karne ka XML-based protocol hai. Yeh aam taur par HTTP par use hota hai, lekin iska aim HTTP se independent rehna hai, aur yeh uske zyadatar features avoid karta hai. Iske badle isme related standards ka ek bada aur complicated set aata hai, jise WS-* kehte hain, jo alag-alag features add karte hain. SOAP service ki API ek XML-based language mein describe hoti hai jise Web Services Description Language, yani WSDL, kehte hain. WSDL se code generation possible hota hai, toh client local classes aur method calls se remote service ko call kar sakta hai, aur framework unhe XML messages mein encode karke wapas decode kar deta hai. Yeh statically typed languages mein kaam ka hai, aur dynamically typed languages mein kam.

WSDL ko insaanon ke padhne ke liye design nahi kiya gaya, aur SOAP messages aksar itne complex hote hain ki haath se banana mushkil hai. Isliye SOAP use karne wale tool support, code generation aur IDEs par bahut depend karte hain. Agar kisi programming language ko SOAP vendors support nahi karte, toh SOAP services ke saath integrate karna mushkil ho jaata hai. SOAP aur uske extensions formally standardized hain, phir bhi alag-alag vendors ki implementations aksar aapas mein interoperate nahi kar paati. In wajahon se SOAP abhi bhi kai bade enterprises mein use hota hai, lekin zyadatar chhoti companies mein yeh pasand se bahar ho gaya hai.

RESTful APIs simple approaches pasand karti hain, jisme code generation aur automated tooling kam hoti hai. OpenAPI (jise Swagger bhi kehte hain) jaisa definition format RESTful API ko describe kar sakta hai aur usse documentation bana sakta hai. Book do notes aur add karti hai. SOAP SOA ke liye zaroori nahi hai, kyunki SOA ek general approach hai jabki SOAP ek specific technology. Aur har camp ke andar bhi kaafi arguments hain, jaise HATEOAS par, yani hypermedia as the engine of application state ka idea.

Trade-offs
OptionKis mein achhaKya cost hai
RESTSimple formats, HTTP features, browser ya curl se try karna aasaan, tool support wide, cross-organization APIs ke liye popularGenerated code kam aur formal typing kam. Responses ka aam taur par formally specified schema nahi hota, isliye compatibility discipline par depend karti hai.
SOAPStrict, machine-readable WSDL contracts aur generated client code, jo statically typed languages ko suit karte hainStandards ka bada aur complex stack. Tools ke bina use karna mushkil. Vendors aksar interoperate nahi kar paate, aur unsupported languages se integrate karna mushkil hai.

Remote procedure calls (RPCs) ki problems

Web services network par API requests karne ki lambi technologies ki line ka latest version hain. Inme se kai purani technologies ko bahut hype mila tha, par unme serious problems thi. Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) aur Java ka Remote Method Invocation (RMI) sirf Java mein kaam karte hain. Distributed Component Object Model (DCOM) sirf Microsoft platforms par kaam karta hai. Common Object Request Broker Architecture (CORBA) zaroorat se zyada complex hai aur backward ya forward compatibility nahi deta.

In sab ki neev remote procedure call, yani RPC, ke idea par hai, jo 1970s se chala aa raha hai. RPC model koshish karta hai ki remote service ko request karna waisa hi dikhe jaise tum apni programming language mein, usi process ke andar, koi function ya method call kar rahe hon. Is abstraction ko location transparency kehte hain. Sunne mein convenient lagta hai, lekin Kleppmann ke hisaab se yeh approach buniyadi taur par galat hai. Network request local function call se bahut alag hoti hai:

  • Outcomes predictable nahi hote. Local function call predictable hota hai. Woh sirf un parameters ke basis par succeed ya fail hota hai jo tumhare control mein hain. Network request lost ho sakti hai, ya remote machine slow ya unavailable ho sakti hai, aur yeh problems tumhare control se bahar hain. Network problems common hain, isliye inke liye plan karna padta hai, jaise failed request ko retry karna.
  • Ek teesra outcome hai: koi jawab nahi. Local call ya toh result return karta hai, ya exception throw karta hai, ya kabhi return nahi karta kyunki woh infinite loop mein hai ya process crash ho gaya. Network request timeout ki wajah se bina result ke bhi return ho sakti hai. Tab tumhe bas pata hi nahi hota ki hua kya. Tum yeh nahi bata sakte ki request pahunchi ya nahi. Chapter 8 mein iske baare mein aur detail hai.
  • Retries action ko repeat kar sakte hain. Agar requests pahunch rahi hain aur sirf responses lost ho rahe hain, toh retry action ko dobara perform kar deta hai. Agar protocol mein deduplicate karne ka koi tarika nahi hai (repeated requests ko harmless banana, jise idempotence kehte hain), toh action do baar ho jaata hai. Local function calls mein yeh problem nahi hoti. Idempotence ke baare mein Chapter 11 mein aur detail hai.
  • Speed bahut vary karti hai. Local function call har baar lagbhag utna hi time leta hai. Network request kaafi slow hoti hai, aur uska time bahut vary karta hai. Achhe moment mein woh ek millisecond se kam mein khatam ho sakti hai, lekin congested network ya overloaded service ke saath wahi request kai seconds le sakti hai.
  • Parameters ko encode karna padta hai. Local call mein tum memory ke kisi object ka reference pass kar sakte ho. Network request mein har parameter ko bytes mein encode karke bhejna padta hai. Numbers aur strings ke liye yeh theek hai, lekin bade objects ke saath problem ban jaata hai.
  • Languages ke types share nahi hote. Client aur service alag-alag languages mein likhe ho sakte hain, isliye RPC framework ko types ek language se doosri mein translate karne padte hain. Yeh ugly ho sakta hai, kyunki sab languages mein ek jaise types nahi hote. Upar 253 se bade integers ke saath JavaScript ki problem yaad karein. Ek hi language mein likhe single process mein aisi problem nahi hoti.

In sab ka matlab yeh hai ki remote service ko apni programming language ke local object jaisa dikhane ka koi faayda nahi. Woh buniyadi taur par ek alag cheez hai. REST ke appeal ka ek hissa yeh hai ki woh service ko local hone ka dikhawa nahi karta. Woh openly ek network protocol hai. Phir bhi log REST ke upar RPC libraries banate rehte hain.

RPC ki current directions

In problems ke baad bhi RPC kahin nahi ja raha. Is chapter ki encodings par kai RPC frameworks bane hain. Thrift aur Avro mein RPC support hai. gRPC ek RPC implementation hai jo Protocol Buffers use karti hai. Finagle Thrift use karta hai. Rest.li HTTP par JSON use karta hai.

RPC frameworks ki nayi generation yeh zyada explicitly maanti hai ki remote request local function call nahi hai. Finagle aur Rest.li futures use karte hain, jinhe promises bhi kehte hain. Yeh aise objects hain jo ek asynchronous action ki jagah khade hote hain, jo fail bhi ho sakti hai. Futures se kai services ko parallel requests bhejna aur unke results combine karna bhi aasaan ho jaata hai. gRPC streams support karta hai, jahan ek single call mein time ke saath requests aur responses ki ek series hoti hai, sirf ek request aur ek response nahi.

Inme se kuch frameworks service discovery bhi dete hain. Isse client pata kar sakta hai ki koi particular service kis IP address aur port number par hai. Book is topic par baad mein request routing ke under wapas aati hai.

Binary encoding wala custom RPC protocol JSON over REST jaise generic option se behtar perform kar sakta hai. Lekin RESTful API ke doosre strong advantages hain. Ise experiment aur debug karna aasaan hai, kyunki tum ise web browser ya curl command-line tool se call kar sakte ho, bina code generation ya kuch install kiye. Ise saari mainstream programming languages aur platforms support karte hain. Aur iske liye tools ka bada ecosystem hai, jisme servers, caches, load balancers, proxies, firewalls, monitoring, debugging aur testing tools shaamil hain.

In wajahon se REST public APIs ke liye predominant style lagta hai. RPC frameworks ka main focus ek hi organization ki services ke beech requests par hai, aam taur par usi datacenter ke andar.

RPC ke liye data encoding aur evolution

Evolvability ke liye RPC clients aur servers ko independently change aur deploy ho paana chahiye. Databases se flow hone wale data ke muqable, services ke liye book ek simplifying assumption leti hai. Yeh expect karna reasonable hai ki pehle saare servers update honge, aur baad mein saare clients. Toh requests par backward compatibility chahiye, yani naye servers purane clients ki requests padh sakein. Aur responses par forward compatibility chahiye, yani purane clients naye servers ke responses padh sakein.

RPC scheme ki compatibility us encoding se aati hai jo woh use karta hai:

  • Thrift, gRPC (jo Protocol Buffers use karta hai) aur Avro RPC apni encoding formats ke compatibility rules ke hisaab se evolve hote hain.
  • SOAP mein requests aur responses XML schemas se specify hote hain. Inhe evolve kiya ja sakta hai, lekin kuch subtle pitfalls hain.
  • RESTful APIs responses ke liye aam taur par JSON use karti hain, bina formally specified schema ke. Requests mein JSON, ya URI-encoded ya form-encoded parameters hote hain. Optional request parameters add karna aur response objects mein naye fields add karna aam taur par compatible changes maane jaate hain.

Compatibility mushkil isliye hoti hai ki RPC aksar organizational boundaries ke paar use hota hai. Service provider aksar apne clients ko control nahi kar sakta, isliye woh unhe upgrade karne par majboor nahi kar sakta. Tab compatibility ko bahut der tak, shayad hamesha ke liye, maintain rakhna padta hai. Agar compatibility todne wala change avoidable nahi hai, toh provider ko aksar service API ke kai versions side by side chalane padte hain.

API versioning kaise kaam kare, yani client kaise bataye ki use API ka kaunsa version chahiye, is par koi agreement nahi hai. RESTful APIs ke liye common approaches hain URL mein ya HTTP Accept header mein version number. Jo services har client ko identify karne ke liye API keys use karti hain, unke liye ek aur option hai ki har client ne jo version maanga tha use server par store kar do. Phir us choice ko ek alag administrative interface se badla ja sakta hai. Book is approach ke example ke roop mein Stripe ka naam leti hai.

Message-passing dataflow

Ab tak humne do patterns dekhe. REST aur RPC mein ek process request bhejta hai aur jitni jaldi ho sake response expect karta hai. Databases mein ek process encoded data likhta hai aur doosra process use baad mein kisi waqt padhta hai. Yeh aakhri section asynchronous message-passing systems dekhta hai, jo in dono ke beech kahin aate hain.

RPC ki tarah, message low latency se doosre process tak deliver hota hai, matlab bahut kam delay se. Database ki tarah, message direct network connection se nahi jaata. Woh ek intermediary se guzarta hai jise message broker kehte hain, jise message queue ya message-oriented middleware bhi kaha jaata hai. Broker message ko kuch der ke liye store karta hai.

Direct RPC ke muqable broker ke kai advantages hain:

  • Agar recipient unavailable ya overloaded hai, toh yeh buffer ka kaam kar sakta hai, jisse reliability improve hoti hai.
  • Yeh crash hue process ko messages dobara deliver kar sakta hai, isliye messages lost nahi hote.
  • Sender ko recipient ka IP address aur port number jaanne ki zaroorat nahi. Cloud mein yeh zaroori hai, jahan virtual machines aksar aate-jaate rehte hain.
  • Ek message kai recipients ko bheja ja sakta hai.
  • Yeh sender ko recipient se decouple kar deta hai. Sender bas messages publish karta hai, aur use parwah nahi ki kaun consume karta hai.

RPC se ek difference hai. Message passing aam taur par one-way hoti hai. Sender normally reply expect nahi karta. Koi process response bhej sakta hai, lekin woh aam taur par alag channel par bhejega. Yeh pattern asynchronous hai. Sender message deliver hone ka intezaar nahi karta. Woh message bhejta hai aur aage badh jaata hai.

Message brokers

Pehle message broker market par TIBCO, IBM WebSphere aur webMethods jaisi companies ka commercial enterprise software chhaya hua tha. Haal hi mein open-source brokers jaise RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, HornetQ, NATS aur Apache Kafka popular ho gaye hain. Chapter 11 mein inki aur detail mein comparison hai.

Delivery ke exact rules implementation aur uski settings par depend karte hain. Aam taur par ek process kisi named queue ya topic ko message bhejta hai, aur broker ensure karta hai ki message ek ya zyada consumers tak pahunche, jo messages padhne wale processes hain, ya us topic ke subscribers tak. Kai producers, jo messages bhejne wale processes hain, ek hi topic mein likh sakte hain, aur kai consumers use padh sakte hain.

Topic one-way dataflow deta hai. Ek consumer kisi doosre topic par bhi messages publish kar sakta hai, toh tum topics ko chain kar sakte ho, jaisa Chapter 11 dikhata hai. Ya ek consumer reply queue par publish kar sakta hai jise original sender padhta hai. Isse RPC jaisa request aur response flow mil jaata hai.

Message brokers aam taur par koi particular data model enforce nahi karte. Message bas kuch metadata ke saath bytes ki sequence hai, isliye tum koi bhi encoding format use kar sakte ho. Agar encoding backward aur forward dono compatible hai, toh tumhe sabse zyada freedom milti hai. Tum publishers aur consumers ko independently badal sakte ho, aur kisi bhi order mein deploy kar sakte ho.

Agar koi consumer messages ko doosre topic par republish karta hai, toh dhyaan rakhein ki jo fields woh nahi samajhta unhe preserve kare. Warna wahi problem aa jaati hai jo humne databases ke liye pehle dekhi thi, jisme old process naya field drop kar deta hai.

Distributed actor frameworks

Actor model ek single process ke andar concurrency ke liye programming model hai. Threads ke saath seedha kaam karne ki jagah, jisme race conditions, locking aur deadlock jaisi problems aati hain, logic ko actors ke andar rakha jaata hai. Har actor aam taur par ek client ya ek entity ko represent karta hai. Uske paas kuch local state ho sakti hai, jo koi aur actor share nahi karta. Actors asynchronous messages bhej kar aur receive karke communicate karte hain. Delivery guaranteed nahi hoti. Kuch error scenarios mein messages lost ho jaate hain. Har actor ek time mein sirf ek message process karta hai, isliye use threads ki fikr nahi karni padti, aur framework har actor ko independently schedule kar sakta hai.

Distributed actor framework is model se application ko kai nodes par scale karta hai. Sender aur recipient chahe same node par hon ya alag nodes par, same message mechanism use hota hai. Agar woh alag nodes par hain, toh message transparently bytes mein encode hota hai, network par bheja jaata hai, aur doosri taraf decode hota hai.

Location transparency actor model mein RPC se behtar kaam karti hai. Wajah yeh hai ki actor model pehle se maanta hai ki messages lost ho sakte hain, ek hi process ke andar bhi. Network latency abhi bhi ek process ke andar se zyada hai. Lekin local aur remote communication ke beech buniyadi mismatch kam hai.

Distributed actor framework asal mein message broker aur actor model ko ek framework mein milakar banta hai. Phir bhi rolling upgrades mein care chahiye. Messages naye version wale node se purane version wale node ko bheje ja sakte hain, aur ulta bhi. Isliye forward aur backward compatibility ab bhi matter karti hain. Book teen popular frameworks aur unke message encode karne ka tarika batati hai:

  • Akka default mein Java ki built-in serialization use karta hai, jo na forward na backward compatibility deti hai. Tum ise Protocol Buffers jaisi kisi cheez se replace kar sakte ho, jisse rolling upgrades kar paana possible ho jaata hai.
  • Orleans default mein custom encoding use karta hai, jo rolling upgrades support nahi karti. Naya version deploy karne ke liye tum naya cluster set up karte ho, traffic purane cluster se naye par move karte ho, aur purana cluster band kar dete ho. Akka ki tarah yahan bhi custom serialization plug-ins use kiye ja sakte hain.
  • Erlang OTP mein record schemas badalna hairaan karne wali had tak mushkil hai, jab ki system mein high availability ke liye design kiye gaye kaafi features hain. Rolling upgrades possible hain, lekin unke liye careful planning chahiye. 2014 mein Erlang R17 mein introduce hua ek experimental naya maps datatype future mein ise aasaan bana sakta hai. Maps JSON jaisa structure hain.

Summary

Short mein
  • Rolling upgrades. Kai services ko rolling upgrades chahiye, jahan naya version ek baar mein kuch nodes par gradually deploy hota hai, sab nodes par ek saath nahi. Isse downtime ke bina releases ho paate hain, toh teams chhote releases aksar ship kar sakti hain. Isse deployments kam risky bhi hote hain, kyunki faulty release ko bahut users tak pahunchne se pehle spot karke rollback kiya ja sakta hai. Yeh sab evolvability mein madad karta hai, yani application ko badalne ki aasaani.
  • Dono directions mein compatibility. Rolling upgrade ke dauran, ya aur wajahon se, alag-alag nodes code ke alag versions chalate hain. Isliye system mein flow hone wala saara data aise encode hona chahiye ki backward compatibility (naya code purana data padhe) aur forward compatibility (purana code naya data padhe) dono mil sakein.
  • Language-specific encodings ek hi language se bandhi hoti hain aur aksar na forward na backward compatibility deti hain.
  • Textual formats jaise JSON, XML aur CSV kaafi widespread hain. Inki compatibility is par depend karti hai ki tum inhe kaise use karte ho. Inki optional schema languages madad bhi kar sakti hain aur raste mein bhi aa sakti hain. Yeh datatypes ke baare mein vague hain, isliye numbers aur binary strings ke saath dhyaan rakhna padta hai.
  • Binary schema-driven formats jaise Thrift, Protocol Buffers aur Avro compact, efficient encoding dete hain, saaf-saaf defined forward aur backward compatibility rules ke saath. Inke schemas documentation ke liye aur statically typed languages mein code generation ke liye kaam ke hain. Downside yeh hai ki insaan ke padhne se pehle data ko decode karna padta hai.
  • Dataflow ke modes. Databases, jahan writer encode karta hai aur reader decode. RPC aur REST, jahan client request encode karta hai, server use decode karke response encode karta hai, aur client use decode karta hai. Aur brokers ya actors ke through asynchronous messaging, jahan sender encode karta hai aur recipient decode.
  • Nateeja. Thodi care ke saath backward aur forward compatibility aur rolling upgrades kaafi achievable hain. Book ek ummeed bhare note par khatam hoti hai: rapid evolution aur frequent deployments.

Chapter ke end mein papers, documentation aur blog posts ke references ki ek lambi list hai jo uske claims ko support karti hai. Yeh retelling us list ko reproduce nahi karti.

Khud check karein

  1. Ek app ka newer version ek field add karke use record mein save karta hai. Older version woh record padhta hai, ek unrelated field badalta hai, aur dobara save karta hai. Naya field na khone ke liye older version ko kya karna hoga?

    Jawab dekho

    Record wapas likhte waqt use unknown field ko intact rakhna hoga. Formats unknown fields preserve kar sakte hain, lekin agar app record ko model objects mein decode karke dobara encode karta hai, toh field drop ho sakta hai, isliye app ko dhyaan rakhna padta hai.

  2. Thrift ya Protocol Buffers schema mein pehli deployment ke baad add kiya gaya har field optional kyun hona chahiye ya default value kyun rakhna chahiye?

    Jawab dekho

    Naya code purana data padhega, jo field ke exist karne se pehle likha gaya tha. Required-field check us data par fail ho jaayega. Field ko optional banane ya default dene se backward compatibility bani rehti hai.

  3. Network request timeout par khatam ho sakti hai, lekin local function call nahi. Retry karne ka faisla lete waqt yeh kyun matter karta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Timeout ke baad tumhe pata nahi hota ki request pahunchi ya nahi. Agar pahunchi thi aur sirf response lost hua, toh retry action ko doosri baar perform kar deta hai, jab tak protocol requests ko deduplicate na kare (repeats ko harmless banana, jise idempotence kehte hain).

  4. Jab schema database table se generate hota hai, toh Avro Thrift ya Protocol Buffers se zyada friendly kyun hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Avro fields ko name se match karta hai aur uske schema mein tag numbers nahi hote. Regenerate kiya hua schema seedha use ho sakta hai. Thrift aur Protocol Buffers mein kisi ko field tags haath se assign aur maintain karne padenge, aur kabhi koi tag reuse nahi karna hoga.

Part II

Distributed Data

Part II mein dekhte hain ki data kai machines par rakha jaaye toh kya badalta hai. Isme data ki copies (replication), data ke splits (partitioning), transactions, aur distributed systems ki limits aati hain.

Yeh Richard Feynman ki Rogers Commission Report (1986) wali baat ka paraphrase hai: sach ko public relations se pehle aana chahiye, kyunki reality ko dhokha nahi diya ja sakta.

Part II · Chapter 5

Replication

Seedhi baat: replication mein same data kai machines par rakha jaata hai, taaki system failures survive kar sake aur zyada readers ko serve kar sake. Mushkil yeh hai ki copies kuch der ke liye ek-doosre se alag ho sakti hain, aur har replication method consistency, speed aur availability ke beech trade-off karta hai.

Zyaadatar log database se pehli baar ek single machine par milte hain. Lekin system bada hota hai, toh ek machine aksar kam padti hai. Book ka Part II yeh poochta hai ki jab database kai machines par ho, jo network se baat karti hain, toh kya badalta hai. Yeh chapter replication se shuru hota hai, yani same data ki copies ek se zyada machines par rakhna. Yahan baat yeh hai ki copies sync mein kaise rehti hain, aur sync na rahein toh kya galat hota hai.

Data distribute kyun karein?

Ek machine ke database ki ek clear limit hoti hai. Data, read load ya write load ek machine ki capacity se bahar chala jaaye, toh tum kaam ko kai machines mein baant sakte ho. Kleppmann database distribute karne ki teen main wajah batate hain:

  • Scalability. Data ka volume ya load ek machine se zyada ho jaaye, toh kaam kai machines mein baanta ja sakta hai.
  • Fault tolerance aur high availability. Maan lo application ko tab bhi chalte rehna hai jab ek machine, kai machines, network, ya poora datacenter (servers se bhari ek building) down ho jaaye. Aise mein extra machines redundancy deti hain. Ek fail ho, toh doosri uski jagah le sakti hai.
  • Latency. Duniya bhar ke users ko unke paas wale servers se serve kiya ja sakta hai. Isse unhe network packets ke aadhi duniya ghoom kar aane ka wait nahi karna padta.

Zyada load handle karna

Zyada load handle karne ka sabse simple tarika hai ki tum ek zyada powerful machine kharid lo. Ise vertical scaling, ya scaling up kehte hain. Kai CPUs (processor chips), kai RAM chips (memory) aur kai disks ko ek operating system ke neeche jod diya jaata hai. Ek fast internal link ki wajah se koi bhi CPU memory ya disk ke kisi bhi hisse tak pahunch sakta hai. Poori cheez ko ek hi machine maana jaata hai. Ise shared-memory architecture kehte hain.

Iski teen limits hain. Pehli, cost capacity se tez badhti hai. Do guna CPUs, RAM aur disk wali machine ki cost aksar do guna se kaafi zyada hoti hai. Doosri, bottlenecks ki wajah se do guna bada machine hamesha do guna load handle nahi kar paata. Teesri, fault tolerance limited hai. High-end machines chalte-chalte disks, memory modules aur CPUs tak badal sakti hain, lekin poori machine phir bhi ek hi jagah par rehti hai. Isliye woh sirf ek geographic location cover karti hai.

Book mein bahut badi machines ke baare mein ek footnote hai. Kuch memory banks ek CPU ke paas hote hain aur doosron se door. Ise nonuniform memory access, ya NUMA kehte hain. Aisi machine ko achhe se use karne ke liye bhi kaam ko split karna padta hai, taaki har CPU zyaadatar apne paas wali memory use kare. Matlab ek single machine par bhi partitioning chahiye.

Doosra option shared-disk architecture hai. Kai machines hoti hain, har ek ka apna CPU aur RAM, lekin sab ek hi disks ke array ko fast network ke through share karti hain. Yeh shared disks network attached storage (NAS) ya storage area network (SAN) se jude hote hain. Yeh kuch data warehousing workloads ke liye theek hai, jo reporting aur analysis ke liye use hone wale bade systems hain. Lekin contention (machines ka ek-doosre ka wait karna) aur locking ka overhead is design ki scaling ko limit kar dete hain.

Shared-Nothing architectures

Doosra approach shared-nothing architecture hai, jo ab kaafi popular ho gaya hai. Yahan database software chalane wali har machine, ya virtual machine, ek node kehlati hai. Har node apne CPUs, RAM aur disks use karta hai. Nodes sirf software mein, ek normal network ke upar coordinate karte hain. Ise scaling out ya horizontal scaling bhi kehte hain, kyunki tum ek machine ko bada karne ke bajay zyada machines saath-saath jodte ho.

Iske fayde real hain. Special hardware nahi chahiye, toh tum jo bhi machines price ke hisaab se sabse achhi performance dein, woh kharid sakte ho. Data kai geographic regions mein failaya ja sakta hai. Isse users ke liye latency kam hoti hai, aur poora datacenter chala jaaye tab bhi system survive kar jaata hai. Cloud platforms ise affordable bana dete hain. Ab ek chhoti company bhi multi-region system chala sakti hai, bina kisi bade internet company jitne scale par kaam kiye.

Book shared-nothing systems par focus karti hai. Yeh isliye nahi ki woh har case ke liye fit hain, balki isliye ki application developer se unhe sabse zyada care chahiye. Data kai nodes par ho, toh distributed systems ke constraints aur trade-offs lagu ho jaate hain, aur database unhe tumse poori tarah chhupa nahi sakta. Shared-nothing designs complexity bhi badhate hain, aur kabhi-kabhi yeh limit kar dete hain ki tum kaun se data models use kar sakte ho. Kleppmann note karte hain ki kuch cases mein ek simple single-threaded program 100 se zyada CPU cores wale cluster se kaafi behtar perform kar sakta hai. Phir bhi, shared-nothing systems bahut powerful ho sakte hain. Agle kuch chapters mein dekhenge ki data distribute karne par kaunsi problems aati hain.

Replication aur Partitioning mein fark

Data ko nodes mein failane ke do common tarike hain. Dono alag mechanisms hain, lekin aksar saath kaam karte hain.

  • Replication mein same data ki copy kai nodes par rakhi jaati hai, shayad alag-alag locations mein. Copies redundancy deti hain. Kuch nodes available na hon, tab bhi data baaki nodes se serve ho sakta hai. Replication se performance bhi behtar ho sakti hai. Iski baat Chapter 5 mein hai.
  • Partitioning, jise sharding bhi kehte hain, ek bade database ko chhote subsets mein todta hai, jinhe partitions kehte hain. Alag-alag partitions alag nodes ko assign ho sakte hain. Iski baat Chapter 6 mein hai.

Dono ko aksar saath use kiya jaata hai. Book ka Figure II-1 ek database dikhata hai jo do partitions mein split hai, aur har partition ki do replicas hain. Har partition ki apni copies apni machines par hoti hain. Aage ke chapters mein transactions (Chapter 7), data system mein jo kuch galat ho sakta hai (Chapter 8), aur distributed systems ki fundamental limits (Chapter 9) cover honge.

Yeh chapter replication ke baare mein hai. Replication yani same data ki copy network se jude kai machines par rakhna. Replicate karne ki teen wajah hain:

  • Data ko users ke geographically paas rakhna, jisse latency kam hoti hai.
  • System ke kuch parts fail ho jaayein, tab bhi system chalta rahe, jisse availability badhti hai.
  • Read queries serve karne wali machines ki count scale out karna, jisse read throughput badhta hai (system ek second mein kitni reads ka jawab de sakta hai).

Abhi maan lete hain ki dataset itna chhota hai ki har machine uski poori copy rakh sakti hai. Chapter 6 yeh assumption hata deta hai aur un datasets ki baat karta hai jo ek machine ke liye bahut bade hain.

Data kabhi change na hota, toh replication aasaan hota. Tum use ek baar har node par copy karke ruk jaate. Saari mushkil changes se aati hai. Is chapter mein changes ko nodes ke beech copy karne ke teen popular algorithms hain: single-leader, multi-leader aur leaderless replication. Lagbhag har distributed database inme se ek approach use karta hai, aur har ek ke apne pros aur cons hain.

Kuch aur trade-offs bhi hain, jaise copying synchronously ho ya asynchronously, aur fail hui replica ko kaise handle karein. Yeh aksar database ke configuration options hote hain. Details ek database se doosre mein badalti hain, lekin general principles milte-julte hain. Replication par 1970s se kaam ho raha hai, aur uske principles zyada nahi badle, kyunki networks ke basic constraints wahi rahe hain. Lekin kaafi time tak bahut se developers maante rahe ki database ek single node par chalta hai. Distributed databases ka mainstream use naya hai, isliye eventual consistency jaise ideas ko kaafi developers ne galat samjha. Chapter in ideas ko aage badhte hue explain karta hai.

Leaders aur Followers

Jo bhi node database ki ek copy rakhta hai, use replica kehte hain. Kai replicas hon, toh turant ek sawaal aata hai: hum kaise pakka karein ki saara data har replica par pahunch jaaye? Har write ko har replica par process karna padta hai. Warna replicas mein same data nahi rahega.

Sabse common solution hai leader-based replication. Ise active/passive ya master-slave replication bhi kehte hain. Yeh aise kaam karta hai:

  1. Ek replica ko leader bana diya jaata hai. Ise master ya primary bhi kehte hain. Client ko write karna ho, toh use write leader ko hi bhejna padta hai. Leader pehle naya data apni storage mein likhta hai.
  2. Baaki replicas followers kehlaate hain. Inhe read replicas, slaves, secondaries ya hot standbys bhi kehte hain. Leader jab bhi naya data likhta hai, woh change apne saare followers ko bhi bhejta hai, ek replication log ya change stream ke roop mein. Replication log changes ka ordered record hota hai. Har follower log padhta hai aur wahi writes usi order mein apply karta hai jis order mein leader ne kiye the.
  3. Client ko read karna ho, toh woh leader ya kisi bhi follower se query kar sakta hai. Lekin writes sirf leader par accept hote hain. Client ke nazariye se followers read-only hote hain.

Book mein bataya hai ki "hot," "warm" aur "cold" standby ki definition alag-alag log alag tarah se karte hain. PostgreSQL mein hot standby client ke reads accept karta hai, jabki warm standby changes apply karta hai par koi query serve nahi karta. Book ke kaam ke liye yeh difference zaroori nahi hai.

Replication ka yeh mode kai relational databases ka built-in feature hai, jaise PostgreSQL (version 9.0 se), MySQL, Oracle Data Guard aur SQL Server ke AlwaysOn Availability Groups. Kuch nonrelational databases bhi ise use karte hain, jaise MongoDB, RethinkDB aur Espresso. Yeh sirf databases tak limited nahi hai. Kafka jaise distributed message brokers aur RabbitMQ ki highly available queues bhi leader-based replication use karti hain. Kuch network filesystems aur replicated block devices, jaise DRBD, bhi isi tarah kaam karte hain.

Synchronous vs Asynchronous Replication

Ek zaroori detail yeh hai ki replication synchronously hota hai ya asynchronously. Relational database mein aksar yeh ek setting hoti hai jo tum badal sakte ho. Baaki systems mein yeh kisi ek par fixed hota hai.

Example

Maan lo ek website ka user apni profile image update karta hai. Book is update ko Figure 5-2 se follow karti hai, jismein chaar parts hain: user ka client, leader, aur do followers. Step by step sequence yeh hai:

  1. Client update request leader ko bhejta hai.
  2. Leader request receive karta hai aur nayi image apni storage mein likh deta hai.
  3. Leader change follower 1 ko forward karta hai aur wait karta hai ki follower confirm kare ki data mil gaya. Yeh synchronous replication hai.
  4. Saath hi, leader change follower 2 ko bhi forward karta hai, lekin reply ka wait nahi karta. Yeh asynchronous replication hai.
  5. Follower 1 ke confirm karne ke baad hi leader client ko batata hai ki update ho gaya. Usi point par woh write doosre clients ko bhi dikhne lagta hai.
  6. Is beech follower 2 ko message kaafi der baad milta hai.

Replication aam taur par kaafi fast hota hai. Zyaadatar database systems followers par changes ek second se kam mein apply kar dete hain. Lekin koi guarantee nahi hai ki kitna time lagega. Follower leader se kai minutes ya usse zyada peeche reh sakta hai. Aisa tab hota hai jab follower kisi failure se recover kar raha ho, system apni maximum capacity ke kareeb chal raha ho, ya nodes ke beech network mein problem ho.

Synchronous replication ka ek clear advantage hai. Synchronous follower ke paas hamesha up-to-date copy hoti hai jo leader se match karti hai. Leader achanak fail ho jaaye, toh bhi data follower par available rehta hai. Iska disadvantage yeh hai ki synchronous follower respond karna band kar de, crash hone se ya network fault se, toh write process nahi ho sakta. Leader ko saare writes block karne padte hain aur tab tak wait karna padta hai jab tak synchronous replica dobara available na ho jaaye.

Isliye har follower ko synchronous banana practical nahi hai. Ek bhi node ka outage poore system ko rok dega. Practice mein, agar tum synchronous replication on karte ho, toh aam taur par ek follower synchronous hota hai aur baaki asynchronous. Synchronous follower unavailable ya slow ho jaaye, toh ek asynchronous follower ko promote karke synchronous bana diya jaata hai. Isse guarantee milti hai ki up-to-date copy kam se kam do nodes par hai: leader aur ek synchronous follower. Book ke hisaab se is setup ko kabhi-kabhi semi-synchronous kehte hain.

Leader-based replication aksar fully asynchronous configure kiya jaata hai. Aise mein agar leader fail ho jaaye aur recover na ho paaye, toh jo writes abhi followers tak copy nahi hue the woh lost ho jaate hain. Matlab client ko success bata dene ke baad bhi write ke durable (hamesha ke liye safely stored) hone ki guarantee nahi hoti. Faayda yeh hai ki saare followers peeche reh jaayein, tab bhi leader writes process karta rehta hai. Durability kamzor karna bura trade lag sakta hai, lekin asynchronous replication kaafi widely use hota hai, khaaskar jab followers bahut zyada hon ya poori duniya mein phaile hon. Chapter is issue par replication lag wale section mein dobara aata hai.

Replication par Research

Asynchronous leader fail hone par data lose hona ek serious problem hai. Isliye researchers aise methods dhoondhte rahe hain jo data lose na karein, phir bhi performance aur availability achhi rakhein. Ek example chain replication hai. Yeh synchronous replication ka ek variant hai, aur Microsoft Azure Storage jaise kuch systems mein successfully use hua hai. Replication consistency aur consensus ke beech bhi strong link hai. Consensus matlab kai nodes ka ek value par agree karna. Chapter 9 us theory ko explore karta hai. Yeh chapter replication ke un simple forms par rehta hai jo practice mein sabse common hain.

Naye Followers Set Up Karna

Kabhi-kabhi tumhe naya follower chahiye hota hai, capacity badhane ke liye ya failed node ko replace karne ke liye. Tum kaise pakka karo ki naye follower ke paas leader ke data ki accurate copy ho?

Data files ko ek machine se doosri mein copy kar dena kaafi nahi hai. Clients likhte rehte hain, isliye data hamesha badalta rehta hai. Simple file copy database ke alag-alag hisson ko alag-alag moments par dekhegi, aur result ka koi matlab nahi bhi nikal sakta. Tum database ko lock kar sakte ho taaki copy ke dauraan kuch na badle, lekin us se writes ruk jaayenge, jo high availability ke goal ke khilaaf hai. Achhi baat yeh hai ki follower aam taur par bina downtime ke set up ho sakta hai. Conceptually, process mein chaar steps hote hain:

  1. Leader ke database ka ek consistent snapshot lo, kisi ek point in time par. Ho sake toh yeh poora database lock kiye bina karo. Zyaadatar databases yeh support karte hain, kyunki backups ko bhi iski zaroorat hoti hai. Kuch systems ke liye third-party tools lagte hain, jaise MySQL ke liye innobackupex.
  2. Snapshot ko naye follower node par copy karo.
  3. Follower leader se connect karta hai aur snapshot ke baad jitne data changes hue hain woh sab maangta hai. Yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab snapshot leader ke replication log ki ek exact position se juda ho. Is position ke naam alag-alag databases mein alag hain. PostgreSQL ise log sequence number kehta hai, aur MySQL ise binlog coordinates kehta hai.
  4. Follower jab backlog process kar leta hai, tab woh caught up ho jaata hai. Uske baad woh changes ko real time mein process karta rehta hai.

Practical steps ek database se doosre mein kaafi alag hote hain. Kuch systems mein process fully automated hota hai. Kuch mein yeh multi-step workflow hota hai jo administrator ko haath se karna padta hai.

Node Outages Handle Karna

Koi bhi node down ho sakta hai. Woh achanak fail ho sakta hai, ya use intentionally band kiya ja sakta hai, jaise machine reboot karne ke liye ya kernel ka security patch install karne ke liye. Individual nodes ko bina downtime ke reboot kar paana operations ke liye bada advantage hai. Isliye goal yeh hai ki individual node failures ke baad bhi poora system chalta rahe, aur har outage ka impact jitna ho sake utna kam rahe. Leader-based replication ke saath yeh kaise hoga?

Follower failure: catch-up recovery. Har follower leader se mile data changes ka ek log apni local disk par rakhta hai. Follower crash hokar restart ho, ya uske aur leader ke beech network kuch der ke liye toot jaaye, toh recovery kaafi aasaan hai. Apne log se follower ko pata hota hai ki fault se pehle usne aakhri transaction kaun si process ki thi. Woh leader se connect karta hai aur jitni der woh gaayab tha, us dauraan hue saare changes maangta hai. Un changes ko apply karte hi woh caught up ho jaata hai aur wapas live stream receive karne lagta hai.

Leader failure: failover. Failed leader ko handle karna zyada mushkil hai. Kisi ek follower ko promote karke naya leader banana padta hai. Clients ko reconfigure karna padta hai taaki woh apne writes naye leader ko bhejein. Baaki followers ko naye leader se changes consume karna shuru karna padta hai. Is process ko failover kehte hain.

Failover manual ho sakta hai, jismein administrator ko notification milta hai aur woh steps khud karta hai, ya automatic. Automatic failover mein aam taur par teen steps hote hain:

  1. Detect karo ki leader fail ho gaya hai. Kai cheezein galat ho sakti hain: crash, power outage, network problem, aur bhi. Yeh pata lagane ka koi foolproof tarika nahi hai ki asli wajah kaun si hai. Isliye zyaadatar systems timeout use karte hain. Nodes aapas mein hamesha messages bhejte rehte hain, aur koi node kuch der, maan lo 30 seconds, tak respond na kare toh use dead maan liya jaata hai. Planned maintenance ke liye intentionally band kiye gaye leader ke liye yeh detection zaroori nahi hota.
  2. Naya leader choose karo. Yeh election se ho sakta hai, jismein bache hue replicas ka majority leader chunta hai. Ya pehle se elected controller node kisi ko appoint kar sakta hai. Sabse achha candidate aam taur par woh replica hota hai jiske paas purane leader ke sabse up-to-date changes hon, kyunki isse data loss kam hota hai. Saare nodes ko naye leader par agree karwana ek consensus problem hai, jise Chapter 9 detail mein discuss karta hai.
  3. System ko reconfigure karo taaki naya leader use ho. Ab clients apne writes naye leader ko bhejte hain. Book isse request routing ke under cover karti hai. Yahan ek catch hai: purana leader wapas aa jaaye, toh ho sakta hai woh ab bhi khud ko leader maanta ho. Ho sakta hai use pata hi na chale ki baaki replicas ne use step down karwa diya hai. System ko pakka karna hoga ki purana leader follower ban jaaye aur naye leader ko accept kare.

Failover mein kaafi cheezein galat ho sakti hain:

  • Lost writes. Asynchronous replication mein ho sakta hai ki purane leader ke fail hone se pehle naye leader ko uske saare writes mile hi na ho. Purana leader cluster mein wapas aaye, toh un writes ka kya hoga? Is beech naye leader ne conflicting writes accept kar liye hon, aisa ho sakta hai. Sabse common solution hai purane leader ke unreplicated writes ko discard kar dena. Isse durability ko le kar clients ki expectations toot sakti hain.
  • Discard karna tab dangerous hai jab doosre systems database par depend karte hon. Kuch data database ke bahar ke storage systems mein bhi rehta hai, aur use database ke saath consistent rakhna padta hai. Neeche wali story dikhati hai ki ek real incident mein kya hua tha.
  • Split brain. Kuch faults mein do nodes dono maan lete hain ki woh leader hain. Ise split brain kehte hain. Dono writes accept karein aur conflicts resolve karne ka koi process na ho, toh data lose ya corrupt hone ka bahut chance hai. Safety ke liye kuch systems do leaders detect hone par ek node ko shut down kar dete hain. Book ke hisaab se is approach ko fencing kehte hain, ya simple words mein Shoot The Other Node In The Head (STONITH). Mechanism ko dhyaan se design na kiya ho, toh dono nodes shut down ho sakte hain.
  • Timeout choose karna. Timeout lamba ho, toh leader sach mein fail hone par recovery mein zyada wait karna padta hai. Timeout chhota ho, toh bekaar ke failovers ka risk rehta hai. Temporary load spike ya delay hua network packet healthy leader ko dead jaisa dikha sakta hai. System pehle se struggle kar raha ho, toh bekaar ka failover cheezein aur bigaad sakta hai.
Example

Book GitHub ka ek incident step by step batati hai, jisse dikhta hai ki failover data problems kaise paida kar sakta hai:

  1. Ek out-of-date MySQL follower ko promote karke leader bana diya gaya.
  2. Database primary keys (row ki unique IDs) autoincrementing counter se assign karta tha. Naye leader ka counter purane leader ke counter se peeche tha.
  3. Nateeja yeh hua ki naye leader ne kuch aise primary keys de diye jo purana leader pehle hi assign kar chuka tha.
  4. Wahi keys ek Redis store mein bhi use ho rahi thi, jo database ka hissa nahi tha.
  5. Dono systems aapas mein inconsistent ho gaye, aur kuch private data galat users ko dikh gaya.

In problems ke aasaan solutions nahi hain. Isi wajah se kuch operations teams failovers manually karna pasand karti hain, chahe unka software automatic failover support karta ho. Is section ke issues sirf databases ke liye khaas nahi hain. Node failures, unreliable networks, aur consistency, durability, availability aur latency ke beech ke trade-offs distributed systems ki buniyaadi problems hain. Chapters 8 aur 9 inhe aur gehrayi mein discuss karte hain.

Replication Logs ka Implementation

Leader-based replication under the hood kaise kaam karta hai? Practice mein kai methods use hote hain, aur book har ek ko thoda sa dekhti hai.

Statement-based replication. Sabse simple case mein leader jo bhi write request, yani statement, execute karta hai use log karta hai, aur woh statement log apne followers ko bhej deta hai. Relational database mein iska matlab hai ki har INSERT, UPDATE ya DELETE statement forward hota hai. Har follower us SQL ko parse karke run karta hai, jaise woh statement kisi client se aaya ho. Yeh reasonable lagta hai, lekin kai tarah se toot sakta hai:

  • Jo statement nondeterministic function call karta hai, jaise current time ke liye NOW() ya random number ke liye RAND(), woh har replica par shayad alag value banayega.
  • Jo statements autoincrementing column use karte hain, ya existing data par depend karte hain (jaise WHERE condition wala UPDATE), unhe har replica par bilkul same order mein run hona chahiye. Warna unke effects alag ho sakte hain. Jab kaafi saari transactions ek saath chal rahi hon, tab yeh limiting ho jaata hai.
  • Side effects wale statements, jaise triggers, stored procedures aur user-defined functions, har replica par alag side effects kar sakte hain, jab tak woh side effects poori tarah deterministic na hon.

In problems ka workaround ho sakta hai. Jaise leader statement log karte waqt nondeterministic call ko ek fixed value se replace kar sakta hai, taaki har follower ko same value mile. Lekin itne saare edge cases hain ki aam taur par doosre methods ko prefer kiya jaata hai. MySQL version 5.1 se pehle statement-based replication use karta tha. Compact hone ki wajah se yeh ab bhi kabhi-kabhi use hota hai. Lekin default mein MySQL ab jab bhi koi statement nondeterministic ho, row-based replication (neeche) par switch ho jaata hai. VoltDB statement-based replication use karta hai aur ise safe banane ke liye transactions ka deterministic hona zaroori rakhta hai.

Write-ahead log (WAL) shipping. Chapter 3 mein bataya tha ki storage engines aam taur par har write ko ek log mein append karte hain. Log-structured storage engine mein log hi main storage hota hai, aur uske segments background mein compact hote rehte hain. B-tree mein, jo disk blocks ko wahin overwrite karta hai, har change pehle write-ahead log mein likha jaata hai, taaki crash ke baad index ko consistent state mein restore kiya ja sake. Dono hi cases mein log bytes ka append-only sequence hota hai jismein har write hota hai. Wahi log replica banane ke kaam aa sakta hai. Leader use disk par likhne ke saath-saath network ke through apne followers ko bhi bhejta hai. Follower log process karta hai aur wahi data structures ki exact copy bana leta hai jo leader ke paas hain.

Yeh method PostgreSQL aur Oracle jaise databases mein use hota hai. Iska main disadvantage yeh hai ki log data ko bahut low level par describe karta hai. Usmein likha hota hai ki kaun se disk blocks mein kaun se bytes badle. Isse replication storage engine se kaafi tight jud jaata hai. Database versions ke beech apna storage format badal de, toh aam taur par leader aur followers par alag versions chalana possible nahi hota. Operations mein yeh bahut matter kar sakta hai. Protocol follower ko leader se newer software version chalane de, toh tum zero downtime ke saath upgrade kar sakte ho. Pehle followers upgrade karo, phir kisi upgraded node par failover karke use naya leader bana do. WAL shipping mein aam taur par yeh version mismatch allowed nahi hota, isliye upgrades mein downtime lagta hai.

Logical (row-based) log replication. Ek alternative yeh hai ki replication ke liye ek log format use karo aur storage engine ke liye doosra. Tab replication log storage engine ke internals se decouple ho jaata hai. Is tarah ke log ko logical log kehte hain, taaki use physical storage format se alag pehchana ja sake. Relational database mein logical log aam taur par records ka ek sequence hota hai jo tables mein writes ko row-by-row describe karta hai:

  • Insert hui row ke liye log mein saare columns ki nayi values hoti hain.
  • Delete hui row ke liye log mein row ko identify karne jitna data hota hai. Aam taur par yeh primary key hoti hai. Table mein primary key na ho, toh saare columns ki old values log karni padti hain.
  • Update hui row ke liye log mein row ko identify karne jitna data hota hai, aur saath mein saare columns ki nayi values, ya kam se kam un columns ki jo badle.

Jo transaction kai rows badalti hai, woh aise kai records banati hai, aur uske baad ek record aata hai jo kehta hai ki transaction commit ho gayi. Jab MySQL ka binlog row-based replication par set ho, toh woh aise hi kaam karta hai. Logical log storage engine se alag hota hai, isliye use backward compatible rakhna aasaan hota hai. Tab leader aur follower alag software versions, ya alag storage engines bhi chala sakte hain. Logical log ko bahar ke programs ke liye padhna bhi aasaan hota hai. Jab tum database ka content offline analysis ke liye data warehouse mein bhejna chahte hon, ya custom indexes aur caches banana chahte hon, tab yeh kaam aata hai. Is technique ko change data capture kehte hain, jise Chapter 11 cover karta hai.

Trigger-based replication. Ab tak ke methods database mein built-in hain aur unhe application code nahi chahiye. Aksar tum yahi chahte ho. Lekin kabhi-kabhi zyada flexibility chahiye hoti hai. Ho sakta hai tum data ka sirf ek subset replicate karna chaho, ek tarah ke database se doosre tarah ke database mein copy karna chahein, ya custom conflict-resolution logic lagana chahein (neeche write conflicts wala section dekho). Aise cases mein replication ko application layer tak upar le jaana pad sakta hai.

Oracle GoldenGate jaise kuch tools database ka log padhte hain aur changes ko application ke liye available kara dete hain. Ek aur option un features par based hai jo kai relational databases dete hain: triggers aur stored procedures. Trigger custom code hota hai jo data change (write transaction) hone par database automatically run karta hai. Trigger change ko ek alag table mein record kar sakta hai. Ek external process us table ko padhta hai, zaroori application logic lagata hai, aur change ko kisi doosre system mein replicate karta hai. Oracle ke liye Databus aur Postgres ke liye Bucardo aise hi kaam karte hain. Trigger-based replication ka overhead built-in methods se zyada hota hai, aur isme bugs aur limitations ka chance bhi zyada hota hai. Lekin iski flexibility is cost ko worth kar sakti hai.

Replication Lag ki Problems

Node failures se bachna replicate karne ki sirf ek wajah hai. Introduction mein aur wajahein bhi thi: scalability, yani ek machine se zyada requests handle karna, aur latency, yani replicas ko users ke paas rakhna.

Leader-based replication saare writes ek hi node se guzaarta hai. Lekin read-only queries kisi bhi replica par ja sakti hain. Kai web workloads mein zyaadatar reads hote hain aur writes ka hissa chhota hota hai. Unke liye ek achha option hai: bahut saare followers banao aur read requests unmein baant do. Isse leader ka load kam hota hai, aur paas ke replicas reads ka jawab de paate hain. Followers add karte hi reads ki total capacity badh jaati hai. Yeh read-scaling design realistically sirf asynchronous replication ke saath kaam karta hai. Har follower par synchronously copy karne ki koshish karein, toh ek node failure ya ek network outage poore system ko writes ke liye unavailable bana dega. Jitne zyada nodes honge, utna zyada chance hai ki koi ek down ho, isliye fully synchronous setup bahut unreliable hoga.

Catch yeh hai ki asynchronous follower se read karne wali application ko outdated information dikh sakti hai, agar woh follower peeche reh gaya ho. Ek hi waqt par chalayi gayi do queries, ek leader par aur ek follower par, alag results de sakti hain. Bas itna hai ki follower ko kuch writes abhi mile nahi hain. Yeh inconsistency temporary hoti hai. Writes ruk jaao aur tum wait karo, toh followers catch up karke leader se match kar jaate ho. Copies aakhir mein agree kar leti hain, isliye is behavior ko eventual consistency kehte hain. Yeh term Douglas Terry aur unke colleagues ne banaya, Werner Vogels ne ise popular kiya, aur yeh kai NoSQL projects ka rallying cry ban gaya. Book ka point hai ki aisa behavior sirf NoSQL databases ka nahi hai. Asynchronously replicated relational database ke followers mein bhi yahi characteristics hoti hain.

"Eventually" word intentionally vague hai. Aam taur par is par koi limit nahi hai ki replica kitna peeche reh sakta hai. Normally leader par write aur follower par uske dikhne ke beech ka delay, jise replication lag kehte hain, second ka ek chhota hissa ho sakta hai aur notice bhi nahi hota. Lekin system capacity ke kareeb chal raha ho, ya network mein problem ho, toh lag kai seconds ya minutes tak bhi ja sakta hai. Lag itna bada ho jaaye, toh inconsistencies theory nahi rehtin, applications ke liye real problem ban jaati hain. Is section ka baaki hissa teen examples aur unhe solve karne ke kuch tarike dekhta hai.

Apne Hi Writes Ko Read Karna

Kai applications user ko kuch data submit karne dete hain aur phir dikhate hain ki usne kya submit kiya. Yeh customer database ka koi record ho sakta hai ya discussion thread par ek comment. Naya data leader ko bhejna padta hai. Lekin user use dekhe, tab read kisi follower se aa sakta hai. Yeh pattern un data ke liye theek baithta hai jo aksar dekha jaata hai par kabhi-kabhi hi likha jaata hai.

Example

Asynchronous replication ke saath problem yeh hai, step by step:

  1. User apni profile mein change save karta hai. Save leader ke paas jaata hai.
  2. Leader use accept kar leta hai, lekin jis follower se user read karta hai use change abhi mila nahi hai.
  3. User turant page reload karta hai. Read us follower ke paas jaata hai.
  4. Page par purana data dikhta hai. User ko lagta hai ki save lost ho gaya, aur woh naraaz ho jaata hai, jo samajh aata hai.

Iska fix ek guarantee hai jise read-after-write consistency kehte hain, ya read-your-writes consistency. Yeh promise karti hai ki user page reload kare, toh use hamesha apne kiye hue updates dikhenge. Doosre users ke baare mein koi promise nahi hai. Unke updates shayad abhi dikhein hi nahi. Lekin yeh har user ko bharosa deti hai ki uska apna input save ho chuka hai.

Leader-based replication wala system yeh kaise de sakta hai? Kai techniques hain:

  • Jab data user ne badla ho sakta hai, tab leader se read karo. Iske liye bina query kiye yeh jaanne ka tarika chahiye ki koi cheez modify hui ho sakti hai ya nahi. Maan lo social network par user ki profile aam taur par sirf uska owner edit kar sakta hai. Ek simple rule hai: apni profile leader se padho aur baaki sabki follower se.
  • Jab zyaadatar cheezein editable hon, tab doosre criteria use karo. Agar lagbhag sab kuch user edit kar sakta hai, toh sab kuch leader se read karne par read scaling ka faayda khatam ho jaayega. Iske bajaye tum last update ka time track kar sakte ho, aur uske ek minute tak leader se read kar sakte ho. Tum followers par replication lag monitor karke aise kisi bhi follower se bach sakte ho jo leader se ek minute se zyada peeche ho.
  • Last write ka timestamp yaad rakho. Client apne sabse recent write ka timestamp rakhta hai. Phir system pakka karta hai ki user ke reads serve karne wala replica kam se kam us timestamp tak ke updates reflect kare. Replica itna current na ho, toh read kisi doosre replica ke paas ja sakta hai, ya replica ke catch up karne tak wait kar sakta hai. Timestamp logical ho sakta hai, jaise log position, ya system clock. Clock use karein, toh clock synchronization bahut critical ho jaata hai. Chapter 8 unreliable clocks ko cover karta hai.
  • Leader-only requests ko sahi datacenter tak route karo. Replicas kai datacenters mein phaile hon, proximity ya availability ke liye, toh jis request ko leader serve kare use us datacenter tak pahunchna hoga jahan leader hai.

Cheezein aur mushkil ho jaati hain jab ek hi user service ko kai devices se access kare, jaise desktop browser aur phone app. Tab tum cross-device read-after-write consistency chahoge. Koi ek device par information daale, toh use woh doosre device par bhi dikhni chahiye. Isse extra issues aate hain. Timestamp approach mushkil ho jaata hai, kyunki ek device par chalta code nahi jaanta ki doosre device par kaun se updates hue. Us metadata ko ek central jagah rakhna padta hai. Yeh guarantee bhi nahi hai ki alag devices ke connections same datacenter tak pahunchein. Home broadband wala desktop aur cellular data wala phone bilkul alag network routes le sakte hain. Approach mein leader se read karna zaroori ho, toh pehle tumhe user ke saare devices ko same datacenter tak route karna pad sakta hai.

Try karo

Ek aisi site socho jahan users apni profile edit karte hain aur doosron ke comments bhi padhte hain. Kaun se reads tum leader ko bhejoge aur kaun se followers ko? Har choice ke liye batao ki user ke paas kaun si guarantee rehti hai aur kaun si woh kho sakta hai.

Monotonic Reads

Doosri anomaly yeh hai ki user ko cheezein time mein peeche jaati dikh sakti hain. Aisa tab hota hai jab user kai reads karta hai aur har read ek alag replica par jaata hai.

Example

Book ka Figure 5-4 dikhata hai ki user 2345 wahi query do baar chalata hai:

  1. Pehli query ek aise follower par jaati hai jiska lag kam hai. Woh ek comment return karta hai jo user 1234 ne haal hi mein add kiya tha.
  2. User page refresh karta hai, aur doosri query ek aise follower par jaati hai jiska lag zyada hai. Us follower ko user 1234 ka comment abhi mila nahi hai, isliye comment missing hai.

User 2345 ke liye yeh bahut confusing hai. Comment aata hai aur phir gaayab ho jaata hai. Asal mein doosra read system ko pehle read se pehle ke point in time par dekhta hai. Problem sabse zyada tab hoti hai jab har page refresh kisi random server par route ho.

Pehli query kuch return na karti, toh user ko pata hi nahi chalta ki koi comment missing hai. Confusion isliye hota hai ki pehle naya data dikha aur phir purana.

Monotonic reads woh guarantee hai jo is anomaly ko rokti hai. Yeh strong consistency se weak hai, lekin eventual consistency se strong. Read phir bhi purani value return kar sakta hai. Monotonic reads yeh promise karta hai ki ek user kai reads sequence mein kare, toh naya data padhne ke baad woh kabhi purana data nahi padhega. Us user ko time kabhi peeche jaata nahi dikhega. Alag-alag users phir bhi alag replicas se read kar sakte hain.

Monotonic reads paane ka ek tarika yeh hai ki har user hamesha ek hi replica se read kare. Replica random pick karne ke bajaye user ID ke hash se choose kiya ja sakta hai. Woh replica fail ho jaaye, toh user ki queries ko kisi doosre replica par reroute karna padega.

Consistent Prefix Reads

Teesri anomaly causality se judi hai, yani cause aur effect se. Ek chhota sa dialog socho. Mr. Poons Mrs. Cake se poochte hain ki woh future mein kitna door tak dekh sakti hain. Mrs. Cake jawab deti hain ki aam taur par lagbhag das seconds.

Example

In do sentences ke beech ek causal link hai: Mrs. Cake ne sawaal suna aur uska jawab diya. Ab maan lo ek teesra insaan followers ke through yeh baatcheet sun raha hai. Mrs. Cake ke words kam lag wale follower se guzarte hain. Mr. Poons ke words zyada lag wale follower se guzarte hain, jaisa Figure 5-5 dikhata hai. Sunne wale ko pehle jawab sunai deta hai aur sawaal baad mein. Use lagta hai ki Mrs. Cake sawaal poochhe jaane se pehle hi jawab de rahi hain. Book aisi psychic powers ko impressive lekin bahut confusing kehti hai.

Is tarah ki anomaly rokne ke liye ek aur guarantee chahiye, jise consistent prefix reads kehte hain. Yeh kehti hai ki writes ka sequence kisi khaas order mein hua ho, toh unhe padhne wala har insaan unhe usi order mein aate dekhega.

Yeh problem partitioned (sharded) databases mein khaas taur par common hai, jinhe Chapter 6 cover karta hai. Database saare writes ko har jagah same order mein apply kare, toh reads hamesha consistent prefix dekhte hain, isliye yeh anomaly nahi ho sakti. Lekin kai distributed databases mein alag-alag partitions independently kaam karte hain. Unke beech writes ka koi global order nahi hota. Database padhne wala user kuch hisse purani state mein aur kuch hisse nayi state mein dekh sakta hai.

Ise address karne ke do tarike hain. Ek yeh ki jo writes causally related hon, woh hamesha same partition par jaayein. Lekin kuch applications mein yeh efficiently nahi ho sakta. Doosra tarika un algorithms ka hai jo causal dependencies ko explicitly track karte hain. Chapter is topic par happens-before relationship wale section mein dobara aata hai.

Replication Lag ke Solutions

Eventually consistent system ke saath kaam karte waqt socho ki replication lag kai minutes ya ghanton tak badh jaaye, toh application kaise behave karegi. Jawab "koi problem nahi" ho, toh theek hai. Lekin users ka experience kharab hoga, toh system ko aisa design karo ki woh stronger guarantee de, jaise read-after-write consistency. Aisa maan lena ki replication synchronous hai, jabki asal mein woh asynchronous hai, aage chalkar problems laata hai.

Jaisa upar discuss hua, application database se stronger guarantee de sakti hai, jaise kuch data leader se read karke. Lekin in issues ko application code mein handle karna complex hai aur galti hone ka chance zyada hai. Behtar yeh hoga ki application developers ko subtle replication issues ke baare mein sochna hi na pade, aur woh database par bharosa kar sakein ki woh sahi cheez karega. Transactions isi liye hote hain. Transaction database ka ek tarika hai stronger guarantees dene ka, taaki application simple ho sake.

Single-node transactions kaafi time se available hain. Lekin distributed databases mein jaate waqt, jo replicated bhi hain aur partitioned bhi, kai systems ne unhe chhod diya. Unka argument tha ki transactions performance aur availability ke hisaab se bahut mehengi hain, aur scalable system mein eventual consistency se bachna mumkin nahi hai. Isme kuch sachchai hai, lekin yeh claim bahut simple hai. Book aage ke hisson mein ek zyada nuanced view develop karti hai. Chapters 7 aur 9 transactions par wapas aate hain, aur Part III kuch alternative mechanisms discuss karta hai.

Asli idea

Replication setup choose karne se pehle yeh choose karo ki tumhare users ko kaun si consistency guarantee chahiye. Stale read se users confuse honge, toh unke apne changes ke liye read-after-write consistency use karo, yeh maan kar mat chalo ki copies agree karti hain.

Multi-Leader Replication

Ab tak is chapter mein hum sirf single leader wali replication dekh rahe the. Yeh common approach hai, lekin aur options bhi hain. Single leader ki sabse badi problem yeh hai ki saari writes usi se guzarni padti hain. Agar kisi bhi wajah se leader tak pahunch nahi paaye, jaise tumhare aur leader ke beech network interruption ho jaaye, toh tum database mein write hi nahi kar sakte.

Iska natural extension yeh hai ki ek se zyada node writes accept karein. Replication ka tarika wahi rehta hai. Jo bhi node write process karta hai, woh us data change ko baaki saare nodes ko forward kar deta hai. Isko multi-leader configuration kehte hain. Ise master-master ya active/active replication bhi bolte hain. Har leader, baaki leaders ke liye saath-saath follower ki tarah kaam karta hai.

Multi-leader replication ke use cases

Ek hi datacenter ke andar multi-leader replication use karna aam taur par sahi nahi hota, kyunki extra complexity ke mukable benefits kam milte hain. Phir bhi kuch situations hain jahan yeh reasonable hai. Book mein teen situations bataye gaye hain.

Multi-datacenter operation. Maan lo ek database ke replicas kai datacenters mein hain. Tum shayad yeh isliye chahte ho ki poora datacenter fail ho jaaye toh bhi system chalta rahe, ya users ke paas rahe. Normal single-leader replication mein leader ek hi datacenter mein hota hai, aur saari writes usi se jaati hain, chahe user duniya ke kisi doosre hisse mein ho.

Multi-leader replication mein har datacenter ka apna leader ho sakta hai. Har datacenter ke andar regular leader-follower replication chalti hai. Datacenters ke beech, har datacenter ka leader apne changes doosre datacenters ke leaders ko replicate karta hai. Book ka Figure 5-6 yahi architecture dikhata hai. Dono approaches ki comparison yeh hai:

  • Performance. Single-leader replication mein har write ko internet cross karke leader wale datacenter tak jaana padta hai. Isse writes mein kaafi latency aa jaati hai, aur kai datacenters rakhne ka purpose hi khatam ho sakta hai. Multi-leader replication mein har write local datacenter mein process hoti hai, phir baaki datacenters ko asynchronously replicate hoti hai. Datacenters ke beech ki delay users se chhup jaati hai, isliye unhe performance behtar mehsoos ho sakti hai.
  • Datacenter outages ko tolerate karna. Jis datacenter mein leader hai woh fail ho jaaye, toh single-leader replication mein kisi doosre datacenter ke follower ko promote kiya ja sakta hai. Multi-leader replication mein har datacenter independently chalta rehta hai. Failed datacenter wapas aata hai, toh replication catch up kar leti hai.
  • Network problems ko tolerate karna. Datacenters ke beech ka traffic aam taur par public internet se guzarta hai, jo local network se kam reliable hota hai. Single-leader replication is link ki problems ke prati bahut sensitive hoti hai, kyunki uski writes is link par synchronously hoti hain. Asynchronous copying wali multi-leader replication aam taur par network trouble ko behtar tolerate kar leti hai, kyunki thodi der ki interruption se writes process hona band nahi hota.
Trade-offs
ConcernDatacenters ke across single leaderDatacenters ke across multi-leader
Remote users ke liye write speedHar write leader ke datacenter tak travel karti haiWrites local par handle hoti hain aur asynchronously copy hoti hain
Poora datacenter fail ho jaayeKisi aur jagah ke follower ko leader promote kar dete hainHar datacenter chalta rehta hai, aur replication baad mein catch up karti hai
Datacenters ke beech ka link unreliable hoSensitive, kyunki writes is link ka wait karti hainAam taur par tolerant, kyunki writes ko iska wait nahi karna padta
Conflicting writesHo hi nahi sakte, kyunki saari writes ek leader se guzarti hainInhe detect aur resolve karna padta hai

Kuch databases multi-leader configurations ko by default support karte hain. Warna aksar ise external tools se set up kiya jaata hai, jaise MySQL ke liye Tungsten Replicator, PostgreSQL ke liye BDR, aur Oracle ke liye GoldenGate.

Multi-leader replication ka ek bada downside hai. Ek hi data do datacenters mein concurrently modify ho sakta hai, aur un write conflicts ko resolve karna padta hai. Write conflicts handle karne wala section isko cover karta hai. Saath hi, multi-leader replication aksar databases bante ke baad add ki gayi thi, isliye isme subtle configuration pitfalls aur doosre features ke saath surprising interactions ho sakte hain. Autoincrementing keys, triggers aur integrity constraints sab problematic ho sakte hain. Isi wajah se book ke hisaab se multi-leader replication ko aksar dangerous territory maana jaata hai, jisse ho sake toh bachna chahiye.

Offline operation wale clients. Multi-leader replication un apps ke liye bhi fit baithti hai jinhe internet se disconnected rehkar bhi kaam karte rehna hai. Phone, laptop aur doosre devices ke calendar apps socho. Tumhe apni meetings dekhni hain aur nayi add karni hain, device online ho ya na ho. Offline rehte hue jo bhi changes kiye gaye, unhe device ke agli baar connect hone par server aur tumhare baaki devices ke saath sync karna padta hai.

Is case mein har device ka ek local database hota hai jo leader ki tarah kaam karta hai, kyunki woh writes accept karta hai. Ek asynchronous multi-leader process tumhare saare devices ke calendar replicas ko sync karta hai. Replication lag ghanton ya din tak bhi ho sakta hai, yeh is par depend karta hai ki internet access kab milta hai. Architecture ke hisaab se yeh datacenters ke beech multi-leader replication jaisa hi hai, bas extreme tak le jaaya gaya. Har device ek “datacenter” hai, aur unke beech ka network extremely unreliable hai. Book ka kehna hai ki calendar sync ki kharab implementations ka itihaas dikhata hai ki multi-leader replication ko sahi karna kitna tricky hai. Kuch tools ise aasaan banane ki koshish karte hain. Jaise CouchDB isi mode of operation ke liye design kiya gaya hai.

Collaborative editing. Real-time editing tools mein kai log ek hi document ko ek saath change kar sakte hain. Etherpad aur Google Docs iske examples hain. Book ke hisaab se hum collaborative editing ko aam taur par replication problem nahi maante. Lekin offline editing se isme kaafi kuch common hai. Jab ek user edit karta hai, change turant uske local replica par apply ho jaata hai, yani uske browser ya app mein document ki state par. Phir woh asynchronously server tak aur usi document ko edit karne wale doosre logon tak replicate hota hai.

Editing conflicts bilkul na ho, iske liye application document ko lock kar sakti hai. User ko edit karne se pehle lock lena padta hai. Agar koi doosra user edit karna chahta hai, toh use wait karna padta hai jab tak pehla user apne changes commit karke lock release na kar de. Yeh model leader par transactions ke saath single-leader replication ke barabar hai. Agar tezi se collaboration chahiye, toh change ki unit bahut chhoti rakh sakte hain, jaise ek keystroke, aur locking skip kar sakte hain. Isse kai log ek saath edit kar paate hain. Lekin phir multi-leader replication ki saari challenges bhi aa jaati hain, jisme conflict resolution ki zaroorat bhi shamil hai.

Write conflicts ko handle karna

Multi-leader replication ki sabse badi problem yeh hai ki write conflicts ho sakte hain, isliye conflict resolution zaroori hai.

Example

Maan lo ek wiki page hai jise do users ek hi moment mein edit kar rahe hain (book ka Figure 5-7). Page ka title abhi A hai.

  1. User 1 title ko A se B kar deta hai. Change leader 1 par successfully apply ho jaata hai.
  2. Usi moment user 2 title ko A se C kar deta hai. Change leader 2 par successfully apply ho jaata hai.
  3. Baad mein dono leaders apne changes ek doosre ko asynchronously replicate karte hain.
  4. Changes pahunchte hain, toh system ko conflict detect hota hai: do writes ne same field ko alag-alag tarike se change kiya.

Single-leader database mein yeh problem nahi aati, kyunki wahan same field par doosri write ko ya toh wait karaya jaata hai ya reject kar diya jaata hai.

Synchronous versus asynchronous conflict detection. Single-leader database mein doosra writer ya toh pehli write khatam hone ka wait karta hai, ya uski transaction abort ho jaati hai, jisse user ko retry karna padta hai.
