Multi-leader setup mein dono writes succeed ho jaati hain. Conflict baad mein hi, asynchronously pakda jaata hai, aur tab tak user se use resolve karwana shayad bahut late ho chuka hota hai. Tum detection ko synchronous bana sakte ho, yani user ko success batane se pehle wait karo jab tak write har replica tak na pahunch jaaye. Lekin phir multi-leader replication ka main advantage chala jaata hai, ki har replica independently writes accept karta hai. Book ka point hai ki agar tumhe synchronous conflict detection chahiye, toh seedha single-leader replication hi use kar lo.

Conflict avoidance. Sabse simple strategy hai conflicts ko avoid karna. Agar application yeh ensure kare ki kisi particular record ki saari writes same leader se jaayein, toh conflicts ho hi nahi sakte. Kai multi-leader implementations conflicts ko poorly handle karti hain, isliye unhe avoid karna aksar recommend kiya jaata hai. Jaise, ek application jahan users apna hi data edit karte hain, wahan ek particular user ki requests hamesha same datacenter par route ki ja sakti hain, aur us datacenter ka leader reads aur writes dono handle karta hai. Alag-alag users ke home datacenters alag ho sakte hain, shayad geographic closeness se chune hue. Kisi ek user ke point of view se yeh setup essentially single-leader hi hai. Lekin kabhi-kabhi kisi record ka designated leader badalna padta hai. Ho sakta hai ek datacenter fail ho gaya ho, isliye traffic reroute hua, ya user kisi doosre datacenter ke paas move kar gaya ho. Aisi situation mein conflict avoidance toot jaata hai, aur tumhe alag leaders par concurrent writes ki possibility handle karni padti hai.

Consistent state ki taraf converge karna. Single-leader database writes ko sequential order mein apply karta hai. Agar kai updates same field ko touch karein, toh aakhri wala final value decide karta hai. Multi-leader setup mein writes ka koi defined order nahi hota, isliye final value clear nahi hoti. Figure 5-7 mein leader 1 pehle title ko B karta hai aur phir C. Leader 2 pehle C karta hai aur phir B. Koi bhi order doosre se zyada sahi nahi hai.

Agar har replica bas writes ko usi order mein apply kar de jisme usne dekhi, toh database inconsistent ho jaayega. Leader 1 ke paas C hoga aur leader 2 ke paas B. Yeh acceptable nahi hai. Har replication scheme ko ensure karna padta hai ki data eventually saare replicas par same ho. Isliye database ko conflict ko convergent tarike se resolve karna padta hai, matlab saari changes replicate hone ke baad saare replicas same final value par pahunchein. Iske kai tarike hain:

  • Har write ko ek unique ID do, jaise timestamp, ek lamba random number, UUID (universally unique identifier), ya key aur value ka hash. Sabse high ID wali write ko winner chuno, aur baaki ko fenk do. Agar ID timestamp hai, toh ise last write wins (LWW) kehte hain. Yeh popular hai, lekin book warn karti hai ki isme data loss ka khatra bahut zyada hai. Chapter aage chalkar end mein LWW par wapas aata hai.
  • Har replica ko ek unique ID do, aur higher-numbered replica ki writes hamesha lower-numbered replica ki writes par jeetein. Isme bhi data loss hota hai.
  • Values ko kisi tarah merge kar do. Jaise, unhe alphabetically sort karke jod do. Figure 5-7 mein merged title kuch “B/C” jaisa ho sakta hai.
  • Conflict ko ek explicit data structure mein record kar lo jisme saari information rahe, aur application code likho jo baad mein ise resolve kare, shayad user se poochkar.

Custom conflict resolution logic. Conflict resolve karne ka sahi tarika aksar application par depend karta hai. Isliye zyadatar multi-leader tools tumhe application code mein resolution logic likhne dete hain. Yeh code write time par ya read time par chal sakta hai:

  • On write. Jaise hi database ko replicated changes mein conflict detect hota hai, woh ek conflict handler call karta hai. Yeh handler aam taur par user ko prompt nahi kar sakta, kyunki woh background process mein chalta hai aur jaldi khatam hona chahiye. Jaise Bucardo tumhe is kaam ke liye Perl ka ek chhota snippet likhne deta hai.
  • On read. Conflict detect hone par saari conflicting writes store kar li jaati hain. Agli baar data read hota hai, toh multiple versions application ko return ho jaate hain. Application user ko prompt kar sakti hai ya conflict automatically resolve kar sakti hai, phir result wapas database mein likh deti hai. CouchDB isi tarah kaam karta hai.
Dhyaan do

Conflict resolution aam taur par ek time par ek row ya document par lagta hai, poori transaction par nahi. Agar ek transaction kai rows ko atomically likhti hai, toh conflicts resolve karte waqt un writes mein se har ek ko alag se consider kiya jaata hai.

Automatic conflict resolution

Conflict resolution ke rules jaldi complicated ho sakte hain, aur custom code mein errors hone ke chances rehte hain. Amazon ek aksar diya jaane wala example hai jahan conflict handler ke surprising effects dikhe. Kuch time tak shopping cart ka handler cart mein add kiye gaye items rakhta tha, lekin remove kiye gaye items nahi. Isliye customers ko kabhi-kabhi remove karne ke baad bhi items cart mein wapas dikh jaate the.

Researchers ne concurrent changes ko automatically resolve karne par kaam kiya hai. Book teen lines of work mention karti hai:

  • Conflict-free replicated datatypes (CRDTs) sets, maps, ordered lists, counters aur isi tarah ki cheezon ke liye data structures ka ek family hain. Inhe kai users concurrently edit kar sakte hain, aur yeh conflicts ko sensible tarike se automatically resolve kar dete hain. Kuch CRDTs Riak 2.0 mein implement kiye gaye hain.
  • Mergeable persistent data structures history ko explicitly track karte hain, kuch-kuch Git version control system ki tarah. Yeh three-way merge function use karte hain, jabki CRDTs two-way merge use karte hain.
  • Operational transformation woh conflict-resolution algorithm hai jo Etherpad aur Google Docs jaise collaborative editors ke peeche hai. Ise ordered list of items ke concurrent editing ke liye design kiya gaya tha, jaise text document banane wale characters.

Databases mein in algorithms ki implementations abhi naye hain. Kleppmann ko ummeed hai ki waqt ke saath yeh aur replicated systems mein built-in honge. Automatic conflict resolution se applications ke liye multi-leader data synchronization kaafi simple ho sakta hai.

Conflict kya hota hai?

Kuch conflicts obvious hote hain. Wiki example mein do writes ne same record ke same field ko change kiya, aur do alag values set ki. Isme koi shak nahi ki yeh conflict hai.

Kuch aur conflicts pakadna mushkil hota hai. Ek meeting room booking system socho jo track karta hai ki kaun sa group kaun sa room kis time book kiye hue hai. Application ko ensure karna hai ki ek room ek time par sirf ek group book kare, yani koi do bookings overlap nahi honi chahiye.

Example
  1. Do alag groups same room ko same time ke liye book karne ki koshish karte hain.
  2. Agar dono requests same leader tak pahunchein, toh application availability check karke ek ko reject kar sakti hai.
  3. Lekin agar dono bookings do alag leaders par hui hain, toh har leader ko room free dikh sakta hai. Har ek apni booking accept kar leta hai.
  4. Leaders replicate karte hain, toh system mein ek room ke liye do overlapping bookings hoti hain. Yeh conflict hai, chahe koi bhi single write galat na lagi ho.

Booking accept karne se pehle availability check karne se yeh nahi rukta, kyunki dono checks alag leaders par hote hain. Book ke hisaab se iska koi quick, ready-made jawab nahi hai. Aage ke chapters is tarah ki problem ko samajhne ka raasta dikhate hain. Chapter 7 mein conflicts ke aur examples hain, aur Chapter 12 replicated systems mein conflicts ko detect aur resolve karne ke scalable tarikon par baat karta hai.

Multi-leader replication topologies

Ek replication topology un communication paths ko describe karti hai jinse writes ek node se doosre node tak jaati hain. Do leaders ho toh sirf ek sensible topology hai: har leader apni saari writes doosre ko bhej deta hai. Teen ya zyada leaders ho toh kai topologies possible hain. Book ka Figure 5-8 teen dikhata hai.

Sabse general topology all-to-all hai, jahan har leader apni writes har doosre leader ko bhejta hai. Isse zyada restricted topologies bhi use hoti hain. MySQL by default sirf circular topology support karta hai. Isme har node ek node se writes receive karta hai aur unhe, apni writes ke saath, ek doosre node ko forward kar deta hai. Ek aur popular shape star hai, jisme ek designated root node writes ko baaki sabko forward karta hai. Star ko tree tak generalize kiya ja sakta hai. (Book ka note hai ki yeh star, star schema se alag hai, kyunki star schema data model ka structure describe karta hai, nodes ke communicate karne ka tarika nahi.)

Circular aur star topologies mein ek write ko har replica tak pahunchne se pehle kai nodes se guzarna pad sakta hai. Isliye nodes ko doosre nodes se mile changes forward karne padte hain. Infinite loops rokne ke liye har node ko ek unique identifier diya jaata hai. Replication log mein har write par un saare nodes ke identifiers ka tag lagta hai jinse woh guzri hai. Kisi node ko jab apne hi identifier ka tag lagi hui change milti hai, toh woh use ignore kar deta hai, kyunki use woh pehle hi process kar chuka hai.

Circular aur star topologies ki ek kamzori yeh hai ki ek single node fail ho jaaye, toh baaki nodes ke beech replication messages ka flow ruk sakta hai. Jab tak failed node theek nahi hota, shayad woh aapas mein communicate nahi kar paayein. Topology ko reconfigure karke failed node ko bypass kiya ja sakta hai, lekin zyadatar deployments mein yeh reconfiguration haath se karna padta hai. Zyada densely connected topology, jaise all-to-all, failures ko behtar tolerate karti hai, kyunki messages alag-alag paths se travel kar sakte hain.

All-to-all ki apni ek problem hai. Kuch network links doosron se tez hote hain, jaise congestion ki wajah se. Isliye kuch replication messages doosron se aage nikal sakte hain.

Example

Book ka Figure 5-9 dikhata hai ki writes kaise replica par galat order mein pahunch sakti hain:

  1. Client A leader 1 par ek table mein row insert karta hai.
  2. Phir Client B leader 3 par usi row ko update karta hai. B ka update A ke insert par depend karta hai.
  3. Leader 2 ko yeh dono writes galat order mein mil sakti hain. Use pehle update milta hai, jo uske point of view se aisi row ka update hai jo abhi exist hi nahi karti.
  4. Insert use baad mein milta hai, jo pehle aana chahiye tha.

Yeh causality problem hai, upar wali consistent prefix reads problem jaisi. Update pehle wale insert par depend karta hai, isliye har node ko pehle insert process karna chahiye. Har write par timestamp laga dena kaafi nahi hai, kyunki clocks par bharosa nahi kiya ja sakta ki woh itni achhi tarah synchronized hain ki leader 2 par in events ko order kar sakein. Book ke hisaab se version vectors naam ki technique inhe sahi order mein laa sakti hai, aur concurrent writes detect karne wala section ise explain karta hai.

Kai multi-leader systems conflict detection poorly implement karte hain. Jab book likhi gayi thi, tab PostgreSQL BDR writes ki causal ordering provide nahi karta tha. MySQL ka Tungsten Replicator toh conflicts detect karne ki koshish bhi nahi karta tha. Agar tum multi-leader system use karte ho, toh book ki salah hai ki documentation dhyaan se padhein aur achhi tarah test karein, taaki confirm ho sake ki woh sach mein wahi guarantees deta hai jo tum maan rahe ho.

Leaderless Replication

Ab tak ke approaches, yani single-leader aur multi-leader, ek hi idea par chalte hain. Client ek write ek node ko bhejta hai, jo leader hota hai, aur database use baaki replicas par copy kar deta hai. Writes kis order mein process hongi, yeh leader decide karta hai, aur followers leader ki writes usi order mein apply karte hain.

Kuch data systems alag approach lete hain. Woh leader ka concept hi hata dete hain aur koi bhi replica seedha clients se writes accept kar sakta hai. Sabse purane replicated data systems mein se kuch leaderless the, lekin relational databases ke daur mein yeh idea lagbhag bhula diya gaya. Amazon ne ise apne in-house Dynamo system mein use kiya, uske baad yeh phir se popular ho gaya. (Book ke hisaab se Dynamo Amazon ke bahar available nahi hai. AWS ka DynamoDB ek alag product hai, jo single-leader replication par bana hai.) Riak, Cassandra aur Voldemort open source datastores hain jinke leaderless models Dynamo se inspired hain, isliye is tarah ke database ko Dynamo-style bhi kehte hain.

Kuch leaderless systems mein client har write seedha kai replicas ko bhejta hai. Kuch mein ek coordinator node client ki taraf se yeh kaam karta hai. Lekin leader ke ulat, coordinator writes ka koi particular order enforce nahi karta. Kleppmann kehte hain ki is farq ke database ke use par bahut gehre asar padte hain.

Node down ho toh database mein write karna

Maan lo ek database ke teen replicas hain, aur ek unavailable hai, shayad isliye ki woh update install karne ke liye reboot ho raha hai. Leader-based replication mein agar tum writes accept karte rehna chahte ho, toh shayad failover karna padega. Leaderless design mein koi failover karna hi nahi padta.

Example

Book ka Figure 5-10 dikhata hai ki kya hota hai. ID 1234 wala user teen-replica store mein write karta hai, aur ek replica down hai:

  1. Client write ek saath teeno replicas ko bhejta hai.
  2. Replicas 1 aur 2 available hain. Woh write store kar lete hain aur “ok” reply dete hain.
  3. Replica 3 down hai, isliye woh write miss kar deta hai.
  4. Write successful maanne ke liye client ko sirf do “ok” replies chahiye. Do mil gaye, toh client write accept kar leta hai. Ek replica ne write miss ki, is baat ko woh bas ignore kar deta hai.

Ab maan lo jo node unavailable tha woh wapas online aa gaya aur clients usse read karne lage. Jab woh down tha, tab ki saari writes uske paas nahi hain, isliye usse aane wale reads stale, purani values return kar sakte hain. Isko solve karne ke liye, client jab read karta hai toh request sirf ek replica ko nahi bhejta. Woh kai nodes ko parallel mein read requests bhejta hai. Alag-alag nodes se alag jawab aa sakte hain. Ek node ki up-to-date value doosre node ki stale value se different ho sakti hai. Version numbers client ko batate hain ki kaunsi value newer hai. Version numbers ke baare mein chapter aage samjhata hai.

Read repair aur anti-entropy

Replication scheme ko yeh ensure karna chahiye ki aakhir mein saara data har replica tak pahunch jaye. Node wapas online aane ke baad woh miss hui writes ko kaise pakadta hai? Dynamo-style datastores aksar do mechanisms use karte hain.

Read repair. Jab client kai nodes se parallel mein read karta hai, toh woh stale responses pehchan sakta hai. Figure 5-10 mein user 2345 ko replica 3 se version 6 ki value milti hai, aur replicas 1 aur 2 se version 7 ki. Client dekh leta hai ki replica 3 stale hai, toh woh newer version 7 ki value replica 3 par wapas likh deta hai. Yeh un values ke liye achha chalta hai jinhe aksar read kiya jaata hai.

Anti-entropy process. Kuch datastores ek background process bhi chalate hain. Yeh process lagataar replicas ke beech data ke differences dhundta rehta hai, aur jo data kam ho woh ek replica se doosre mein copy kar deta hai. Leader-based replication ke replication log ke ulat, yeh process writes ko kisi particular order mein copy nahi karta. Data copy hone mein kaafi der bhi lag sakti hai.

Har system dono implement nahi karta. Jaise Voldemort mein abhi koi anti-entropy process nahi hai. Iske bina, jin values ko kam read kiya jaata hai woh kuch replicas par missing reh sakti hain, aur isse durability kam hoti hai. Read repair tabhi hota hai jab application koi value read kare, isliye jise koi read nahi karta woh value bahut der tak missing reh sakti hai.

Reading aur writing ke liye quorums

Upar ke example mein write successful maani gayi, jabki teen mein se sirf do replicas ne use process kiya tha. Agar teen mein se sirf ek ne accept kiya hota toh? Isse kitna door tak khinch sakte hain?

Maan lo har successful write kam se kam teen mein se do replicas par guaranteed hai. Toh zyada se zyada ek replica stale ho sakta hai. Agar tum kam se kam do replicas se read karte ho, toh unmein se kam se kam ek up to date hoga hi. Teesra replica down ya slow ho, tab bhi reads up-to-date value return kar sakte hain.

Ab general baat karte hain. Maan lo n replicas hain. Har write ko successful maanne ke liye w nodes se confirm hona zaroori hai. Har read ko kam se kam r nodes ko query karna hoga. Example mein n = 3, w = 2 aur r = 2 hai. Jab tak w + r > n hai, hum up-to-date value milne ki ummeed kar sakte hain. Wajah yeh hai ki jin r nodes se hum read karte hain, unmein se kam se kam ek woh bhi hoga jo un w nodes mein se hai jinhone latest write li thi. Jo reads aur writes in rules ko follow karte hain, unhe quorum reads and writes kehte hain. Tum w aur r ko aise soch sakte ho ki read ya write valid hone ke liye kam se kam itne votes chahiye.

n = 3 replicas, w = 2 write confirmations, r = 2 read replies
w + r = 2 + 2 = 4, which is greater than n = 3
so every read set overlaps every write set in at least one node

Dynamo-style databases mein n, w aur r aam taur par configurable hote hain. Common choice yeh hai ki n ko odd number rakhein, aksar 3 ya 5, aur w = r = (n + 1) / 2 set karein, round up karke. Lekin tum numbers apne hisaab se badal sakte ho. Jaise jis workload mein writes kam aur reads bahut zyada hain, use w = n aur r = 1 se fayda ho sakta hai. Reads tez ho jaate hain, lekin ek nuksaan hai: ek bhi node fail ho jaye toh saari writes fail ho jaati hain.

Cluster mein n se zyada nodes ho sakte hain. Lekin koi bhi value sirf unmein se n nodes par store hoti hai. Isse dataset ko partition kiya ja sakta hai, aur aise datasets support ho jaate hain jo ek node mein na aa sakein. Partitioning par Chapter 6 mein wapas aayenge.

Quorum condition, w + r > n, system ko unavailable nodes tolerate karne deti hai, in tarikon se:

  • Agar w, n se kam hai, toh ek node unavailable hone par bhi writes process ho sakti hain.
  • Agar r, n se kam hai, toh ek node unavailable hone par bhi reads process ho sakte hain.
  • n = 3, w = 2 aur r = 2 ke saath ek unavailable node tolerate ho jaata hai.
  • n = 5, w = 3 aur r = 3 ke saath do unavailable nodes tolerate ho jaate hain.

Normally reads aur writes saare n replicas ko parallel mein bheje jaate hain. w aur r yeh decide karte hain ki operation ko successful maanne se pehle n mein se kitne nodes ka reply aana zaroori hai. Agar required w ya r se kam nodes available hain, toh write ya read error return karta hai. Node kai wajahon se unavailable ho sakta hai. Woh down ho sakta hai, operation chalate waqt fail ho sakta hai (jaise uski disk full hone ki wajah se), ya network interruption use client se kaat sakta hai. System ko inme farq karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Use bas itna dekhna hai ki node ne successful response diya ya nahi.

Example

Paanch replicas lo, n = 5, w = 3 aur r = 3 ke saath. Book is case ko yeh dikhane ke liye use karti hai ki do unavailable nodes kaise tolerate hote hain:

  1. Write tab successful hai jab paanch mein se koi bhi 3 replicas use confirm kar dein.
  2. Read paanch mein se 3 replicas se unki values poochta hai.
  3. 3 + 3, 5 se bada hai, isliye jo bhi 3 replicas tum read karte ho, woh un 3 replicas se kam se kam ek node share karenge jinhone write li thi. Wahi shared node latest value rakhta hai.
  4. Agar do replicas down hain, toh bache hue teen phir bhi write confirm kar sakte hain aur read ka jawab de sakte hain, isliye system chalta rehta hai.
Try karo

Book kam writes aur bahut zyada reads wale workloads ke liye w = n aur r = 1 suggest karti hai. Maan lo tum ise 5-node cluster ke liye chunte ho. Kaun se operations tez ho jaate hain, aur ek node down hone par writes ka kya hota hai? Apna jawab n = 5, w = 3, r = 3 wale case se compare karein.

Quorum consistency ki limitations

Agar tumhare paas n replicas hain, aur tum w aur r aise chunte ho ki w + r > n ho, toh tum aam taur par ummeed kar sakte ho ki har read kisi key ki sabse recent likhi hui value return karega. Jin nodes par likha gaya aur jin nodes se padha gaya, un dono sets ka overlap hona zaroori hai. Jin nodes se tum read karte ho, unmein se kam se kam ek ke paas latest value hoti hai (book ka Figure 5-11 yeh dikhata hai).

Aksar r aur w ko majority chuna jaata hai, yani n/2 se zyada nodes. Isse w + r > n bhi ho jaata hai aur n/2 tak node failures bhi tolerate ho jaate hain. Lekin quorums ka majority hona zaroori nahi hai. Bas itna zaroori hai ki reads aur writes ke nodes ke sets kam se kam ek node par overlap karein. Doosre quorum assignments bhi possible hain, jisse distributed algorithms mein designers ko thodi flexibility milti hai.

Tum w aur r ko chhote numbers par bhi set kar sakte ho, taaki w + r ≤ n ho. Reads aur writes tab bhi n nodes ko bheje jaate hain, lekin kam successful responses chahiye hote hain. Isse stale values ka chance badh jaata hai, kyunki read ke latest value wale node ko miss karne ka chance zyada hota hai. Faayda yeh hai ki latency kam hoti hai aur availability zyada. Agar network interruption bahut saare replicas ko kaat de, toh reads aur writes phir bhi process hone ka chance behtar rehta hai. Database writes ya reads tabhi lena band karta hai jab reachable replicas ki ginti w ya r se neeche chali jaye.

w + r > n hone par bhi kuch edge cases mein stale values return ho sakti hain. Exact list implementation par depend karti hai, lekin book yeh naam leti hai:

  • Sloppy quorums. Agar sloppy quorum use ho (aage explain kiya hai), toh w writes un nodes se alag nodes par ja sakti hain jahan se r reads hote hain. Tab overlap guaranteed nahi rehta.
  • Concurrent writes. Agar do writes ek saath hoti hain, toh clear nahi hota ki pehle kaunsi hui. Ekdum safe jawab yahi hai ki concurrent writes ko merge karein. Agar timestamp se winner chunte hain (last write wins), toh clock skew ki wajah se writes lost ho sakti hain, matlab jab clocks ek doosre se match nahi karte.
  • Read ke dauran write. Agar write aur read ek saath hote hain, toh ho sakta hai write sirf kuch replicas par dikhe. Tab undetermined hai ki read purani value dega ya nayi.
  • Failed write jo partly apply ho gayi. Ek write kuch replicas par succeed ho sakti hai aur kuch par fail, jaise kuch nodes ki disks full hone ki wajah se. Agar woh overall w replicas se kam par succeed hui, toh jahan succeed hui wahan se rollback nahi hoti. Baad ke reads us write ki value return kar bhi sakte hain aur nahi bhi, chahe client ko bataya gaya ho ki woh fail ho gayi.
  • Purane replica se restore karna. Agar nayi value wala node fail ho jaye, aur uska data kisi purani value wale replica se restore kiya jaye, toh nayi value store karne wale replicas ki ginti w se neeche ja sakti hai. Tab quorum condition toot jaati hai.
  • Bad timing. Sab kuch sahi chalne par bhi timing aise unlucky ho sakti hai ki guarantee toot jaye. Linearizability aur quorums par Chapter 9 mein baat hogi.

Toh quorums dekhne mein guarantee dete lagte hain ki read latest likhi hui value return karega, lekin practice mein baat itni simple nahi hai. Dynamo-style databases aam taur par aise use cases ke liye optimize hote hain jo eventual consistency tolerate kar sakte hain. w aur r se tum stale values read karne ki probability adjust kar sakte ho, lekin unhe absolute guarantee nahi maanna chahiye.

Rule of thumb

w + r > n se latest value read hone ka achha chance milta hai, promise nahi. Quorum ko stale reads ka chance kam karne ka tarika samjhein, unhe khatam karne ka nahi.

Khaas taur par, tumhe aam taur par woh guarantees nahi milti jo chapter mein pehle discuss hui thi, yani read-your-writes, monotonic reads ya consistent prefix reads. Isliye us section mein bataye gaye anomalies in applications mein ho sakte hain. Stronger guarantees ke liye aam taur par transactions ya consensus chahiye. In topics par Chapters 7 aur 9 mein wapas aayenge.

Staleness ko monitor karna

Operations ke nazariye se yeh matter karta hai ki tumhare databases up-to-date results return kar rahe hain ya nahi. Tumhari application stale reads tolerate kar sakti ho, tab bhi tumhe pata hona chahiye ki tumhara replication kitna healthy hai. Agar replication bahut peeche reh jaye, toh system ko alert karna chahiye, taaki tum wajah dhundh sako, jaise network problem ya overloaded node.

Leader-based replication mein database aam taur par replication lag ke metrics expose karta hai, jinhe tum monitoring system mein feed kar sakte ho. Yeh isliye possible hai kyunki writes leader aur followers par same order mein apply hoti hain, aur har node ki replication log mein ek position hoti hai, yani usne locally kitni writes apply ki hain. Leader ki position mein se follower ki position ghata do, toh replication lag mil jaata hai.

Leaderless replication mein monitoring mushkil hai, kyunki writes apply hone ka koi fixed order nahi hota. Agar database sirf read repair use karta hai aur anti-entropy process nahi hai, toh value kitni purani ho sakti hai, uski koi limit nahi hai. Jis value ko kam read kiya jaata hai woh bahut der tak stale replica par reh sakti hai, aur return hone wali value bahut purani ho sakti hai.

Kuch research mein leaderless databases mein replica staleness measure karne par kaam hua hai, aur n, w, r parameters se stale reads ka expected percentage predict karne par bhi. Yeh abhi common practice nahi hai. Kleppmann ka kehna hai ki staleness measurements ko database metrics ke standard set mein shamil karna achha hoga. Eventual consistency intentionally ek vague guarantee hai. Operations ke liye zaroori hai ki practice mein “eventual” ka matlab measure kiya ja sake.

Sloppy quorums aur hinted handoff

Achhe se configure kiye hue quorums wala database individual nodes ke failure ko bina failover ke tolerate kar leta hai. Woh slow nodes bhi tolerate kar leta hai, kyunki request ko saare n nodes ka intezaar nahi karna padta. Jaise hi w ya r nodes respond kar dein, woh return kar sakta hai. In khoobiyon ki wajah se leaderless databases un use cases ke liye attractive hain jinhe high availability aur low latency chahiye, aur jo kabhi-kabhi stale reads accept kar sakte hain.

Lekin ab tak jaise quorums bataye gaye, woh utne fault-tolerant nahi hain jitne ho sakte hain. Network interruption aasaani se client ko bahut saare database nodes se kaat sakta hai. Woh nodes alive ho sakte hain, aur doosre clients unhe reach kar sakte hain. Lekin is client ke liye, jo unse kata hua hai, woh dead jaise hi hain. Aisi situation mein w ya r se kam reachable nodes bach sakte hain, aur client quorum tak nahi pahunch paata.

Bade cluster mein, jahan n se kaafi zyada nodes hain, client interruption ke dauran shayad kuch database nodes tak phir bhi pahunch sakta hai. Bas woh particular nodes nahi jo kisi value ka quorum banane ke liye chahiye. Yahan designers ke saamne ek trade-off aata hai:

  • Kya un saari requests ko error return karein jo w ya r nodes ke quorum tak nahi pahunch paatin?
  • Ya phir writes ko phir bhi accept kar lein, aur unhe aise reachable nodes par store karein jo un n nodes mein se nahi hain jahan woh value normally rehti hai?

Doosre option ko sloppy quorum kehte hain. Writes aur reads ko tab bhi w aur r successful responses chahiye. Lekin yeh responses value ke designated n “home” nodes ke bahar ke nodes se bhi aa sakte hain. Book iski tulna aise se karti hai jaise tum apne ghar se bahar lock ho gaye hon. Tum padosi ka darwaza khatkhatate ho aur poochte ho ki kya thodi der unke sofa par baith sakte hain.

Network interruption theek hone ke baad, ek node ne jo writes doosre node ki taraf se temporarily accept ki thin, woh sahi “home” nodes ko bhej di jaati hain. Ise hinted handoff kehte hain. Analogy par wapas aayein: jaise hi tumhe ghar ki chaabiyan mil jaati hain, padosi politely tumse kehta hai ki sofa se uthkar ghar jaiye.

Sloppy quorums write availability ke liye khaas taur par useful hain. Jab tak koi bhi w nodes available hain, database writes accept kar sakta hai. Lekin iska matlab yeh bhi hai ki w + r > n hone par bhi tum pakka nahi keh sakte ki kisi key ki latest value hi read hogi. Ho sakta hai latest value temporarily n home nodes ke bahar ke nodes par likhi gayi ho. Isliye sloppy quorum traditional sense mein quorum nahi hai. Woh sirf durability ka assurance deta hai: data kahin na kahin w nodes par store hai. Hinted handoff complete hone tak koi guarantee nahi ki r nodes ka read use dekh lega.

Saari common Dynamo implementations mein sloppy quorums optional hain. Riak mein yeh by default enabled hain. Cassandra aur Voldemort mein by default disabled hain.

Multi-datacenter operation

Pehle chapter mein cross-datacenter replication ko multi-leader replication ke use case ke roop mein discuss kiya gaya tha. Leaderless replication bhi multi-datacenter operation ke liye fit baithta hai, kyunki yeh conflicting concurrent writes, network interruptions aur latency spikes tolerate karne ke liye hi design hua hai.

Cassandra aur Voldemort multi-datacenter support ko normal leaderless model ke andar hi build karte hain. Replicas ki ginti n mein saare datacenters ke nodes shamil hote hain, aur configuration batati hai ki n replicas mein se kitne har datacenter mein hone chahiye. Client ki har write saare replicas ko bheji jaati hai, chahe woh kahin bhi hon. Lekin client aam taur par sirf apne local datacenter ke nodes ke quorum ka intezaar karta hai. Isse datacenters ke beech ke link par delays aur interruptions ka uspar asar nahi padta. Doosre datacenters ko writes aksar asynchronously hone ke liye configure ki jaati hain, halanki configuration thodi flexibility deti hai.

Riak alag raasta leta hai. Woh clients aur database nodes ke beech ka saara communication ek datacenter ke andar hi rakhta hai, isliye n ek single datacenter ke andar replicas ki ginti batata hai. Alag-alag datacenters ke database clusters ke beech replication background mein asynchronously hota hai. Yeh multi-leader replication jaisa hai.

Concurrent writes detect karna

Dynamo-style databases mein kai clients ek hi key par ek saath write kar sakte hain. Isliye conflicts honge, strict quorums use karne par bhi. Situation multi-leader replication jaisi hai, halanki Dynamo-style databases mein conflicts read repair ya hinted handoff ke dauran bhi aa sakte hain.

Asli problem yeh hai ki events alag-alag nodes par alag order mein pahunch sakte hain. Network delays alag-alag hote hain, aur failures partial hote hain. Book ek example deti hai.

Example

Book ka Figure 5-12 do clients, A aur B, ko dikhata hai jo teen-node datastore mein ek hi key X par write kar rahe hain:

  1. Node 1 ko A ki write mil jaati hai, lekin transient outage ki wajah se B ki write kabhi nahi milti.
  2. Node 2 ko pehle A ki write milti hai, phir B ki.
  3. Node 3 ko pehle B ki write milti hai, phir A ki.

Agar har node write aane par key ki value ko bas overwrite kar deta, toh nodes hamesha ke liye inconsistent rehte. Book ke final read mein node 2 maanta hai ki X, B hai, jabki baaki nodes maante hain ki woh A hai.

Eventually consistent hone ke liye replicas ko ek hi value par converge karna padega. Woh yeh kaise karte hain? Replicated databases principle mein ise automatically handle kar sakte hain, lekin zyadatar implementations isme kaafi kamzor hain. Agar tum data lose nahi karna chahte, toh tumhe apne database ke conflict handling ke internals ke baare mein kaafi kuch jaanna padega. Ab chapter is issue ko thoda detail mein dekhta hai.

Last write wins (concurrent writes ko discard karna)

Eventual convergence ka ek tarika yeh kehna hai ki har replica ko sirf sabse recent value store karni hai. Purani values overwrite hokar discard ho sakti hain. Agar tumhare paas unambiguously decide karne ka tarika hai ki kaunsi write zyada recent hai, aur har write aakhir mein har replica tak copy ho jaati hai, toh replicas converge kar jayenge.

Lekin yahan “recent” ek confusing word hai. Upar ke example mein dono clients ko write bhejte waqt doosre ke baare mein pata nahi tha. Isliye clear nahi hai ki kaunsi write pehle hui. Sach kaho toh yeh kehna ki koi ek pehle hui, sahi lagta hi nahi. Dono writes concurrent hain, yani unka order undefined hai.

Phir bhi tum ek arbitrary order force kar sakte ho. Har write ke saath ek timestamp lagao, sabse bade timestamp ko most recent maano, aur chhote timestamp wali kisi bhi write ko discard kar do. Is algorithm ko last write wins kehte hain, ya LWW. Cassandra mein yahi ek hi conflict resolution method supported hai, aur Riak mein yeh optional feature hai.

LWW convergence deta hai, lekin durability ki keemat par. Agar kai concurrent writes ek hi key par aayein, toh ho sakta hai un sabko client ko successful bataya gaya ho, kyunki har ek w replicas par likhi gayi thi. Phir bhi unmein se sirf ek bachti hai. Baaki silently discard ho jaati hain. LWW kuch aisi writes bhi drop kar sakta hai jo concurrent thi hi nahi, jaisa book events ko order karne ke liye timestamps wale section mein discuss karti hai.

Kuch situations mein writes ka lost hona acceptable ho sakta hai, jaise caching mein. Agar data lose karna acceptable nahi hai, toh LWW ek kharab choice hai. LWW wale database ko safely use karne ka ek hi tarika hai: yeh pakka karein ki har key sirf ek baar likhi jaye aur phir use immutable (kabhi change na hone wala) maana jaye. Isse same key par koi concurrent updates hote hi nahi. Jaise book Cassandra mein key ke roop mein UUID use karne ki salaah deti hai, taaki har write operation ko ek unique key mile.

Happens-before relationship aur concurrency

Hum kaise decide karein ki do operations concurrent hain ya nahi? Book examples se intuition banati hai. Figure 5-9 mein dono writes concurrent nahi hain. A ka insert B ke increment se pehle hota hai, kyunki B jis value ko increment karta hai woh A ne insert ki thi. B ka operation A ke operation par build karta hai, isliye B baad mein hua hoga. Hum kehte hain ki B, A par causally dependent hai. Iske ulat, Figure 5-12 ki do writes concurrent hain. Jab har client ne apna operation shuru kiya, use pata nahi tha ki koi doosra client usi key par operation kar raha hai. Koi bhi doosre par depend nahi karta.

Book terms ko is tarah define karti hai. Operation A, doosre operation B se happens before hai agar B ko A ke baare mein pata hai, B A par depend karta hai, ya kisi tarah A par build karta hai. Ek operation doosre se pehle hua ya nahi, yahi concurrency define karne ki chaabi hai. Do operations concurrent hain agar koi bhi doosre se pehle nahi hua. Simple words mein, kisi ko doosre ke baare mein pata nahi. Toh kisi bhi do operations A aur B ke liye teen possibilities hain. Ya A, B se pehle hua, ya B, A se pehle hua, ya woh concurrent hain. Agar ek operation doosre se pehle hua, toh baad wale ko pehle wale ko overwrite karna chahiye. Agar woh concurrent hain, toh resolve karne ke liye ek conflict hai.

Concurrency, time aur relativity. Tum soch sakte ho ki do operations tabhi concurrent hain jab woh “ek hi time par” hon. Lekin yeh matter nahi karta ki woh literally time mein overlap karte hain ya nahi. Distributed systems mein clocks unreliable hote hain, isliye yeh batana mushkil hai ki do cheezein sach mein ek hi moment par hui ya nahi. Isko Chapter 8 cover karta hai. Concurrency define karne ke liye exact timing matter nahi karti. Do operations concurrent hain agar dono ek doosre se unaware hain, unka physical time kuch bhi ho. Is idea ka special theory of relativity se halka sa connection hai, jo kehti hai ki information light se tez travel nahi kar sakti. Do events jo itne door hain ki ek doosre ko affect nahi kar sakte, woh beech ke time mein ek doosre ko influence nahi kar sakte. Computer systems mein bhi situation aisi hi hai. Agar network slow ya interrupted tha, toh do operations kuch time ke gap se hone ke baad bhi concurrent ho sakte hain, kyunki network problem ne ek ko doosre ke baare mein jaanne se rok diya.

Happens-before relationship ko capture karna

Ab ek algorithm dekhte hain jo decide karta hai ki do operations concurrent hain ya ek doosre se pehle hua. Cheezein simple rakhne ke liye, ek aise database se shuru karte hain jisme sirf ek replica hai. Phir ise kai replicas wale leaderless database tak generalize karenge.

Book ka Figure 5-13 do clients ko dikhata hai jo ek hi shopping cart mein concurrently items add kar rahe hain. (Agar yeh bahut trivial lage, toh socho do air traffic controllers apne track kiye jaane wale sector mein aircraft add kar rahe hain.) Cart shuru mein khaali hai. Dono clients milkar paanch writes karte hain:

Example
  1. Client 1 cart mein milk add karta hai. Us key par yeh pehli write hai, isliye server use store karta hai aur version 1 assign karta hai. Server value aur version number client ko wapas echo kar deta hai.
  2. Client 2 eggs add karta hai. Use pata nahi ki client 1 ne abhi milk add kiya hai, isliye woh sochta hai ki uske eggs hi akela item hain. Server is write ko version 2 assign karta hai. Server yeh nahi jaan sakta ki eggs milk ko replace karte hain, isliye woh eggs aur milk ko do alag values ki tarah store karta hai. Woh dono values version 2 ke saath client 2 ko return kar deta hai.
  3. Client 1 ne client 2 ki write nahi dekhi. Woh flour add karna chahta hai, toh sochta hai ki cart mein milk hai aur version 1 ke saath [milk, flour] bhejta hai. Server samajh jaata hai ki yeh write pehle wali [milk] value ko supersede karti hai, lekin [eggs] ke saath concurrent hai. Isliye server [milk, flour] ko version 3 assign karta hai, version 1 ki value overwrite karta hai, version 2 ki value [eggs] rakhta hai, aur bachi hui dono values return karta hai.
  4. Client 2 ham add karna chahta hai, aur use flour ke baare mein pata nahi hai. Usne apne last response mein [milk] aur [eggs] receive kiye the, toh woh unhe ham ke saath merge karke [eggs, milk, ham] banata hai. Woh ise version 2 ke saath bhejta hai. Server dekhta hai ki version 2, [eggs] ko overwrite karta hai, lekin [milk, flour] ke saath concurrent hai. Isliye bachi hui do values yeh hain: version 3 par [milk, flour] aur version 4 par [eggs, milk, ham].
  5. Client 1 bacon add karna chahta hai. Usne last mein version 3 par [milk, flour] aur [eggs] receive kiye the, toh woh unhe merge karke bacon add karta hai, aur [milk, flour, eggs, bacon] banta hai. Woh ise version 3 ke saath bhejta hai. Isse [milk, flour] overwrite ho jaata hai, aur [eggs] pehle hi overwrite ho chuka tha. Lekin nayi value [eggs, milk, ham] ke saath concurrent hai, isliye server dono rakhta hai.

Book in operations ke beech ke dataflow ko ek graph ki tarah draw karti hai, jahan arrows dikhate hain ki kaunsa operation kaunse operation se pehle hua. Baad wala operation pehle wale ke baare mein jaanta tha ya usper depend karta tha. Clients server ke saath kabhi poori tarah up to date nahi hote, kyunki hamesha koi na koi operation concurrently chal raha hota hai. Lekin value ke purane versions aakhir mein overwrite ho jaate hain, aur koi write lost nahi hoti.

Server version numbers dekhkar decide kar sakta hai ki do operations concurrent hain ya nahi. Use value ko interpret karne ki zaroorat nahi, isliye value koi bhi data structure ho sakti hai. Algorithm aise kaam karta hai:

  • Server har key ke liye ek version number rakhta hai. Key jab bhi likhi jaati hai woh version number increment karta hai, aur naya version number value ke saath store karta hai.
  • Jab client koi key read karta hai, server saari woh values return karta hai jo overwrite nahi hui hain, saath mein latest version number. Client ko key likhne se pehle use read karna zaroori hai.
  • Jab client koi key likhta hai, use apne pichle read ka version number include karna hota hai. Use us read mein mili saari values ko bhi merge karna hota hai. Write ka response read jaisa dikh sakta hai, jisme saari current values return hoti hain, jisse kai writes ko ek ke baad ek chain kiya ja sakta hai, jaise shopping cart example mein.
  • Jab server ko kisi particular version number ke saath write milti hai, woh us version number aur usse neeche ki saari values overwrite kar sakta hai, kyunki woh nayi value mein merge ho chuki hain. Lekin use higher version number wali saari values rakhni hoti hain, kyunki woh incoming write ke saath concurrent hain.

Jo write pichle read ka version number include karti hai, woh server ko batati hai ki yeh write kis pehle wali state par based hai. Agar tum version number ke bina likhte ho, toh woh write baaki saari writes ke saath concurrent maani jaati hai. Isliye woh kuch overwrite nahi karti. Woh bas aage ke reads mein values mein se ek ki tarah return hoti hai.

Concurrently likhi values ko merge karna

Yeh algorithm pakka karta hai ki koi data silently drop na ho. Lekin isme clients ko extra kaam karna padta hai. Jab kai operations concurrently hote hain, toh clients ko baad mein concurrent values ko merge karke cleanup karna padta hai. Riak in concurrent values ko siblings kehta hai.

Siblings ko merge karna essentially wahi problem hai jo multi-leader replication mein conflict resolution ki hai. Ek simple approach yeh hai ki version number ya timestamp ke basis par ek value chun li jaye, jo ki last write wins hai. Lekin isme data lose hota hai. Isliye application code mein kuch zyada intelligent chahiye ho sakta hai.

Shopping cart ke liye siblings merge karne ka ek reasonable tarika unke items ka union lena hai. Example mein aakhri do siblings [milk, flour, eggs, bacon] aur [eggs, milk, ham] hain. Dhyaan do ki milk aur eggs dono mein hain, jabki har ek sirf ek baar likha gaya tha. Merged cart [milk, flour, eggs, bacon, ham] ho sakta hai, duplicates ke bina.

Lekin agar log apne carts se items remove bhi kar sakte hain, toh simple union galat jawab de sakta hai. Maan lo ek item sirf do sibling carts mein se ek mein se remove hua. Union us removed item ko wapas le aayega, kyunki doosre sibling mein woh abhi bhi hai. Isse bachne ke liye, system item remove hone par use database se seedha delete nahi kar sakta. Uski jagah use ek suitable version number ke saath ek marker chhodna hoga, jo dikhaye ki item remove hua tha. Aise deletion marker ko tombstone kehte hain. Book yaad dilati hai ki tombstones pehle bhi aaye the, hash indexes mein log compaction ke context mein.

Application code mein siblings merge karna complex hai aur galtiyon ka khatra rehta hai. Isliye kuch efforts aise data structures design karne ki koshish karte hain jo automatically merge ho jayein, jaisa automatic conflict resolution wale section mein discuss hua. Jaise Riak ka datatype support CRDTs use karta hai jo siblings ko sensibly merge kar sakte hain, deletions ko preserve karna bhi shamil hai.

Version vectors

Upar ke example mein sirf ek replica tha. Jab kai replicas hon aur leader na ho, toh algorithm kaise badalta hai?

Jab kai replicas ek saath writes accept karte hain, toh har key ke liye ek single version number kaafi nahi hota. Uski jagah, per-key number ke saath-saath har key ko har replica ke liye ek version number chahiye. Har replica write process karte waqt apna version number increment karta hai. Woh baaki har replica se jo version numbers dekhe hain, unka bhi track rakhta hai. Yeh saari information milkar system ko batati hai ki kaunsi values overwrite karni hain aur kaunsi siblings ke roop mein rakhni hain. Saare replicas ke version numbers ke collection ko version vector kehte hain.

Is idea ke kuch variants use mein hain. Sabse interesting shayad dotted version vector hai, jo Riak 2.0 mein use hota hai. Book details mein nahi jaati, lekin yeh kaafi had tak shopping cart example jaise hi kaam karta hai.

Single-replica example ke version numbers ki tarah, version vectors bhi values read hone par database replicas se clients ko bheje jaate hain. Value baad mein likhte waqt unhe database ko wapas bhejna padta hai. Riak version vector ko ek string mein encode karta hai jise woh causal context kehta hai. Version vector database ko overwrites aur concurrent writes mein farq karne deta hai.

Pehle ki tarah, application ko ab bhi siblings merge karne pad sakte hain. Version vector structure ek replica se read karke doosre par wapas write karna safe bana deta hai. Aisa karne se siblings ban sakte hain, lekin koi data lose nahi hota, bas siblings sahi tarah merge ho jayein.

Version vectors aur vector clocks. Version vector ko kabhi-kabhi vector clock bhi kehte hain, halanki dono bilkul same nahi hain. Farq subtle hai, aur book details ke liye references batati hai. Short mein, replicas ki state compare karte waqt version vectors hi sahi data structure hain.

Trade-offs
ApproachGood atCosts
Single-leaderSamajhna aasaan, conflict resolution ki zaroorat nahi. Saari writes ek node se ordered hoti hain.Saari writes ek node se guzarti hain. Followers stale reads de sakte hain. Failover risky hai, aur asynchronous copies recent writes lose kar sakti hain.
Multi-leaderWrites kai jagah accept hoti hain, datacenters ke beech aur offline devices par bhi. Faulty nodes aur network problems ke khilaf robust.Write conflicts detect aur resolve karne padte hain. Configuration subtle hai, aur kai systems conflicts ko kharab tarah detect karte hain.
LeaderlessFailover ki zaroorat nahi. Nodes down ya slow hone par bhi chalta rehta hai, aur latency spikes tolerate kar sakta hai.Reads stale ho sakte hain. Conflicts hote hain, aur application ko siblings merge karne pad sakte hain. Transactions ya consensus add na karein toh guarantees kamzor hain.

Summary

Short mein

Is chapter mein replication dekha, yani ek hi data ki copies kai machines par rakhna. Kleppmann replicate karne ki teen wajah batate hain: data ko users ke paas rakhna, kuch parts fail hone par bhi system chalta rakhna, aur system jitne reads serve kar sake unhe scale out karna.

  • Teen approaches. Single-leader replication mein clients saari writes ek leader ko bhejte hain, jo changes followers ko stream karta hai. Reads kisi bhi replica par ja sakte hain, lekin followers se reads stale ho sakte hain. Multi-leader replication mein clients har write kai leaders mein se ek ko bhejte hain, jo changes ek doosre ko aur followers ko exchange karte hain. Leaderless replication mein clients har write kai nodes ko bhejte hain aur kai nodes se parallel mein read karte hain, taaki stale copies detect aur fix ho sakein.
  • Synchronous ya asynchronous. Asynchronous replication tab tez hai jab system smoothly chal raha ho. Lekin jab replication lag badh jaye aur servers fail hon, toh asynchronously update hue follower ko leader promote karne se recently committed data lose ho sakta hai. Failover split brain aur doosre risks bhi laata hai, isliye ise dhyaan se karna padta hai.
  • Lag aur guarantees. Replication lag se ajeeb effects ho sakte hain. Teen guarantees applications ko sensibly behave karne mein madad karti hain: read-after-write consistency, taaki users ko apna submit kiya hua data dikhe; monotonic reads, taaki users ko time kabhi peeche jaata na dikhe; aur consistent prefix reads, taaki users ko causally ordered data dikhe, jaise ek sawaal aur uska jawab sahi order mein.
  • Concurrency. Multi-leader aur leaderless replication concurrent writes allow karte hain, isliye conflicts ho sakte hain. Happens-before relationship batati hai ki do operations concurrent the ya nahi. Version numbers aur version vectors database ko concurrency detect karne dete hain. Concurrent values ko merge karna, deletions ke liye tombstones ke saath, data ko silently lose hone se bachata hai.

Replication ka goal simple hai, ek hi data ki copy kai machines par rakhna. Phir bhi yeh ek tricky problem nikalti hai. Isme concurrency ke baare mein aur un saari cheezon ke baare mein dhyaan se sochna padta hai jo galat ho sakti hain. Kam se kam tumhe unavailable nodes aur network interruptions se nipatna hoga. Subtler faults, jaise software bugs se hone wala silent data corruption, aur bhi mushkil hain. Agla chapter un data par aage badhta hai jo kai machines mein distributed hota hai, replication ke counterpart ke zariye: ek bade dataset ko partitions mein todna. Is chapter ke liye book ki reference list mein 61 entries hain. Yeh retelling unhe reproduce nahi karti.

Check yourself

  1. Ek asynchronous leader fail ho jaata hai, aur ek asynchronous follower ko naya leader promote kiya jaata hai. Un writes ka kya ho sakta hai jinke baare mein clients ko bataya gaya tha ki woh succeed hui?

    Jawab dekho

    Jo writes us follower tak copy nahi hui thi, woh lost ho sakti hain. Asynchronous replication durability guarantee nahi karta, isliye naya leader unhe kabhi dekh hi nahi paata, aur sabse common fix yeh hai ki purane leader ke rejoin karne par uski unreplicated writes discard kar di jaayein.

  2. Ek user profile change save karta hai, phir page reload karta hai aur purana data dekhta hai, kyunki read ek aise follower ne serve kiya jo abhi peeche tha. Kaunsi guarantee missing hai, aur application use kaise de sakti hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Missing guarantee read-after-write consistency hai, jise read-your-writes bhi kehte hain. Ek fix yeh hai ki user ki apni profile leader se read karein aur doosron ki followers se. Doosra fix yeh hai ki last write ka timestamp yaad rakhein aur pakka karein ki reads ke liye use hone wala replica kam se kam utna current ho.

  3. Ek database mein n = 5 replicas hain, w = 3 aur r = 3 ke saath. Kitne nodes unavailable ho sakte hain jab tak reads aur writes succeed hote rahein, aur read ko latest write kyun dikhti hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Do nodes unavailable ho sakte hain. Kyunki w + r = 6, n = 5 se bada hai, read ke liye use hone wala 3 nodes ka koi bhi set, latest write accept karne wale 3 nodes ke kisi bhi set se kam se kam ek node share karega. Wahi shared node latest value rakhta hai.

  4. Multi-leader system mein do leaders concurrently ek wiki page ka title B aur C set karte hain. Last write wins yahan data kyun lose karta hai, aur zyada information rakhne wale do alternatives kya hain?

    Jawab dekho

    Last write wins sirf sabse bade timestamp wali write rakhta hai aur doosri ko silently discard kar deta hai. Dono writes successful report hui thi, isliye ek user ka change gayab ho jaata hai. Do alternatives yeh hain: values ko merge karna, jaise “B/C” mein, ya dono ko conflicting values ki tarah rakhna aur application code ya kisi user ko baad mein resolve karne dena.

Part II · Chapter 6

Partitioning

Seedhi baat: jab dataset ya uski traffic ek machine ke liye bahut badi ho jaati hai, toh use partitions mein split karke nodes par phaila dete hain. Mushkil cheezein yeh hain: data kaise split karein, load ko even kaise rakhein, aur har request ko sahi node tak kaise bhejein.

Chapter 5 mein replication dekha tha, yani same data ki kai copies alag-alag nodes par rakhna. Node matlab cluster ki ek machine. Jab dataset bahut bada ho ya queries bahut zyada rate par aa rahi hon, tab akela replication kaafi nahi hota. Aise cases mein data ko partitions mein todna padta hai, jinhe shards bhi kehte hain. Har partition poore dataset ka ek slice hota hai.

Chapter ki shuruaat computing pioneer Grace Murray Hopper ki 1962 ki ek line se hoti hai: “We must state relationships, not procedures.” Isse epigraph kehte hain, yani chapter se pehle likhi hui ek chhoti quote.

Dhyaan do

Alag-alag products same idea ke liye alag naam use karte hain. Book mein list hai: MongoDB, Elasticsearch aur SolrCloud mein shard, HBase mein region, Bigtable mein tablet, Cassandra aur Riak mein vnode (virtual node), aur Couchbase mein vBucket. Book partitioning word hi use karti hai, kyunki yeh sabse established term hai. Ek aur baat: yahan partitioning ka network partition se koi lens-den nahi hai. Network partition ek fault hota hai jisme nodes ek-doosre tak pahunch nahi paate. Un faults ki baat Chapter 8 mein hai.

Partitioning aur Replication

Data ko split kyun karein? Main wajah scalability hai. Alag-alag partitions alag-alag nodes par reh sakte hain, ek shared-nothing cluster mein. Shared-nothing matlab har machine ki apni memory aur disks hoti hain, jo woh doosri machines ke saath share nahi karti. Is tarah bada dataset kaafi saari disks par phail jaata hai, aur query load kaafi saare processors par. Jo query sirf ek partition ko touch karti hai, woh akele us partition ke node par chal sakti hai. Isliye nodes add karne se query throughput badhta hai. Jo bade aur complex queries kaafi partitions ko touch karti hain, unhe parallel mein bhi chala sakte hain, lekin use sahi karna bahut mushkil hai.

Partitioned databases koi nayi cheez nahi hain. Teradata aur Tandem NonStop SQL jaise products ne 1980s mein yeh idea shuru kiya tha. Baad mein NoSQL databases aur Hadoop-based data warehouses isse wapas laaye. Kuch systems transactional workloads ke liye bane hain (bahut saare chhote reads aur writes), aur kuch analytics ke liye (bade scans aur reports). Workload se system ki tuning badal jaati hai, lekin partitioning ki basics dono par lagti hain.

Chapter pehle yeh dekhta hai ki bade datasets ko partition kaise karte hain, aur indexes partitioning ke saath kaise interact karte hain. Phir rebalancing aati hai, yani nodes add ya remove hone par data ko move karna. Aakhir mein overview hai ki database har request ko sahi partition tak kaise route karta hai aur queries kaise chalata hai.

Partitioning ko aam taur par replication ke saath combine kiya jaata hai, taaki har partition ki copies kai nodes par rahein. Yeh fault tolerance ke liye hota hai, taaki ek machine mar jaaye toh data na khoye. Har record phir bhi exactly ek partition ka hota hai, lekin woh partition kai nodes par store ho sakta hai.

Ek node par ek se zyada partitions bhi ho sakte hain. Leader–follower replication mein, har partition ki ek copy leader hoti hai, jo writes leti hai, aur baaki copies followers hoti hain, jo leader ke changes copy karti hain. Har partition ka leader ek node par hota hai, aur uske followers doosre nodes par. Matlab ek node kuch partitions ka leader aur kuch ka follower ho sakta hai. Book ka Figure 6-1 yahi layout dikhata hai.

Chapter 5 mein replication ke baare mein jo kuch bhi tha, woh partitions par bhi same tarah lagta hai. Partitioning scheme ka choice zyadatar replication scheme ke choice se independent hota hai. Isliye ab aage chapter replication ko side mein rakh deta hai.

Key-Value data ki partitioning

Maan lo tumhare paas bahut saara data hai aur tum use partition karna chahte ho. Kaun sa record kis node par jaayega, yeh kaise decide karenge?

Goal yeh hai ki data aur query load dono evenly phail jaayein. Agar har node ko fair share mile, toh theory mein 10 nodes ek node se 10 guna data aur 10 guna read-write throughput handle kar sakte hain. Yahan abhi replication ko ignore kar rahe hain.

Agar split unfair ho, yani kuch partitions mein zyada data ho ya unpe zyada queries aayein, toh partitioning skewed kehlati hai. Skew se partitioning kaafi kam effective ho jaati hai. Extreme case mein poora load ek hi partition par aa jaata hai. Tab das mein se nau nodes idle baithe rehte hain, aur ek busy node bottleneck ban jaata hai. Jis partition par load disproportionately zyada ho, use hot spot kehte hain.

Hot spots se bachne ka sabse simple tarika yeh hota ki har record ko random node par assign kar do. Isse data kaafi evenly phail jaata hai. Lekin ek bada disadvantage hai. Jab tumhe koi particular item read karna ho, toh tumhe pata hi nahi ki woh kis node par hai, isliye saare nodes ko parallel mein query karna padta hai.

Hum isse behtar kar sakte hain. Abhi ke liye ek simple key-value model maan lo, jisme har record apni primary key se milta hai. Primary key woh field hai jo record ko uniquely identify karti hai. Purana paper encyclopedia aise hi kaam karta hai. Tum entry ko uske title se dhoondhte ho, aur entries alphabetical order mein hoti ho, isliye sahi entry jaldi mil jaati hai.

Key range se partitioning

Ek tarika yeh hai ki har partition ko keys ki ek continuous range de do, kisi minimum se kisi maximum tak. Yeh paper encyclopedia ke volumes jaisa hai, jo book ke Figure 6-2 mein dikhaya gaya hai. Agar tumhe ranges ke boundaries pata hain, toh tum bata sakte ho ki koi key kis partition mein hai. Aur agar yeh bhi pata ho ki kaun sa partition kis node par hai, toh request seedhe usi node ko bhej sakte hain. Encyclopedia mein tum shelf se sahi volume utha lete ho.

Key ranges ka evenly spaced hona zaroori nahi hai, kyunki data khud bhi evenly phaila hua nahi hota. Encyclopedia mein volume 1 mein A aur B se shuru hone wale words hain, lekin volume 12 mein T, U, V, X, Y aur Z se shuru hone wale words hain. Har volume ko do letters dene se kuch volumes baaki se bahut bade ho jaate. Data ko evenly phailane ke liye boundaries ko data ke hisaab se adapt hona padta hai. Boundaries administrator haath se choose kar sakta hai, ya database automatically bhi kar sakta hai. Book rebalancing wale section mein is par wapas aati hai. Bigtable aur uska open-source equivalent HBase key range partitioning use karte hain, aur RethinkDB aur MongoDB (version 2.4 se pehle) bhi.

Har partition ke andar keys ko sorted order mein rakha ja sakta hai. Isse range scans aasaan ho jaate hain, yani do values ke beech ki saari keys read karna. Tum key ko concatenated index ki tarah bhi treat kar sakte ho, jo kai fields ko ek key mein jod deta hai, pehle pehli field se sorted aur phir agli se. Isse tum ek hi query mein kaafi related records fetch kar sakte ho.

Maan lo ek application sensors ke network ki readings store karti hai, aur key har measurement ka timestamp hai, year-month-day-hour-minute-second format mein. Yahan range scans bahut kaam ke hain. Inse tum, jaise, ek mahine ki saari readings ek saath fetch kar sakte ho.

Example

Sensors aur timestamp key. Yahan kya galat hota hai, step by step:

  1. Partitions time ranges hain, har din ke liye ek partition.
  2. Sensors apni readings database mein likhte hain jaise-jaise measurements hoti hain.
  3. Har nayi reading ka timestamp aaj ka hota hai, isliye woh aaj ki range mein jaati hai.
  4. Toh aaj ki saari writes ek hi partition par jaati hain, aur purane partitions idle pade rehte hain.

Aaj wala partition writes se overload ho sakta hai, jabki cluster ka baaki hissa kuch nahi kar raha hota. Book ka solution yeh hai ki key mein timestamp ke alawa kuch aur pehle rakho. Jaise har timestamp ke aage sensor ka naam laga do. Tab partitioning pehle sensor name se hoti hai, phir time se. Agar kaafi sensors ek saath active hain, toh write load partitions mein phail jaata hai. Iski cost yeh hai ki agar kai sensors ki values ek time range mein padhni hon, toh har sensor name ke liye alag range query chalani padegi.

Hot:    2026-10-19 08:00:01
Better: sensor-17 | 2026-10-19 08:00:01
        sensor-42 | 2026-10-19 08:00:01
Asli idea

Sorted keys se range scans aasaan ho jaate hain. Lekin jo key time ke saath badhti hai, jaise timestamp, woh saari nayi writes ek hi partition par bhej sakti hai. Key choose karne se pehle access pattern check kar lein.

Key ke hash se partitioning

Skew aur hot spots ke risk ki wajah se kaafi distributed datastores hash function use karte hain, yeh decide karne ke liye ki key kis partition ki hai. Hash function ek formula hai jo kisi bhi input ko ek number bana deta hai. Achha hash function skewed input ko bhi apni output range mein evenly phaila deta hai.

Maan lo ek 32-bit hash function hai jo strings par kaam karta hai. Har nayi string ke liye woh 0 aur 232 − 1 ke beech ek random jaisa dikhne wala number deta hai. Do input strings bahut similar hon, tab bhi unke hashes poori range mein idhar-udhar bikhre hote hain. Partitioning ke liye hash function ka security ke level ka strong hona zaroori nahi hai. Cassandra aur MongoDB MD5 use karte hain, aur Voldemort Fowler–Noll–Vo function. Kaafi programming languages mein apni hash tables ke liye built-in hash functions hote hain, lekin book ki warning hai ki yeh aksar yahan suitable nahi hote. Java ke Object.hashCode() aur Ruby ke Object#hash mein same key alag-alag processes mein alag hash values de sakti hai.

Suitable hash function mil jaaye, toh tum har partition ko keys ki range ki jagah hash values ki range de dete ho. Jis bhi key ka hash kisi partition ki range ke andar aata hai, woh usi partition mein store hoti hai. Yeh book ke Figure 6-3 mein dikhaya gaya hai. Partition boundaries evenly spaced ho sakti hain, ya pseudorandomly pick ki ja sakti hain. Doosra option consistent hashing ka approach hai, jise book neeche ek chhote section mein cover karti hai.

Yeh technique keys ko partitions mein fairly phailane mein achhi hai. Lekin iski ek cost hai. Partitioning ke liye key ka hash use karne se key range partitioning ki ek kaam ki property chali jaati hai, yani efficient range queries. Jo keys pehle paas-paas thi, woh ab saare partitions mein bikhar jaati hain, isliye unka sort order khatam ho jaata hai. MongoDB mein agar hash-based sharding on karein, toh har range query saare partitions ko bhejni padti hai. Riak, Couchbase aur Voldemort primary key par range queries support hi nahi karte.

Hash partitioning range queries chhod deta hai, lekin Cassandra dono strategies ke beech ka ek compromise deta hai. Cassandra ki table mein kai columns se bani compound primary key ho sakti hai. Sirf pehla column hash hota hai, jisse partition choose hota hai. Baaki columns ek concatenated index ki tarah kaam karte hain, jo partition ke andar data ko disk par sort karta hai.

Toh query pehle column ki values ki range par search nahi kar sakti. Lekin agar query pehle column ki ek single value fix kar de, toh woh baaki columns par efficient range scan chala sakti hai.

Example

Social media user ke updates. Maan lo update ki primary key (user_id, update_timestamp) hai. Is design se yeh milta hai:

  1. Pehla hissa, user_id, hash hokar partition pick karta hai. Alag users alag partitions par ja sakte hain.
  2. Ek user ke saare updates ek saath, ek hi partition par store hote hain.
  3. Us partition ke andar updates timestamp se sorted hote hain.
  4. Toh tum ek user ke ek time interval ke saare updates, timestamp order mein pehle se sorted, ek efficient query mein fetch kar sakte ho.

Book ke hisaab se yeh one-to-many relationships ke liye ek neat data model banta hai, jahan ek user kai updates post karta hai.

Consistent Hashing

Consistent hashing term Karger aur unke saathiyon se aayi hai. Yeh ek aisa tarika batati hai jisse internet-wide caches ke bade system mein load evenly phailaya jaata hai, jaise content delivery network (CDN, servers ka network jo content ki copies users ke paas rakhta hai). Isme partition boundaries randomly choose hoti hain, isliye central control ya distributed consensus (nodes ka kisi shared decision par agree karna) ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Yahan “consistent” word ka replica consistency se koi lens-den nahi hai, jo Chapter 5 mein hai, aur na hi ACID consistency se, jo Chapter 7 mein hai. Yeh rebalancing ke ek particular approach ko describe karta hai. Book ke hisaab se yeh approach databases ke liye zyada achha kaam nahi karta, isliye practice mein kam use hota hai. Kuch database documentation mein abhi bhi consistent hashing ka zikr milta hai, lekin book ke hisaab se woh documentation aksar inaccurate hoti hai. Book ki salah hai ki is confusing term se bachein aur technique ko seedha hash partitioning kahein. Phir bhi book khud aage ek approach ke liye yeh term use karti hai, jise woh original definition ke sabse kareeb batati hai, isliye tumhe yeh uske text mein dikh jaayegi.

Skewed workloads aur hot spots ko kam karna

Key ko hash karke partition choose karne se hot spots kam hote hain. Lekin woh poori tarah khatam nahi hote. Extreme case mein, jahan saare reads aur writes ek hi key ke liye hain, har request phir bhi ek hi partition par jaati hai. Do identical keys ka hash same hota hai.

Aisa workload unusual hai, lekin hota zaroor hai. Social media site par kisi celebrity ke millions followers hon, toh woh kuch post kare tab activity ka toofan aa sakta hai. Isse ek hi key par bahut saari writes aa sakti hain. Key celebrity ki user ID ho sakti hai, ya us post ki ID jis par sab comment kar rahe hain. Key ko hash karne se koi fayda nahi hota, kyunki identical IDs ka hash same jagah hi jaata hai.

Aaj ke zyadatar data systems itne skewed workload ko khud compensate nahi kar paate. Isliye skew kam karna application ka kaam hai. Agar ek key bahut hot hai, toh ek simple technique hai ki key ke shuru ya end mein ek random number jod do. Do-digit decimal random number, 00 se 99 tak, writes ko 100 alag keys mein split kar deta hai. Phir un keys ko alag-alag partitions par rakha ja sakta hai.

Example

Ek hot key ko 100 mein todna. Technique step by step yeh hai:

  1. Woh key pehchaano jis par writes ki baadh aa rahi hai.
  2. Har write par ek random do-digit number append kar do, toh wahi key 100 keys mein se ek ban jaati hai.
  3. Ab writes 100 keys mein phail jaati hain, jo cluster mein 100 alag jagah par ho sakti hain.
  4. Ab read ko saari 100 keys fetch karni padti hain aur results combine karne padte hain.
  5. Yeh record rakho ki kaun si keys split hain, taaki reads ko pata ho ki kahan dekhna hai.

Is split ki ek price hai. Reads ko ab extra kaam karna padta hai, kyunki unhe saari 100 keys se data padhkar combine karna padta hai. Yeh technique sirf thodi si hot keys ke liye hi worth it hai. Zyadatar keys ka write throughput kam hota hai, unke liye random number bekaar ki mehnat hogi. Isliye tumhe yeh track karne ka koi tarika bhi chahiye ki kaun si keys split hain.

Shayad aage chalkar data systems skewed workloads ko automatically detect karke compensate karne lagein. Abhi ke liye, book ke hisaab se, tumhe apni application ke liye in trade-offs ko khud sochna padega.

Try karo

Book sensor timestamp hot spot ka fix yeh batati hai ki sensor name ko key mein pehle rakho. Is change ke baad ek hi ghante ke dauraan saare sensors ki query karne mein kitni cost aayegi? Use change se pehle ki cost se compare karo.

Partitioning aur Secondary Indexes

Ab tak jo bhi dekha, woh key-value model par based hai. Agar records sirf primary key se hi access hote hain, toh us key se partition nikaala ja sakta hai. Phir reads aur writes ko us partition tak route kar sakte hain jo uske liye responsible hai.

Cheezein tab complicated ho jaati hain jab secondary indexes aate hain. Secondary index kisi aur field par index hota hai, primary key par nahi. Woh aam taur par ek record ko uniquely identify nahi karta. Bas yeh deta hai ki tum un records ko search kar sako jinki koi particular value ho. Jaise: user 123 ke saare actions dhoondho, “hogwash” word wale saare articles dhoondho, ya woh saari cars dhoondho jinka color red hai.

Secondary indexes relational databases ki bread and butter hain, aur document databases mein bhi common hain. Kuch key-value stores, jaise HBase aur Voldemort, ne inhe avoid kiya hai kyunki yeh implementation complexity badhate hain. Doosron ne, jaise Riak, inhe add karna shuru kiya hai kyunki data model karne ke liye yeh bahut useful hain. Solr aur Elasticsearch jaise search servers ke exist karne ki wajah bhi secondary indexes hi hain.

Problem yeh hai ki secondary indexes partitions par neatly map nahi hote. Jis database mein yeh hon, use partition karne ke do main tarike book batati hai: document-based partitioning aur term-based partitioning.

Dhyaan do

Agar tumhara database sirf key-value model support karta hai, toh tum application code mein khud secondary index banane ke liye lalchaoge, values se primary keys ka ek mapping. Yeh possible hai, lekin index ko data ke saath consistent rakhne mein bahut dhyaan dena padta hai. Race conditions, yani jab do operations unlucky order mein interleave ho jaate hain, aur intermittent write failures, jahan kuch changes save hote hain aur kuch nahi, dono aasaani se index aur data ko out of step kar sakte hain. Iski gehri wajah ke liye book Chapter 7 mein multi-object transactions ki discussion ki taraf point karti hai.

Document ke hisaab se Secondary Indexes ki partitioning

Socho tum used cars bechne ki website chalate ho. Har listing ki ek unique ID hoti hai, jise document ID kehte hain. Tum database ko document ID se partition karte ho. Jaise ID 0 se 499 partition 0 mein, ID 500 se 999 partition 1 mein, aur aise hi aage. Yeh book ke Figure 6-4 mein dikhaya gaya hai.

Tum chahte ho ki users cars ko color aur make se search kar sakein, isliye color aur make dono par secondary index chahiye. Document database mein yeh fields hote, aur relational database mein columns. Agar tum index declare kar do, toh database use automatically maintain kar sakta hai. Jaise, jab bhi koi red car add hoti hai, toh jis partition mein woh hai, woh us car ki ID ko index entry color:red ki list mein jod deta hai.

Is design mein har partition bilkul alag hota hai. Har partition apne secondary indexes khud rakhta hai, aur woh sirf us partition ke documents ko cover karte hain. Use is baat se koi matlab nahi ki doosre partitions mein kya store hai. Jab bhi tum database mein likhte ho, yani document add, remove ya update karte ho, tumhe sirf us partition se kaam padta hai jisme us document ki ID hai. Isliye document-partitioned index ko local index bhi kehte hain, global index ke opposite mein, jo agle section mein aayega.

Lekin document-partitioned index se read karne mein dhyaan rakhna padta hai. Agar tumne document IDs ke saath kuch special nahi kiya, toh koi wajah nahi hai ki saari red cars ek hi partition mein hon. Book ke example mein red cars partition 0 aur partition 1 dono mein hain. Isliye red cars search karne ke liye query har partition ko bhejni padti hai aur saare results combine karne padte hain. Is pattern ko scatter/gather kehte hain. Isse secondary indexes par reads kaafi expensive ho sakte hain. Partitions ko parallel mein query karne par bhi scatter/gather par tail latency amplification ka khatra rehta hai, jo Chapter 1 mein tha, jahan sabse slow partition response time decide karta hai.

Phir bhi yeh approach kaafi widely use hota hai. MongoDB, Riak, Cassandra, Elasticsearch, SolrCloud aur VoltDB sab document-partitioned secondary indexes use karte hain. Zyadatar database vendors yeh recommend karte hain ki partitioning ko aise structure karein ki secondary index query ek hi partition se serve ho jaaye. Lekin yeh hamesha possible nahi hota, khaaskar jab query ek saath kai secondary indexes use kare, jaise cars ko color aur make dono se filter karna.

Example

Used-car site par red cars search karna. Yahan kya hota hai, step by step:

  1. Client “color is red” ko har partition ko bhejta hai, kyunki red cars kisi bhi partition mein ho sakti hain.
  2. Har partition apne local index mein color:red dhoondhta hai aur jo IDs mili, woh return karta hai.
  3. Saare partitions ke results combine hokar ek list ban jaate hain.

Writing sasti hai. Jab ek nayi red car add hoti hai, toh sirf wahi partition change hota hai jisme uski ID hai.

Term ke hisaab se Secondary Indexes ki partitioning

Har partition ko apna index dene ki jagah, tum ek global index bana sakte ho jo saare partitions ke data ko cover kare. Lekin us index ko ek node par store nahi kar sakte, kyunki woh bottleneck ban jaata aur partitioning ka maksad hi khatam kar deta. Isliye global index ko bhi partition karna padta hai. Use primary key index se alag tarah se partition kiya ja sakta hai.

Book ka Figure 6-5 yahi idea dikhata hai. Saare partitions ki red cars index mein color:red ke neeche aati hain. Index ko aise partition kiya gaya hai ki a se r tak ke letters se shuru hone wale colors partition 0 mein hain, aur s se z tak wale partition 1 mein. Make ka index bhi isi tarah partition hota hai, f aur h ke beech boundary ke saath.

Ise term-partitioned index kehte hain, kyunki jis term ko tum dhoondh rahe ho, wahi decide karta hai ki index entry kis partition mein hogi. Yahan term color:red hoga. “Term” word full-text indexes se aaya hai, jo ek special kism ka secondary index hota hai, aur wahan terms woh saare words hote hain jo document mein aate hain.

Pehle ki tarah, tum index ko term se khud partition kar sakte ho, ya term ke hash se. Term se partition karna range scans ke liye useful hai, jaise kisi numeric property par, maan lo car ki asking price. Term ke hash par partition karne se load zyada evenly phailta hai.

Document-partitioned index ke muqable global, term-partitioned index ka fayda yeh hai ki reads zyada efficient ho sakte hain. Saare partitions par scatter/gather karne ki jagah, client ko sirf us partition se baat karni hoti hai jisme uska chahiya hua term hai.

Nuksaan yeh hai ki writes slow aur zyada complicated ho jaate hain. Ek document ki write index ke kai partitions ko affect kar sakti hai, kyunki us document ka har term shayad alag partition par ho, alag node par.

Ideal duniya mein index hamesha up to date hota, yani likha gaya har document turant index mein dikhta. Term-partitioned index mein iske liye un saare partitions ke across ek distributed transaction chahiye, jo write se affect hote hain. Distributed transaction ek atomic change hota hai jo kai machines par phailta hai. Har database ise support nahi karta. Book transactions ko Chapter 7 aur 9 mein cover karti hai.

Practice mein global secondary indexes ke updates aksar asynchronous hote hain. Matlab index write return hone ke baad update hota hai, write ka hissa nahi hota. Isliye agar tum write ke thodi der baad index padho, toh jo change abhi kiya woh shayad abhi dikhe nahi. Jaise Amazon DynamoDB kehta hai ki uske global secondary indexes normally second ke ek hisse mein update ho jaate hain, lekin infrastructure mein faults hon toh zyada delay aa sakta hai. Riak ka search feature bhi global term-partitioned indexes use karta hai, aur Oracle data warehouse bhi, jahan tum local aur global indexing mein se choose kar sakte ho. Chapter 12 wapas aata hai yeh dikhane ke liye ki term-partitioned indexes implement kaise hote hain.

Trade-offs
OptionKahan achha haiCost
Document-partitioned (local) indexWrites ek hi partition ko touch karti hain. Sahi rakhna aasaan hai.Reads saare partitions par scatter hote hain aur results gather karne padte hain. Yeh slow hai aur tail latency amplification ka shikaar hota hai.
Term-partitioned (global) indexReads ek partition par jaate hain, isliye fast aur sasti hain.Writes kai index partitions ko touch karti hain, slow aur mushkil hoti hain. Index updates aksar asynchronous hote hain, isliye read thodi der ke liye stale ho sakta hai.

Partitions ko rebalance karna

Time ke saath database mein cheezein badalti rehti hain. Query throughput badhta hai, toh load handle karne ke liye aur CPUs chahiye. Dataset badhta hai, toh use store karne ke liye aur disks aur RAM chahiye. Koi machine fail ho jaati hai, toh baaki machines ko uska kaam sambhalna padta hai. In sab changes mein data aur requests ko ek node se doosre node par move karna padta hai. Cluster mein load ko ek node se doosre node par shift karne ko rebalancing kehte hain.

Partitioning scheme chahe jo bhi ho, rebalancing se aam taur par kuch minimum requirements poori hone ki umeed hoti hai:

  • Rebalancing ke baad load (stored data, reads aur writes) nodes ke beech fairly share hona chahiye.
  • Rebalancing chal rahi ho, tab bhi database ko reads aur writes accept karte rehna chahiye.
  • Nodes ke beech zaroorat se zyada data move nahi hona chahiye, taaki rebalancing fast ho aur network ya disks overload na hon.

Rebalancing ki strategies

Partitions ko nodes par assign karne ke kai tarike hain. Hum ek-ek karke dekhte hain.

Yeh tarika nahi apnana chahiye: hash mod N. Pehle bataya tha ki sabse achha hai possible hashes ki range ko chhoti ranges mein baantna aur har range ek partition ko dena. Jaise, key partition 0 mein jaati hai agar uska hash boundary b0 se kam hai, partition 1 mein jaati hai agar hash b0 aur b1 ke beech hai, aur aise hi aage. Tum soch sakte ho ki hum seedha mod (remainder operator) kyun nahi use karte. Jaise, hash(key) mod 10 se 0 se 9 ke beech ka number milta hai. 10 nodes hain jinke number 0 se 9 hain, toh har key ko node assign karne ka yeh aasaan tarika lagta hai.

Problem yeh hai ki agar nodes ki count N badalti hai, toh zyaadatar keys ko ek node se doosre node par move karna padta hai. Maan lo ek key ka hash 123456 hai. 10 nodes ke saath woh node 6 par hogi, kyunki 123456 mod 10 is 6. Cluster 11 nodes ka hone par use node 3 par jaana padega, kyunki 123456 mod 11 is 3. 12 nodes hone par use node 0 par jaana padega. Itni baar move hone se rebalancing bahut zyada expensive ho jaati hai. Humein aisa approach chahiye jo data ko zaroorat se zyada move na kare.

Example

Ek key, teen cluster sizes. Key ka hash poore time 123456 hi rehta hai:

  1. 10 nodes ke saath key node 6 par jaati hai (123456 mod 10 is 6).
  2. 11 nodes tak badhao, toh key ko node 3 par jaana padega (123456 mod 11 is 3).
  3. 12 nodes tak badhao, toh use phir move hona padega, node 0 par (123456 mod 12 is 0).

Har change par key move hui, aur baaki zyaadatar keys bhi hoti hain.

Fixed number of partitions. Iska fix kaafi simple hai. Nodes se kaafi zyada partitions bana lo, aur har node ko kai partitions assign kar do. Jaise, 10 nodes ke cluster par ek database ko shuru se hi 1,000 partitions mein baanta ja sakta hai, toh har node ko lagbhag 100 partitions mil jaate hain.

Ab jab cluster mein naya node add hota hai, toh woh har existing node se kuch partitions le leta hai, jab tak partitions dobara fairly distributed na ho jaayein. Node remove hone par yahi cheez ulti taraf hoti hai. Book ke Figure 6-6 mein is tarah naya node add hote dikhaya gaya hai.

Nodes ke beech sirf poore partitions move hote hain. Partitions ki count nahi badalti, aur keys ka partitions mein assignment bhi nahi badalta. Sirf partitions ka nodes par assignment badalta hai. Yeh change turant nahi hota, kyunki network par bahut saara data transfer karne mein time lagta hai. Isliye transfer chal raha ho, tab tak reads aur writes ke liye purana assignment hi use hota hai.

Principle mein, tum mismatched hardware ko bhi handle kar sakte ho. Zyada powerful nodes ko zyada partitions dekar tum un nodes se load ka bada hissa uthawa sakte ho. Yeh approach Riak, Elasticsearch, Couchbase aur Voldemort use karte hain.

Is setup mein partitions ki count aam taur par database pehli baar set up karte waqt fix kar di jaati hai, aur baad mein badli nahi jaati. Kleppmann maante hain ki partitions ko split aur merge kiya ja sakta hai, lekin fixed number operationally zyada simple hai, isliye kai fixed-partition databases splitting ko poori tarah skip kar dete hain. Matlab shuru mein jo partitions ki count chunte hain, wahi tumhare maximum nodes ki limit ban jaati hai. Isliye use itna high rakhna padta hai ki future growth ke liye jagah ho. Lekin har partition ka apna management overhead hota hai, toh bahut high number chunna bhi galat hai.

Sahi number chunna mushkil hai jab total dataset size ka andaaza lagana mushkil ho. Dataset chhota shuru hokar bahut bada ho sakta hai. Har partition total data ka ek fixed fraction rakhta hai, isliye cluster ka data badhne par har partition bhi badhta hai. Agar partitions bahut bade ho jaayein, toh rebalancing aur node failures se recovery expensive ho jaati hai. Agar woh bahut chhote hon, toh overhead jud-jud kar bahut ho jaata hai. Best performance tab milti hai jab partitions “just right” hon, na bahut bade na bahut chhote. Jab partitions ki count fixed ho lekin dataset size badalta rahe, tab yeh paana mushkil hai.

Dynamic partitioning. Key range partitioning ke liye fixed boundaries ke saath fixed number of partitions bahut inconvenient hoga.
