Boundaries galat ho gayi, toh saara data ek partition mein aa sakta hai aur baaki khaali rahenge. Boundaries ko haath se dobara configure karna bahut thakaane wala kaam hoga. Isliye HBase aur RethinkDB jaise key range databases partitions dynamically banate hain.

Jab koi partition configured size se bada ho jaata hai, toh use do partitions mein split kar diya jaata hai, taaki lagbhag aadha data har side chala jaaye. HBase par default size 10 GB hai. Ulta, agar bahut saara data delete ho jaaye aur partition kisi threshold se chhota ho jaaye, toh use adjacent partition ke saath merge kiya ja sakta hai. Yeh process kuch-kuch B-tree (Chapter 3 mein cover hua common on-disk index structure) ke top level par hone wali cheez jaisa hai.

Fixed partitions ki tarah, har partition ek node ko assign hota hai, aur har node kai partitions handle kar sakta hai. Bade partition ko split karne ke baad, uske do halves mein se ek ko load balance karne ke liye doosre node par move kiya ja sakta hai. HBase par partition files HDFS (underlying distributed filesystem) ke through transfer hoti hain.

Example

Ek partition jo badhta hi jaata hai. Dynamic partitioning mein ek partition ki life aisi hoti hai:

  1. Partition chhota shuru hota hai aur ek node par rehta hai.
  2. Writes aate rehte hain, aur partition configured size se bada ho jaata hai, jo HBase par default 10 GB hai.
  3. Partition ko do mein split kar diya jaata hai, har ek mein lagbhag aadha data.
  4. Do halves mein se ek ko doosre node par transfer kar diya jaata hai, taaki load share ho.
  5. Agar baad mein deletes se koi partition threshold se chhota ho jaaye, toh use neighbor ke saath merge kar diya jaata hai.

Dynamic partitioning ka ek fayda yeh hai ki partitions ki count total data volume ke hisaab se adjust ho jaati hai. Data kam hai, toh kam partitions kaafi hain, isliye overhead kam rehta hai. Data bahut zyada hai, toh har partition ka size configured maximum tak limited rehta hai.

Lekin ek caveat hai. Empty database ek hi partition ke saath shuru hota hai, kyunki boundaries kahan khinchni hain, iski abhi koi information nahi hoti. Jab tak dataset chhota hai, yani pehle partition ke split hone tak, saari writes ek hi node se hoti hain aur baaki nodes idle baithe rehte hain. Isse bachne ke liye HBase aur MongoDB tumhe empty database par initial partitions ka set configure karne dete hain. Ise pre-splitting kehte hain. Key range partitioning mein pre-splitting ke liye tumhe pehle se pata hona chahiye ki key distribution kaisi hogi.

Dynamic partitioning sirf key range partitioning tak limited nahi hai. Yeh hash-partitioned data ke saath bhi utna hi achha kaam karta hai. MongoDB version 2.4 se key range aur hash dono partitioning support karta hai, aur dono case mein partitions dynamically split karta hai.

Nodes ke proportional partitioning. Dynamic partitioning mein partitions ki count dataset size ke proportional hoti hai, kyunki splitting aur merging har partition ka size ek fixed minimum aur maximum ke beech rakhte hain. Fixed number of partitions mein har partition ka size dataset ke proportional hota hai. Dono case mein partitions ki count nodes ki count par depend nahi karti.

Teesra option, jo Cassandra aur Ketama use karte hain, yeh hai ki partitions ki count nodes ki count ke proportional rakhi jaaye. Yani har node ke paas fixed number of partitions hote hain. Ab nodes ki count wahi rahe aur dataset badhe, toh har partition ka size badhta hai. Lekin nodes add karne par partitions dobara chhote ho jaate hain. Zyada data volume ko aam taur par store karne ke liye zyada nodes chahiye, isliye is approach mein har partition ka size kaafi stable rehta hai.

Jab naya node cluster join karta hai, toh woh randomly ek fixed number of existing partitions chunta hai jinhe split karna hai. Har ek ke liye woh ek half ka ownership le leta hai aur doosra half wahin chhod deta hai. Random choice se unfair splits ho sakte hain. Lekin kai partitions par average nikaalein, toh naye node ko load ka fair share mil jaata hai. Cassandra mein default 256 partitions per node hai. Cassandra 3.0 ne ek alternative rebalancing algorithm introduce kiya jo unfair splits se bachata hai.

Partition boundaries randomly chunne ke liye hash-based partitioning chahiye, kyunki boundaries us numbers ki range se chuni jaati hain jo hash function produce karta hai. Yeh approach consistent hashing ki original definition ke sabse kareeb hai. Naye hash functions kam metadata overhead ke saath milta-julta effect de sakte hain.

Trade-offs
StrategyFaydaCosts
Hash mod NLikhna bahut simple hai.Nodes ki count badalne par zyaadatar keys move hoti hain.
Fixed number of partitionsSirf poore partitions move hote hain. Operationally simple.Partition count setup ke time fix ho jaata hai. Dataset ke saath partition sizes upar-neeche hote hain, aur bahut zyada partitions overhead badhate hain.
Dynamic partitioningPartitions ki count data ke hisaab se adjust hoti hai. Key range partitioning ke saath fit baithta hai.Empty database ek partition se shuru hota hai, isliye shuru ki writes ek hi node par jaati hain. Pre-splitting ke liye keys ke baare mein pehle se pata hona chahiye.
Nodes ke proportional partitionsCluster badhne par bhi partition size kaafi stable rehta hai.Kisi ek join ke liye random splits unfair ho sakte hain, aur is approach ke liye hash partitioning chahiye.

Operations: automatic ya manual rebalancing

Rebalancing ke baare mein ek zaroori sawaal yeh hai ki woh automatically hoti hai ya manually. In dono extremes ke beech ka poora gradient hai. Ek taraf rebalancing fully automatic hoti hai: system khud decide karta hai ki partitions ko kab ek node se doosre par move karna hai, aur koi administrator involved nahi hota. Doosri taraf woh fully manual hoti hai: administrator explicitly configure karta hai ki kaun sa node kaun sa partition rakhega, aur assignment tabhi badalta hai jab administrator badalta hai. Couchbase, Riak aur Voldemort beech mein aate hain. Woh suggested partition assignment automatically generate karte hain, lekin use effect mein aane se pehle administrator ko approve karna padta hai.

Fully automatic rebalancing convenient hai, kyunki routine kaam kam ho jaata hai. Lekin woh unpredictable ho sakti hai. Rebalancing ek expensive operation hai. Isme requests reroute karni padti hain aur nodes ke beech bahut saara data move karna padta hai. Agar yeh dhyaan se na kiya jaaye, toh network ya nodes overload ho sakte hain, aur chalte waqt doosri requests slow ho sakti hain.

Example

Automatic rebalancing kharab situation ko aur kharab kar deti hai. Book batati hai ki automation, automatic failure detection ke saath milkar kaise bura asar kar sakta hai:

  1. Ek node overloaded ho jaata hai aur requests ka jawab dene mein slow ho jaata hai.
  2. Baaki nodes maan lete hain ki slow node dead hai.
  3. Woh automatically cluster ko rebalance karte hain taaki load us node se door chala jaaye.
  4. Isse already overloaded node, baaki nodes aur network par extra load aa jaata hai.
  5. Situation aur kharab ho jaati hai, aur yeh cascading failure ban sakti hai, jahan ek failure agle failure ko trigger karta hai.
Asli idea

Rebalancing expensive hoti hai aur surprise de sakti hai. Isliye human in the loop rakhna achha idea ho sakta hai. Process fully automatic wale se slow hota hai, lekin operational surprises se bachne mein madad karta hai.

Request routing

Ab dataset kai machines ke kai nodes par partitioned hai. Ek sawaal bacha hai. Jab client ko request karni hoti hai, toh use kaise pata chalega ki kis node se connect karna hai? Partitions rebalance hone par partitions ka nodes par assignment badalta rehta hai. Kisi ko in changes ka track rakhna padta hai, taaki is sawaal ka jawab hamesha sahi rahe. Agar main key “foo” read ya write karna chahun, toh mujhe kaun sa IP address aur port number connect karna chahiye?

Yeh ek zyada general problem ka example hai jise service discovery kehte hain, aur yeh sirf databases tak limited nahi hai. Jo bhi software network par reachable hai, usse yeh problem hoti hai, khaaskar agar woh high availability ke liye kai machines par redundant setup mein chal raha ho. Kai companies ne apne service discovery tools khud likhe hain, aur inmein se kaafi open source release hue hain.

High level par teen approaches hain, jo book ke Figure 6-7 mein dikhaye gaye hain:

  1. Any node. Clients kisi bhi node se contact kar sakte hain, jaise round-robin load balancer ke through, jo har request ko agle server ko deta jaata hai. Agar us node ke paas sahi partition hai, toh woh request seedha handle kar leta hai. Nahi hai, toh woh request ko sahi node par forward karta hai, reply leta hai, aur use client ko wapas pass kar deta hai.
  2. A routing tier. Saari requests pehle ek routing tier ke paas jaati hain. Yeh tier decide karta hai ki har request kaun sa node handle karega aur use forward kar deta hai. Woh khud koi request handle nahi karta. Woh bas ek partition-aware load balancer hai.
  3. Client awareness. Client ko pata hota hai ki data kaise partitioned hai aur kaun sa node kaun sa partition rakhta hai. Woh bina kisi intermediary ke seedha sahi node se connect karta hai.

Har case mein central problem yeh hai: routing decision lene wala component, chahe woh node ho, routing tier ho ya client, use partitions ke nodes par assignment ke changes kaise pata chalenge?

Yeh mushkil hai, kyunki saare participants ko agree karna padta hai. Agar woh disagree karein, toh requests galat nodes par chali jaati hain aur sahi tarah handle nahi hoti. Distributed system mein agreement tak pahunchne ke protocols hain, lekin unhe sahi tarah implement karna mushkil hai. Chapter 9 inhe cover karta hai.

Kai distributed data systems is cluster metadata (cluster ke layout ki information) ka track rakhne ke liye ek alag coordination service use karte hain, jaise ZooKeeper. Har node apne aap ko ZooKeeper mein register karta hai. ZooKeeper partitions se nodes ka authoritative mapping rakhta hai. Doosre actors, jaise routing tier ya partition-aware client, is information ko subscribe karte hain. Jab bhi kisi partition ka owner badalta hai, ya node add ya remove hota hai, ZooKeeper routing tier ko notify karta hai taaki woh apni routing information update kar sake. Book ne ise Figure 6-8 ki tarah dikhaya hai.

LinkedIn ka Espresso cluster management ke liye Helix use karta hai, aur Helix khud ZooKeeper par depend karta hai. Espresso uske upar ek routing tier implement karta hai. HBase, SolrCloud aur Kafka bhi partition assignment track karne ke liye ZooKeeper use karte hain. MongoDB ka architecture milta-julta hai, lekin woh apna config server implementation use karta hai, jisme mongos daemons routing tier hain.

Cassandra aur Riak alag approach lete hain. Woh changes spread karne ke liye gossip protocol use karte hain, jisme nodes aapas mein cluster-state information pass karte hain. Request kisi bhi node ko bheji ja sakti hai, aur woh node use requested partition ke sahi node par forward kar deta hai. Yeh upar ki list ka pehla approach hai. Isme database nodes mein zyada complexity aati hai, lekin ZooKeeper jaise external coordination service par depend nahi karna padta.

Couchbase automatically rebalance nahi karta, isse uska design simple ho jaata hai. Aam taur par isse moxi naam ke routing tier ke saath set up kiya jaata hai, jo cluster nodes se routing changes ke baare mein seekhta hai.

Clients ko phir bhi connect karne ke liye IP addresses chahiye, chahe woh routing tier use karein ya random node ko requests bhejein. Yeh addresses partitions ke nodes par assignment se kaafi kam badalte hain. Isliye unhe look up karne ke liye aam taur par DNS (domain name system) kaafi hota hai.

Trade-offs
Routing approachFaydaCosts
Any node, with forwardingClients simple rehte hain, aur kisi bhi node se contact ho sakta hai.Node ke paas partition na ho toh extra network hop lagta hai. Har database node ke andar zyada logic.
Routing tierClients simple rehte hain, aur routing logic ek jagah rehta hai.Chalane ke liye ek aur component. Yeh ek hop add karta hai, aur ise har change ke baare mein pata hona chahiye.
Client-aware routingKoi intermediary nahi, isliye sabse kam hops.Har client ko partition changes track karne padte hain, jisse clients zyada complex ho jaate hain.

Jab partition move ho raha hota hai, tab routing ko rebalancing section ka rule follow karna padta hai. Transfer khatam hone tak requests purane owner ke paas jaati rehti hain. Uske baad hi routing information badalti hai. Figure 6-7 routing options dikhata hai; neeche ka diagram dikhata hai ki rebalance partitions ko kaise move karta hai jabki routing rule laagu rehta hai.

Parallel query execution

Ab tak chapter ne simple queries par focus kiya hai jo ek single key read ya write karti hain, aur document-partitioned secondary indexes ke liye scatter/gather queries par. Zyaadatar NoSQL distributed datastores itne hi level ka access support karte hain.

Massively parallel processing (MPP) relational databases, jo aksar analytics ke liye use hote hain, apni supported queries mein kaafi zyada sophisticated hote hain. Ek typical data warehouse query mein kai joins (kai tables ki rows ko combine karna), filters, groupings aur aggregations (jaise totals ya averages) hote hain. MPP query optimizer, yani woh hissa jo plan banata hai ki query kaise chalegi, aisi query ko stages aur partitions mein tod deta hai. Inmein se kaafi cluster ke alag-alag nodes par parallel chal sakte hain. Jo queries dataset ke bade hisse scan karti hain, unhe is parallel execution se khaas fayda hota hai.

Data warehouse queries ka fast parallel execution ek specialized topic hai, aur analytics businesses ke liye itna zaroori hai ki isme commercial interest bahut hai. Parallel query execution ki kuch techniques Chapter 10 mein discuss hui hain. Parallel databases ka zyada detailed overview chahiye, toh book apne references ki taraf point karti hai.

Summary

Short mein
  • Partition kyun karein. Partitioning tab chahiye jab itna data ho ki use ek machine par store aur process karna feasible na rahe. Goal yeh hai ki data aur query load machines mein evenly spread ho aur hot spots (aise nodes jin par load disproportionately zyada ho) se bacha jaaye. Iske liye tumhare data ke hisaab se partitioning scheme chahiye, aur jab nodes join ya leave karo tab rebalancing.
  • Key range partitioning. Keys sorted hoti hain, aur partition kisi minimum se kisi maximum tak ki saari keys ka owner hota hai. Sorting se range queries efficient hoti hain. Risk yeh hai ki agar application sorted order mein paas-paas ki keys aksar read ya write kare, toh hot spots ban jaate hain. Aise partitions aam taur par dynamically rebalance hote hain, jab partition bahut bada ho jaaye toh range ko do mein split karke.
  • Hash partitioning. Har key par hash function lagaya jaata hai, aur partition hash values ki ek range ka owner hota hai. Isse keys ki ordering khatam ho jaati hai, isliye range queries inefficient ho jaati hain, lekin load zyada evenly spread ho sakta hai. Hashing mein pehle se fixed number of partitions banana, har node ko kai assign karna, aur nodes aane-jaane par poore partitions move karna aam hai. Dynamic partitioning bhi kaam karti hai.
  • Hybrid. Ek compound key dono ko mix kar sakti hai, key ka ek hissa partition chunne ke liye aur doosra hissa sort order ke liye use karke.
  • Document-partitioned (local) secondary indexes. Har index usi partition mein store hota hai jahan woh primary key aur value hai jise woh describe karta hai. Write sirf ek partition update karti hai, lekin index ke read ke liye saare partitions par scatter/gather chahiye.
  • Term-partitioned (global) secondary indexes. Index indexed values ke hisaab se partitioned hota hai. Ek index entry primary key ke saare partitions ke records ko point kar sakti hai. Write kai index partitions update kar sakti hai, lekin read ek hi partition se serve ho sakta hai.
  • Request routing. Query ko sahi partition tak route karne ke tarike simple partition-aware load balancing se lekar sophisticated parallel query engines tak hote hain. Clients, routing tiers aur nodes sabko current pata hona chahiye ki kaun sa node kaun sa partition own karta hai, jo aksar ZooKeeper jaisi coordination service ya gossip protocol se milta hai.
  • Independence aur uski limits. Har partition zyaadatar independently kaam karta hai, aur isi wajah se partitioned database kai machines par scale kar pata hai. Lekin jin operations ko kai partitions par write karna padta hai, unke baare mein sochna mushkil hota hai. Jaise, agar ek partition par write succeed ho jaaye aur doosre par fail ho jaaye, toh kya hoga? Aage ke chapters is sawaal ko address karte hain.

Chapter ke end mein papers, books aur online articles ke 33 references ki numbered list hai, jise yeh retelling repeat nahi karti.

Khud ko check karein

  1. Ek sensor database timestamps ko keys ki tarah use karta hai aur din ke hisaab se range partitioning karta hai. Writes ek hi partition par kyun jama ho jaati hain, aur book kaun sa change suggest karti hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Har naye reading ka timestamp aaj ka hota hai, isliye saari writes aaj ke partition par jaati hain aur baaki idle rehte hain. Kleppmann timestamp se pehle sensor name rakhne ko kehte hain, jisse writes sensors mein spread ho jaati hain. Cost yeh hai ki kai sensors ko read karte waqt har sensor ke liye alag range query karni padti hai.

  2. Hashing keys ko evenly spread karta hai, phir bhi ek celebrity ki post se ek partition overload ho jaata hai. Hashing yahan madad kyun nahi karta, aur application kya kar sakti hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Ek hi key par saari writes ka hash same aata hai, isliye woh phir bhi ek partition par jaati hain. Application ek random number append kar sakti hai, jaise 100 keys ke liye do digits, taaki writes split ho jaayein. Phir reads ko saari 100 keys fetch karke combine karni padti hain, aur app ko track karna padta hai ki kaun si keys split hain.

  3. Ek site mostly “all red cars” read karti hai aur slower writes accept kar sakti hai. Uska secondary index document-partitioned hona chahiye ya term-partitioned, aur kyun?

    Jawab dekho

    Term-partitioned. Term-partitioned index mein read ek partition par jaata hai, isliye woh sasta hai. Uski writes slower hoti hain aur kai index partitions ko touch karti hain, aur updates aksar asynchronous hote hain. Document-partitioned index mein har red-car search ke liye saare partitions par scatter/gather karna padega.

  4. Hash mod N ke saath, cluster 10 se 11 nodes hone par kya galat hota hai, aur fixed number of partitions kya badalta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    N badalne par zyaadatar keys kisi doosre node par move ho jaati hain. Book ki example key node 6 se node 3 par jaati hai. Fixed number of partitions mein keys hamesha usi partition par map hoti hain. Nodes ke beech sirf poore partitions move hote hain, aur key-to-partition mapping kabhi nahi badalti.

Part II · Chapter 7

Transactions

Seedhi baat: transaction kai reads aur writes ko ek all-or-nothing unit mein group kar deta hai. Isolation level decide karta hai ki doosre clients ki activity ka kitna hissa tumhe khud handle karna padega. Stronger isolation mein performance ka cost lagta hai, aur weaker isolation mein kuch race conditions application ko khud solve karne padte hain.

Chapter ek 2012 ke Google paper se shuru hota hai, jo uske Spanner database ke baare mein hai. Kuch logon ka kehna tha ki full two-phase commit (ek protocol jo kai machines ko saath mein commit karwata hai, Chapter 9 mein aayega) support karna bahut expensive hai. Spanner ke authors ne iske ulta stand liya. Unka kehna tha ki transactions ke zyada use se jo slowdowns aate hain, programmers unhe tab handle karein jab woh aayein, “rather than always coding around the lack of transactions.”

Data systems kai tarah se galat ho sakte hain:

  • Database software ya hardware kabhi bhi fail ho sakta hai, write ke beech mein bhi.
  • Application kabhi bhi crash ho sakti hai, operations ki series ke beech mein bhi.
  • Network application ko database se, ya ek database node ko doosre se kaat sakta hai.
  • Kai clients ek saath write karke ek-doosre ke changes overwrite kar sakte hain.
  • Client aisa data read kar sakta hai jo samajh se bahar ho, kyunki woh sirf aadha update hua tha.
  • Clients ke beech race conditions, jahan result steps ki exact timing par depend karta hai, surprising bugs la sakti hain.

Reliable system ko in faults ko handle karna padta hai, taaki poora system down na ho jaaye. Lekin fault handling mein kaafi mehnat lagti hai. Tumhe sochna padta hai ki kya-kya galat ho sakta hai, aur phir test karna padta hai ki tumhara solution sach mein kaam karta hai.

Kaafi saalon se transactions hi is problem ko aasaan banane ka main tarika rahe hain. Transaction mein application kai reads aur writes ko ek logical unit mein group kar sakti hai. Conceptually, sab ek hi operation ki tarah chalte hain. Ya toh poori transaction succeed hoti hai, jise commit kehte hain, ya woh fail hoti hai, jise abort (ya rollback) kehte hain, aur uski koi write save nahi hoti. Transaction abort ho jaaye, toh application safely dobara try kar sakti hai. Error handling bhi kaafi simple ho jaati hai, kyunki application ko partial failure deal nahi karna padta. Partial failure woh situation hai jab kuch operations succeed ho jaate hain aur kuch fail.

Transactions koi kudrat ka niyam nahi hain. Logon ne inhe programming model simple banane ke liye banaya. Kuch errors aur concurrency problems database sambhal leta hai, isliye application unhe ignore kar sakti hai. Book in promises ko safety guarantees kehti hai.

Har application ko transactions ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Kabhi-kabhi better performance ya availability ke liye guarantees weak karna, ya hata dena, sahi rehta hai. Kuch safety properties transactions ke bina bhi mil jaati hain. Toh asli sawaal yeh hai ki tumhe kaunse guarantees chahiye, aur har ek ka cost kya hai. Iska jawab dene ke liye tumhe exactly pata hona chahiye ki transactions kya promise karte hain, bure halaat mein bhi.

Yeh chapter bahut saari cheezon ko dekhta hai jo galat ho sakti hain, aur un algorithms ko jo databases inse bachne ke liye use karte hain. Yeh concurrency control mein gehra jaata hai, yani database kaise handle karta hai ki kai clients ek hi data ko ek saath use kar rahe hain. Isme dirty reads, lost updates, write skew aur phantoms jaisi race conditions aati hain, aur read committed, snapshot isolation aur serializability jaise isolation levels samjhaye gaye hain. Yeh sab single-node aur distributed databases, dono par lagu hota hai. Distributed systems ki extra problems Chapter 8 mein hain.

Transaction ka slippery concept

Aaj lagbhag har relational database transactions support karta hai, aur kuch nonrelational bhi. Zyadatar 1975 mein IBM System R (pehla SQL database) ke introduce kiye style ko follow karte hain. Tab se kuch details badli hain, lekin basic idea chaalis saal se lagbhag wahi hai. MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle aur SQL Server ka transaction support System R se kaafi milta-julta hai.

2000s ke end mein nonrelational databases, jinhe aksar NoSQL kehte hain, popular ho gaye. Unhone naye data models diye (Chapter 2 dekhein), aur replication (data ki copies kai machines par rakhna) aur partitioning (data ko machines mein baantna) default mein diye. Transactions sabse bada nuksaan jhel gaye. In mein se kai naye databases ne transactions poori tarah hata diye, ya is word ka matlab bahut weaker guarantees bana diya.

In systems ke saath ek popular belief bhi bana. Transactions ko scalability ka ulta samjha gaya, aur maana gaya ki koi bhi bada system good performance aur high availability ke liye transactions chhod dega. Doosri taraf, database vendors aksar transactions ko aisi applications ke liye essential feature batate the jo valuable data rakhti hain. Kleppmann ke hisaab se dono views exaggerated hain. Har design choice ki tarah transactions ke fayde aur limits dono hain, aur chapter ka baaki hissa dono samjhata hai.

ACID ka matlab

Transactions jo safety guarantees dete hain, unhe ACID acronym se describe kiya jaata hai. Iska full form hai Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation aur Durability. Yeh term Theo Härder aur Andreas Reuter ne 1983 mein banaya tha, databases ke fault-tolerance mechanisms ke liye precise words dene ke liye.

Practice mein har database ACID apne tarike se implement karta hai, isliye do “ACID” systems alag behave kar sakte hain. Khaas kar isolation mein bahut ambiguity hai. High-level idea sahi hai, par details matter karti hain. Vendor jab kehta hai ki uska system ACID compliant hai, toh saaf nahi hota ki tum asal mein kya expect kar sakte ho. Author ka kehna hai ki ACID ab zyadatar ek marketing term ban gaya hai.

Jo systems ACID nahi hote, unhe kabhi-kabhi BASE kaha jaata hai, yani Basically Available, Soft state aur Eventual consistency. BASE toh ACID se bhi zyada vague hai. BASE ki ek hi sensible definition hai ki iska matlab “not ACID” hai, aur woh lagbhag kuch bhi ho sakta hai.

Chalo har letter ko ek-ek karke dekhte hain, kyunki isse transaction ka idea aur clear ho jaayega.

Atomicity. Roz ki computing mein “atomic” ka matlab hai woh cheez jo chhote parts mein tod nahi sakte. Multi-threaded programming mein atomic operation ka matlab hai ki koi doosra thread usse aadha-adhoora nahi dekh sakta. ACID mein atomicity ka matlab alag hai. Iska concurrency se koi lena-dena nahi hai. Yeh batati hai ki writes ke set ke beech mein fault aa jaaye toh kya hota hai. Process crash ho sakta hai, network connection toot sakta hai, disk full ho sakti hai, ya constraint violate ho sakta hai. Agar writes ek atomic transaction mein group thi, aur transaction commit nahi ho sakti, toh database use abort kar deta hai aur jo bhi writes ho chuki thi, sab undo kar deta hai.

Atomicity ke bina, kai changes ke beech error aaye toh tum andaza hi lagate reh jaate ho ki kaunse changes lage. Retry karne par wahi change do baar ho sakta hai, aur duplicate ya galat data ban sakta hai. Atomicity ke saath aborted transaction ne kuch change nahi kiya hota, isliye application safely retry kar sakti hai. Transaction abort karke uski saari writes discard kar paana hi ACID atomicity ki pehchaan hai. Kleppmann maante hain ki abortability zyada accurate naam hota, lekin atomicity hi woh word hai jo sab use karte hain. Atomic ka multi-threaded wala matlab isolation cover karta hai, jo agla letter hai.

Consistency. Consistency word ke kaafi saare matlab ho gaye hain. Book chaar matlab list karti hai. Chapter 5 mein yeh replicas ke agree karne ke liye use hota hai, aur eventual consistency ke liye, jab copies asynchronously update hoti hain. Chapter 6 mein consistent hashing hai, jo rebalancing ke liye ek partitioning method hai. CAP theorem (Chapter 9) mein consistency ka matlab linearizability hai, yani ek strict rule ki read kitna recent hona chahiye. ACID mein consistency ka matlab kuch aur hai: database application ke define kiye rules ke hisaab se ek achhi state mein hai.

In rules ko invariants kehte hain, yani data ke baare mein aise statements jo hamesha true hone chahiye. Maan lo accounting system hai, toh sabhi accounts ke credits aur debits balance hone chahiye. Transaction aisi database se shuru ho jo invariants follow karta hai, aur transaction ki har write usse valid rakhe, toh end mein bhi invariants hold karte hain. Lekin database tumhare invariants jaan nahi sakta. Kuch woh check kar sakta hai, jaise foreign key ya uniqueness constraints, par baaki application jo likhti hai woh bas store kar leta hai. Transactions sahi define karna application ki zimmedari hai.

Yahan Kleppmann ek sharp point rakhte hain. Atomicity, isolation aur durability database ki properties hain. ACID wali consistency application ki property hai, jo use paane ke liye database ki atomicity aur isolation par depend karti hai. Isliye book kehti hai ki letter C ka ACID mein asal mein koi haq nahi banta. Joe Hellerstein ne kaha hai ki C isliye jod diya gaya taaki acronym ban jaaye, aur us waqt ise important nahi maana gaya tha.

Isolation. Zyadatar databases ek saath kai clients use karte hain. Agar woh database ke alag-alag hisson ko read aur write karein, toh koi problem nahi. Problem tab aati hai jab woh same records ko touch karte hain, kyunki tab race conditions ho sakti hain. Yeh ek simple example hai.

Example

Do clients database mein stored ek counter ko increment karte hain. Database mein built-in increment nahi hai, isliye har client ko current value read karni hai, usme 1 add karna hai, aur nayi value wapas write karni hai. Counter 42 se shuru hota hai, aur do increments se use 44 ho jaana chahiye. Step by step yeh ho sakta hai:

  1. Client 1 counter read karta hai aur 42 milta hai.
  2. Client 2 counter ko tab read karta hai jab client 1 ne kuch write nahi kiya, aur use bhi 42 milta hai.
  3. Client 1 usme 1 add karke 43 write karta hai.
  4. Client 2 apni 42 ki copy mein 1 add karta hai, jisse 43 banta hai, aur 43 write kar deta hai. Uski write client 1 ki write ko replace kar deti hai.

Do increments hue, par counter 44 ki jagah 43 dikhata hai. Book ka Figure 7-1 yeh race dikhata hai, aur neeche uska ek simplified version hai.

ACID wale sense mein isolation ka matlab hai ki saath chalne wali transactions ek-doosre ke kaam mein taang nahi adati. Classic database textbooks isolation ko serializability ke roop mein formalize karti hain. Har transaction aise behave karti hai jaise database par sirf wahi chal rahi ho. Transactions commit hone ke baad result waisa hi hota hai jaise woh ek ke baad ek chali hon, chahe asal mein woh overlap hui hon.

Practice mein serializable isolation kam use hota hai, kyunki isme performance cost hai. Kuch popular databases, jaise Oracle 11g, ise implement hi nahi karte. Oracle mein “serializable” naam ka ek isolation level hai, lekin asal mein woh snapshot isolation deta hai, jo weaker guarantee hai. Snapshot isolation aur doosre weaker levels ko chapter mein aage dekha gaya hai.

Durability. Database ko data rakhne ki ek safe jagah hona chahiye. Durability ka promise yeh hai ki transaction commit hone ke baad uska data bhoola nahi jaayega, hardware fault ya crash ke baad bhi.

Single node par durability ka matlab aam taur par hota hai ki data nonvolatile storage par likha gaya hai, jaise hard drive ya SSD (aisi storage jo power off hone par bhi data rakhti hai). Aksar isme ek write-ahead log bhi hota hai, yani main data structures badalne se pehle changes ka log likhna. Disk par data corrupt ho jaaye toh log se recovery ho sakti hai. Replicated database mein durability ka matlab ho sakta hai ki data kuch nodes par copy ho chuka hai. Database ko in writes ya copies ke khatam hone tak ruk-na padta hai, tabhi woh transaction ko committed report karta hai.

Yaad rakhein ki perfect durability jaisi koi cheez nahi hoti. Tumhari saari hard disks aur saare backups ek saath destroy ho jaayein, toh database kuch bhi karke tumhara data nahi bacha sakta.

Replication aur durability. Pehle durability ka matlab archive tape par likhna tha. Phir yeh disk ya SSD par likhna ho gaya, aur haal mein replication ho gaya. Kaunsa best hai? Book ke hisaab se koi bhi perfect nahi hai:

  • Disk par likhne ke baad machine mar jaaye, toh data safe rehta hai lekin tab tak reach se bahar rehta hai jab tak tum machine theek na karo ya disk doosri machine mein na lagao. Replicated system available reh sakta hai.
  • Correlated fault, jaise power outage ya aisa bug jo same input par har node ko crash kar de, saari replicas ek saath gira sakta hai. Jo kuch sirf memory mein hai woh chala jaata hai. Isliye in-memory databases ke liye bhi disk par likhna matter karta hai.
  • Asynchronously replicated system mein leader (jo node writes accept karta hai) fail hone par sabse recent writes lost ho sakti hain. Yeh Chapter 5 mein cover hua hai.
  • Dekha gaya hai ki achanak power kat jaane par SSDs apne guarantees tod dete hain. Fsync call, jo operating system se data disk par flush karwati hai, woh bhi hamesha reliable nahi hoti. Disk firmware mein bhi bugs ho sakte hain.
  • Storage engine aur filesystem ke beech ki subtle interactions se aise bugs aa sakte hain jinhe track karna mushkil hai, aur crash ke baad files corrupt ho sakti hain.
  • Disk par data dheere-dheere corrupt ho sakta hai aur kisi ko pata bhi nahi chalta. Aisa ho, toh replicas aur recent backups bhi corrupt ho sakte hain, aur tumhe purane backup se restore karna pad sakta hai.
  • Ek study mein paya gaya ki 30 se 80 percent SSDs ke pehle chaar saalon mein kam se kam ek bad block ban jaata hai. Magnetic hard drives mein bad sectors kam hote hain, lekin woh poori tarah zyada fail hoti hain.
  • Bina power ke rakhi SSD temperature ke hisaab se kuch hafton mein data khona shuru kar sakti hai.

Practice mein koi bhi ek technique absolute guarantee nahi deti. Sirf risk kam karne ki techniques hain, jaise disk par likhna, remote machines par replicate karna, aur backups rakhna. Inhe saath mein use karna chahiye. Book ki salaah hai ki kisi bhi theoretical guarantee ko thodi skepticism ke saath lein.

Single-object aur multi-object operations

Recap karein toh, atomicity aur isolation batate hain ki client ek transaction mein kai writes kare, toh database ko kya karna chahiye. Atomicity ka matlab hai ki beech mein error aaye toh transaction abort ho jaati hai aur ab tak ki writes discard ho jaati hain. Tumhe partial failure ki chinta nahi karni padti, kyunki all-or-nothing guarantee milti hai. Isolation ka matlab hai ki saath chalne wali transactions ek-doosre mein interfere na karein. Ek transaction kai writes kare, toh doosri transaction ya toh sab dekhe ya koi nahi, kabhi unka sirf ek hissa nahi.

Yeh definitions maan ke chalti hain ki tum kai objects (rows, documents ya records) ek saath badalna chahte hain. Aisi multi-object transactions aksar tab zaroori hoti hain jab data ke kai pieces ko sync mein rakhna ho. Email application ka ek example dekhte hain.

Example

User ke unread messages ki ginti dikhane ke liye tum query se unhe count kar sakte ho. Lekin user ke paas bahut emails hon, toh woh query bahut slow ho sakti hai. Isliye tum unread count ko alag field mein store karne ka faisla karte ho, jo ek tarah ki denormalization hai (same information do jagah store karna taaki reads tez ho). Ab har naye message par counter bhi increment karna padega, aur read mark hone par decrement.

Book ke Figure 7-2 mein user 2 ko ek problem dikhti hai. Mailbox listing mein ek unread message hai, lekin counter abhi bhi zero dikha raha hai, kyunki counter update abhi hua nahi hai. Isolation isse rok deta. User 2 ko ya toh naya email aur updated counter dono dikhte, ya koi nahi, beech ki halat kabhi nahi. Book ke mutabik email app mein galat counter koi critical problem nahi hai, lekin customer ke account balance aur payment ke saath yahi pattern bahut matter karega.

Book ka Figure 7-3 dikhata hai ki yahan atomicity kyun zaroori hai. Transaction ke beech kahin error aaye, toh mailbox aur unread counter sync se bahar ho sakte hain. Atomic transaction mein counter update fail ho jaaye, toh poori transaction abort ho jaati hai, aur insert kiya hua email rollback ho jaata hai.

Multi-object transactions ko yeh decide karne ka tarika chahiye ki kaunse reads aur writes saath mein belong karte hain. Relational databases mein yeh aam taur par client ke TCP connection se hota hai, yani database server tak network link. Ek connection par BEGIN TRANSACTION aur COMMIT ke beech ka sab kuch ek transaction maana jaata hai. Kleppmann ke hisaab se yeh ideal nahi hai. Connection toot jaaye toh transaction abort karni padti hai. Agar tootna tab ho jab client ne commit maanga ho lekin server ne confirm na kiya ho, toh client ko pata nahi chal sakta ki transaction commit hui ya nahi. Transaction manager iske bajaye operations ko ek unique transaction identifier se group kar sakta hai, jo kisi ek connection se bandha nahi hota. Book is idea par aage dobara aati hai.

Kai nonrelational databases mein operations ko group karne ka koi tarika hi nahi hota. Kuch multi-put dete hain jo ek call mein kai keys update karta hai. Lekin zaroori nahi ki woh transaction ho. Call kuch keys ke liye succeed ho sakti hai aur kuch ke liye fail, aur database aadha updated reh jaata hai.

Single-object writes. Ek single object badalte waqt bhi atomicity aur isolation matter karte hain. Socho tum database mein 20 KB ka JSON document likh rahe ho. Kai cheezein galat ho sakti hain:

  • Pehle 10 KB ke baad network drop ho jaaye, toh kya database woh unparseable fragment store kar leta hai?
  • Database disk par purani value overwrite kar raha ho aur power fail ho jaaye, toh kya purani aur nayi values aapas mein jud jaati hain?
  • Write chal rahi ho aur doosra client document read kare, toh kya use aadhi updated value dikhti hai?

Yeh issues bahut confusing hote, isliye storage engines lagbhag hamesha ek node par single object ke liye atomicity aur isolation dene ki koshish karte hain, jaise ek key-value pair. Atomicity aam taur par crash recovery ke liye use hone wale log se aati hai. Isolation aam taur par har object ke lock se aati hai, jo ek time par sirf ek thread ko object access karne deta hai.

Kuch databases aur complex single-object operations bhi dete hain. Atomic increment counter example jaise read-modify-write cycle ki zaroorat hata deta hai. Compare-and-set operation nayi value tabhi likhta hai jab current value tumhare last read ke baad se change na hui ho. Dono lost updates rokne mein kaam aate hain, jis par hum jaldi wapas aayenge. Lekin yeh aam matlab mein transactions nahi hain. Transaction multiple objects par operations ko ek unit mein group karti hai. Kuch vendors ne single-object operations ke liye marketing labels use kiye hain, jaise lightweight transactions, aur Kleppmann is terminology ko misleading maante hain.

Strictly kehein toh “atomic increment” mein atomic word multi-threaded wale matlab mein hai. ACID ke sense mein ise isolated ya serializable increment kehna chahiye. Author maante hain ki yeh bas nitpick hai.

Multi-object transactions ki zaroorat

Kai distributed datastores ne multi-object transactions chhod diye hain. Unhe partitions ke across banana mushkil hai, aur jab bahut high availability ya performance chahiye tab woh raste mein aa sakte hain. Lekin distributed database mein transactions ko fundamentally koi cheez rokti nahi, aur Chapter 9 batata hai ki unhe kaise banaya ja sakta hai.

Kya application sirf key-value model aur single-object operations ke saath chal sakti hai? Kuch chal sakti hain. Lekin kai cases mein kai objects par writes ko coordinate karna padta hai:

  • Relational data. Ek table ki row mein aksar doosre table ki row ka foreign key (reference) hota hai. Graph-like model mein vertex ke doosre vertices tak edges hote hain. Multi-object transactions in references ko valid rakhti hain. Tum aise kai records insert karo jo ek-doosre ko refer karte hain, toh references sahi hone chahiye, warna data bekaar ho jaata hai.
  • Document data. Jo fields saath mein change hoti hain woh aksar same document mein hoti hain, aur ek document update karna single-object write hai, isliye multi-object transaction nahi chahiye. Lekin joins ke bina document databases denormalization ko badhava dete hain, yani same information kai documents mein copy hoti hai. Woh information badle toh kai documents ek saath update karne padte hain, aur transactions copies ko sync se bahar jaane se rokti hain.
  • Secondary indexes. Secondary indexes (main key ke alawa kisi field par bana extra lookup structure) wale database mein lagbhag har change par index bhi update karna padta hai. Transaction ke nazariye se har index ek alag object hai. Isolation ke bina, doosra update pending ho tab record ek index mein dikh sakta hai aur doosre mein nahi.

Aisi applications transactions ke bina bhi ban sakti hain. Lekin atomicity ke bina error handling kaafi mushkil ho jaati hai, aur isolation ke bina concurrency problems aa jaati hain. Book aage weak isolation discuss karti hai, aur alternative approaches Chapter 12 mein dekhti hai.

Errors aur aborts handle karna

Transaction ka ek key feature yeh hai ki error ke baad use abort karke safely retry kiya ja sakta hai. ACID databases isi philosophy ko follow karte hain. Database atomicity, isolation ya durability violate karne ke khatre mein ho, toh woh transaction ko aadha chhodne ke bajaye poori tarah chhod dena pasand karta hai.

Har system yeh rule follow nahi karta. Leaderless replication wale datastores (Chapter 5) best effort basis par chalte hain. Database jitna kar sakta hai karta hai, aur error aaye toh jo ho chuka use undo nahi karta. Phir errors se recover karna application ka kaam ban jaata hai.

Kai developers sirf happy path ke baare mein sochna pasand karte hain, error handling ki details ke baare mein nahi. Popular object-relational mapping (ORM) frameworks, jaise Rails ka ActiveRecord aur Django, aborted transactions ko retry nahi karte. Error aam taur par exception ban jaata hai jo program mein upar tak bubble up hota hai, isliye user ka input phenk diya jaata hai aur use error message dikhta hai. Kleppmann ise sharm ki baat kehte hain, kyunki aborts ka poora maksad hi safe retries ko possible banana hai.

Aborted transaction ko retry karna simple aur effective hai, lekin iski limits hain:

  • Transaction asal mein succeed ho gayi thi, lekin server confirmation bhej raha tha tab network fail ho gaya, toh client sochta hai ki woh fail hui. Phir retry karne par transaction do baar ho jaati hai, jab tak application level par extra deduplication mechanism na ho.
  • Error overload ki wajah se aaya ho, toh retry karne se load aur badhta hai aur problem aur bigad jaati hai. Is feedback cycle se bachne ke liye retries ki limit rakhein, exponential backoff use karein (har failed attempt ke baad zyada der ruk-na), aur jahan ho sake overload errors ko doosre errors se alag handle karein.
  • Retry sirf transient errors ke baad karein, jaise deadlock, isolation violation, temporary network problem ya failover (backup node par switch hona). Permanent error ke baad, jaise constraint violation, retry karna bekaar hai.
  • Transaction ke database ke bahar bhi side effects hon, toh transaction abort hone par bhi woh ho sakte hain. Jaise, tum nahi chahoge ki har retry par email dobara bheja jaaye. Kai systems ko saath mein commit ya abort karna ho, toh two-phase commit madad kar sakta hai, jise Chapter 9 discuss karta hai.
  • Retry ke dauraan client process crash ho jaaye, toh jo data woh likhne ki koshish kar raha tha woh lost ho jaata hai.

Weak Isolation Levels

Agar do transactions same data ko touch nahi karte, toh woh safely parallel chal sakte hain, kyunki ek doosre par depend nahi karta. Concurrency problems tab aati hain jab ek transaction aisa data read kare jise doosra transaction change kar raha ho, ya jab do transactions ek hi data ko ek saath change karne ki koshish karein.

Concurrency bugs testing se pakadna mushkil hota hai. Yeh sirf tab dikhte hain jab timing galat baith jaaye, jo shayad kabhi-kabhi hi hota hai aur reproduce karna mushkil hota hai. Concurrency ke baare mein sochna bhi aasaan nahi hai, khaaskar bade application mein, jahan tumhe pata nahi hota ki database ko aur kaun sa code touch kar raha hai. Ek time par sirf ek user ho, tab bhi development mushkil hai. Bahut saare users ho toh data ka koi bhi hissa kisi bhi pal change ho sakta hai.

Isi wajah se databases kaafi time se transaction isolation dekar concurrency issues ko chhupane ki koshish karte aaye hain. Theory mein serializable isolation tumhe aisa maan lene deta hai ki koi concurrency ho hi nahi rahi. Database guarantee deta hai ki transactions ka effect waisa hi hoga jaise woh ek-ek karke chale hon.

Practice mein serializable isolation ka performance cost hota hai, aur kaafi databases yeh cost dena nahi chahte. Isliye systems aksar weaker isolation levels use karte hain. Yeh kuch concurrency problems se bachate hain, sab se nahi. Inhe samajhna kaafi mushkil hai, aur inse subtle bugs aa sakte hain. Phir bhi inka use bahut hota hai.

Weak isolation se hone wale concurrency bugs sirf theoretical nahi hain. Inse kaafi paisa doob chuka hai, financial auditors ne investigation ki hai, aur customer data corrupt hua hai. Aam reaction yeh hota hai ki "financial data sirf ACID database mein hi handle karna chahiye." Book ke hisaab se yeh baat point miss kar deti hai. Kaafi popular relational databases, jinhe aam taur par ACID kaha jaata hai, default mein weak isolation use karte hain, isliye zaroori nahi ki woh in bugs ko rok paate. Label par bharosa karne ke bajaye humein samajhna hoga ki kaun si concurrency problems hoti hain aur unhe kaise rokein.

Is section mein hum practice mein use hone wale kuch weak isolation levels dekhenge. Har level kaun si race conditions allow karta hai aur kaun si block karta hai, yeh dekhenge, taaki tum apne application ke liye sahi level chun sako. Uske baad serializability detail mein samjhayenge. Discussion informal hai aur examples ke saath chalti hai. Rigorous definitions academic literature mein milengi.

Read Committed

Transaction isolation ka sabse basic level read committed hai. Yeh do guarantees deta hai:

  1. Database se read karte waqt tumhe sirf committed data dikhta hai. Yani koi dirty reads nahi.
  2. Database mein write karte waqt tum sirf committed data ko overwrite karte ho. Yani koi dirty writes nahi.

Kuch databases ek aur weaker level bhi support karte hain, read uncommitted. Yeh dirty writes rokta hai, par dirty reads nahi rokta.

No dirty reads. Maan lo ek transaction ne kuch data write kiya hai, par abhi commit ya abort nahi hua. Agar doosra transaction yeh uncommitted data dekh sake, toh use dirty read kehte hain. Read committed level ke transactions ko dirty reads rokne hi padte hain. Transaction ki saari writes doosron ko tabhi dikhti hain jab woh commit ho, aur tab saari writes ek saath visible hoti hain. Book ka Figure 7-4 yahi dikhata hai. User 1 ne x ko 3 set kiya hai, par user 2 ko ab bhi purani value, 2, milti hai, kyunki user 1 ne abhi commit nahi kiya.

Dirty reads rokna kyun useful hai, iski book mein do wajah di gayi hain:

  • Agar ek transaction kai objects update karta hai, toh dirty read mein doosra transaction kuch updates dekh leta hai aur kuch nahi. Figure 7-2 mein user ko naya unread email dikhta hai, par updated counter nahi. Aadha-update hua database users ko confuse karta hai, aur doosre transactions ko galat decisions lene par majboor kar sakta hai.
  • Agar transaction abort hota hai, toh uski writes rollback honi chahiye, jaise Figure 7-3 mein. Dirty reads allow hote, toh doosra transaction aisa data read kar chuka hota jo baad mein rollback ho gaya aur kabhi commit hi nahi hua. Iske consequences ke baare mein sochna jaldi hi dimaag ghuma deta hai.

No dirty writes. Kya hota hai jab do transactions ek hi object ko ek saath update karne ki koshish karein? Writes ka order pata nahi hota, par aam taur par baad wali write pehle wali ko overwrite kar deti hai. Dirty write isse alag hai. Yeh tab hota hai jab baad wali write aise transaction ki likhi value ko overwrite kar de jo abhi commit nahi hua. Read committed ise rokta hai, aam taur par doosri write ko tab tak delay karke jab tak pehla transaction commit ya abort na ho jaaye.

Example

Socho ek used car site hai jahan Alice aur Bob ek hi car ko ek hi moment par khareedne ki koshish kar rahe hain. Car khareedne mein do writes lagti hain. Listing update karni hoti hai taaki buyer dikhe, aur sales invoice buyer ko bhejna hota hai. Dirty writes in dono writes ko mix kar sakte hain:

  1. Alice ka transaction listing mein uska naam likhta hai. Yeh abhi commit nahi hua.
  2. Bob ka transaction, Alice ke transaction ke khatam hone se pehle, listing ko apne naam se overwrite kar deta hai. Yeh dirty write hai.
  3. Bob ka transaction Bob ke liye sales invoice likhta hai.
  4. Alice ka transaction Alice ke liye sales invoice likhta hai, aur yeh last invoice write hai.

Ab listing mein buyer Bob dikhta hai, par invoice Alice ko jaata hai. Dono writes mein se har ek alag table ki winner ban gayi.

Book ka Figure 7-5 yeh mix-up dikhata hai. Read committed ise rokta hai, kyunki doosri write tab tak wait karti hai jab tak pehla transaction commit ya abort na ho jaaye.

Lekin read committed pehle wali counter race ko nahi rokta. Us case mein doosri write pehle transaction ke commit hone ke baad hoti hai, isliye woh dirty write nahi hai. Phir bhi woh galat hai, bas alag wajah se. Aisi counter increments ko safe kaise banayein, yeh lost updates rokne wale section mein aayega.

Implementing read committed. Read committed bahut popular isolation level hai. Yeh Oracle 11g, PostgreSQL, SQL Server 2012, MemSQL aur kaafi doosre databases mein default hai. Zyadatar databases dirty writes ko row-level locks se rokte hain. Lock matlab ek claim jo doosron ko wahi cheez use karne se rokta hai. Jab transaction kisi row ya document ko modify karna chahta hai, toh use pehle us par lock lena padta hai, aur commit ya abort hone tak lock hold karna padta hai. Ek time par sirf ek transaction lock hold kar sakta hai. Doosra transaction usi object par write karna chahe, toh use wait karna padta hai. Databases read committed mode aur usse strong modes mein yeh automatically karte hain.

Dirty reads rokne ke liye bhi aisa hi lock use ho sakta hai. Reader thodi der ke liye lock lega aur read karte hi chhod dega. Lekin book ke hisaab se yeh tarika practice mein achha kaam nahi karta. Ek long-running write transaction kaafi read-only transactions ko khatam hone tak wait karwa sakta hai. Isse read-only kaam slow ho jaata hai aur system operate karna mushkil ho jaata hai, kyunki application ke ek hisse ki slowdown lock waiting ke through doosre hisse tak phail sakti hai.

Isliye zyadatar databases dirty reads alag tarike se rokte hain. Jis object par write ho rahi hai, uske liye database do values yaad rakhta hai: purani committed value, aur woh nayi value jo abhi write lock hold karne wale transaction ne set ki hai. Transaction chalte waqt, us object ko read karne wale doosre transactions ko bas purani value de di jaati hai. Nayi value commit hone par hi readers us par switch karte hain. Kleppmann ka kehna hai ki read committed ke liye ab bhi locks use karne wale mainstream databases sirf IBM DB2, aur read_committed_snapshot band karke SQL Server hain.

Snapshot Isolation and Repeatable Read

Read committed dekhne mein aisa lagta hai ki transaction ko jo chahiye woh sab deta hai. Yeh aborts allow karta hai, jo atomicity ke liye zaroori hai. Yeh doosre transactions ke incomplete results padhne se rokta hai. Yeh concurrent writes ko mix hone se rokta hai. Yeh useful features hain, aur bina transactions wale system se kaafi strong hain.

Lekin is level par bhi concurrency bugs ho sakte hain. Book ka Figure 7-6 ek aisa bug dikhata hai, jise read skew kehte hain.

Example

Maan lo Alice ke bank mein $1,000 ki savings hain, do accounts mein $500-$500 karke. Ek transaction $100 ek account se doosre mein move karta hai. Agar Alice usi moment apne balances dekhe jab transfer chal raha ho, toh use before aur after ka mix dikh sakta hai. Kaun sa account kaun sa hai, yeh book mein nahi bataya gaya, par numbers tabhi match karte hain jab woh receiving account pehle read kare. Yeh ek tarika hai jisse aisa ho sakta hai:

  1. Alice receiving account read karti hai. Usme $500 dikhta hai, kyunki incoming payment abhi aayi nahi.
  2. Transfer commit ho jaata hai. $100 doosre account se nikal kar receiving account mein chala jaata hai.
  3. Alice doosra account read karti hai. Usme $400 dikhta hai, kyunki outgoing transfer ho chuka hai.
  4. Alice ne ab total $900 dekha. Aisa lagta hai jaise $100 hawa mein gayab ho gaye.

Agar Alice transaction ke end mein receiving account dobara read karti, toh use $600 dikhta. Isi wajah se is anomaly ko nonrepeatable read, ya read skew kehte hain. Usne jo har balance dekha, woh read karte waqt committed tha, isliye read committed isse allow karta hai. Skew word kai matlab mein use hota hai. Book mein pehle iska matlab hot spots wala unbalanced workload tha, par yahan iska matlab timing anomaly hai.

Alice ke liye yeh lasting problem nahi hai. Kuch seconds baad page reload karne par use shayad consistent balances dikh jaayenge. Lekin kuch situations temporary inconsistency bhi tolerate nahi kar sakti:

  • Backups. Backup poora database copy karta hai, jisme bade database par ghante lag sakte hain. Copy ke dauran writes aati rehti hain, isliye backup ke kuch parts mein purana data hota hai aur kuch mein naya. Us backup se restore karenge toh gayab hote paise jaisi inconsistencies permanent ho jaati hain.
  • Analytic queries and integrity checks. Kuch queries database ke bade hisse scan karti hain, analytics ke liye ya periodic check ke liye ki data corrupt toh nahi. Agar woh database ke alag-alag hisse alag-alag time points par dekhein, toh unke results ke bekaar hone ke chances zyada hain.

Snapshot isolation is problem ka sabse common solution hai. Idea yeh hai ki har transaction database ke ek consistent snapshot se read karta hai. Transaction ko woh saara data dikhta hai jo uske start hone ke moment par committed tha. Baad mein doosre transactions data change bhi kar dein, toh bhi yeh transaction us point ka purana data hi dekhta rehta hai. Snapshot isolation backups aur analytics jaisi long-running, read-only queries ke liye bahut kaam ki cheez hai, kyunki query jo data read karti hai woh frozen ho toh uske baare mein sochna kaafi aasaan ho jaata hai. Snapshot isolation PostgreSQL, InnoDB storage engine ke saath MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server aur kuch aur databases support karte hain.

Implementing snapshot isolation. Read committed ki tarah snapshot isolation bhi dirty writes rokne ke liye aam taur par write locks use karta hai. Matlab write karne wala transaction usi object par write karne wale doosre transaction ko block kar sakta hai. Lekin reads ko kisi lock ki zaroorat hi nahi hoti. Key principle yeh hai ki readers kabhi writers ko block nahi karte, aur writers kabhi readers ko block nahi karte. Long-running read query ek consistent snapshot par kaam kar sakti hai aur saath mein normal writes chalti rehti hain, dono ke beech lock contention nahi hota.

Isko kaam karwane ke liye database ko object ke kai committed versions rakhne padte hain, kyunki alag-alag in-progress transactions ko alag-alag points ka state dekhna pad sakta hai. Kai versions saath-saath rakhne ki wajah se is technique ko multi-version concurrency control, ya MVCC kehte hain. Snapshot isolation support karne wale storage engines aam taur par read committed ke liye bhi MVCC use karte hain. Farak yeh hai ki read committed har query ke liye naya snapshot leta hai, jabki snapshot isolation poore transaction ke liye ek hi snapshot use karta hai.

Book mein dikhaya gaya hai ki PostgreSQL yeh kaise karta hai. Transaction start hone par use ek unique, hamesha badhne wala transaction ID milta hai, jise txid kehte hain. Transaction jab bhi kuch write karta hai, toh jo data woh likhta hai us par uska apna txid tag ho jaata hai. (Txids 32-bit numbers hain, isliye lagbhag chaar billion transactions ke baad wrap around ho jaate hain. PostgreSQL ka vacuum process purana data clean karta hai taaki wrap-around se errors na aayein.)

Table ki har row mein do extra fields hote hain. created_by field us transaction ka txid rakhta hai jisne row insert ki. deleted_by field shuru mein empty hota hai. Jab transaction koi row delete karta hai, toh row turant remove nahi hoti. Usko deleting transaction ke txid par deleted_by set karke deletion ke liye mark kar diya jaata hai. Baad mein, jab koi transaction purane data ko access nahi kar sakta, tab garbage collection process aisi rows ko hata deta hai aur unki space free kar deta hai.

Update ko delete aur phir create ki tarah handle kiya jaata hai. Book ka example transaction 13 hai, jo account 2 se $100 kaat leta hai, yani balance $500 se $400 ho jaata hai. Uske baad accounts table mein account 2 ki do rows hoti hain. Ek row mein $500 hai aur woh transaction 13 se deleted mark hai. Doosri mein $400 hai aur woh transaction 13 ne create ki hai. Neeche wala figure yeh do versions dikhata hai.

Visibility rules. Transaction jab database se read karta hai, toh transaction IDs decide karte hain ki use object ke kaun se versions dikhenge. Clear visibility rules ki wajah se database application ko consistent snapshot de paata hai. Rules aise kaam karte hain:

  1. Har transaction ke start par database un saare doosre transactions ki list banata hai jo abhi in progress hain, yani na commit hue na abort. Un transactions ne jo bhi writes ki hain, woh ignore ki jaati hain, chahe woh baad mein commit ho jaayein.
  2. Aborted transactions ki saari writes ignore hoti hain.
  3. Jis transaction ka transaction ID baad ka hai, yani jo current transaction ke baad start hua, uski saari writes ignore hoti hain, chahe woh commit ho chuka ho ya nahi.
  4. Baaki saari writes application ki queries ko visible hoti hain.

Yeh rules objects ke creating aur deleting, dono par lagte hain. Wapas transaction 13 par aate hain: jab transaction 12 account 2 read karta hai, toh use $500 ka balance dikhta hai. $500 wali row ka deletion transaction 13 ne kiya tha, aur rule 3 ke hisaab se transaction 12 woh deletion nahi dekh sakta. $400 wali row bhi 13 ne create ki thi, isliye wahi wajah se woh 12 ke liye invisible hai.

Doosre tarike se kahein toh, ek object reader ko tab visible hota hai jab do cheezein sach hon. Pehli, object create karne wala transaction reader ke transaction ke start hone par already commit ho chuka tha. Doosri, object deletion ke liye marked nahi hai, ya agar hai, toh deletion maangne wala transaction reader ke transaction ke start hone tak commit nahi hua tha.

Long-running transaction apne snapshot ko bahut der tak use karta reh sakta hai. Ho sakta hai woh aisi values read karta rahe jinhe doosre transactions ne bahut pehle overwrite ya delete kar diya ho. Database values ko kabhi in place update nahi karta, balki value badalne par har baar naya version banata hai, isliye woh yeh consistent snapshots sirf thode se extra cost par de paata hai.

Indexes and snapshot isolation. Jab har object ke kai versions hon, toh indexes kaise kaam karte hain? Ek option yeh hai ki index object ke saare versions ko point kare. Phir index query un versions ko filter kar deti hai jo current transaction ko visible nahi hain. Jab garbage collection aise purane versions hata deta hai jo koi transaction nahi dekh sakta, toh unki matching index entries bhi hataayi ja sakti hain. Real systems mein yahan kaafi optimizations hote hain. Jaise, PostgreSQL index update karne se bachta hai jab ek hi object ke do versions same page par fit ho jaate hain.

Doosra approach CouchDB, Datomic aur LMDB mein use hota hai. Yeh systems B-trees (indexes ke liye common on-disk tree structure) use karte hain, lekin append-only, copy-on-write form mein. Update karte waqt woh tree ke pages ko kabhi overwrite nahi karte. Uski jagah har modified page ki nayi copy bana dete hain. Parent pages, root tak, copy hote hain aur update hote hain taaki naye child pages ko point karein. Jin pages ko write touch nahi karti, woh copy nahi hote aur unchanged rehte hain. Har write transaction, ya unka batch, naya tree root banata hai, aur har root us moment par database ka consistent snapshot hota hai. Isliye objects ko transaction ID se filter karne ki zaroorat nahi padti. Iski cost yeh hai ki compaction aur garbage collection ke liye ek background process chalana padta hai.

Repeatable read and naming confusion. Snapshot isolation useful hai, khaaskar read-only transactions ke liye. Lekin ise implement karne wale kaafi databases ise alag-alag naam dete hain. Oracle ise serializable kehta hai, jabki PostgreSQL aur MySQL ise repeatable read kehte hain. Wajah yeh hai ki SQL standard mein snapshot isolation ka concept hi nahi hai. Standard System R ki 1975 wali isolation levels ki definition par based hai, aur snapshot isolation tab tak invent nahi hua tha. Standard repeatable read naam ka ek level define karta hai, jo upar se dekhne mein similar lagta hai. PostgreSQL aur MySQL apne snapshot isolation level ko repeatable read kehte hain, kyunki isse woh standards compliance ka claim kar paate hain.

Book ka point hai ki standard ki isolation levels ki definition flawed hai. Woh ambiguous aur imprecise hai, aur standard jitna implementation se independent hona chahiye utni nahi hai. Kai databases repeatable read implement karte hain, par woh actually kya guarantee karte hain, isme kaafi farak hai. Repeatable read ki formal definition research literature mein hai, par zyadatar implementations use satisfy nahi karte. Aur gadbad yeh ki IBM DB2 repeatable read naam ko serializability ke matlab mein use karta hai. Natija yeh hai ki asal mein koi nahi jaanta ki repeatable read ka matlab kya hai.

Asli idea

Snapshot isolation har transaction ko data ka ek frozen view deta hai, isliye readers aur writers ek doosre ko block nahi karte. Apne database ki documentation check karein ki uska “repeatable read” ya “serializable” level asal mein kya guarantee karta hai.

Lost updates ko rokna

Ab tak read committed aur snapshot isolation levels is baare mein the ki doosre transactions ke write karte waqt read-only transaction ko kya dikhta hai. Do transactions ek saath write karein toh kya hota hai, ise hum zyadatar ignore karte aaye hain. Hum dirty writes dekh chuke hain, jo write-write conflict ka ek type hai. Writing transactions ke beech aur bhi conflicts hote hain, aur sabse jaana-pehchana counter example wala lost update problem hai.

Lost update tab ho sakta hai jab application koi value read kare, apne code mein change kare, aur nayi value wapas write kare. Ise read-modify-write cycle kehte hain. Do transactions yeh ek saath karein, toh ek change lost ho sakta hai, kyunki doosri write mein pehla change shamil nahi hota. Book ke words mein baad wali write pehli ko clobber kar deti hai. Yeh pattern kai scenarios mein dikhta hai:

  • Counter increment karna ya account balance update karna. Tumhe current value read karni padti hai, nayi calculate karni padti hai, aur wapas write karni padti hai.
  • Kisi complex value mein local change karna, jaise JSON document ki list mein element add karna. Tumhe document parse karna padta hai, change karna padta hai, aur poora wapas write karna padta hai.
  • Do users ek hi wiki page ek saath edit kar rahe hain, aur har user poora page server ko bhejkar save karta hai, jisse wahan jo bhi tha woh overwrite ho jaata hai.

Yeh problem bahut common hai, isliye iske kai solutions develop hue hain.

Atomic write operations. Kaafi databases atomic update operations dete hain. Inse application code mein read-modify-write cycle ki zaroorat nahi padti, aur agar tumhara change inke terms mein express ho sakta hai toh aam taur par yahi best solution hota hai. Jaise, yeh instruction zyadatar relational databases mein concurrent changes ke saamne safe hai:

UPDATE counters SET value = value + 1 WHERE key = 'foo';

MongoDB jaise document databases JSON document ka ek hissa change karne ke liye atomic operations dete hain. Redis priority queues jaisi data structures par atomic operations deta hai. Har write is tarah express nahi ho sakti. Wiki edit mein arbitrary text editing hoti hai, isliye woh fit nahi hoti. Lekin jahan atomic operations fit hote hain, wahan woh aam taur par best choice hain.

Atomic operations aam taur par aise implement hote hain ki object read hote waqt us par exclusive lock le liya jaata hai, taaki update apply hone tak koi aur transaction use read na kar sake. Is technique ko kabhi-kabhi cursor stability kehte hain. Ek aur option hai ki saare atomic operations ko ek single thread par force kar diya jaaye. Kleppmann warn karte hain ki object-relational mapping frameworks mein database ke atomic operations use karne ke bajaye galti se unsafe read-modify-write code likh dena aasaan hota hai. Yeh subtle bugs ka potential source hai jinhe testing se pakadna mushkil hai.

Explicit locking. Agar database ke atomic operations tumhe wahi nahi dete jo chahiye, toh application un objects ko lock kar sakti hai jo woh update karne wali hai. Application read, modify aur write karti hai, aur agar us beech doosra transaction wahi object read karne ki koshish kare, toh use pehle wale ke khatam hone tak wait karna padta hai.

Ek multiplayer game socho jisme kai players ek hi piece move kar sakte hain. Atomic operation shayad kaafi na ho, kyunki application ko yeh bhi check karna hota hai ki har move game ke rules follow karta hai. Aisi logic ko sensibly database query mein nahi likha ja sakta. Isliye tum lock use kar sakte ho taaki do players ek saath same piece move na kar sakein, jaise is example mein:

BEGIN TRANSACTION;
SELECT * FROM figures
WHERE name = 'robot' AND game_id = 222
FOR UPDATE;
-- Check whether move is valid, then update the position
-- of the piece that was returned by the previous SELECT.
UPDATE figures SET position = 'c4' WHERE id = 1234;
COMMIT;

FOR UPDATE clause database ko batata hai ki query jo saari rows return kare un par lock le. Yeh kaam karta hai, par tumhe application logic ke baare mein dhyaan se sochna padta hai. Code mein kahin zaroori lock lagana bhool jaana aasaan hai, aur isse race condition ban jaati hai.

Automatically detecting lost updates. Atomic operations aur locks read-modify-write cycles ko ek ke baad ek chalane par majboor karke lost updates rokte hain. Ek aur option hai. Cycles ko parallel chalne dein, aur transaction manager se lost update detect karwayein. Detect hone par woh offending transaction ko abort kar deta hai, aur application apna read-modify-write cycle retry karti hai.

Snapshot isolation ke saath yeh check efficient hota hai. PostgreSQL ka repeatable read, Oracle ka serializable level, aur SQL Server ka snapshot isolation level, sab lost updates automatically detect karke offending transaction abort kar dete hain. Lekin InnoDB ke saath MySQL apne repeatable read level par lost updates detect nahi karta. Kuch authors ka kehna hai ki snapshot isolation dene ke liye database ko lost updates rokne hi chahiye, toh us definition ke hisaab se MySQL snapshot isolation nahi deta. Automatic detection ka fayda yeh hai ki application code ko kisi special database feature ki zaroorat nahi padti. Tum lock ya atomic operation bhool kar bug la sakte ho, par automatic detection toh hota hi hai, isliye isme galti kam hoti hai.

Compare-and-set. Jin databases mein full transactions nahi hote, wahan kabhi-kabhi atomic compare-and-set operation milta hai. Iska purpose lost updates se bachna hai: yeh change tabhi allow karta hai jab value tumhare last read ke baad badli na ho. Agar current value ab us value se match nahi karti jo tumne read ki thi, toh update ka koi effect nahi hota, aur read-modify-write cycle retry karna padta hai.

Jaise, do users ek wiki page par ek doosre ke edits overwrite na karo, iske liye tum yeh likh sakte ho:

-- This may or may not be safe, depending on the database implementation
UPDATE wiki_pages SET content = 'new content'
WHERE id = 1234 AND content = 'old content';

Content change ho chuka ho toh update kuch nahi karta, isliye tumhe check karna padta hai ki woh effect mein aaya ya nahi, aur zaroorat ho toh retry karna padta hai. Lekin agar database WHERE clause ko purane snapshot se read karne deta hai, toh statement lost updates nahi rok paata, kyunki doosri write chalte waqt bhi condition true reh sakti hai. Compare-and-set par depend karne se pehle check karo ki tumhare database ka compare-and-set safe hai ya nahi.

Conflict resolution and replication. Replicated databases mein lost updates rokne ka ek aur pehlu hota hai. Data ki copies kai nodes par hoti hain, aur same data alag nodes par ek saath change ho sakta hai. Locks aur compare-and-set maan kar chalte hain ki data ki ek hi up-to-date copy hai. Multi-leader aur leaderless databases aam taur par kai concurrent writes allow karte hain aur unhe asynchronously replicate karte hain. Woh ek single up-to-date copy guarantee nahi kar sakte, isliye lock-based aur compare-and-set techniques yahan apply nahi hoti. (Yeh baat linearizability ki discussion mein dobara aayegi.)

Uski jagah, jaisa Chapter 5 mein discuss hua, ek common approach yeh hai ki concurrent writes ko ek value ke kai conflicting versions banane diya jaaye, jinhe siblings kehte hain. Phir application code ya special data structures baad mein unhe resolve aur merge karte hain. Atomic operations replicated setting mein achhe chal sakte hain, khaaskar agar woh commutative hon. Matlab tum unhe alag replicas par alag order mein apply karo, tab bhi result wahi aaye. Counter increment karna aur set mein element add karna, dono commutative hain. Riak 2.0 ke datatypes ka yahi idea hai, jo concurrent updates ko merge karke replicas ke across lost updates rokte hain, taaki koi update lost na ho.

Iske ulat, last write wins (LWW) conflict resolution method lost updates ke liye prone hai, jaisa Chapter 5 mein discuss hua. LWW kaafi replicated databases mein default hai, isliye yeh ek real trap hai.

Trade-offs
OptionFaydaCost
Atomic operations (jaise value = value + 1)Simple aur fast, application locks ki zaroorat nahi. Counters aur ek value ke changes ke liye achha.Tabhi kaam karta hai jab tumhara change operation mein fit ho. ORMs ise bina kisi ko pata chale bypass kar sakte hain.
Explicit locking (jaise SELECT FOR UPDATE)Kisi bhi logic ke liye kaam karta hai, un game rules ke liye bhi jo queries mein nahi likhe ja sakte.Lock lagana bhool jaana aasaan hai. Transactions ek doosre ka wait karte hain, jisse cheezein slow hoti hain.
Automatic lost update detectionSpecial application code nahi chahiye. Galti kam hoti hai, kyunki check har update par chalta hai.Sirf kuch databases mein available hai. Abort hua kaam retry karna padta hai. MySQL ka repeatable read ise detect nahi karta.
Compare-and-setJab database mein full transactions nahi hote, tab ek halka-sa check.Tabhi safe hai jab database ka check current data read kare. Retry loop chahiye.
Replicated databases mein commutative mergesAlag replicas par concurrent updates bina kuch lose kiye combine ho jaate hain.Merging ke liye design kiye gaye datatypes chahiye, jaise counters aur sets. Last write wins mein data lose hota hai.

Write Skew and Phantoms

Dirty writes aur lost updates aisi race conditions hain jahan concurrent transactions ek hi object par write karte hain. Kuch aur subtle race conditions bhi hoti hain. Kleppmann inme se ek ko hospital example se samjhate hain.

Maan lo tum doctors ke on-call shifts manage karne ka application likh rahe ho. Hospital mein aam taur par kisi bhi time kai doctors on call hote hain, par kam se kam ek hamesha hona chahiye. Doctor shift chhod sakta hai, jaise bimaar hone par, lekin tabhi jab us shift ke liye koi colleague on call reh raha ho.

Example

Alice aur Bob ek particular shift ke liye on call do doctors hain. Dono ko tabiyat theek nahi lag rahi, aur dono lagbhag ek hi time par off call jaane ka button click karte hain. Step by step yeh hota hai (book ka Figure 7-8):

  1. Alice ka transaction check karta hai ki kam se kam do doctors on call hain ya nahi. Jawab haan hai, do hain, isliye woh aage badhta hai.
  2. Bob ka transaction wahi check usi time chalata hai. Use bhi do doctors dikhte hain, isliye woh bhi aage badhta hai.
  3. Alice ka transaction apna record update karke khud ko off call kar deta hai.
  4. Bob ka transaction bhi apna record isi tarah update kar deta hai.
  5. Dono transactions commit ho jaate hain. Ab koi on call nahi hai, jo is rule ko todta hai ki kam se kam ek doctor on call hona chahiye.

Database snapshot isolation use karta hai, isliye dono checks ne aisa snapshot read kiya jisme do doctors dikh rahe the. Har transaction ne usi snapshot par kaam kiya, aur kisi ko doosre ka pata nahi chala.

Characterizing write skew. Is anomaly ko write skew kehte hain. Yeh na dirty write hai na lost update, kyunki dono transactions do alag objects update karte hain, Alice ka record aur Bob ka record. Conflict kam obvious hai, phir bhi yeh race condition hi hai. Agar dono transactions ek ke baad ek chalte, toh doosre doctor ko rok diya jaata. Anomaly sirf isliye possible hui kyunki transactions concurrently chale.

Write skew ko tum lost update problem ka generalization maan sakte ho. Write skew tab ho sakta hai jab do transactions same objects read karein, aur phir har ek unme se kuch update kare. Alag transactions alag objects update kar sakte hain. Agar woh same object update karein, toh timing ke hisaab se dirty write ya lost update ban jaata hai.

Write skew rokne ke tarike lost updates se kam hain. Options yeh hain:

  • Atomic single-object operations se madad nahi milti, kyunki kai objects involve hain.
  • Automatic lost update detection se bhi madad nahi milti. PostgreSQL ke repeatable read, MySQL ke InnoDB repeatable read, Oracle ke serializable level, ya SQL Server ke snapshot isolation level mein write skew automatically detect nahi hota. Ise automatically rokne ke liye true serializable isolation chahiye.
  • Kuch databases tumhe constraints configure karne dete hain, jaise uniqueness, foreign keys, ya kisi value par restrictions, aur phir unhe enforce karte hain. “Kam se kam ek doctor on call” rule mein kai objects involve hain, aur zyadatar databases mein iske liye built-in constraint nahi hota. Database ke hisaab se tum ise triggers ya materialized views se implement kar sakte ho.
  • Serializable isolation use nahi kar sakte, toh second-best option shayad yeh hai ki jin rows par transaction depend karta hai unhe explicitly lock kar dein. Doctors ke liye tum yeh likh sakte ho:
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
SELECT * FROM doctors
WHERE on_call = true
AND shift_id = 1234 FOR UPDATE;
UPDATE doctors
SET on_call = false
WHERE name = 'Alice'
AND shift_id = 1234;
COMMIT;

Pehle ki tarah, FOR UPDATE database ko batata hai ki query jo saari rows return karti hai un sab ko lock kar le.

Dhyaan do

Snapshot isolation serializability nahi hai. Transaction consistent snapshot read karke bhi aisa decision le sakta hai jise koi concurrent transaction galat bana chuka hai. Code mein jahan bhi data read karke uske basis par write hoti hai, wahan check karein.

More examples of write skew. Write skew pehle shayad obscure issue lage, par pattern pata chalne ke baad tumhe yeh aur jagah bhi dikhne lagega. Book mein kai examples hain.

Meeting room booking. Maan lo tum chahte ho ki koi meeting room ek hi time par do baar book na ho. Koi room book karna chahta hai toh pehle us room ki overlapping bookings check karte hain. Koi na ho, toh meeting create kar dete hain. Code aisa dikhta hai:

BEGIN TRANSACTION;
-- Check for any existing bookings that overlap with the period of noon-1pm
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bookings
WHERE room_id = 123 AND
end_time > '2015-01-01 12:00' AND start_time < '2015-01-01 13:00';
-- If the previous query returned zero:
INSERT INTO bookings
(room_id, start_time, end_time, user_id)
VALUES (123, '2015-01-01 12:00', '2015-01-01 13:00', 666);
COMMIT;

Snapshot isolation kisi doosre user ko concurrently conflicting meeting insert karne se nahi rokta. Scheduling conflicts na hon, yeh guarantee karne ke liye tumhe dobara serializable isolation chahiye. (PostgreSQL range types se ise zyada elegantly kar sakta hai, jo baaki jagah widely support nahi hote.)

Multiplayer game. Pehle wale game example ka explicit lock do players ko ek saath same piece move karne se rokta hai. Lekin woh do players ko do alag pieces same square par le jaane se, ya game ke rules todne wali koi aur move karne se nahi rokta. Rule ke hisaab se, unique constraint madad kar sakta hai. Warna game write skew ke liye khula hai.

Claiming a username. Jis site par har user ko unique username chahiye, wahan do log ek hi time par same naam register karne ki koshish kar sakte hain. Tum transaction se check kar sakte ho ki naam liya hua hai ya nahi, aur nahi hai toh account bana sakte ho. Lekin snapshot isolation mein yeh safe nahi hai, wahi wajah jo pehle thi. Yahan unique constraint simple fix hai. Jo doosra transaction wahi naam register karne ki koshish karta hai woh constraint violate karne ki wajah se abort ho jaata hai.

Preventing double-spending. Jo service users ko paise ya points kharch karne deti hai, use check karna hota hai ki user apne paas jitna hai usse zyada kharch na kare. Ek tarika yeh hai ki user ke account mein ek tentative spending item insert karein, saare items list karein, aur check karein ki total abhi bhi positive hai. Agar do spending items concurrently insert hon, toh woh milkar balance negative kar sakte hain, aur kisi transaction ko doosre ka pata nahi chalta.

Phantoms causing write skew. Yeh saare examples ek jaise pattern follow karte hain:

  1. Ek SELECT query condition match karne wali rows search karke check karti hai ki koi requirement poori hai ya nahi. Jaise, kam se kam do doctors on call hain, ya us time room ki koi booking nahi hai, ya board par woh position khali hai, ya username free hai, ya paise kaafi hain.
  2. Result ke basis par application decide karti hai ki aage kaise badhna hai. Woh aage badh sakti hai, ya error report karke abort kar sakti hai.
  3. Application aage badhti hai toh woh ek write (INSERT, UPDATE ya DELETE) karti hai aur commit kar deti hai.

Yeh write step 2 ke decision ka premise badal deti hai. Write ke baad SELECT dobara chalate, toh alag jawab milta, kyunki write ne condition match karne wali rows ka set badal diya. Steps alag order mein bhi ho sakte hain. Jaise, pehle write ho, phir SELECT, aur phir transaction decide kare ki commit karna hai ya abort.

Doctor example mein step 3 mein jo row change hui woh step 1 mein return hui rows mein se ek thi. Isliye un rows ko SELECT FOR UPDATE se lock karke transaction ko safe banaya ja sakta tha. Baaki examples alag hain. Woh condition match karne wali rows ke absent hone ko check karte hain, aur write ek nayi row add karti hai jo usi condition ko match karti hai. Step 1 ki query koi row return nahi karti, toh SELECT FOR UPDATE ke paas lock karne ke liye kuch nahi hota.

Is effect ko phantom kehte hain. Yeh tab hota hai jab ek transaction ki write doosre transaction ki search query ka result badal deti hai. Snapshot isolation read-only queries ke liye phantoms se bachata hai. Lekin aise read-write transactions mein phantoms tricky write skew la sakte hain. Neeche ka figure meeting room ke saath dikhata hai ki yeh kaise hota hai.

Materializing conflicts. Phantoms ki problem yeh hai ki lock lagane ke liye koi object nahi hota, toh shayad tum ek bana sakte ho. Meeting room ke liye tum rooms aur time slots ki ek table bana sakte ho, har room aur har 15-minute period ke liye ek row. Yeh rows tum pehle se bana loge, jaise agle six months ke liye. Booking transaction phir SELECT FOR UPDATE se apne room aur time wali rows ko lock karta hai. Locks milne ke baad woh overlapping bookings check kar sakta hai aur pehle ki tarah nayi booking insert kar sakta hai. Yeh extra table booking details store nahi karti. Yeh bas locks ka set hai.

Is approach ko materializing conflicts kehte hain, kyunki yeh phantom ko database ki concrete rows ke set par lock conflict mein badal deta hai. Lekin conflicts ko kaise materialize karna hai, yeh figure out karna mushkil hai aur isme galti hone ke chances hain. Concurrency control mechanism ko application ke data model mein leak hone dena bhi ugly hai. Isliye Kleppmann ke hisaab se materializing conflicts last resort hona chahiye. Zyadatar cases mein serializable isolation level kaafi behtar hai.
