Agla figure weak levels ko side by side rakhta hai. Is section ke examples use karke yeh dikhata hai ki har level par kaun si race conditions ab bhi ho sakti hain.

Serializability

Is chapter mein hamne kai aise transactions dekhe jo race conditions ke shikaar ho sakte hain. Kuch read committed aur snapshot isolation se bach jaate hain, lekin kuch nahi bachte, aur write skew aur phantoms especially tricky hain. Kleppmann is situation ko sad kehte hain, aur iske teen reasons hain:

  • Isolation levels samajhna mushkil hai, aur alag-alag databases unhe alag tarah se implement karte hain. “Repeatable read” ka matlab ek system se doosre system mein kaafi badal jaata hai.
  • Apna application code dekhkar yeh batana mushkil hai ki woh kisi particular isolation level par safe hai ya nahi. Bade application mein toh yeh aur mushkil hai, kyunki tumhe pata hi nahi hota ki ek saath aur kya-kya chal raha hai.
  • Race conditions detect karne ke liye achhe tools nahi hain. Static analysis principle mein madad kar sakta hai, lekin research techniques abhi practical nahi bani hain. Concurrency problems ko test karna bhi mushkil hai, kyunki yeh nondeterministic hoti hain aur sirf tab dikhti hain jab timing tumhare against chali jaaye.

Yeh koi nayi problem nahi hai. Yeh 1970s se chali aa rahi hai, jab weak isolation levels pehli baar aaye the. Researchers ka jawab hamesha ek hi raha hai: serializable isolation use karo.

Serializable isolation ko aam taur par sabse strong level maana jaata hai. Transactions parallel mein chal sakte hain, phir bhi final result waisa hi hota hai jaise woh ek ke baad ek chale hon. Agar har transaction akele chalne par sahi behave karta hai, toh doosron ke saath chalne par bhi sahi hi behave karega. Yani database saari possible race conditions rok deta hai.

Agar serializable isolation itna behtar hai, toh sab log ise use kyun nahi karte? Iska jawab dene ke liye hume dekhna padega ki serializability kaise implement hoti hai aur har approach ki performance kaisi hai. Aaj zyadatar databases jo serializability dete hain, woh teen techniques mein se ek use karte hain:

  • Actual serial execution, jisme transactions ek fixed order mein ek-ek karke chalte hain.
  • Two-phase locking (2PL), jo kai decades tak ek hi viable option tha.
  • Optimistic concurrency control, serializable snapshot isolation (SSI) ke form mein.

Abhi hum in techniques ko mainly single-node databases ke liye dekhenge. Chapter 9 mein dekhenge ki inhe multiple nodes tak phailne wale transactions ke liye kaise extend kiya jaata hai.

Actual Serial Execution

Concurrency problems se bachne ka sabse simple tarika hai concurrency ko hi hata dena. Ek time par sirf ek transaction chalao, serial order mein, ek single thread par. Isse conflicts detect aur prevent karne ki problem hi khatam ho jaati hai, kyunki isolation definition se hi serializable hota hai.

Hairaani ki baat hai ki database designers ne haal hi mein maana ki yeh feasible hai. Around 2007 mein unhone conclude kiya ki transactions chalane ke liye single-threaded loop kaam kar sakta hai. Pichle tees saal tak good performance ke liye multi-threaded concurrency ko zaroori maana jaata tha. Do developments ne yeh soch badal di:

  • RAM itni sasti ho gayi ki kai use cases mein poora active dataset memory mein fit ho jaata hai. Jab transaction ko chahiye har item pehle se memory mein ho, toh transactions disk se data load hone ka wait karne ke mukable kaafi tez chalte hain.
  • Designers ko samajh aaya ki OLTP (online transaction processing, yani live application ke bahut saare chhote reads aur writes) transactions aam taur par short hote hain aur sirf kuch records touch karte hain. Long-running analytic queries aam taur par read-only hoti hain, isliye woh snapshot isolation use karke ek consistent snapshot par, serial execution loop ke bahar chal sakti hain.

Serial execution VoltDB/H-Store, Redis aur Datomic mein use hota hai. Single-threaded execution ke liye bana system kabhi-kabhi concurrency support karne wale system se behtar perform kar sakta hai, kyunki ismein locking ka coordination overhead nahi hota. Lekin iski throughput ek single CPU core ki limit tak hi rehti hai. Us ek thread ka poora fayda uthane ke liye transactions ko traditional form se alag tarah se structure karna padta hai.

Transactions ko stored procedures mein encapsulate karna. Databases ke shuruaati dino mein idea yeh tha ki ek database transaction user activity ke poore flow ko cover kar sake. Airline ticket book karna ek multi-stage process hai. Tum routes, fares aur seats search karte ho. Phir itinerary decide karte hain. Phir har flight par seats book karte hain, passenger details daalte hain aur payment karte hain. Yeh sab ek hi transaction hota, jo atomically commit hota, toh kaafi neat lagta tha.

Lekin insaan faisla karne mein aur respond karne mein slow hote hain. Agar transaction ko user input ka wait karna pade, toh database ko potentially bahut saare open transactions sambhalne padenge, jinmein se zyadatar idle honge. Zyadatar databases yeh efficiently nahi kar paate. Isliye lagbhag saare OLTP applications transactions ko short rakhte hain aur transaction ke andar interactive wait avoid karte hain. Web par iska matlab hai ki transaction usi HTTP request (browser se server tak ek single request) ke andar commit ho jaata hai. Nayi request nayi transaction shuru karti hai.

Insaan ko critical path se hata bhi do, phir bhi transactions aam taur par interactive, client-server style mein chalte hain, ek-ek statement karke. Application ek query karta hai, result padhta hai, phir us result ke hisaab se shayad doosri query karta hai, aur aise hi aage. Queries aur results application aur database server ke beech aate-jaate rehte hain, jo aksar doosri machine par hota hai. Is network traffic mein kaafi time lagta hai. Agar database ek time par sirf ek transaction handle kare, toh throughput bahut kharab hogi, kyunki database zyadatar time application se agli query aane ka wait karta rahega. Isliye single-threaded serial execution wale systems interactive multi-statement transactions allow nahi karte.

Iske bajaye application poora transaction code pehle se hi database ko bhej deta hai, ek stored procedure ke roop mein. Stored procedure code ka ek hissa hota hai jo database ke andar rehta hai aur call karne par chalta hai. Agar transaction ko chahiye saara data memory mein hai, toh stored procedure bahut tezi se execute ho sakta hai, bina kisi network ya disk input/output ka wait kiye. Figure on-call example ke saath yeh difference dikhata hai.

Stored procedures ke pros aur cons. Stored procedures relational databases mein kaafi time se hain. Yeh 1999 se SQL standard (SQL/PSM) ka hissa hain. Inki reputation thodi kharab hai, kai wajahon se:

  • Har database vendor ki apni language hoti hai, jaise Oracle ke liye PL/SQL, SQL Server ke liye T-SQL, aur PostgreSQL ke liye PL/pgSQL. Yeh languages general-purpose programming languages ke saath kadam nahi mila payi. Yeh purani lagti hain, aur inke paas woh library ecosystem nahi hai jo zyadatar programming languages ke paas hota hai.
  • Database ke andar ka code manage karna mushkil hota hai. Application server ke mukable ismein debug karna mushkil hai, version control aur deploy karna awkward hai, test karna tricky hai, aur monitoring ke liye metrics system se jodna difficult hai.
  • Database aksar application server se zyada performance-sensitive hota hai, kyunki ek database instance ko kai application servers share karte hain. Kharab likha stored procedure jo bahut memory ya CPU time use kare, application code mein wahi galti hone se kahin zyada problem khadi kar sakta hai.

Kleppmann ke hisaab se yeh problems door ki ja sakti hain. Stored procedures ke modern implementations ne PL/SQL chhod diya hai aur general-purpose languages use karte hain. VoltDB Java ya Groovy use karta hai, Datomic Java ya Clojure, aur Redis Lua. Stored procedures aur in-memory data ke saath saare transactions ek single thread par chalana practical ho jaata hai. Stored procedures I/O ka wait avoid karte hain, aur doosre concurrency control methods ka overhead bhi skip karte hain, isliye ek thread par bhi achhi throughput mil sakti hai.

VoltDB replication ke liye bhi stored procedures use karta hai. Transaction ke writes ko ek node se doosre node par copy karne ke bajaye, woh har replica par wahi stored procedure chala deta hai. Iske liye zaroori hai ki procedures deterministic hon, yani har node par same result dein. Agar transaction ko current date aur time chahiye, toh use special deterministic APIs se lena padega.

Rule of thumb

Jab transactions ek-ek karke chalte hain, toh har transaction chhota aur fast hona chahiye. Ek slow transaction baaki sabko rok deta hai, isliye har transaction short rakhein aur uska kaam memory ke andar hi rakhein.

Partitioning. Saare transactions serially chalane se concurrency control kaafi simple ho jaata hai. Lekin database ki transaction throughput ek machine ke ek CPU core ki speed tak limited ho jaati hai. Read-only transactions snapshot isolation use karke kahin aur chal sakte hain. Lekin high write throughput wale applications mein single transaction processor ek serious bottleneck ban sakta hai.

Kai CPU cores aur kai nodes tak scale karne ke liye tum apna data partition kar sakte ho, jaisa Chapter 6 mein bataya tha. VoltDB yeh support karta hai. Agar tum dataset ko aise split kar paao ki har transaction sirf ek partition ke andar read aur write kare, toh har partition ka apna transaction thread ho sakta hai, jo doosron se independently chalta hai. Har CPU core ko apna partition mil sakta hai, isliye throughput cores ki count ke saath seedhi line mein badh sakti hai.

Jo transaction kai partitions access karta hai, woh alag baat hai. Database ko use un sabhi partitions ke beech coordinate karna padta hai jinhe woh touch karta hai. Stored procedure ko un saare partitions par lockstep mein chalna padta hai, taaki poora system serializable rahe. Cross-partition transactions mein extra coordination overhead hota hai, isliye woh single-partition transactions se kaafi slow hote hain. Book mein VoltDB ka ek figure hai: lagbhag 1,000 cross-partition writes per second. Yeh uski single-partition throughput se orders of magnitude kam hai, aur zyada machines jodne se ise badhaya nahi ja sakta.

Transactions ek partition ke andar reh sakte hain ya nahi, yeh application ke data ke structure par depend karta hai. Simple key-value data ko aksar aasaani se partition kiya ja sakta hai. Jis data mein kai secondary indexes hon, usmein shayad kaafi cross-partition coordination chahiye hoga (partitioning aur secondary indexes ke liye Chapter 6 dekhein).

Serial execution ka summary. Serial execution ab serializable isolation paane ka ek practical tarika ban gaya hai, lekin kuch limits ke andar:

  • Har transaction chhota aur fast hona chahiye, kyunki ek slow transaction poori transaction processing rok sakta hai.
  • Yeh sirf wahin kaam karta hai jahan active dataset memory mein fit ho jaaye. Kam use hone wala data disk par move kiya ja sakta hai, lekin agar single-threaded transaction ko woh chahiye ho, toh system bahut slow ho jaayega. Kleppmann batate hain ki us case mein sabse achha solution shayad yeh hai ki transaction abort kar do, background mein data memory mein fetch karo jabki doosre transactions chalte rahein, aur phir transaction restart karo. Ise anti-caching kehte hain.
  • Write throughput itni kam honi chahiye ki ek single CPU core sambhal le. Warna transactions ko aise partition karna padega ki cross-partition coordination avoid ho.
  • Cross-partition transactions possible hain, lekin unhe kitna use kiya ja sakta hai, us par ek hard limit hai.

Two-Phase Locking (2PL)

2PL aur 2PC alag hain. Two-phase locking sunne mein two-phase commit jaisa lagta hai, lekin yeh bilkul alag cheezein hain. Two-phase commit Chapter 9 mein cover hoga.

Lagbhag tees saal tak databases mein serializability ke liye sirf ek widely used algorithm tha: two-phase locking, yani 2PL. (Doosre variants se alag batane ke liye ise kabhi-kabhi strong strict two-phase locking, SS2PL, bhi kehte hain.)

Hum pehle dekh chuke hain ki dirty writes rokne ke liye aksar locks use hote hain. Agar do transactions ek hi object par write karne ki koshish karein, toh lock second writer ko tab tak wait karata hai jab tak pehla khatam na ho jaaye, chahe woh commit ho ya abort. Two-phase locking is jaisa hi hai, lekin uski lock requirements kaafi strong hoti hain. Kai transactions ek hi object ko ek saath read kar sakte hain, jab tak koi use write nahi kar raha. Lekin jaise hi koi write karna chahe, yani object modify ya delete karna chahe, us transaction ko exclusive access chahiye:

  • Agar transaction A ne ek object read kiya hai aur transaction B use write karna chahta hai, toh B ko tab tak wait karna padega jab tak A commit ya abort na ho jaaye. Isse pakka hota hai ki B, A ke peeche se object change nahi kar sakta.
  • Agar transaction A ne ek object write kiya hai aur transaction B use read karna chahta hai, toh B ko tab tak wait karna padega jab tak A commit ya abort na ho jaaye. Object ka purana version padhna, jaisa counter race mein hua tha, 2PL mein acceptable nahi hai.

2PL mein writers readers ko block karte hain, aur readers writers ko block karte hain. Snapshot isolation ka mantra ulta hai: readers kabhi writers ko block nahi karte, aur writers kabhi readers ko block nahi karte. Dono ke beech yahi key performance difference hai. Doosri taraf, 2PL serializability deta hai, isliye yeh is chapter ki saari race conditions se bachata hai, lost updates aur write skew samet.

Two-phase locking ka implementation. 2PL ko MySQL (InnoDB) aur SQL Server ke serializable isolation level mein, aur IBM DB2 ke repeatable read level mein use kiya jaata hai. Readers aur writers ko block karna database ke har object par ek lock se implement hota hai. Lock shared mode mein ya exclusive mode mein hold kiya ja sakta hai:

  • Object read karne ke liye transaction ko pehle lock shared mode mein acquire karna padta hai. Kai transactions ek saath shared lock hold kar sakte hain. Agar kisi aur transaction ke paas us object par pehle se exclusive lock hai, toh reader ko wait karna padega.
  • Object write karne ke liye transaction ko lock exclusive mode mein acquire karna padta hai. Koi aur transaction us par kisi bhi tarah ka lock, shared ya exclusive, hold nahi kar sakta, isliye agar koi bhi lock present hai toh writer ko wait karna padega.
  • Agar transaction pehle object read karta hai aur phir write, toh woh apna shared lock exclusive lock mein upgrade kar sakta hai. Upgrade waise hi kaam karta hai jaise seedha exclusive lock lena.
  • Transaction ek baar lock acquire kar le, toh use transaction ke end tak hold karna padta hai, chahe woh commit ho ya abort. Naam yahin se aaya hai. Pehle phase mein, jab transaction chal raha hota hai, woh locks acquire karta hai. Doosre phase mein, end par, woh sabhi locks release kar deta hai.

Itne saare locks hone par yeh aasaani se ho sakta hai ki transaction A, transaction B ke lock release karne ka wait karta rahe, aur B, A ka wait kar raha ho. Is situation ko deadlock kehte hain. Database deadlocks ko automatically detect karta hai aur ek transaction abort kar deta hai, taaki baaki aage badh sakein. Application ko aborted transaction retry karna padta hai. Neeche ka figure basic rule ko timeline mein dikhata hai.

Two-phase locking ki performance. 2PL ka bada downside, aur wajah jisse kai systems ne 1970s se ise use nahi kiya, performance hai. Weak isolation ke mukable 2PL mein transaction throughput aur query response times kaafi kharab hote hain. Iski ek wajah yeh hai ki itne saare locks acquire aur release karne ka overhead hota hai. Us se bhi zyada important wajah yeh hai ki concurrency kam ho jaati hai. Design ke hisaab se, agar do transactions aisa kuch kar sakte hain jisse race condition ho sakti hai, toh ek ko doosre ke khatam hone ka wait karna padta hai.

Traditional relational databases transaction kitni der chal sakta hai, us par limit nahi lagate, kyunki unhe un interactive applications ke liye design kiya gaya tha jo human input ka wait karte hain. Jab ek transaction ko doosre ka wait karna padta hai, toh wait kitna lamba ho sakta hai, iski koi limit nahi hoti. Tum apne transactions short bhi rakho, tab bhi jab kai transactions ek hi object chahte ho toh queue ban sakti hai. Ek transaction ko kuch bhi karne se pehle kai doosre transactions ke khatam hone ka wait karna pad sakta hai. Isliye 2PL chalane wale databases ki latencies kaafi unstable ho sakti hain. Contention hone par high percentiles (Chapter 1 dekhein) par yeh bahut slow ho sakte hain. Sirf ek slow transaction, ya aisa transaction jo bahut saara data touch kare aur kai locks acquire kare, baaki system ko thap kar sakta hai. Jahan robust operation chahiye, wahan yeh instability ek problem hai.

Lock-based read committed mein bhi deadlocks ho sakte hain. Lekin 2PL serializable isolation mein yeh kahin zyada hote hain, tumhare transactions ke access patterns par depend karta hai. Yeh ek extra performance problem hai. Jab transaction deadlock ki wajah se abort hota hai aur phir retry hota hai, toh use apna poora kaam dobara karna padta hai. Agar deadlocks aksar hon, toh barbaad hua effort kaafi bada ho sakta hai.

Predicate locks. Ab tak ke lock description mein ek subtle detail ko skip kiya gaya tha. Pehle hamne phantoms ki baat ki thi, jahan ek transaction doosre transaction ki search ka result badal deta hai. Serializable isolation wale database ko phantoms bhi rokne padte hain.

Meeting room example mein, agar ek transaction ne kisi room ki bookings ek certain time window mein search ki hain, toh koi aur transaction concurrently usi room aur usi time range ke liye booking insert ya update nahi kar sakta. Doosre rooms ki bookings insert karna, ya usi room ka aisa alag time jo proposed booking ko affect nahi karta, bilkul theek hai.

Yeh kaise implement hoga? Conceptually hume ek predicate lock chahiye. Yeh upar bataye shared aur exclusive locks jaisa hi kaam karta hai. Lekin kisi ek particular object, jaise row, ka hone ke bajaye, yeh har us object ka hota hai jo ek search condition se match karta hai. Maan lo, lock un sabhi bookings ko cover karega jo is query se match karti hain:

SELECT * FROM bookings
WHERE room_id = 123 AND
end_time > '2018-01-01 12:00' AND
start_time < '2018-01-01 13:00';

Predicate lock access ko do tarah se restrict karta hai:

  • Agar transaction A ek condition se match karne wale objects read karna chahta hai, jaise us SELECT mein, toh use us condition par shared predicate lock acquire karna padega. Agar transaction B ke paas condition se match karne wale kisi bhi object par exclusive lock pehle se hai, toh A ko tab tak wait karna padega jab tak B use release na kar de.
  • Agar transaction A koi object insert, update ya delete karna chahta hai, toh use pehle check karna padega ki purani ya nayi value kisi existing predicate lock se match karti hai ya nahi. Agar transaction B ke paas matching predicate lock hai, toh A ko tab tak wait karna padega jab tak B commit ya abort na ho jaaye.

Key idea yeh hai ki predicate lock un objects par bhi lagta hai jo abhi exist hi nahi karte, lekin baad mein add ho sakte hain. Yahi phantoms hain. Agar 2PL mein predicate locks shaamil hain, toh database write skew ke saare forms aur doosri race conditions rok deta hai, isliye uska isolation sach mein serializable hota hai.

Index-range locks. Predicate locks achha perform nahi karte. Agar kai transactions locks hold kar rahe hon, toh yeh check karne mein bahut time lagta hai ki nayi write unmein se kisi se match karti hai ya nahi. Isliye 2PL use karne wale zyadatar databases index-range locks implement karte hain, jinhe next-key locking bhi kehte hain. Yeh predicate locking ka ek simplified approximation hai.

Predicate ko simplify karna safe hota hai, bas use objects ke bade set se match karwa do. Jaise room 123 ki noon se 1 p.m. ke beech ki bookings par predicate lock ko approximate kiya ja sakta hai room 123 ki kisi bhi time ki bookings lock karke. Ya phir noon se 1 p.m. ke beech saare rooms lock karke. Yeh safe hai, kyunki jo bhi write original predicate se match karti hai woh approximation se bhi match karegi.

Room booking database mein tumhare paas shayad room_id column par index hoga, aur shayad start_time aur end_time par bhi. Inke bina upar wali query bade database par bahut slow hogi. Ab do cases dekhte hain:

  • Agar index room_id par hai, aur database use room 123 ki existing bookings dhoondhne ke liye use karta hai, toh database us index entry par ek shared lock laga sakta hai. Isse yeh mark ho jaata hai ki ek transaction ne room 123 ki bookings search ki hain.
  • Agar database bookings dhoondhne ke liye time-based index use karta hai, toh woh us index ki values ki ek range par shared lock laga sakta hai. Isse yeh mark ho jaata hai ki ek transaction ne January 1, 2018 ko noon se 1 p.m. ke overlap wali bookings search ki hain.

Dono tarah se, search condition ka ek approximation kisi ek index se attach ho jaata hai. Agar koi aur transaction usi room ya overlapping time ki booking insert, update ya delete karna chahe, toh use index ka wahi hissa update karna padega. Use shared lock milega aur lock release hone tak wait karna padega. Isse phantoms aur write skew se effective protection milti hai. Index-range locks predicate locks se kam precise hote hain, aur strictly zaroori se bade range of objects ko lock kar sakte hain. Lekin unka overhead kaafi kam hota hai, isliye yeh ek achha compromise hain.

Agar koi suitable index nahi hai jahan range lock attach kiya ja sake, toh database poore table par shared lock par fall back kar sakta hai. Yeh safe fallback hai, lekin performance ke liye achha nahi hai, kyunki isse baaki saare transactions us table par write nahi kar paate.

Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI)

Is chapter mein concurrency control ki kaafi nirasha bhari tasveer dikhi hai. Two-phase locking serializability deta hai lekin performance kharab hai. Serial execution serializability deta hai lekin achha scale nahi karta. Weak isolation levels achha perform karte hain lekin lost updates, write skew aur phantoms jaisi race conditions allow karte hain. Kya serializable isolation aur achhi performance fundamentally ek doosre ke against hain?

Shayad nahi. Serializable snapshot isolation (SSI) naam ka ek algorithm kaafi promising hai. Yeh full serializability deta hai, lekin snapshot isolation ke mukable sirf chhoti si performance penalty ke saath. SSI kaafi naya hai. Ise pehli baar 2008 mein describe kiya gaya tha, aur yeh Michael Cahill ki PhD thesis ka subject tha. Aaj SSI single-node databases mein use hota hai, PostgreSQL mein version 9.1 se serializable level ke roop mein. Yeh distributed databases mein bhi use hota hai, aur FoundationDB ek similar algorithm use karta hai. SSI doosre concurrency control methods ke mukable young hai, isliye abhi practice mein khud ko prove kar raha hai. Lekin ho sakta hai yeh itna fast ho ki ek din default ban jaaye.

Pessimistic versus optimistic concurrency control. Two-phase locking ek pessimistic concurrency control method hai. Yeh maanta hai ki agar kuch bhi galat ho sakta hai, toh behtar hai ki situation safe hone tak wait kiya jaaye. Kisi aur transaction ka hold kiya hua lock is baat ka sign hai ki kuch galat ho sakta hai. Yeh multi-threaded programming mein data structures ko protect karne wale mutual exclusion jaisa hai. Serial execution pessimistic hai, extreme tak. Yeh aisa hai jaise har transaction ko uske poore chalne ke time ke liye poore database par, ya ek partition par, exclusive lock de diya jaaye. Design iski bharpai har transaction ko bahut fast bana kar karta hai, taaki lock sirf thodi der hold ho.

Iske ulta, serializable snapshot isolation ek optimistic concurrency control method hai. Jab kuch potentially dangerous hota hai, toh block hone ke bajaye transactions aage badhte rehte hain, is umeed mein ki sab theek ho jaayega. Jab transaction commit karna chahta hai, toh database check karta hai ki kuch bura hua ya nahi, yani isolation violate hua ya nahi. Agar hua, toh transaction abort ho jaata hai aur use retry karna padta hai. Sirf wahi transactions commit ho sakte hain jo serializably execute hue the.

Optimistic concurrency control ek purana idea hai, aur iske advantages aur disadvantages par kaafi time se debate hota raha hai. High contention mein, jahan kai transactions ek hi objects access karne ki koshish karte hain, yeh kharab perform karta hai, kyunki unmein se bahut saare abort karne padte hain. Agar system pehle se hi apni maximum throughput ke kareeb hai, toh retried transactions ka extra load performance aur kharab kar sakta hai. Lekin agar kaafi spare capacity hai, aur contention bahut zyada nahi hai, toh optimistic methods aam taur par pessimistic methods se behtar perform karte hain. Contention ko commutative atomic operations se bhi kam kiya ja sakta hai. Agar kai transactions ek counter increment karna chahte hain, toh increments ka order matter nahi karta, bas counter usi transaction mein read na ho. Isliye saare increments bina conflict ke apply ho sakte hain.

SSI snapshot isolation par bana hai. Transaction ke saare reads ek consistent snapshot se aate hain, jaisa pehle bataya tha. Purani optimistic techniques se yahi main difference hai. Snapshot isolation ke upar SSI ek algorithm add karta hai jo writes ke beech serialization conflicts detect karta hai, aur decide karta hai ki kaun se transactions abort karne hain.

Outdated premise par based decisions. Pehle hamne snapshot isolation mein ek baar-baar aane wala pattern dekha tha. Transaction kuch data read karta hai, result examine karta hai, aur jo dekha uske hisaab se koi action, yani write, lene ka decide karta hai. Lekin snapshot isolation mein, transaction ke commit hone tak original query ka result up to date nahi rehta, kyunki is beech data badal chuka ho sakta hai.

Doosre words mein, transaction ek premise par act kar raha hai, yani ek aisi fact par jo transaction shuru hote waqt sach thi. Jaise, “abhi do doctors on call hain.” Transaction ke commit hone tak shayad premise sach na rahe. Database ko pata nahi hota ki application query result ko kaise use karta hai. Safe rehne ke liye use maanna padta hai ki result mein koi bhi change ka matlab hai ki transaction ke writes invalid ho sakte hain. Yani queries aur writes ke beech ek causal dependency ho sakti hai. Serializable isolation dene ke liye database ko detect karna padta hai ki kab koi transaction outdated premise par act kar chuka ho sakta hai, aur phir us transaction ko abort karna padta hai.

Detect karne ke liye do cases hain. Pehla, stale MVCC version ka read, jahan ek uncommitted write read se pehle hua tha. Doosra, aisa write jo pichle read ko affect karta hai, jahan write read ke baad hota hai.

Stale MVCC reads detect karna. Yaad rakhein ki snapshot isolation aam taur par MVCC se implement hota hai. Jab transaction consistent snapshot se read karta hai, toh woh un doosre transactions ke writes ignore kar deta hai jo snapshot lete waqt tak commit nahi hue the. Book ka Figure 7-10 dikhata hai ki yeh kaise galat ho sakta hai.

Example
  1. Transaction 42 Alice ka on-call status change karta hai. Change abhi commit nahi hua hai.
  2. Transaction 43 shuru hota hai aur on-call doctors ki list read karta hai. 42 commit nahi hua hai, isliye 43 us write ko ignore kar deta hai. Use Alice abhi bhi on call dikhti hai, on_call = true ke saath.
  3. Transaction 42 commit ho jaata hai.
  4. Ab transaction 43 commit karna chahta hai. Jo write usne ignore kiya tha woh ab effect mein aa gaya hai. Uska premise, ki Alice on call hai, ab sach nahi hai, isliye use commit nahi karna chahiye.

Isse rokne ke liye database track karta hai ki transaction kab MVCC visibility rules ki wajah se doosre transaction ke writes ignore karta hai. Jab transaction commit karna chahta hai, toh database check karta hai ki unme se koi ignored write ab commit ho chuka hai ya nahi. Agar ho chuka hai, toh transaction abort karna padega.

Commit tak wait kyun karna? Stale read hote hi transaction 43 ko abort kyun nahi kar dete? Agar transaction 43 read-only hota, toh use abort karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti, kyunki write skew ka koi risk nahi hota. Jab transaction 43 apna read karta hai, tab database ko abhi pata nahi hota ki woh baad mein write karega ya nahi. Transaction 42 shayad abort bhi ho jaaye, ya 43 ke commit karne ki koshish karte waqt bhi uncommitted ho, aur tab read stale nikalta hi nahi. Unnecessary aborts avoid karke SSI snapshot isolation ka woh support bachaye rakhta hai jisme consistent snapshot se long-running reads ho sakte hain.

Pichle reads ko affect karne wale writes detect karna. Doosra case tab hota hai jab koi aur transaction data ke read hone ke baad use modify karta hai. Book ka Figure 7-11 yeh dikhata hai. Transactions 42 aur 43 dono shift 1234 ke dauran on-call doctors search karte hain. Two-phase locking mein is tarah ki search ke liye index-range locks the. SSI similar technique use karta hai, bas iske locks doosre transactions ko block nahi karte.

Agar shift_id par index hai, toh database shift 1234 ki index entry use karke record kar sakta hai ki transactions 42 aur 43 ne yeh data read kiya. Agar index nahi hai, toh database yeh information table level par track kar sakta hai. Yeh information sirf kuch der ke liye rakhni padti hai. Jab transaction aur uske saare concurrent transactions khatam ho jaate hain, toh database bhool sakta hai ki us transaction ne kya read kiya tha.

Jab transaction database mein write karta hai, toh woh indexes mein dekhta hai ki affected data ko haal hi mein kin doosre transactions ne read kiya hai. Yeh affected key range par write lock acquire karne jaisa hai. Lekin readers ke commit hone tak block karne ke bajaye, lock ek tripwire ki tarah kaam karta hai. Yeh transactions ko batata hai ki jo data unhone read kiya tha woh ab up to date nahi ho sakta.

Example
  1. Transactions 42 aur 43 dono shift 1234 ke on-call doctors read karte hain.
  2. Transaction 43 us shift mein ek change write karta hai. Tripwire transaction 42 ko batata hai ki uska pehle ka read outdated hai, aur 43 ko 42 ke write ke baare mein yahi batata hai.
  3. Transaction 42 pehle commit karta hai, aur successful hota hai. 43 ke write ne 42 ke read ko affect kiya, phir bhi 43 ne commit nahi kiya hai, isliye uska write abhi effect mein nahi aaya.
  4. Jab transaction 43 commit karne ki koshish karta hai, toh 42 ka conflicting write pehle hi commit ho chuka hota hai. Isliye 43 ko abort karna padta hai.

Serializable snapshot isolation ki performance. Hamesha ki tarah, kai engineering details tay karte hain ki algorithm practice mein kitna achha kaam karega. Ek trade-off yeh hai ki database reads aur writes ko kitni granularity par track karta hai. Agar woh har transaction ki activity ko bahut detail mein track kare, toh woh precise ho sakta hai ki kaun se transactions abort karne hain. Lekin yeh bookkeeping mehngi ho sakti hai. Coarser tracking tez hoti hai, lekin strictly zaroori se zyada aborts ho sakte hain.

Kabhi-kabhi transaction aisi information safely read kar sakta hai jise doosre transaction ne overwrite kar diya ho. Aur kya hua uske hisaab se, yeh prove karna possible ho sakta hai ki result phir bhi serializable hai. PostgreSQL unnecessary aborts kam karne ke liye isi tarah ka reasoning use karta hai.

Two-phase locking ke mukable SSI ka bada advantage yeh hai ki kisi transaction ko doosre ke hold kiye lock ka wait karke block nahi hona padta. Snapshot isolation ki tarah, writers readers ko block nahi karte, aur readers writers ko block nahi karte. Isse query latency zyada predictable aur kam variable ho jaati hai. Read-only queries bina kisi lock ke consistent snapshot par chal sakti hain, jo read-heavy workloads ke liye bahut attractive hai.

Serial execution ke mukable SSI ek CPU core ki throughput tak limited nahi hai. FoundationDB serialization conflicts ki detection ko kai machines mein faila deta hai, isliye woh bahut high throughput tak scale kar sakta hai. Data machines mein split hone par bhi, transactions kai partitions read aur write kar sakte hain aur phir bhi serializable isolation paa sakte hain.

Aborts ki rate SSI ki overall performance par bada asar daalti hai. Jo transaction lambe time tak data read aur write karta hai, usme conflicts aur abort hone ke chances zyada hote hain. Isliye SSI ko read-write transactions kaafi short chahiye, halanki long-running read-only transactions chal sakte hain. Phir bhi, SSI shayad two-phase locking ya serial execution se slow transactions ke prati kam sensitive hai.

Trade-offs
ApproachGood atCosts
Actual serial executionDesign se hi serializable, conflict detection ki zaroorat nahi. Data memory mein fit ho aur transactions short hon, toh fast.Har partition par ek CPU core tak limited. Interactive transactions nahi. Ek slow transaction sab kuch rok deta hai. Cross-partition kaam slow.
Two-phase locking (2PL)Har race condition ke against strong guarantee. Iske peeche decades ka experience.Readers aur writers ek doosre ko block karte hain. Contention mein latency unstable. Deadlocks zyada, aur retries kaam barbaad karte hain.
Serializable snapshot isolation (SSI)Readers kabhi block nahi hote. Latency predictable. Read-only queries ko locks nahi chahiye. Snapshot isolation par sirf chhoti si penalty.Kuch transactions abort hote hain aur retry karne padte hain. Read-write transactions short rakhne padte hain. Reads aur writes track karne ki extra bookkeeping.
Asli idea

Sirf serializable isolation is chapter ki har race condition se bachata hai. Weaker levels faster hain, lekin har ek kuch race conditions application ke bharose chhod deta hai.

Summary

Short mein
  • Transactions application ko reads aur writes ke group ko ek unit ki tarah treat karne dete hain. Agar unit fail ho jaaye, toh woh abort ho jaata hai, aur application retry kar sakta hai. Kai concurrency aur fault problems ek simple abort mein simat jaati hain.
  • Atomicity ka matlab all-or-nothing: aborted transaction ke writes discard ho jaate hain. Isolation ka matlab concurrent transactions ek doosre mein interfere nahi karte. Durability ka matlab committed data bhoola nahi jaata. Consistency application ki zimmedaari hai, uske apne rules ke hisaab se.
  • Dirty reads, jahan ek client doosre client ke uncommitted writes dekhta hai, aur dirty writes, jahan ek client doosre ka uncommitted data overwrite karta hai, read committed aur stronger levels se prevent hote hain.
  • Read skew, jahan client database ke alag-alag hisse alag-alag time par dekhta hai, aam taur par snapshot isolation se prevent hota hai. Ise aam taur par MVCC se banaya jaata hai.
  • Lost updates, jahan do read-modify-write cycles ek doosre ko overwrite kar dete hain, atomic operations, explicit locks, kuch systems mein automatic detection, ya compare-and-set se prevent hote hain. Replicated systems ko iske bajaye merge-friendly approaches chahiye.
  • Write skew, jahan decision ek aise premise par based hai jise doosre transaction ne galat bana diya, sirf serializable isolation se, ya careful explicit locking se prevent hota hai.
  • Phantom reads, jahan koi write doosre transaction ki search ka result badal deta hai, read-only queries ke liye snapshot isolation se block hote hain. Jo phantoms write skew karte hain, unke liye index-range locks, materialized conflicts, ya serializable isolation chahiye.
  • Serializability paane ke teen tarike hain: actual serial execution, two-phase locking, aur serializable snapshot isolation. Har ek speed, scaling aur aborts ke beech alag trade-off karta hai.

Transactions ek abstraction layer hain. Yeh application ko aisa maanne dete hain jaise kuch concurrency problems, aur kuch hardware aur software faults, exist hi nahi karte. Errors ki ek badi class ek simple transaction abort mein simat jaati hai, aur application ko bas dobara try karna hota hai.

Har application in saari problems se affected nahi hota. Jis application ke access patterns bahut simple hon, jaise ek single record read aur write karna, woh shayad transactions ke bina chal jaaye. Lekin zyada complex access patterns ke liye transactions un error cases ki count bahut kam kar dete hain jinke baare mein tumhe sochna padta hai. Transactions ke bina process crashes, network interruptions, power outages, full disks, aur unexpected concurrency jaise errors data ko kai tarah se inconsistent chhod sakte hain. Denormalized data aasaani se apne source se out of sync ho sakta hai. Transactions ke bina yeh reason karna bahut mushkil ho jaata hai ki kai interacting accesses ka database par kya asar ho sakta hai.

Is chapter mein Kleppmann concurrency control mein kaafi gehre gaye. Unhone kai widely used isolation levels discuss kiye, khaaskar read committed, snapshot isolation (jise kabhi-kabhi repeatable read kehte hain), aur serializable. Har ek ko unhone is tarah describe kiya ki woh kaun si race conditions allow karta hai aur kaun si block karta hai, aur yeh bhi bataya ki alag databases ke use kiye naam hamesha match nahi karte. Distributed databases mein transactions naye hard challenges lekar aate hain, jinhe agle do chapters mein dekhenge.

Khud check karo

  1. Do clients ek counter read karte hain jisme 42 hai, aur phir dono 43 write karte hain. Counter 44 ke bajaye 43 par kyun khatam hota hai? Kya sirf read committed isolation ise rok deta?

    Jawab dekho

    Dono clients ne kisi ke bhi write karne se pehle read kiya, isliye second write ne pehle write ko same value se replace kar diya, aur ek increment lost ho gaya. Read committed ise nahi rokta, kyunki second write pehle transaction ke commit hone ke baad hota hai, isliye woh dirty write nahi hai. Fixes mein atomic increment, explicit lock, automatic lost update detection, ya compare-and-set shaamil hain.

  2. Snapshot isolation mein transaction 12 transaction 13 ke commit hone se pehle shuru hota hai. Transaction 13 account 2 ko $500 se $400 kar deta hai. Transaction 12 ko kaunsa balance dikhega, aur kyun?

    Jawab dekho

    Use $500 dikhega. Transaction 13 ne $400 wala version banaya, jo 12 nahi dekh sakta. Usne $500 wale version ko deleted mark bhi kiya, lekin woh deletion 12 ko invisible hai kyunki 12 ke shuru hote waqt 13 ne commit nahi kiya tha.

  3. Ek booking transaction SELECT chalakar kisi room ki overlapping bookings dhoondhta hai, koi nahi milti, aur phir booking insert kar deta hai. SELECT FOR UPDATE is race ko kyun fix nahi kar sakta?

    Jawab dekho

    SELECT koi row return nahi karta, isliye lock karne ke liye kuch hai hi nahi. Doosre transaction ka concurrent insert ek phantom hai, kyunki yeh search ka result badal deta hai. Fixes hain conflicts ko lock rows mein materialize karna, index-range locks use karna, ya serializable isolation use karna.

  4. Serializable snapshot isolation stale read hote hi abort karne ke bajaye commit time par stale reads kyun check karta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Jab read hota hai, tab database ko pata nahi hota ki transaction baad mein write karega ya nahi. Read-only transaction ko abort karne ki zaroorat nahi, kyunki woh write skew nahi kar sakta. Jis writer ko read ne ignore kiya tha, woh abort bhi ho sakta hai, jisse read aakhir mein valid ho jaata. Commit tak wait karne se unnecessary aborts bachte hain.

Part II · Chapter 8

Distributed systems ki mushkilein

Seedhi baat: jab ek program network se jude kai machines par chalta hai, toh kuch hisse fail ho sakte hain aur baaki chalte rahte hain. Messages lost ya delay ho sakte hain, clocks galat ho sakte hain, aur ek process bahut der ke liye freeze ho sakta hai, bina ise jaane. Har machine ko doosri machines ke baare mein andaaze par kaam karna padta hai, isliye software aisa banana padta hai jo andaaze galat nikalne par bhi correct rahe.

Pichhle chapters mein ek tarah se kaafi narmi thi. Wahan hamne dekha ki leader mar jaaye toh replica uski jagah le leta hai, replication lag kya hota hai, aur isolation levels concurrent writes ko kaise handle karte hain. In sab mein kuch na kuch galat hota hi hai. Lekin Kleppmann ke hisaab se pichhle kuch chapters tab bhi kaafi optimistic the. Is chapter mein pessimism ko maximum par le jaate hain aur maan lete hain ki jo kuch galat ho sakta hai, woh hoga. Experienced operators kehte hain ki yeh assumption bilkul reasonable hai, aur kuch ke paas purani ladaaiyon ki dara dene wali kahaniyaan bhi hain.

Distributed system (alag-alag computers jo network se jude hain aur milkar kaam karte hain) par kaam karna ek single computer ke liye software likhne se bilkul alag hai. Sabse bada fark yeh hai ki cheezein galat hone ke bahut saare naye tarike aa jaate hain. Yeh chapter dikhata hai ki practice mein kaun si problems aati hain, aur hum kis cheez par bharosa kar sakte hain aur kis par nahi.

Scope ke baare mein ek baat. Book maanti hai ki faults non-Byzantine hain, matlab machines intentionally jhooth nahi bolti. Byzantine faults ka section chapter mein aage hai, wahan samjhaya gaya hai ki iska kya matlab hai aur book ise side mein kyun rakhti hai.

Engineer ka kaam phir bhi yahi hai ki aise systems banaye jo apna kaam karein, yani users ki expected guarantees poori karein, chahe sab kuch galat ho raha ho. Chapter 9 un algorithms ko dekhta hai jo aisi guarantees de sakte hain. Yeh chapter pehle challenges samjhata hai. Isme networks ki problems, clocks aur timing ki problems, aur har ek ko kitna avoid kiya ja sakta hai, yeh sab aata hai. Phir sawaal uthta hai ki ek node poore system ki state ke baare mein kaise soche, aur jo cheezein ho chuki hain unke baare mein kaise reason kare, jab use pakka pata hi nahi ki kya hua hai.

Faults aur partial failures

Jab tum ek single computer par program likhte ho, toh woh aam taur par predictable tarike se behave karta hai. Ya toh kaam karta hai, ya nahi karta. Buggy software se lag sakta hai ki computer ka din kharab chal raha hai, aur reboot se theek bhi ho sakta hai, lekin wajah lagbhag hamesha kharab software hoti hai, machine nahi.

Ek computer ke flaky hone ki koi basic wajah nahi hai. Hardware sahi chal raha ho, toh same operation har baar same result deta hai. Book ise deterministic kehti hai. Agar hardware toot jaaye, jaise memory corruption ya loose connector, toh aam result total failure hota hai: kernel panic, crash screen, ya aisi machine jo start hi nahi hoti. Achhe software wala single computer ya toh poori tarah kaam kar raha hota hai ya toot chuka hota hai. Beech ki halat kam hi milti hai.

Yeh ek soch-samajh kar liya gaya design choice hai. Agar andar koi fault ho jaaye, toh computers ko is tarah banaya jaata hai ki woh poori tarah crash ho jaayein, galat answer return na karein, kyunki galat answers se deal karna mushkil aur confusing hota hai. Isliye computer neeche ki messy physical reality ko chhupa deta hai aur ek idealized model dikhata hai jo mathematical precision se behave karta hai. CPU instruction hamesha wahi karti hai. Memory ya disk mein likha data intact rehta hai. Kleppmann batate hain ki hamesha-correct computation ka yeh goal bilkul pehle digital computers se chala aa raha hai.

Distributed system alag hota hai. Jaise hi software network se jude kai computers par chalta hai, hum us idealized model mein kaam nahi kar rahe hote. Humein messy physical duniya ka saamna karna padta hai, jahan bahut kuch galat ho sakta hai. Book is range of failures ko Coda Hale naam ke ek operator ke kisse se dikhati hai. Apne limited experience mein unhone ek data center ke andar lambe chalne wale network partitions dekhe the, racks ko power dene wali power distribution units ke failures, switch failures, galti se power-cycle ho gaye racks, poore data center ke network aur power failures, aur ek driver jisne apna pickup truck data center ke air conditioning system mein thok diya. Unka kehna tha ki woh toh ops ke aadmi bhi nahi the.

Distributed system mein kuch hisse unpredictable tarike se toote ho sakte hain aur baaki theek chalte hain. Ise partial failure kehte hain. Mushkil yeh hai ki partial failures nondeterministic hote hain, matlab har baar same tarike se nahi hote. Tum kuch bhi aisa karo jisme kai nodes aur network shaamil hon, toh woh kabhi chalega aur kabhi aise tarike se fail hoga jo tum predict nahi kar sakte. Tumhe yeh tak pata nahi chalega ki kaam succeed hua ya nahi, kyunki message ko network cross karne mein lagne wala time bhi unpredictable hota hai. Book ke hisaab se yahi nondeterminism aur partial failures ki possibility distributed systems par kaam karna mushkil banati hai.

Cloud computing aur supercomputing

Logon ne bade computing systems kai alag tarikon se banaye hain, aur har philosophy faults ko alag tarike se handle karti hai. Book ek spectrum batati hai:

  • High-performance computing (HPC) ek end par hai. Hazaron CPUs wale supercomputers bhaari scientific jobs chalate hain, jaise weather forecasting ya molecular dynamics, jisme simulate kiya jaata hai ki atoms aur molecules kaise move karte hain.
  • Cloud computing doosre end par hai. Is term ki definition kaafi clear nahi hai, lekin aam taur par iska matlab hota hai multi-tenant data centers (kai customers same facilities share karte hain), commodity computers (aam, sasti machines) jo IP network se jude hain, aksar Ethernet, resources on demand milna, aur metered billing.
  • Traditional enterprise data centers beech mein kahin aate hain.

Supercomputer faults ko ek khaas tarike se handle karta hai. Job time-time par durable storage (jo crash ke baad bhi bachi rehti hai) mein ek checkpoint, yani apni state ka snapshot, save karti hai. Agar ek node fail ho jaaye, toh aam solution hai poore cluster ka kaam rok dena. Faulty node repair hone ke baad computation last checkpoint se dobara start hota hai. Matlab supercomputer distributed system se zyada ek single computer jaisa behave karta hai. Partial failure ko total failure mein badalne diya jaata hai. Koi bhi hissa toot jaaye toh sab kuch ruk jaata hai, bilkul jaise kernel panic single machine ko rok deta hai.

Book ka focus internet services ke systems par hai, jo supercomputers se kaafi alag dikhte hain. Farq yeh hain:

  • Bahut saari internet services online hoti hain. Unhe kisi bhi waqt low latency (kam delay) ke saath users ko serve karna hota hai. Repair ke liye poora cluster rok dena acceptable nahi hai. Offline batch jobs, jaise weather simulations, ko rok kar dobara chalaya ja sakta hai aur impact kaafi kam hota hai.
  • Supercomputers specialized hardware use karte hain, jahan har node kaafi reliable hota hai. Nodes shared memory aur remote direct memory access (RDMA, ek machine ka doosri machine ki memory ko seedha read karne ka tarika) se baat karte hain. Cloud nodes commodity machines hote hain. Economies of scale ki wajah se woh kam cost mein similar performance de sakte hain, lekin zyada fail hote hain.
  • Bade datacenter networks aam taur par IP aur Ethernet par bante hain, Clos topologies mein arranged, yani aise designs jo high bisection bandwidth dete hain (network ke do aadhe hisson ke beech bahut saari capacity). Supercomputers aksar specialized layouts use karte hain, jaise meshes aur toruses, jo unki jobs ke known communication patterns ke liye fit baithte hain.
  • System jitna bada hota hai, usme kuch na kuch toota hone ki possibility utni badhti hai. Waqt ke saath toote hue cheezein theek hoti hain aur nayi toot jaati hain. Hazaron nodes ke saath yeh maan lena reasonable hai ki kuch na kuch hamesha toota rehta hai. Agar error strategy bas haar maan lena hai, toh bada system apna zyada time faults se recover karne mein laga dega, kaam ka kaam karne mein nahi.
  • Agar system nodes fail hone par bhi chalta rahe, toh operations aasaan ho jaate hain. Tum rolling upgrade (Chapter 4) kar sakte ho, ek-ek node restart karte hue, jabki service users ko serve karti rehti hai. Cloud mein agar ek virtual machine slow hai, toh use kill karke nayi maang sakte hain, is umeed mein ki nayi tez hogi.
  • Geographically distributed deployment data ko users ke paas rakhta hai taaki latency kam ho. Tab communication aam taur par internet par hoti hai, jo local network se slow aur kam reliable hai. Supercomputers maante hain ki unke nodes paas-paas hain.

Toh agar distributed systems ko kaam karwana hai, toh maanna padega ki partial failure ho sakta hai, aur software mein fault tolerance banani padegi. Yani unreliable parts se ek reliable system banana hoga. Kleppmann yaad dilate hain ki perfect reliability jaisi koi cheez hoti hi nahi, isliye humein samajhna hoga ki realistically hum kya promise kar sakte hain aur uski limits kya hain.

Partial failure chhote system mein bhi matter karta hai, jisme sirf kuch nodes hon. Chhote system mein zyadatar parts shayad zyadatar time sahi chal rahe hote hain. Lekin der-saver koi na koi part faulty hoga hi, aur software ko use handle karna padega. Fault handling software ke design ka hissa honi chahiye. Jo log software operate karte hain, unhe bhi pata hona chahiye ki fault hone par kaisa behavior expect karein.

Yeh maan lena ki faults kam hote hain aur bas umeed rakhna, samajhdaari nahi hai. Tumhe faults ki ek wide range sochni chahiye, kaafi unlikely wale bhi, aur apne test environment mein intentionally wahi situations banakar dekhna chahiye ki kya hota hai. Book is attitude ko aise summarize karti hai: distributed systems mein suspicion, pessimism aur paranoia kaam aate hain.

Unreliable components se reliable system banana

Tum soch sakte ho ki system utna hi reliable ho sakta hai jitna uska sabse kamzor part. Yeh andaaza galat hai. Computing mein kam reliable parts se zyada reliable system banana ek purana idea hai. Book ke do examples:

  • Error-correcting codes digital data ko aise channel se guzarne dete hain jo kabhi-kabhi bits galat kar deta hai, jaise radio interference wala wireless network. Data ke saath bheje gaye extra bits receiver ko chhoti errors theek karne dete hain.
  • IP, yani Internet Protocol, unreliable hai. Woh packets (data ke chhote chunks) drop, delay, duplicate ya reorder kar sakta hai. TCP, yani Transmission Control Protocol, IP ke upar chalta hai aur ek zyada reliable transport deta hai. Woh missing packets dobara bhejta hai, duplicates hata deta hai, aur packets ko usi order mein jodta hai jisme bheje gaye the.

Phir bhi ek limit hai. Error-correcting codes kuch single-bit errors handle kar sakte hain, lekin agar interference signal par haavi ho jaaye, toh kitna data pass ho sakta hai us par hard limit hoti hai. TCP application se packet loss, duplication aur reordering chhupa sakta hai, lekin network ke delays hata nahi sakta.

Ek zyada reliable higher layer perfect na hone par bhi kaam ki hoti hai. Woh kuch tricky low-level faults sambhal leti hai, isliye jo faults bachte hain unke baare mein sochna aur unhe handle karna aam taur par aasaan hota hai. Book is idea par aage end-to-end argument ki discussion mein wapas aati hai.

Unreliable networks

Jin distributed systems par book focus karti hai woh shared-nothing systems hain. Matlab network se jude machines ka ek group. Network hi ek zariya hai jisse machines ek doosre se baat kar sakti hain. Har machine ki apni memory aur disk hoti hai, aur ek machine doosri machine ki memory ya disk read nahi kar sakti. Woh bas network par request bhejkar kuch maang sakti hai.

Shared-nothing system banane ka ekmaatra tarika nahi hai, lekin internet services ke liye yeh main approach ban gaya hai. Yeh relatively sasta hai kyunki special hardware nahi chahiye. Yeh commodity cloud services par chal sakta hai. Aur kai geographically distributed data centers mein copies faila kar high reliability bhi mil sakti hai.

Internet aur zyadatar internal data center networks (aksar Ethernet) asynchronous packet networks hain. Ek node doosre ko message, yani packet, bhej sakta hai. Lekin network yeh promise nahi karta ki packet kab pahunchega, ya pahunchega bhi ya nahi. Tum request bhejo aur response ki umeed rakho, toh bahut kuch galat ho sakta hai. Book chhe cheezein ginati hai:

  1. Tumhari request lost ho gayi ho sakti hai. Shayad kisi ne network cable nikaal di.
  2. Tumhari request kisi queue mein wait kar rahi ho sakti hai aur baad mein deliver hogi. Shayad network ya recipient overloaded hai.
  3. Remote node fail ho gaya ho sakta hai. Shayad crash hua ya power down ho gaya.
  4. Remote node kuch der ke liye respond karna band kar sakta hai, jaise ek lambe garbage collection pause mein (jab language runtime program ko rok kar memory saaf karta hai). Woh baad mein phir respond karne lagega.
  5. Remote node ne tumhari request process kar li ho, lekin response network par lost ho gaya. Shayad kisi switch ka configuration galat tha.
  6. Remote node ne tumhari request process kar li ho, lekin response delay ho gaya hai aur baad mein pahunchega. Shayad network ya tumhari apni machine overloaded hai.

Book ka Figure 8-1 in possibilities ko dikhata hai. Key point yeh hai ki sending side se tum inhe alag-alag pehchaan nahi sakte. Response na aaye toh tumhe pata nahi chal sakta ki request lost hui, remote node down hai, ya response lost hua.

Example

Book jo situation batati hai use step by step dekhte hain. Ek client server ko request bhejta hai. Server use receive karta hai aur kaam kar deta hai, jaise database mein ek record likhna. Phir server response wapas bhejta hai, lekin response network par lost ho jaata hai. Client wait karta hai. Koi reply nahi aata. Client ka timeout fire hota hai aur woh haar maan leta hai. Ab client ko decide karna hai ki kya kare. Use nahi pata ki write hua ya nahi. Agar retry karta hai, toh write do baar ho sakta hai. Agar retry nahi karta, toh ho sakta hai write kabhi hua hi na ho. Sirf messages se client ke paas pata lagane ka koi tarika nahi hai.

Sender ko yeh tak nahi pata chal sakta ki uska packet deliver hua ya nahi. Pata lagane ka ekmaatra tarika yeh hai ki recipient response bheje, aur woh response bhi lost ya delay ho sakta hai. Asynchronous network mein yeh sab cases ek jaise dikhte hain. Bas itna pata hota hai ki abhi tak koi response nahi aaya. Request bhejne ke baad reply na mile, toh wajah batana impossible hai.

Ise handle karne ka aam tarika timeout hai. Tum ek tay time tak wait karte ho, phir haar maan lete ho aur maan lete ho ki response nahi aayega. Lekin timeout se sawaal ka jawab nahi milta. Tumhe ab bhi nahi pata ki remote node ko tumhari request mili ya nahi. Aur agar request abhi bhi kisi queue mein pasi hai, toh tumhare haar maan lene ke baad bhi woh baad mein recipient tak pahunch sakti hai.

Practice mein network faults

Logon ne computer networks dashakon se banaye hain, aur tum soch sakte ho ki ab tak woh reliable ho gaye honge. Book kehti hai ki abhi tak hum ye nahi kar paye. Systematic studies aur bahut saare kisson se pata chalta hai ki network problems hairaan karne wali had tak common hain, ek hi company ke data center mein bhi. Ek medium-sized data center ki study mein mahine mein lagbhag 12 network faults mile. Inme se aadhe ek single machine ko disconnect karte the, aur aadhe poore rack ko. Ek aur study ne top-of-rack switches, aggregation switches aur load balancers ke failure rates naape. Usme mila ki redundant networking gear jodne se faults utne kam nahi hote jitni umeed hoti hai, kyunki redundancy human error se nahi bachati, jaise galat configured switch. Human error outages ki ek badi wajah hai.

Amazon EC2 jaisi public cloud services baar-baar aane wale chhote network glitches ke liye jaani jaati hain. Achhe se chalaye jaane wale private data center networks zyada stable ho sakte hain. Lekin koi bhi poori tarah safe nahi hai. Ek case mein, switch ke software upgrade ke dauraan ek problem se network topology reconfiguration trigger hua, aur packets ek minute se zyada delay hue. Sharks ke undersea cables kaatne ki reports bhi hain. Ek aur ajeeb fault yeh hai ki network interface kabhi-kabhi saare incoming packets drop kar deta hai, jabki outgoing packets bhejta rehta hai. Ek direction mein chalne wala link is baat ki guarantee nahi hai ki doosri direction bhi chal rahi hai.

Dhyaan do

Network partition, jise netsplit bhi kehte hain, tab hota hai jab network ka ek hissa baaki se kat jaata hai. Book zyadatar isse broad term network fault use karti hai, taaki storage system ke partitions, yani shards, se confusion na ho, jo Chapter 6 mein aaye the.

Tumhare yahan network faults kam bhi hon, tab bhi tumhare software ko unhe handle karna hoga, kyunki network par hone wali koi bhi communication fail ho sakti hai. Iska koi bypass nahi hai. Agar network faults ki error handling define aur test nahi ki gayi, toh lagbhag kuch bhi ho sakta hai. Book do examples deti hai. Cluster deadlock ho sakta hai aur network recover hone ke baad bhi requests serve nahi kar paata. Ya system tumhara poora data delete bhi kar sakta hai. Agar software aisi situation mein pahunch jaaye jiski kisi ne ummeed nahi ki thi, toh woh arbitrary cheezein kar sakta hai.

Network faults handle karne ka matlab hamesha yeh nahi hota ki unhe bina kisi visible effect ke tolerate kiya jaaye. Agar tumhara network aam taur par reliable hai, toh ek sensible choice yeh ho sakta hai ki network mein problem ke dauraan users ko error message dikha diya jaaye. Lekin tumhe phir bhi pata hona chahiye ki tumhara software network trouble par kaise react karta hai, aur yeh pakka karna chahiye ki woh recover kar sake. Intentionally network problems trigger karke dekhna ki system kaise respond karta hai, yeh bhi sahi ho sakta hai. Chaos Monkey ka yahi idea hai, jiska zikr book ne Chapter 1 mein reliability ki discussion mein kiya tha.

Faults detect karna

Bahut saare systems ko faulty nodes automatically detect karne hote hain. Load balancer ko dead node ko rotation se nikaal kar usse requests bhejna band karna padta hai. Single-leader replication wale database mein agar leader fail ho jaaye, toh ek follower ko naya leader promote karna padta hai. Lekin network ki uncertainty ki wajah se yeh batana mushkil hota hai ki node chal raha hai ya nahi. Kuch specific cases mein tumhe explicit feedback mil sakta hai ki kuch galat hai:

  • Agar tum us machine tak pahunch sakte ho jahan node chalna chahiye, lekin port par koi process listen nahi kar raha, toh operating system aam taur par connection jaldi refuse kar deta hai. Woh TCP RST ya FIN packet se reply karta hai. Lekin agar node tumhari request handle karte waqt crash hua, toh tumhare paas ab bhi jaanne ka tarika nahi ki usne kitna kaam finish kiya.
  • Agar node ka process crash ho gaya ya administrator ne use kill kar diya, lekin machine ka operating system abhi bhi chal raha hai, toh ek script baaki nodes ko crash ke baare mein bata sakti hai. Phir doosra node timeout ka wait kiye bina kaam sambhal sakta hai. Book ke hisaab se HBase aisa karta hai.
  • Agar tum apne data center ke network switches ka management interface dekh sakte ho, toh hardware level ke link failures ke baare mein unse pooch sakte ho, jaise koi machine power down ho gayi ho. Yeh internet par possible nahi hai, ya aise shared data center mein jahan switches tak tumhari pahunch nahi, ya jab network problem ki wajah se management interface hi unreachable ho.
  • Agar router ko pakka pata hai ki jis address tak tum pahunchna chahte ho woh unreachable hai, toh woh ICMP Destination Unreachable message se reply kar sakta hai. Lekin router ke paas bhi failures detect karne ka koi jaadui tarika nahi hai. Us par bhi network ki baaki cheezon jaisi hi limits lagti hain.

Remote node down hone ki fast feedback kaam ki hoti hai, lekin us par bharosa nahi kar sakte. TCP acknowledge kar sakta hai ki packet deliver ho gaya, lekin application us packet ko handle karne se pehle hi crash ho sakti hai. Agar tumhe pakka karna hai ki request succeed hui, toh application se hi positive response chahiye.

Ulta bhi sach hai. Kuch galat ho toh stack ki kisi layer se tumhe error response mil sakta hai. Lekin aam taur par maan kar chalna chahiye ki koi response nahi milega. Tum kuch baar retry kar sakte ho (TCP khud retry karta hai, lekin tum application level par bhi retry kar sakte ho), timeout poora hone ka wait kar sakte ho, aur agar tab bhi jawab na mile toh node ko dead declare kar sakte ho.

Timeouts aur unbounded delays

Agar timeout hi fault detect karne ka ekmaatra pakka tarika hai, toh woh kitna lamba hona chahiye? Kleppmann ke hisaab se koi simple jawab nahi hai.

Lamba timeout matlab node ko dead declare karne se pehle lamba wait. Is dauraan users ko wait karna pad sakta hai ya error messages dikh sakte hain. Chhota timeout faults jaldi detect karta hai, lekin node ko galti se dead declare karne ka risk badh jaata hai jabki usme sirf temporary slowdown aaya ho, jaise node ya network par load spike.

Node ko bahut jaldi dead declare karna ek asli problem hai. Maan lo node actually zinda hai aur koi action kar raha hai, jaise email bhejna. Doosra node uska kaam sambhal leta hai, aur phir pehla node apna kaam khatam kar deta hai. Action do baar ho sakta hai. Book is issue par chapter mein aage knowledge aur truth ki discussion mein, aur Chapters 9 aur 11 mein wapas aati hai.

Jab node dead declare hota hai, toh uski responsibilities doosre nodes par chali jaati hain. Isse doosre nodes aur network par load badhta hai. Agar system pehle se hi high load mein struggle kar raha hai, toh nodes ko bahut jaldi dead declare karne se halat aur kharab ho sakti hai. Jo node dead nahi tha, bas overload ki wajah se slow tha, uska kaam doosron ko chala jaata hai, aur isse woh bhi overload ho sakte hain. Ise cascading failure kehte hain. Extreme case mein har node har doosre node ko dead declare kar deta hai, aur sab kuch kaam karna band kar deta hai.

Example

Book ek kaalpanik system sochti hai jo strong guarantees deta hai, taaki dikha sake ki achha timeout kaisa dikhega. Maan lo network har packet ke liye ek maximum delay guarantee karta hai, jise d kehte hain. Har packet ya toh time d ke andar pahunchta hai, ya lost ho jaata hai, aur delivery kabhi d se zyada nahi leti. Ab maan lo ki jo node fail nahi hua, woh hamesha kisi time r ke andar request handle kar leta hai. Tab tum guarantee kar sakte ho ki har successful request ko time 2d + r ke andar response mil jaayega. Request ko pahunchne mein zyada se zyada d lagta hai, handling mein zyada se zyada r, aur reply ko wapas aane mein zyada se zyada d. Agar 2d + r ke andar response na aaye, toh tumhe pata chal jaata hai ki ya toh network ya remote node kaam nahi kar raha. Us kaalpanik system mein 2d + r ek reasonable timeout hota.

Real systems mein na yeh guarantee hai, na woh. Asynchronous networks mein unbounded delays hote hain. Woh packets jitni jaldi ho sake deliver karne ki koshish karte hain, lekin packet ko kitna time lag sakta hai us par koi upper limit nahi hai. Aur zyadatar server software yeh promise nahi kar sakta ki woh request ko kisi maximum time ke andar handle kar dega. Failure detection ke liye itna kaafi nahi hai ki system zyadatar time fast ho. Agar tumhara timeout chhota hai, toh round-trip times mein ek chhota sa spike poore system ko hila sakta hai.

Network congestion aur queueing

Gaadi chalate waqt road network par travel time sabse zyada traffic jams ki wajah se badalta hai. Computer networks mein packet delays ka variation zyadatar queueing, yani line mein wait karne, se hota hai. Chaar main jagahein hain jahan packets wait karte hain:

  • Network switches. Agar kai nodes ek saath same destination ko packets bhejein, toh switch ko unhe queue karna padta hai aur ek-ek karke destination link mein daalna padta hai. Busy link par packet ko apni baari ke liye kuch der wait karna pad sakta hai. Ise network congestion kehte hain. Agar itna data aa jaaye ki switch ki queue bhar jaaye, toh packets drop ho jaate hain aur dobara bhejne padte hain, jabki network khud theek chal raha hota hai.
  • Receiving machine. Jab packet destination machine par pahunchta hai aur uske saare CPU cores busy hain, toh operating system incoming request ko queue kar deta hai jab tak application use handle karne ke liye ready na ho. Load ke hisaab se yeh wait kitna bhi lamba ho sakta hai.
  • Virtual machines. Virtualized environment mein chalta hua operating system kuch dus milliseconds ke liye pause ho sakta hai jabki doosri virtual machine CPU core use kar rahi hoti hai. Is dauraan paused VM incoming data read nahi kar sakti, isliye virtual machine monitor use buffer kar leta hai. Isse network delays mein aur variation aa jaata hai.
  • TCP flow control. TCP yeh bhi limit karta hai ki node kitni tezi se bheje, taaki network link ya receiver overload na ho. Ise congestion avoidance ya backpressure bhi kehte hain. Matlab data sender par hi queue ho sakta hai, network mein enter karne se pehle hi.

Book ka Figure 8-2 switch wala case dikhata hai. Ports 1, 2 aur 4 sab port 3 ko packets bhejne ki koshish kar rahe hain, isliye port 3 ki switch queue bhar sakti hai.

TCP yeh bhi khud decide karta hai ki packet kab lost hua. Agar packet ka acknowledgement timeout ke andar nahi aaya, jise TCP dekhe hue round-trip times se calculate karta hai, toh packet ko lost maan kar automatically dobara bheja jaata hai. Application ko loss ya resend kabhi dikhta nahi. Use delay dikhta hai, jisme timeout ka wait aur phir retransmitted packet ke acknowledge hone ka wait shaamil hai.

TCP versus UDP

Kuch latency-sensitive applications, jaise video calls aur Voice over IP (VoIP), TCP ki jagah UDP use karti hain. UDP ek simpler protocol hai jo TCP ki guarantees ke bina packets bhejta hai. Yeh reliability aur delay ke variability ke beech ka trade-off hai. UDP flow control nahi karta aur lost packets dobara nahi bhejta, isliye variable delay ke kuch causes avoid ho jaate hain. Phir bhi switch queues aur machines par scheduling delays ka asar uspar padta hai.

UDP tab achha choice hai jab late data bekaar hota hai. VoIP call mein aam taur par lost packet ko dobara bhejne ka time hi nahi hota, kyunki uski audio play hone ka waqt aa chuka hota hai. Isliye application missing audio ko silence se bhar deti hai, jisse awaaz mein chhota sa break aata hai, aur aage badh jaati hai. Retry human layer par hota hai, jab listener speaker se kehta hai ki woh sentence dobara bolo.

Book shared networks ke baare mein ek practical baat jodti hai. Public clouds aur multi-tenant data centers mein network links, switches, aur har machine ka network card aur CPUs (virtual machines par) bhi doosre customers ke saath share hote hain. MapReduce jaisi batch jobs aasaani se network links saturate kar sakti hain. Doosre customers kya use kar rahe hain, us par na tumhara control hai, na tumhe dikhta hai. Agar paas ka koi noisy neighbor bahut resources use kare, toh tumhare network delays bahut zyada badal sakte hain.

Aise environments mein timeout chunne ka ekmaatra tarika experiment hai. Lambe time tak aur kai machines par network round-trip times ka distribution measure karein, taaki pata chale ki woh aam taur par kitna vary karte hain. Phir apni application ki zarooraton ko dhyaan mein rakhte hue slow failure detection aur premature timeouts ke risk ke beech balance chunein.

Isse behtar approach hai ki fixed timeout use hi na karein. System response times aur unke variability (jise jitter kehte hain) ko measure karta reh sakta hai, aur jo observe karta hai uske hisaab se apne timeouts automatically adjust kar sakta hai. Yeh Phi Accrual failure detector se ho sakta hai, jo book ke hisaab se Akka aur Cassandra use karte hain. TCP ke retransmission timeouts bhi isi tarah kaam karte hain.

Synchronous versus asynchronous networks

Distributed systems bahut aasaan ho jaate agar network packets ko kisi fixed maximum delay mein deliver karta aur kabhi drop na karta. Hum ise hardware level par hi kyun fix nahi kar sakte, taaki software ko iski chinta na karni pade?

Book datacenter networks ki tulna traditional fixed-line telephone network se karti hai, jo bahut reliable hai. Delayed audio aur dropped calls bahut rare hain. Phone call ko hamesha low end-to-end delay chahiye, aur tumhari awaaz le jaane ke liye kaafi bandwidth. Computer networks mein bhi aisi predictability ho, toh kitna achha hota na?

Telephone network par call ek circuit set up karti hai. Do callers ke beech poore route par call ke liye ek fixed, guaranteed bandwidth reserve ho jaati hai, aur woh call khatam hone tak wahi rehti hai.

Example

Book example ke liye ISDN telephone network leti hai. Woh 4,000 frames per second ke fixed rate par chalta hai. Jab call set up hoti hai, toh use har frame mein, har direction mein, 16 bits ki jagah milti hai. Isliye call ke poore time tak, har side ko guarantee hai ki woh har 250 microseconds mein exactly 16 bits audio bhej sakti hai. Data move hone se pehle hi jagah reserve ho jaati hai, isliye frame ko raaste ke har router par queue mein wait nahi karna padta. Isliye maximum end-to-end delay fixed hota hai. Book ise bounded delay kehti hai.

Computer networks ke liye bhi yahi kyun nahi karte? Circuit TCP connection se bahut alag hai. Circuit ek fixed amount of bandwidth reserve karta hai jise call chalne tak koi aur use nahi kar sakta. TCP connection jo bandwidth free ho use opportunistically use karta hai. Tum TCP ko data ka koi block do, jaise email ya web page, toh woh use jitni tezi se ho sake transfer karne ki koshish karta hai. Jab TCP connection idle hota hai, toh woh koi bandwidth use nahi karta. Book ek footnote jodti hai ki TCP keepalive packets rare exception hain.

Agar datacenter networks aur internet circuit-switched hote, toh circuit set up hote waqt tum ek guaranteed maximum round-trip time tay kar sakte the. Lekin woh aise nahi hain. Ethernet aur IP packet-switched protocols hain, matlab packets links share karte hain aur queue ho sakte hain, isliye delays bounded nahi hote. In protocols mein circuit ka koi concept hi nahi hai.

Datacenters aur internet packet switching kyun use karte hain? Jawab yeh hai ki woh bursty traffic ke liye optimized hain, jo achanak bursts mein aata hai aur beech mein shaanti rehti hai. Circuit audio ya video call ke liye theek hai, jisme poori call mein har second ek lagbhag constant number of bits chahiye. Lekin web page maangna, email bhejna ya file transfer karne ki koi khaas bandwidth requirement nahi hoti. Hum bas chahte hain ki jitni jaldi ho sake ho jaaye.

Socho ki tum circuit par file transfer kar rahe ho. Tumhe reserve karne ke liye ek bandwidth andaaze se chunni padegi. Agar andaaza bahut kam hai, toh transfer bekaar mein slow hoga aur network capacity unused padi rahegi. Agar andaaza bahut zyada hai, toh circuit set up hi nahi ho payega, kyunki network itni bandwidth ka promise nahi kar sakta. Isliye bursty transfers ke liye circuits use karne se capacity waste hoti hai aur transfers slow hote hain. TCP, iske ulat, apna rate jo capacity available ho uske hisaab se adapt kar leta hai.

Aise hybrid networks banane ki koshishein hui hain jo circuit aur packet switching dono support karein. Book ATM, yani Asynchronous Transfer Mode, ka zikr karti hai, jo 1980s mein Ethernet se compete karta tha. Telephone networks ke core switches ke bahar use zyada adoption nahi mila. (Iska cash machines se koi lena-dena nahi hai, bhale acronym same ho.) InfiniBand kuch-kuch waisa hi hai. Woh link layer par flow control karta hai, jisse network ke andar queueing kam hoti hai, lekin links congested hone par delays phir bhi ho sakte hain. Quality of service (packets ko prioritize aur schedule karna) aur admission control (senders kitni tezi se bhej sakte hain, use limit karna) ke dhyaan se use ke saath, packet network par circuit switching ki nakal karna, ya statistically bounded delay dena possible hai.

Latency aur resource utilization

Aur general tarike se dekho, toh tum variable delays ko dynamic resource partitioning ka nateeja maan sakte ho, matlab resource ko fixed slices mein baantne ki jagah on the fly share karna.

Maan lo do telephone switches ke beech ek wire ek saath 10,000 calls tak carry kar sakti hai. Har circuit un call slots mein se ek use karta hai. Wire static tarike se divide hui hai. Tumhari call wire par akeli ho, aur baaki 9,999 slots khaali hon, tab bhi tumhare circuit ko wahi fixed bandwidth milti hai jo wire poori bhari hone par milti.

Internet bandwidth ko dynamically share karta hai. Senders apne packets ko wire par jitni tezi se ho sake pahunchane ke liye dhakka-mukki karte hain, aur switches ek pal se doosre pal tay karte hain ki agla packet kaun sa jaayega. Isme queueing ka nuksaan hai. Lekin isse wire ka zyada se zyada hissa use hota hai. Wire ka cost fixed hota hai, isliye tum jitna zyada use karo, bheja gaya har byte utna sasta padta hai.

CPUs ke saath bhi aisa hi trade-off aata hai. Agar kai threads ek CPU core ko dynamically share karein, toh ek thread ko kabhi-kabhi operating system ki run queue mein wait karna padta hai jabki doosra thread chal raha hota hai. Isliye uske pauses ki length vary karti hai. Lekin yeh hardware ko har thread ko CPU cycles ka fixed share dene se behtar use karta hai. Hardware ka behtar use virtual machines chalane ki bhi ek badi wajah hai.

Latency guarantees tab mil sakti hain jab resources static tarike se partitioned hon, dedicated hardware aur exclusive bandwidth ke saath. Lekin isme utilization ka nuksaan hota hai, isliye yeh zyada mehnga hai. Dynamic partitioning ke saath multi-tenancy behtar utilization deti hai aur sasti hai, lekin variable delays laati hai. Book ka nishkarsh yeh hai ki networks mein variable delays koi kudrat ka niyam nahi hain. Woh bas cost aur benefit ke trade-off ka nateeja hain.

ApproachKis mein achhaCost
Circuits, ya reserved bandwidth ke saath static partitioningBounded, predictable delay aur latency guaranteesReserved capacity unused pad sakti hai. Hardware use kam hota hai aur cost badhti hai.
Dynamic sharing ke saath packet switching (IP, Ethernet)High utilization, isliye har byte sasta. Bursty traffic ke liye achha.Queueing se variable, unbounded delays hote hain.

Quality of service abhi multi-tenant datacenters, public clouds ya internet par enabled nahi hai. Isliye aaj ki technology network delays ya reliability guarantee nahi kar sakti. Humein maan kar chalna padega ki congestion, queueing aur unbounded delays honge. Matlab timeout ki koi ek sahi value nahi hoti. Timeouts experiment se set karne padte hain.

Unreliable Clocks

Clocks aur time bahut zaroori hain. Applications clocks ka use aise sawalon ka jawab dene ke liye karti hain:

  1. Kya yeh request timeout ho chuki hai?
  2. Is service ka 99th percentile response time kya hai?
  3. Pichle paanch minute mein is service ne average kitni queries per second handle ki?
  4. User ne hamari site par kitna time bitaya?
  5. Yeh article kab publish hua tha?
  6. Reminder email kis date aur time par bhejni chahiye?
  7. Yeh cache entry kab expire hogi?
  8. Log file mein is error message ka timestamp kya hai?

Pehle chaar sawal ek duration naapte hain, yani do events ke beech ka time. Aakhri chaar ek point in time batate hain, yani ek particular date aur time.

Distributed system mein time tricky hota hai. Communication instant nahi hoti. Message ko network cross karne mein time lagta hai. Message receive hone ka time hamesha bhejne ke time se baad ka hota hai, lekin delays alag-alag hoti hain, isliye hume pata nahi hota ki kitna baad. Jab kai machines involved hon, toh yeh kabhi-kabhi order samajhna mushkil bana deta hai ki cheezein kis order mein hui thi.

Har machine ki apni clock bhi hoti hai, jo ek hardware device hai, aam taur par quartz crystal oscillator. Yeh devices perfectly accurate nahi hote, isliye har machine ka time ka apna sense hota hai, jo doosron se thoda tez ya dheema chal sakta hai. Clocks ko kuch had tak synchronize kiya ja sakta hai. Sabse common tarika Network Time Protocol (NTP) hai, jo servers ke ek group ke bataye time ke hisaab se computer ki clock adjust karta hai. Woh servers apna time kisi zyada accurate source se lete hain, jaise GPS receiver.

Monotonic vs time-of-day clocks

Modern computers mein kam se kam do tarah ki clocks hoti hain, aur dono ka kaam alag hai. Dono time naapti hain, lekin tumhe pata hona chahiye ki kaunsi kab use karni hai.

Ek time-of-day clock wahi karti hai jo tum clock se expect karte ho. Yeh calendar ke hisaab se current date aur time return karti hai, jise wall-clock time bhi kehte hain. Jaise Linux par clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME) aur Java mein System.currentTimeMillis() epoch ke baad se seconds ya milliseconds ki ginti return karte hain. Epoch matlab Gregorian calendar ke hisaab se 1 January 1970 ki midnight UTC, aur ismein leap seconds count nahi hote. Kuch systems doosri reference dates bhi use karte hain.

Time-of-day clocks aam taur par NTP se synchronized hoti hain. Isliye ek machine ka timestamp doosri machine ke timestamp ke barabar meaning rakhna chahiye. Lekin time-of-day clocks ki kuch oddities hoti hain. Agar local clock NTP server se kaafi aage ho, toh use forcibly reset kiya ja sakta hai, aur phir lagta hai ki woh pichle time par kood gayi. Yeh jumps, aur yeh baat ki clocks aksar leap seconds ignore karti hain, time-of-day clocks ko elapsed time naapne ke liye unsuitable bana dete hain. Purane Windows systems time ko 10 milliseconds ke coarse steps mein aage badhate the. Naye systems kaafi behtar hain, isliye ab yeh kam problem hai.

Ek monotonic clock duration naapne ke liye suitable hai, jaise timeout ya service ka response time. Linux par clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) aur Java mein System.nanoTime() iske examples hain. Naam is wajah se hai ki monotonic clock hamesha aage hi badhne ki guarantee deti hai, jabki time-of-day clock peeche kood sakti hai.

Tum monotonic clock ko ek point par padhte ho, kuch kaam karte ho, aur baad mein dobara padhte ho. Dono readings ka difference elapsed time hota hai. Lekin monotonic clock ki absolute value ka koi matlab nahi hota. Ho sakta hai woh computer boot hone ke baad se nanoseconds gin rahi ho, ya kuch aur arbitrary. Do alag computers ki monotonic values compare karna bekaar hai, kyunki unka matlab same nahi hota.

Kai CPU sockets wale server par har CPU ka apna timer ho sakta hai, aur woh timers zaroori nahi ki synchronized hon. Operating systems isse chhupane ki koshish karte hain aur application threads ko monotonic view dikhate hain, chahe woh alag CPUs par chal rahe hon. Book salaah deti hai ki us guarantee ko thoda soch-samajh kar lein. NTP monotonic clock ki speed bhi adjust kar sakta hai, jise slewing kehte hain, agar use lage ki local quartz NTP server se tez ya dheema chal raha hai. Default mein NTP clock ko 0.05 percent tak tez ya dheema kar sakta hai. Lekin NTP monotonic clock ko aage ya peeche kooda nahi sakta. Monotonic clocks aam taur par microseconds ya usse behtar accuracy tak achhi hoti hain.

Distributed system mein elapsed time naapne ke liye, jaise timeouts, monotonic clock aam taur par theek rehti hai. Woh yeh assume nahi karti ki alag nodes ki clocks synchronized hain, aur chhoti measurement inaccuracies se use farak nahi padta.

ClockKis kaam ke liyeCosts
Time-of-day (wall-clock)Woh dates aur times jo machines ke beech match hone chahiye, jaise article ka publish timePeeche ya aage kood sakti hai. Kitna time guzra yeh naapne ke liye reliable nahi.
MonotonicDurations, jaise ek machine par timeouts aur response timesSirf usi machine par meaningful hai. Iski absolute value ka koi matlab nahi.

Clock synchronization aur accuracy

Monotonic clocks ko synchronize karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Time-of-day clocks ko NTP server ya kisi aur external time source ke hisaab se set karna padta hai, warna woh kaam ki nahi.
