Lekin clock ko sahi time dikhane ke hamare tarike utne reliable ya accurate nahi hain jitna hum chahenge. Hardware clocks aur NTP dono fickle ho sakte hain. Book kai examples deti hai:

  • Drift. Computer ki quartz clock bahut accurate nahi hoti. Woh drift karti hai, matlab jitna chalna chahiye usse tez ya dheema chalti hai, aur drift temperature ke saath badalta hai. Google apne servers ke liye 200 ppm (parts per million) drift maanta hai. Yani jo clock har 30 second mein server se resynchronize hoti hai, usmein 6 milliseconds ka drift. Jo clock din mein sirf ek baar resynchronize hoti hai, usmein drift badhkar lagbhag 17 seconds ho jaata hai. Sab kuch theek chalne par bhi yeh drift best accuracy ko limit karta hai.
  • Forced resets. Agar computer ki clock NTP server se bahut zyada alag ho, toh woh synchronize karne se mana kar sakta hai, ya uski local clock forcibly reset ho sakti hai. Jo bhi application reset se pehle aur baad ka time dekhti hai, use time peeche jaata ya achanak aage kooda hua dikh sakta hai.
  • Silent firewalls. Agar kisi node ko galti se NTP servers tak pahunchne se block kar diya jaaye, toh galti kuch time tak notice nahi hoti. Book kehti hai ki anecdotal evidence batata hai ki aisa sach mein hota hai.
  • Network delay. NTP utna hi accurate ho sakta hai jitni network delay allow kare. Congested network mein jahan delays badalti rehti hain, uski accuracy ki ek limit hoti hai. Ek experiment mein internet par minimum 35 ms ka error mila, aur kabhi-kabhi delay ke spikes se lagbhag ek second ke errors aaye. Bade delays mein NTP client poori tarah haar bhi maan sakta hai.
  • Wrong servers. Kuch NTP servers galat ya misconfigured hote hain, aur ghanton ka galat time batate hain. NTP clients kaafi robust hote hain, kyunki woh kai servers se query karte hain aur outliers ignore kar dete hain. Phir bhi book ke hisaab se thoda pareshaan karne wali baat hai ki tum apne systems ki correctness ka daaon internet par kisi ajnabi ke bataye time par lagao.
  • Leap seconds. Leap second se ek minute 59 ya 61 seconds ka ho jaata hai. Isse un systems ki timing assumptions toot jaati hain jo iske liye design nahi hue. Leap seconds ne kai bade systems ko crash kiya hai, jisse pata chalta hai ki clocks ke baare mein galat assumptions system mein kitni aasaani se ghus jaati hain. Ek possible fix yeh hai ki NTP servers thoda jhooth bolein. Woh leap second ka adjustment ek din mein dheere-dheere failate hain, jise smearing kehte hain. Lekin practice mein actual NTP server ka behavior alag-alag hota hai.
  • Virtual machines. VM mein hardware clock khud virtualized hoti hai. Jab ek CPU core VMs ke beech share hota hai, toh jab doosri VM chalti hai tab har VM kuch dus milliseconds ke liye pause ho jaati hai. Application ke point of view se yeh pause aisa lagta hai jaise clock achanak aage kood gayi.
  • Devices jo tumhare control mein nahi. Phones aur embedded devices par shayad tum hardware clock par bilkul bharosa nahi kar sakte. Kuch users intentionally apni clock galat date par set kar dete hain, jaise games ki timing limits se bachne ke liye. Phir clock bahut pehle ya bahut aage ka time dikha sakti hai.

Agar tum kaafi invest karo, toh bahut achhi clock accuracy possible hai. Book finance se ek example deti hai. MiFID II naam ka ek draft European regulation high-frequency trading firms se maangta hai ki woh apni clocks ko UTC ke 100 microseconds ke andar synchronize rakhein. Maksad hai market anomalies, jaise flash crashes, ko debug karna aur market manipulation detect karna. Itni accuracy GPS receivers, Precision Time Protocol (PTP), aur careful deployment aur monitoring se mil sakti hai. Lekin ismein kaafi effort aur expertise lagti hai, aur clock synchronization kai tarah se galat ho sakta hai. Agar tumhara NTP daemon misconfigured ho, ya firewall NTP traffic block kar de, toh drift se clock error jaldi bahut bada ho sakta hai.

Synchronized clocks par depend karna

Clocks simple aur use karne mein aasaan lagti hain, lekin unmein hairaan karne wale kaafi pitfalls hain. Ek din mein hamesha exactly 86,400 seconds nahi hote. Time-of-day clocks peeche ja sakti hain. Aur ek node ka time doosre node ke time se kaafi alag ho sakta hai.

Pehle is chapter mein dikhaya tha ki networks packets drop kar sakte hain aur unhe arbitrarily delay kar sakte hain. Networks zyadatar time theek chalte hain, lekin software ko phir bhi kabhi-kabhi aane wale fault ke liye design karna padta hai aur use gracefully handle karna padta hai. Clocks ke saath bhi yahi baat hai. Woh zyadatar time achhe se kaam karti hain, lekin robust software ko galat clocks ke liye ready rehna chahiye.

Galat clocks ko miss karna aasaan hai. Agar kisi machine ka CPU defective ho ya network misconfigured ho, toh machine shayad kaam hi nahi karegi, aur koi notice karke jaldi fix kar dega. Lekin agar uski quartz clock defective ho ya NTP client misconfigured ho, toh zyadatar cheezein theek chalti dikhengi. Clock chupke se reality se aur door hoti jaati hai. Agar software accurately synchronized clock par depend karta hai, toh result dramatic crash se zyada silent, subtle data loss hone ke chances hain.

Isliye agar tum aisa software use karte ho jise synchronized clocks chahiye, toh tumhe apni saari machines ke beech clock offsets bhi monitor karne honge. Jis node ki clock baaki nodes se bahut zyada drift kar jaaye, use dead declare karke cluster se hata dena chahiye. Yeh monitoring toote hue clocks ko zyada nuksaan karne se pehle pakad leti hai.

Events ko order karne ke liye timestamps

Ek situation dikhati hai ki clocks par depend karna kitna lubhavna aur kitna khatarnaak hai. Problem hai kai nodes ke beech events ko order karna. Agar do clients distributed database mein write karein, toh pehle kaunsi write hui? Kaunsi zyada recent hai?

Book ka Figure 8-3 multi-leader replication wale database mein time-of-day clocks ka ek khatarnaak use dikhata hai. (Multi-leader replication mein kai nodes writes accept kar sakte hain, aur yeh example Chapter 5 ke Figure 5-9 jaisa hai.)

Example

Book ka example step by step dekhte hain. Client A node 1 par x = 1 likhta hai. Yeh write node 3 par replicate hoti hai. Client B woh value padhta hai aur node 3 par use increment karta hai, toh ab x = 2 hai. Aakhir mein dono writes node 2 par replicate hoti hain. Har write ko us node ki clock ka timestamp lagta hai jahan woh start hui thi. Node 1 apni write ko 42.004 seconds par stamp karta hai. Node 3 client B ki baad ki write ko 42.003 seconds par stamp karta hai. Yahan clocks achhe se synchronized hain. Node 1 aur node 3 ke beech skew 3 ms se kam hai, jo book ke hisaab se practice mein jitna expect kar sakte hain usse shayad behtar hai.

Phir bhi timestamps events ko ulte order mein rakhte hain. Write x = 1 ka timestamp bada hai, 42.004, jabki x = 2 ka 42.003 hai. Lekin x = 2 saaf taur par baad mein hua tha. Jab node 2 dono writes receive karta hai, toh woh decide karta hai ki x = 1 zyada recent value hai, aur x = 2 ko phenk deta hai. Client B ka increment lost ho jaata hai.

Yahan jo conflict resolution strategy use hui hai, use last write wins (LWW) kehte hain. Sabse bade timestamp wali write rakh li jaati hai aur baaki discard ho jaati hain. LWW multi-leader replication mein aur Cassandra aur Riak jaise leaderless databases mein kaafi use hota hai. Kuch systems timestamps server ke bajaye client par banate hain, lekin isse LWW ki basic problems fix nahi hoti:

  • Writes gayab ho sakti hain. Slow clock wala node, fast clock wale node ki likhi values ko tab tak overwrite nahi kar sakta jab tak un dono ke beech ka clock skew guzar na jaaye. Isse silently arbitrary matra mein data drop ho sakta hai, aur application ko koi error report nahi hota.
  • Sequential aur concurrent writes ek jaisi dikhti hain. LWW un writes mein fark nahi kar paata jo ek ke baad ek jaldi-jaldi hui hon, jaise example mein client B ka increment, aur un writes mein jo sach mein concurrent thi, jahan kisi writer ko doosre ka pata nahi tha. Causality violate hone se bachne ke liye extra causality tracking chahiye, jaise version vectors.
  • Ties. Do nodes same timestamp bana sakte hain, khaaskar jab clock ki resolution sirf millisecond ho. Tumhe tiebreaker chahiye, jo ek bada random number ho sakta hai, lekin yeh approach bhi causality violate kar sakta hai.

Toh sabse recent value rakhna aur baaki phenkna lubhavna hone par bhi, recent ki definition local time-of-day clock par depend karti hai, jo galat ho sakti hai. Tightly synchronized clocks hone par bhi, ek packet sender ki clock ke hisaab se 100 ms par bheja ja sakta hai aur recipient ki clock ke hisaab se 99 ms par pahunch sakta hai. Isse lagega ki packet bhejne se pehle hi pahunch gaya, jo impossible hai.

Kya NTP ko itna accurate banaya ja sakta hai ki aise galat orderings na ho? Book ke hisaab se shayad nahi. NTP ki accuracy network round-trip time se limited hoti hai, aur quartz drift jaise doosre errors bhi hote hain. Sahi ordering ke liye clock ko us cheez se kahin zyada accurate hona padega jise tum naap rahe ho, yani network delay.

Logical clocks events ko order karne ka zyada safe tarika hain. Yeh oscillating quartz crystal ke bajaye badhte hue counters par based hoti hain. Logical clock time of day ya beete hue seconds nahi naapti. Woh sirf yeh record karti hai ki ek event doosre se pehle hua ya baad mein. Time-of-day aur monotonic clocks, jo real elapsed time naapti hain, physical clocks bhi kehlaati hain. Chapter 9 ordering ko aur detail mein dekhta hai.

Clock readings ka confidence interval hota hai

Ho sakta hai tum machine ki time-of-day clock ko microsecond ya nanosecond resolution tak padh sako. Lekin fine-grained reading ka matlab yeh nahi ki value utni precision tak accurate hai. Asal mein, zyada chance hai ki nahi hai. Imprecise quartz clock ka drift aasaani se kai milliseconds ho sakta hai, chahe tum local network ke NTP server se har minute sync karo. Public internet ke NTP server ke saath best accuracy shayad dus-dus milliseconds ki hoti hai, aur network congested hone par error 100 ms se upar spike kar sakta hai.

Isliye clock reading ko ek single point in time maanna sahi nahi hai. Behtar hai ki ise confidence interval wali range ki tarah dekhein. Jaise, ek system 95 percent confident ho sakta hai ki abhi ka time minute ke 10.3 aur 10.5 seconds ke beech hai, lekin usse zyada precisely woh nahi jaan sakta. Agar tumhe time sirf plus ya minus 100 ms tak pata hai, toh timestamp ke microsecond digits essentially meaningless hain.

Uncertainty kitni hai, yeh tumhare time source par depend karta hai. Agar tumhare computer se GPS receiver ya atomic clock directly attached hai, toh manufacturer expected error range batata hai. Agar tum server se time lete ho, toh uncertainty teen cheezon par based hoti hai: tumhare last sync ke baad se expected quartz drift, NTP server ki uncertainty, aur server tak network round-trip time. Yeh pehla approximation hai, aur isme maana gaya hai ki tum server par trust karte ho.

Unfortunately, zyadatar systems yeh uncertainty expose nahi karte. Jab tum clock_gettime() call karte hain, toh return value yeh nahi batati ki expected error kya hai. Tum nahi bata sakte ki confidence interval paanch milliseconds hai ya paanch saal.

Spanner mein Google ka TrueTime API ek interesting exception hai. Woh local clock ka confidence interval explicitly report karta hai. Jab tum usse time poochhte ho, toh tumhe do values milti ho, [earliest, latest]. Yeh earliest aur latest possible times hain. Apni uncertainty calculations ke basis par clock jaanti hai ki actual current time us interval ke andar kahin hai. Interval kitna wide hai, yeh doosri cheezon ke saath is par depend karta hai ki local quartz clock ko aakhri baar kisi zyada accurate source se synchronize kiye hue kitna time ho gaya hai.

Asli idea

Clock reading ek point in time nahi hai. Woh ek range hai, aur sahi sawal yeh hai ki range kitni wide hai. Zyadatar clocks yeh batati nahi, isliye tum kisi timestamp se uske error bound se zyada precise hone ki ummeed nahi kar sakte.

Global snapshots ke liye synchronized clocks

Chapter 7 mein snapshot isolation ki baat hui thi. Yeh ek feature hai jo read-only transactions ko database ek point in time par consistent state mein dikhata hai, bina read-write transactions ko lock out kiye. Yeh backups aur lambe chalne wale analytics ke liye bahut kaam ka hai.

Snapshot isolation implement karne ka sabse common tarika ek aisa transaction ID use karta hai jo hamesha badhta rehta hai. Jis write ka transaction ID snapshot se bada ho, woh us snapshot ko dikhai nahi deti. Single node par in IDs ko generate karne ke liye simple counter kaafi hai.

Lekin jab database kai machines par, shayad kai data centers mein, faila ho, toh single global counter banana mushkil hai, kyunki ise generate karne ke liye coordination chahiye. IDs ko causality bhi reflect karni hoti hai. Agar transaction B ne transaction A ki likhi value padhi hai, toh B ka ID A se bada hona chahiye. Warna snapshot consistent nahi hoga. Bahut saare chhote, fast transactions ho toh distributed system mein IDs generate karna ek unbearable bottleneck ban jaata hai. Book yeh bhi kehti hai ki distributed sequence generators, jaise Twitter ka Snowflake, scale par lagbhag badhte hue unique IDs bana sakte hain, lekin aam taur par causality se match karta order guarantee nahi kar sakte.

Kya hum synchronized time-of-day clocks ke timestamps ko transaction IDs ki tarah use kar sakte hain? Agar synchronization kaafi achha ho, toh IDs ki properties sahi hongi. Baad ke transactions ke timestamps bade honge. Problem clock accuracy ki uncertainty hai.

Spanner bilkul yahi data centers ke across karta hai, TrueTime ke confidence interval ka use karke. Key observation simple hai. Do confidence intervals lo, jinme se har ek ka earliest aur latest possible time hai. Unhe A aur B kehte hain. Agar dono intervals overlap nahi karte, yani A, B ke shuru hone se pehle khatam ho jaata hai, toh B definitely A ke baad hua. Isme koi shak nahi. Sirf jab intervals overlap karte hain tabhi humein pata nahi hota ki pehle kaun aaya.

Example

Neeche wali figure ko dekhte hain. Interval A time line ke ek hisse ko cover karta hai, aur interval B poori tarah uske baad hai, beech mein gap ke saath. Spanner pakka keh sakta hai ki B, A ke baad hua. Ab intervals C aur D dekho. Woh beech mein overlap karte hain, isliye Spanner nahi bata sakta ki pehle kaunsa hua.

Transaction timestamps ko causality reflect karwane ke liye, Spanner read-write transaction commit karne se pehle intentionally confidence interval ki lambai jitna wait karta hai. Is wait se yeh pakka hota hai ki jo bhi transaction baad mein us data ko padh sakta hai, uska time kaafi baad ka ho, taaki unke confidence intervals overlap na karein. Wait ko chhota rakhne ke liye clock uncertainty bhi chhoti honi chahiye. Isi wajah se Google har data center mein GPS receiver ya atomic clock lagata hai, jisse clocks lagbhag 7 ms ke andar synchronized rehti hain.

Book ke hisaab se distributed transaction semantics ke liye synchronized clocks use karna ek active research area hai. Yeh ideas interesting hain, lekin Google ke bahar yeh abhi mainstream databases tak nahi pahunche.

Process Pauses

Clock ke khatarnaak use ka ek aur example yeh hai. Maan lo tumhare paas ek database hai jisme har partition ka ek single leader hai, aur sirf leader hi writes accept kar sakta hai. Ek node ko kaise pata chale ki woh abhi bhi leader hai, yani baaki nodes ne use dead declare nahi kiya, taaki woh safely writes accept kar sake?

Ek option yeh hai ki leader baaki nodes se ek lease le. Lease timeout wale lock jaisi hoti hai. Ek time par sirf ek node lease hold kar sakta hai. Jab kisi node ko lease milti hai, toh use pata hota hai ki woh ek set time ke liye, lease expire hone tak, leader hai. Leader bane rehne ke liye node ko lease expire hone se pehle periodically use renew karna padta hai. Agar node fail ho jaaye, toh woh renew karna band kar deta hai, aur lease khatam hone par doosra node take over kar sakta hai.

Book aise leader ka request-handling loop is tarah sketch karti hai:

while (true) {
  request = getIncomingRequest();
  // Ensure that the lease always has at least 10 seconds remaining
  if (lease.expiryTimeMillis - System.currentTimeMillis() < 10000) {
    lease = lease.renew();
  }
  if (lease.isValid()) {
    process(request);
  }
}

Book is code ki do problems batati hai. Inhe order mein dekhte hain.

Pehli problem yeh hai ki code synchronized clocks par depend karta hai. Lease ka expiry time ek alag machine set karti hai. Ho sakta hai woh machine use current time plus 30 seconds calculate kare. Lekin expiry ko local system clock se compare kiya jaata hai. Agar dono clocks kuch seconds se zyada out of sync hon, toh code ajeeb cheezein karne lagta hai.

Doosri problem tab bhi rehti hai jab hum local machine par monotonic clock use karne lagein. Code maanta hai ki lease check karne aur request process karne ke beech bahut kam time guzarta hai. Normally yeh sach hota hai, isliye 10 seconds ka buffer kaafi se zyada hai. Lekin agar program achanak pause ho jaaye toh? Socho thread lease.isValid() check ke aas-paas 15 seconds ke liye ruk jaata hai, phir aage chalta hai. Jab tak woh request process karta hai, lease shayad expire ho chuki hoti hai, aur doosra node leader ban chuka hota hai. Thread ko kuch nahi batata ki woh itni der pause tha. Code ko expired lease tab tak pata nahi chalega jab tak next loop iteration na aaye, aur tab tak ho sakta hai woh kuch unsafe kar chuka ho.

Example

Dono problems ko numbers ke saath jodte hain, sirf samajhne ke liye. Maan lo loop jab lease check karta hai, tab uske paas 12 seconds bache hain. Yeh 10 seconds se zyada hai, isliye code renew nahi karta. isValid() ka check true return karta hai. Phir thread 15 seconds ke liye freeze ho jaata hai, shayad garbage collection pause se. Jab woh jaagta hai, lease 3 seconds pehle expire ho chuki hai. Ab doosra node leader hai. Lekin process(request) phir bhi chal jaata hai, kyunki thread ko pata hi nahi ki time guzar gaya.

Kya yeh assume karna pagalpan hai ki thread itni der pause ho sakta hai? Unfortunately, nahi hai. Book kai tarike gintati hai jinse aisa ho sakta hai:

  • Garbage collection. Kai language runtimes, jaise Java Virtual Machine, mein garbage collector hota hai jise kabhi-kabhi saare running threads ko rokna padta hai. Yeh stop-the-world pauses kai minutes tak chalte dekhe gaye hain. HotSpot JVM ke CMS jaise so-called concurrent collectors ko bhi time-time par world rokna padta hai. Allocation patterns badalkar ya settings tune karke pauses aksar kam kiye ja sakte hain, lekin agar tumhe robust guarantees chahiye, toh worst case maanna hi padega.
  • Virtual machine suspension. Virtual machine ko suspend kiya ja sakta hai, jisse uske saare processes pause ho jaate hain aur memory disk par save ho jaati hai, aur baad mein resume kiya ja sakta hai. Yeh kisi bhi point par ho sakta hai aur kitni bhi der chal sakta hai. Kabhi-kabhi ise VM ko ek host se doosre par bina reboot ke live migrate karne ke liye use kiya jaata hai. Tab pause ki lambai is par depend karti hai ki processes memory mein kitni tezi se write kar rahe hain.
  • Laptops. End-user devices par execution kisi bhi time suspend aur resume ho sakta hai, jaise jab tum laptop ka lid band karte ho.
  • Context switches aur steal time. Jab operating system kisi doosre thread par switch karta hai, ya hypervisor kisi doosri VM par, toh running thread kisi bhi point par pause ho sakta hai. Doosri VMs mein kharch hua CPU time steal time kehlaata hai. Bahut load wali machine par jahan threads ki lambi queue ho, paused thread ko dobara chalne ke liye kaafi der wait karna pad sakta hai.
  • Disk access. Agar application synchronous disk access karti hai, toh slow disk operation poora hone tak thread pause ho sakta hai. Disk access tab bhi ho sakta hai jab code mein files ka zikr nahi dikhta. Jaise Java class loader class files ko lazily load karta hai, pehli baar use hone par. I/O pauses aur GC pauses mil bhi sakte hain. Agar disk network filesystem ya network block device ho, jaise Amazon ka EBS, toh I/O delay network ke saath bhi badalti rehti hai.
  • Paging. Agar operating system memory ko disk par swap karne deta hai, toh ek simple memory access bhi page fault kara sakta hai, aur thread tab tak wait karta hai jab tak disk se page read na ho. High memory pressure mein system ka zyadatar time pages ko andar-bahar swap karne mein jaa sakta hai aur real kaam kam hota hai. Ise thrashing kehte hain. Isse bachne ke liye server machines par aksar paging disable kar di jaati hai, kyunki thrashing ka risk lene se behtar hai ki process ko kill kar diya jaaye.
  • Signals. Unix process ko SIGSTOP signal bhejkar pause kiya ja sakta hai, jaise shell mein Ctrl-Z dabakar. Woh CPU time milna band ho jaata hai jab tak SIGCONT se resume na ho, aur phir wahin se aage chalta hai jahan ruka tha. Tumhara environment normally SIGSTOP use na bhi kare, toh bhi koi operations engineer ise galti se bhej sakta hai.

Yeh sab kisi bhi point par running thread ko preempt karke baad mein resume kar sakte hain, aur thread ko pata bhi nahi chalta. Yeh problem ek machine par multi-threaded code ko thread-safe banane jaisi hai. Tum timing ke baare mein kuch assume nahi kar sakte, kyunki arbitrary context switches aur parallel execution ho sakte ho.

Ek machine par thread safety ke liye humare paas achhe tools hain, jaise mutexes, semaphores, atomic counters, lock-free data structures, aur blocking queues. Yeh distributed systems mein seedhe kaam nahi karte. Distributed system mein shared memory nahi hoti. Bas unreliable network par bheje gaye messages hote hain.

Isliye distributed system ke node ko maanna padega ki uski execution kisi bhi point par, function ke beech mein bhi, kaafi der ke liye pause ho sakti hai. Us pause ke dauran baaki duniya chalti rehti hai, aur paused node ko dead bhi declare kar sakti hai. Aakhir mein node phir chalne lagta hai, bina yeh jaane ki woh soya tha, jab tak woh baad mein clock check na kare.

Response time guarantees

Kai programming languages aur operating systems mein threads aur processes unbounded time ke liye pause ho sakte hain. Pause hone ki yeh wajahein khatam ki ja sakti ho agar tum poori koshish karo.

Kuch software aisi jagah chalta hai jahan specified time ke andar respond na karne se serious nuksaan ho sakta hai. Aircraft, rockets, robots aur cars control karne wale computers ko sensor input par tezi se aur predictably respond karna padta hai. Software ke paas ek deadline hoti hai, aur use miss karne se poora system fail ho sakta hai. Inhe hard real-time systems kehte hain.

Dhyaan do

Embedded systems mein real-time ka matlab hai ki system ko carefully design aur test kiya gaya hai taaki woh har halaat mein timing guarantees poori kare. Web par yeh word zyada dheele tarike se use hota hai, servers ke clients ko data push karne ke liye, ya hard response time limits ke bina stream processing ke liye. Book ka matlab strict wala hai.

Car ka airbag socho. Agar sensors crash detect karo, toh tum nahi chahoge ki airbag release airbag software ke kisi galat time par aaye garbage collection pause se delay ho.

Real-time guarantees dene ke liye software stack ke har level se support chahiye. Tumhe real-time operating system chahiye jo processes ko set intervals par CPU time ke guaranteed hisse ke saath schedule kar sake. Library functions ko apne worst-case execution times document karne padte hain. Dynamic memory allocation restricted ya poori tarah banned ho sakti hai. Real-time garbage collectors hote hain, lekin application ko phir bhi dhyaan rakhna padta hai ki woh collector ko bahut zyada kaam na de. Aur guarantees sahi hain yeh confirm karne ke liye bahut saari testing aur measurement chahiye.

Yeh sab kaafi zyada kaam maangta hai, aur isse limit ho jaata hai ki tum kaunsi programming languages, libraries aur tools use kar sakte ho, kyunki unme se zyadatar real-time guarantees nahi dete. Isi wajah se real-time development mehngi hai, aur zyadatar safety-critical embedded devices mein use hoti hai. Real-time ka matlab high performance bhi nahi hai. Real-time systems ka throughput kam ho sakta hai, kyunki unhe sabse pehle timely responses ko rakhna padta hai. Book yahan us idea se jodti hai ki resource sharing se performance badalta rehta hai.

Zyadatar server-side data processing systems ke liye real-time guarantees na economical hain, na suitable. Isliye in systems ko un pauses aur clock instability ke saath jeena padta hai jo non-real-time environment mein chalne se aati hain.

Garbage collection ka impact kam karna

Process pauses ke bure effects ko mehnge real-time scheduling ke bina bhi kam kiya ja sakta hai. Language runtimes ko garbage collection kab schedule karna hai, ismein thodi azaadi hoti hai. Woh track kar sakte hain ki objects kitni tezi se allocate ho rahe hain aur time ke saath kitni free memory bachi hai.

Ek emerging idea yeh hai ki GC pause ko node ke ek chhote, planned outage ki tarah treat karein. Jab ek node apna garbage collect kar raha ho, tab baaki nodes clients ki requests handle karte hain. Agar runtime application ko warn kar sake ki GC pause jaldi aane wala hai, toh application us node ko nayi requests bhejna band kar sakti hai. Woh chal rahi requests ke khatam hone ka wait karti hai, aur phir GC tab chalata hai jab koi request active na ho. Isse clients se GC pauses chhup jaate hain aur response time ke high percentiles kam hote hain. Kuch latency-sensitive financial trading systems yeh approach use karte hain.

Ek variant yeh hai ki garbage collector sirf short-lived objects ke liye use karein, jo collect karne mein fast hote hain. Process ko periodically restart kiya jaata hai, us se pehle ki woh itne long-lived objects jama kare ki full collection chahiye. Ek time par ek node restart hota hai, aur planned restart se pehle traffic us se hata diya jaata hai, bilkul Chapter 4 ke rolling upgrade ki tarah.

Yeh measures garbage collection pauses ko poori tarah nahi rok sakte. Lekin application par unka impact kaam ki hadd tak kam zaroor kar sakte hain.

Knowledge, Truth aur Lies

Ab tak is chapter mein humne dekha ki distributed systems ek single computer ke programs se kaise alag hote hain. Yahan shared memory nahi hoti. Sirf unreliable network par message passing hoti hai, jisme delay kabhi kam kabhi zyada ho sakta hai. Upar se partial failures, unreliable clocks aur process pauses ki problem alag.

Agar tum distributed systems ke aadi nahi ho, toh yeh sab kaafi confusing lagta hai. Ek node kisi cheez ke baare mein pakka nahi jaan sakta. Woh sirf un messages se andaza laga sakta hai jo network se usse mile, ya nahi mile. Doosre node ki state, jaise usne kaunsa data store kiya hai ya woh sahi chal raha hai ya nahi, yeh pata karne ka ek hi tarika hai: uske saath messages exchange karna. Agar remote node jawab nahi deta, toh uski state jaanne ka koi tarika nahi hai. Network ki problem aur node ki problem mein bharose ke saath fark karna possible nahi hota.

Yahan se kuch philosophical sawal uthte hain. Hamare system mein kya sach hai aur kya jhooth, yeh hum kaise jaanein? Agar cheezein sense aur measure karne ke hamare tarike hi unreliable hain, toh us knowledge par hum kitna bharosa kar sakte hain? Kya software ko woh niyam follow karne chahiye jo hum physical world se expect karte hain, jaise cause aur effect?

Ek working system banane ke liye zindagi ka matlab solve karna zaroori nahi hai. Distributed system mein hum apne behavior ke baare mein assumptions likh sakte hain, jise system model kehte hain, aur system ko aise design kar sakte hain ki woh un assumptions par khara utre. Kisi diye hue system model ke andar algorithms ko correct prove kiya ja sakta hai. Matlab underlying model bahut kam promise kare, tab bhi reliable behavior possible hai.

Lekin unreliable system model mein software ko well behaved banana aasaan nahi hai. Is chapter ka baaki hissa distributed systems mein knowledge aur truth explore karta hai. Isse hume samajhne mein madad milti hai ki hum kaunse assumptions le sakte hain aur kaunse guarantees dena chahte hain. Phir Chapter 9 un algorithms ko dekhta hai jo khaas assumptions ke under khaas guarantees dete hain.

Truth ka faisla majority karti hai

Maan lo network mein ek asymmetric fault hai. Ek node ko apne taraf bheje gaye saare messages mil jaate hain, lekin jo messages woh bhejta hai woh drop ho jaate hain ya late pahunchte hain. Node bilkul theek chal raha hai aur doosre nodes ki requests receive kar raha hai. Par doosre nodes ko uske responses kabhi milte hi nahi. Kuch timeout ke baad woh use dead declare kar dete hain. Book ise ek nightmare bataati hai. Node ko kabristan le jaaya ja raha hai, woh chilla raha hai ki main zinda hoon, par koi sun nahi sakta, isliye funeral chalta rehta hai.

Example

Book mein teen scenarios hain, aur har ek mein ek node apne hi view par bharosa nahi kar sakta.

Scenario one: silent node. Node messages receive karta hai, par uske replies gayab ho jaate hain. Doosre nodes timeout hone par use dead declare kar dete hain. Node kehta rehta hai ki main theek hoon, par koi sunta nahi.

Scenario two: jo node notice kar leta hai. Thodi kam darawni version mein node dekhta hai ki uske apne messages acknowledge nahi ho rahe, toh use samajh aa jaata hai ki network mein koi fault hai. Phir bhi doosre nodes use dead declare kar dete hain, aur node is baare mein kuch kar nahi sakta.

Scenario three: lamba pause. Ek node ko poore ek minute ka lamba stop-the-world garbage collection pause lag jaata hai. Uske saare threads freeze ho jaate hain, toh woh na koi request process karta hai na koi response bhejta hai. Doosre nodes wait karte hain, retry karte hain, thak jaate hain, aur aakhir mein node ko dead declare kar dete hain. Phir garbage collection khatam hota hai, aur node aise kaam karne lagta hai jaise kuch hua hi nahi. Doosre nodes ko hairani hoti hai ki jise dead maana tha woh bilkul healthy wapas aa gaya aur khushi se baatein kar raha hai. Node ko pata hi nahi chalta ki ek minute guzar gaya, kyunki uske hisaab se toh bas zara sa time hi beeta hai.

In kahaniyon ka sabak yeh hai ki ek node apne judgment par hamesha bharosa nahi kar sakta. Distributed system ek single node par depend nahi kar sakta, kyunki koi bhi node kabhi bhi fail ho sakta hai, aur isse system atak sakta hai aur recover nahi kar paayega.

Isliye kaafi distributed algorithms quorum par depend karte hain, yani nodes ke beech ek vote. Decision ke liye kai nodes se minimum number mein votes chahiye, toh system kisi ek node par depend nahi karta. Reading aur writing ke liye quorums book mein Chapter 5 mein hain.

Isme yeh decision bhi aata hai ki kisi node ko dead declare karna hai ya nahi. Agar nodes ka quorum kisi doosre node ko dead declare kar de, toh us node ko dead hi maana jaayega, chahe woh khud ko poori tarah zinda mehsoos kar raha ho. Akele node ko quorum ka decision maan kar step down karna padta hai.

Aam taur par quorum ek absolute majority hota hai, matlab aadhe se zyada nodes, haalaanki doosre kisam ke quorums bhi possible hain. Majority quorum se kuch nodes fail hone par bhi system chalta rehta hai. Teen nodes ho toh ek failure tolerate ho jaata hai. Paanch nodes ho toh do failures. Yeh safe bhi hai. System mein ek hi majority ho sakti hai, isliye do majorities ek saath conflicting decisions par nahi pahunch sakti. Quorums use karne wale consensus algorithms Chapter 9 mein cover hote hain.

Leader aur Lock

Kai systems ko kisi cheez ka bilkul ek hi chahiye hota hai. Jaise:

  • Database partition ka leader sirf ek node ho sakta hai. Do leaders hue toh split brain hoga, jisme do nodes conflicting writes accept karte hain.
  • Kisi resource ya object ka lock sirf ek transaction ya client hold kar sakta hai. Isse do writers use corrupt nahi kar paate.
  • Ek particular username sirf ek user register kar sakta hai, kyunki username se user ki unique pehchaan honi chahiye.

Distributed system mein yeh karne ke liye dhyaan chahiye. Node ko lagta ho ki woh chosen one hai, chahe partition ka leader ho, lock ka holder ho, ya us user ka handler ho jisne username grab kiya, tab bhi iska matlab yeh nahi ki quorum bhi agree karta hai. Ho sakta hai node kabhi leader raha ho. Par agar beech mein network interruption ya GC pause ki wajah se doosre nodes ne use dead declare kar diya, toh shayad use demote kar diya gaya ho, aur koi doosra leader pehle hi elect ho chuka ho.

Agar aisa node chosen one ki tarah kaam karta rahe, toh jis system ko carefully design nahi kiya gaya, usme dikkat ho sakti hai. Woh apne self-appointed role mein doosre nodes ko messages bhej sakta hai. Agar doosre nodes uski baat maan lein, toh poora system kuch galat kar sakta hai.

Book mein locking ke galat implementation se hui ek data corruption bug ka example hai. HBase mein pehle yeh problem thi. Maan lo tum chahte ho ki storage service ki ek file ko ek time par sirf ek client access kare, kyunki kai clients likhenge toh file corrupt ho jaayegi. Tum yeh aise karne ki koshish karte ho ki har client file ko haath lagane se pehle lock service se lease le.

Example

Figure 8-4 ka failure step by step dekhte hain. Client 1 ko file ki lease mil jaati hai. Phir client 1 bahut der ke liye pause ho jaata hai, shayad lambe GC pause se. Lease expire ho jaati hai. Client 2 usi file par lease le leta hai aur usme likhna shuru kar deta hai. Phir client 1 wapas aata hai. Use galat tarike se lagta hai ki uski lease abhi valid hai, isliye woh bhi file mein likh deta hai. Dono clients ke writes takra jaate hain, aur file corrupt ho jaati hai.

Yeh wahi process-pause problem hai jo is chapter mein pehle aayi thi. Lease hold karne wala client bahut der ke liye pause ho sakta hai, aur wapas aane par use pata nahi hota ki uski lease expire ho chuki hai.

Fencing Tokens

Jab koi lock ya lease kisi resource ka access protect karti hai, jaise Figure 8-4 ki file storage, tab hume yeh pakka karna hota hai ki jis node ko galat yakeen hai ki woh chosen one hai, woh baaki system ko disturb na kar sake. Iske liye ek simple technique hai, jise fencing kehte hain.

Maan lo lock server jab bhi lock ya lease grant karta hai, toh saath mein ek fencing token bhi return karta hai. Yeh ek number hota hai jo har baar lock grant hone par badhta hai. Lock service use har baar increment kar sakti hai. Phir storage service ko bheja gaya har write client ka current fencing token include karega.

Example

Book Figure 8-5 samjhati hai. Client 1 token 33 ke saath lease acquire karta hai. Phir woh lambe pause mein chala jaata hai, aur lease expire ho jaati hai. Client 2 token 34 ke saath lease acquire karta hai. Number hamesha badhta hai. Client 2 apna write storage service ko bhejta hai, token 34 ke saath. Baad mein client 1 jaagta hai aur apna write bhejta hai, apne purane token 33 ke saath. Storage server ko yaad hai ki woh pehle hi ek zyada token, 34, wala write process kar chuka hai. Isliye woh token 33 wali request reject kar deta hai. Client 1 ka stale write block ho jaata hai.

Numbering lock server karta hai, aur checking storage server. Storage ko tokens actively check karne padte hain: jis write ka token pehle process ho chuke token se purana ho, use reject kar dena hai. Clients ka apna lock status check karna kaafi nahi hai, kyunki paused client ko pata hi nahi hota ki uska lock chala gaya.

Kuch resources fencing tokens ko directly support nahi karte. Phir bhi tum shayad iska koi workaround nikaal sakte ho. Jaise file storage service ke case mein tum fencing token ko file name mein daal sakte ho. Lekin koi na koi check zaroori hai, taaki lock ki protection ke bahar ki requests process na hon.

ZooKeeper, ek lock service, is tarah ka number de sakti hai. Uska transaction ID, jise zxid kehte hain, ya uska node version, jise cversion kehte hain, guaranteed monotonically badhta hai, isliye dono mein se koi bhi fencing token ban sakta hai.

Server par tokens check karna extra burden lag sakta hai. Lekin Kleppmann ke hisaab se yeh achhi cheez hai. Service ko yeh assume nahi karna chahiye ki uske clients hamesha sahi behave karenge. Clients aksar aise logon ke chalaye hote hain jinki priorities service chalane walon se alag hoti hain. Isliye har service ko accidentally abusive clients se khud ko protect karna chahiye.

Try karo

Ek client lock hold karta hai aur file storage service mein likhta hai. Maan lo storage service mein koi fencing check hai hi nahi. Events ka woh order batao jisme purana client naye client ka write overwrite kar de. Phir batao ki storage server par ek extra check, yani tokens compare karna, kya badal dega.

Byzantine Faults

Fencing tokens aise node ko pakad kar block kar sakte hain jo galti se kuch kar raha ho, jaise isliye ki use abhi tak pata nahi chala ki uski lease expire ho gayi hai. Lekin agar koi node intentionally system ko subvert karna chahe, toh woh aaram se fake fencing token ke saath messages bhej sakta hai.

Is book mein working assumption yeh hai ki nodes unreliable but honest hote hain. Fault ki wajah se woh slow ho sakte hain ya kabhi respond nahi karte. GC pause ya network delay ki wajah se unki state outdated ho sakti hai. Lekin agar koi node respond karta hai, toh woh apni jaankari ke hisaab se sach bolta hai. Woh protocol ke rules ke andar kaam kar raha hai.

Distributed systems ki problems kaafi mushkil ho jaati hain agar nodes jhooth bol sakein, yani arbitrary faulty ya corrupted responses bhej sakein. Jaise, ek node claim kar sakta hai ki usne message receive kiya, jabki usne kiya nahi. Aise behavior ko Byzantine fault kehte hain. Is untrusting environment mein agreement tak pahunchna Byzantine Generals Problem kehlaata hai.

The Byzantine Generals Problem

Byzantine Generals Problem, Two Generals Problem ka generalization hai. Us puzzle mein do army generals ko ek battle plan par agree karna hota hai. Woh do alag jagah camp kiye hue hain aur sirf messenger ke through baat kar sakte hain, aur messengers late ho sakte hain ya kho sakte hain, bilkul network ke packets ki tarah. Consensus ki is problem par Chapter 9 mein aur detail se baat hoti hai.

Byzantine version mein n generals hain jinhe agree karna hai, aur unme se kuch traitors hain. Zyadatar generals loyal hain aur sachche messages bhejte hain. Traitors chhupe rehkar fake messages bhej kar doosron ko deceive aur confuse karne ki koshish kar sakte hain. Traitors kaun hain, yeh pehle se kisi ko nahi pata.

Yeh naam history par ek mazaak hai. Byzantium ek ancient Greek city thi jo baad mein Constantinople bani, aur ab Istanbul hai. Is baat ka koi saboot nahi ki wahan ke generals doosron se zyada saazish karne wale the. Byzantine word politics mein computers se bahut pehle se kisi bahut zyada complicated, bureaucratic aur devious cheez ke liye use hota tha. Author Leslie Lamport ko aisi nationality chahiye thi jisse readers offend na hon, aur unhe salah di gayi thi ki kisi asli nationality ke naam par problem ka naam rakhna sahi nahi hoga.

Ek system Byzantine fault-tolerant hota hai agar woh tab bhi sahi chalta rahe jab kuch nodes malfunction karein aur protocol na maanein, ya malicious attackers network mein interfere karein. Book do situations batati hai jahan yeh matter karta hai:

  • Aerospace. Spacecraft ya aircraft mein radiation computer ki memory ya CPU register ka data corrupt kar sakta hai. Phir computer doosre nodes ko unpredictable tarike se respond kar sakta hai. Failure bahut mehenga padta hai, jaise aircraft crash ho jaana ya rocket ka International Space Station se takra jaana, isliye flight control systems ko Byzantine faults tolerate karne padte hain.
  • Aise organizations jo ek doosre par trust nahi karte. Jahan kai organizations shaamil hon, wahan kuch doosron ko cheat ya defraud karne ki koshish kar sakte hain. Node kisi doosri party ke messages par seedha bharosa nahi kar sakta, kyunki ho sakta hai woh bure irade se bheje gaye hon. Bitcoin jaise peer-to-peer networks aur doosri blockchains ek tarika hain jisse aapas mein bharosa na karne wali parties bina kisi central authority ke yeh agree kar leti hain ki transaction hua ya nahi.

Jis tarah ke systems ki yeh book baat karti hai, unme aam taur par maana jaata hai ki Byzantine faults nahi hote. Tumhare data center mein saare nodes tumhari organization ke control mein hain, toh unpar umeed hai ki bharosa kiya ja sakta hai. Radiation levels itne kam hain ki memory corruption badi problem nahi hai. Byzantine fault-tolerant protocols kaafi complicated hote hain, aur fault-tolerant embedded systems hardware ke support par depend karte hain. Zyadatar server-side data systems ke liye Byzantine fault tolerance deploy karne ki cost ise impractical bana deti hai.

Lekin web applications ko end-user ke control wale clients, jaise web browsers, se arbitrary aur malicious behavior expect karna padta hai. Isi wajah se input validation, sanitization aur output escaping itne zaroori hain, taaki SQL injection aur cross-site scripting jaise attacks rokein. Lekin Kleppmann yeh bhi kehte hain ki iske liye hum aam taur par Byzantine fault-tolerant protocols use nahi karte. Uski jagah server ko authority bana diya jaata hai ki client ka kaunsa behavior allowed hai. Peer-to-peer networks mein, jahan aisi koi central authority nahi hoti, Byzantine fault tolerance zyada relevant hai.

Example

Software bug ko bhi ek Byzantine fault maana ja sakta hai. Lekin agar tum har node par same software deploy karte ho, toh Byzantine fault-tolerant algorithm tumhe bacha nahi sakta. In algorithms ko aam taur par supermajority chahiye, yani do-tihai se zyada nodes sahi kaam kar rahe hon. Chaar nodes mein se zyada se zyada ek malfunction kar sakta hai. Is tarah bug se bachne ke liye tumhe same software ke chaar independent implementations chahiye honge, aur umeed karni hogi ki bug sirf ek mein ho.

Security bhi kuch aisi hi hai. Tum umeed kar sakte ho ki koi protocol tumhe vulnerabilities, security breaches aur malicious attacks se bacha lega. Book ke hisaab se yeh bhi realistic nahi hai. Zyadatar systems mein agar attacker ek node compromise kar le, toh woh shayad sabhi ko compromise kar sakta hai, kyunki sab par same software chal raha hai. Isliye authentication, access control, encryption aur firewalls jaise traditional tools hi attackers se bachne ki main protection bane rehte hain.

Jhooth bolne ke weak forms

Book maanti hai ki nodes aam taur par honest hote hain, phir bhi weak forms ke jhooth se bachne ke liye mechanisms jodna worth it ho sakta hai. Isme hardware problems, software bugs aur misconfiguration se bane invalid messages aate hain. Aisi protections poori Byzantine fault tolerance nahi hain, kyunki woh kisi determined attacker ko nahi rok paayengi. Lekin better reliability ki taraf yeh simple aur practical steps hain. Book teen examples deti hai:

  • Corrupted packets. Hardware faults ya operating systems, drivers aur routers ke bugs ki wajah se packets kabhi-kabhi corrupt ho jaate hain. Corrupted packets aam taur par TCP aur UDP ke built-in checksums se pakde jaate hain, lekin kabhi-kabhi nikal jaate hain. Apne application-level protocol mein simple checksums aam taur par kaafi protection de dete hain.
  • Bahar se aane wala input. Public application ko saara user input carefully check karna chahiye. Jaise, confirm karna ki value reasonable range ke andar hai, aur strings ki size limit karna taaki bada input huge memory allocations ke zariye denial of service na kara sake. Firewall ke peeche ki internal service kam strict checks se kaam chala sakti hai, lekin basic sanity checks, jaise protocol parsing mein, achhi idea hain.
  • Kai time servers. NTP client ko kai server addresses ke saath configure kiya ja sakta hai. Synchronize karte waqt woh sabse contact karta hai, unke errors ka estimate lagata hai, aur check karta hai ki zyadatar servers ek time range par agree karte hain. Jab tak zyadatar servers healthy hain, galat time batane wala misconfigured server outlier ki tarah detect hokar exclude ho jaata hai. Kai servers use karne se NTP sirf ek server use karne se zyada robust ho jaata hai.

System Model aur Reality

Distributed systems ki problems solve karne ke liye kaafi algorithms design kiye gaye hain. Jaise, Chapter 9 mein consensus problem ke solutions dekhe jaate hain. Useful hone ke liye in algorithms ko is chapter mein bataye distributed systems ke faults tolerate karne padte hain. Saath hi woh jis hardware aur software par chalte hain, uski details par zyada depend nahi hone chahiye.

Matlab hume jin faults ki expect hai, unhe formalize karna padega. Hum yeh system model define karke karte hain. Yeh ek abstraction hai jo batata hai ki algorithm kya assume kar sakta hai. Timing assumptions ke teen system models common use mein hain.

  • Synchronous model. Is model mein network delay, process pauses aur clock error teeno bounded maane jaate hain. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki clocks bilkul synchronized hain ya delay zero hai. Bas itna ki tumhe pata hai ki network delay, pauses aur clock drift kabhi kisi fixed upper bound se zyada nahi honge. Book ke hisaab se yeh zyadatar practical systems ka realistic model nahi hai, kyunki unbounded delays aur pauses hote hain.
  • Partially synchronous model. Yahan system zyadatar time synchronous jaisa behave karta hai, lekin kabhi-kabhi network delay, process pauses aur clock drift ki bounds cross kar jaata hai. Book ise kai systems ka realistic model kehti hai. Zyadatar time networks aur processes sahi behave karte hain, warna kuch kaam hota hi nahi. Lekin koi bhi timing assumption kabhi na kabhi toot sakti hai. Aisa hone par delay, pauses aur clock error arbitrarily bade ho sakte hain.
  • Asynchronous model. Algorithm ko koi timing assumption karne ki ijaazat nahi hoti. Uske paas clock tak nahi hota, toh woh timeouts use nahi kar sakta. Is model ke liye kuch algorithms design ho sakte hain, lekin yeh bahut restrictive hai.

Timing ke alawa node failures bhi dekhne padte hain. Nodes ke teen common models book batati hai:

  • Crash-stop faults. Node sirf ek tarah se fail ho sakta hai, crash hokar. Woh kisi bhi moment achanak respond karna band kar sakta hai, aur uske baad hamesha ke liye gaya. Woh kabhi wapas nahi aata.
  • Crash-recovery faults. Node kisi bhi moment crash ho sakta hai aur kuch unknown time baad dobara respond karna shuru kar sakta hai. Uska stable storage, yani nonvolatile disk storage, crash ke baad bhi bacha rehta hai. Lekin uski in-memory state lost maani jaati hai.
  • Byzantine (arbitrary) faults. Node kuch bhi kar sakta hai, doosre nodes ko trick aur deceive karne ki koshish bhi.

Real systems ko model karne ke liye aam taur par crash-recovery faults ke saath partially synchronous model sabse useful hai. Neeche ki table teeno timing models ka summary deti hai.

Timing modelKya assume karta haiKitna realistic
SynchronousDelay, pauses aur clock error ki known upper boundsRealistic nahi. Unbounded delays aur pauses hote hain.
Partially synchronousBounds zyadatar time hold karti hain, aur kabhi-kabhi buri tarah toot jaati hainKai systems ke liye realistic, aur modeling ke liye usual choice.
AsynchronousKoi timing assumption nahi, aur clock nahi, toh timeouts bhi nahiDesign karna possible hai, lekin bahut restrictive.

Algorithm ki Correctness

Algorithm correct hai, yeh kehne ke liye hum uski properties describe kar sakte hain. Book sorting ko simple example ki tarah leti hai. Sorted output ki property yeh hai ki kisi bhi do distinct elements mein se jo left mein zyada door hai, woh right wale se chhota hota hai. Yeh bas formal tarika hai yeh kehne ka ki list sorted hai.

Isi tarah hum distributed algorithm se jo properties chahte hain, unhe likh sakte hain. Jaise, agar hum lock ke liye fencing tokens generate kar rahe hain, toh teen properties maang sakte hain:

  • Uniqueness. Fencing token ki do requests same value return nahi karti.
  • Monotonic sequence. Agar request x ne token tx return kiya, request y ne token ty return kiya, aur x y ke shuru hone se pehle complete ho gayi, toh tx ty se chhota hai.
  • Availability. Jo node fencing token maangta hai aur crash nahi hota, use eventually response mil jaata hai.

Algorithm kisi system model mein tab correct hai jab woh un sabhi situations mein apni properties hamesha satisfy kare jo model ke hisaab se ho sakti hain. Lekin yahan ek sawal uthta hai. Agar saare nodes crash ho jaayein, ya har network delay achanak infinitely lamba ho jaaye, toh koi bhi algorithm kuch nahi kar sakta. Model ko is case ka dhyaan rakhna padega.

Safety aur Liveness

Isse aur saaf karne ke liye book do tarah ki properties alag karti hai. Fencing example mein uniqueness aur monotonic sequence safety properties hain. Availability ek liveness property hai. Ek clue yeh hai ki liveness properties ki definition mein aksar eventually word hota hai. Aur haan, book batati hai, eventual consistency ek liveness property hai.

Safety ko aksar informally aise describe kiya jaata hai ki kuch bura nahi hota, aur liveness ko aise ki kuch achha eventually hota hai. Kleppmann in phrases ka zyada matlab nikaalne se mana karte hain, kyunki kya achha hai aur kya bura, yeh subjective hai. Asli definitions precise aur mathematical hoti hain.

  • Agar safety property violate ho, toh tum ek particular moment bata sakte ho jab woh tooti. Jaise, uniqueness violate hui ho toh tum exact woh operation pehchaan sakte ho jisne duplicate token return kiya. Safety property ek baar violate ho jaaye toh violation undo nahi ho sakta. Nuksaan ho chuka hota hai.
  • Liveness property ulti tarah kaam karti hai. Ho sakta hai woh kisi point par hold na kare. Jaise, node ne request bheji ho par abhi response na mila ho. Lekin hamesha umeed rehti hai ki future mein woh satisfy ho jaayegi, response aane se.

Yeh distinction hume mushkil system models mein madad karta hai. Distributed algorithms ke liye aam baat yeh hai ki safety properties hamesha hold karni chahiye, model ki har possible situation mein. Saare nodes crash ho jaayein ya poora network fail ho jaaye, tab bhi algorithm ko galat result return nahi karna chahiye. Liveness properties mein caveats allowed hain. Jaise, hum keh sakte hain ki request ko response tabhi chahiye jab nodes ki majority crash na hui ho, aur sirf tab jab network outage se eventually recover ho jaaye. Partially synchronous model maanta hai ki system eventually synchronous state mein wapas aata hai. Koi bhi network interruption sirf finite time tak rehti hai aur phir repair ho jaati hai.

System Models ko real world se map karna

Safety aur liveness, system models ke saath, yeh sochne mein bahut useful hain ki distributed algorithm correct hai ya nahi. Lekin jab tum practice mein algorithm implement karte ho, toh reality ki messy sachchaiyan wapas kaat leti ho. System model reality ka ek simplified abstraction nikalta hai.

Jaise, crash-recovery model ke algorithms aam taur par maante hain ki stable storage ka data crashes ke baad bacha rehta hai. Lekin agar disk ka data corrupt ho jaaye, ya hardware error ya misconfiguration se mit jaaye, toh kya hoga? Agar server mein firmware bug ho aur reboot par woh apni hard drives pehchaan hi na paaye, chahe drives sahi se attached hon, toh kya hoga?

Quorum algorithms is par depend karte hain ki har node jo data store karne ka claim karta hai, use yaad rakhe. Agar node ko amnesia ho jaaye aur woh pehle store kiya data bhool jaaye, toh quorum condition toot jaati hai, aur saath mein algorithm ki correctness bhi. Kleppmann sujhaate hain ki shayad ek naya system model chahiye, jisme stable storage zyadatar crashes se bachta hai par kabhi-kabhi kho jaata hai. Lekin us model par reason karna aur mushkil hai.

Theoretical description keh sakti hai ki kuch cheezein bas assume ki gayi hain ki hoti hi nahi. Non-Byzantine systems mein hume maanna padta hai ki kuch faults nahi ho sakte. Lekin real implementation ko phir bhi us case ke liye code chahiye ho sakta hai jab kuch aisa ho jaaye jo impossible maana gaya tha. Book batati hai ki yeh handling bhi shayad bas ek message print karke exit karne tak simat jaaye, taaki koi human operator gandagi saaf kare. Kleppmann ke hisaab se computer science aur software engineering ka fark shayad yahi hai.

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki theoretical system models bekaar hain. Bilkul ulta. Woh real systems ki complexity ko faults ke ek manageable set mein distill karne mein madad karte hain, jis par hum reason kar sakein. Isse hum problem samajh sakte hain aur use systematic tarike se solve kar sakte hain. Hum algorithm ko correct prove kar sakte hain yeh dikha kar ki uski properties kisi system model mein hamesha hold karti hain.

Proof is baat ki guarantee nahi deta ki implementation real system par hamesha sahi behave karega. Lekin yeh bahut achha pehla kadam hai. Theoretical analysis algorithm ki aisi problems nikaal sakta hai jo real system mein lambe time tak chhupi reh sakti hain, aur tabhi kaat-ti hain jab koi timing assumption kisi unusual situation mein toot jaaye. Kleppmann ka nateeja yeh hai ki theoretical analysis aur empirical testing dono barabar zaroori hain.

Summary

Short mein
  • Packets. Network par bheja gaya packet lost ya arbitrarily delayed ho sakta hai. Reply bhi lost ya delayed ho sakta hai. Toh agar reply na mile, tumhe bilkul pata nahi ki message pahuncha ya nahi.
  • Clocks. Node ki clock doosre nodes se kaafi out of sync ho sakti hai, NTP ke saath bhi. Woh achanak aage ya peeche jump kar sakti hai. Us par depend karna khatarnaak hai, kyunki shayad tumhare paas uske error interval ka achha measure hota hi nahi.
  • Processes. Process kisi bhi point par lambe time ke liye pause ho sakta hai, jaise stop-the-world garbage collector run ke dauraan. Doosre nodes use dead declare kar sakte hain, aur phir woh bina jaane ki woh paused tha, wapas zinda ho sakta hai.
  • Partial failure. Yeh partial failures distributed systems ki pehchaan hain. Jab bhi software doosre nodes se jude kisi kaam mein ho, woh fail ho sakta hai, random slow ho sakta hai, ya bilkul respond nahi kar sakta, aur eventually timeout ho jaata hai. Hum aisa software banane ki koshish karte hain jo partial failure tolerate kare, taaki kuch parts toote hon tab bhi poora system chalta rahe.
  • Detection mushkil hai. Faults tolerate karne ka pehla step unhe detect karna hai, aur yeh bhi mushkil hai. Zyadatar systems ke paas yeh batane ka accurate tarika nahi hota ki node fail hua ya nahi. Isliye algorithms timeouts par depend karte hain. Lekin timeouts network failures aur node failures mein fark nahi kar sakte, aur variable delays healthy node ko bhi crashed dikha sakte hain. Nodes degraded, yani limping, bhi ho sakte hain, jise handle karna clean failure se zyada mushkil hai. Book ek gigabit network card ka example deti hai jo driver bug ki wajah se 1 Kb/s par aa gaya.
  • Faults tolerate karna bhi mushkil hai. Machines ke beech koi global variable nahi, koi shared memory nahi, aur koi common knowledge nahi hai. Nodes yeh tak agree nahi kar sakte ki abhi time kya hai. Information sirf unreliable network par bhej kar hi flow hoti hai. Koi ek node akela koi bada decision safely nahi le sakta. Hume aise protocols chahiye jo doosre nodes ki madad lein aur quorum agreement tak pahunchne ki koshish karein.
  • Ho sake toh ek machine par rakhein. Aajkal ek single computer bahut kuch kar sakta hai, aur distributed systems engineers aksar kisi problem ko trivial maante hain agar woh ek computer par solve ho sakti ho. Ho sake toh woh dabba kholne se bachein. Lekin scalability distribute karne ki akeli wajah nahi hai. Fault tolerance aur low latency, data ko users ke paas rakh kar, single node se nahi mil sakti.
  • Yeh law of nature nahi hai. Book ne explore kiya ki unreliable networks, clocks aur processes avoidable hain ya nahi. Yeh avoidable hain. Hard real-time guarantees aur bounded delays possible hain, lekin yeh bahut mehenge hain aur hardware kam utilize hota hai. Zyadatar non-safety-critical systems expensive aur reliable ki jagah cheap aur unreliable chunte hain.
  • Supercomputers aur services. Supercomputer reliable parts maan kar chalta hai, isliye jab koi component fail hota hai toh poora job ruk kar restart hota hai. Distributed system theory mein service level par bina interruption ke hamesha chal sakta hai, kyunki faults aur maintenance node by node handle ho sakte hain. Practice mein, saare nodes par roll out hui ek bad configuration change distributed system ko ghutno par la sakti hai.
  • Aage kya. Yeh chapter problems ke baare mein tha aur intentionally pessimistic raha. Agla chapter solutions par jaata hai, aise algorithms ke saath jo in problems se nipatne ke liye design kiye gaye hain.

Khud check karein

  1. Ek client server ko write bhejta hai aur uski request timeout ho jaati hai. Client yeh kyun nahi bata sakta ki server ne write process kiya ya nahi?

    Jawab dekho

    Ho sakta hai request lost ho gayi ho, server down ya slow ho, ya server ne request process kar li ho aur sirf reply lost ya delayed hua ho. Asynchronous network mein sender ki taraf se yeh saare cases ek jaise dikhte hain. Client ko bas itna pata hota hai ki abhi tak koi response nahi aaya.

  2. Book ke clock example mein node 3 x = 2 timestamp 42.003 ke saath likhta hai, jabki node 1 ne x = 1 timestamp 42.004 ke saath likha tha. Last write wins later write ko kyun drop kar deta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Last write wins sabse bada timestamp wala write rakhta hai. Node 1 ka timestamp bada hai, toh x = 1 zyada recent lagta hai, jabki x = 2 asal mein baad mein hua tha. Clocks lagbhag synchronized thi, lekin kuch milliseconds ka skew order ulta karne ke liye kaafi tha, aur client B ka increment lost ho gaya.

  3. Lease holder check karta hai ki uski lease abhi valid hai, aur phir request process karne se pehle 15 seconds ke liye pause ho jaata hai. Kya galat hota hai, aur fencing tokens nuksaan se kaise bachate hain?

    Jawab dekho

    Pause ke dauraan lease expire ho sakti hai, aur koi doosra node leader ban kar write kar sakta hai. Paused node ko apne agle loop tak pata nahi chalta, isliye ho sakta hai woh pehle hi stale request process kar chuka ho. Fencing tokens ke saath storage server sabse bada token yaad rakhta hai jo usne dekha hai aur kisi bhi purane token wale write ko reject kar deta hai, toh stale write block ho jaata hai, chahe paused client ko lagta rahe ki lease uske paas hai.

  4. Spanner read-write transaction commit karne se pehle clock confidence interval ki length tak wait karta hai. Yeh wait kyun zaroori hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Wait yeh pakka karta hai ki baad ki kisi bhi transaction ka timestamp interval pehle wali se overlap na kare. Non-overlapping intervals dono transactions ka order prove karte hain, toh timestamps causality reflect karte hain. Wait ko chhota rakhne ke liye clock uncertainty kam rakhi jaati hai, har data center mein GPS receivers ya atomic clocks use karke.

Part II · Chapter 9

Consistency aur Consensus

Seedhi baat: ek distributed system kuch strong promises de sakta hai, jaise aisa behave karna ki data ki sirf ek hi copy hai. Lekin in promises ki keemat speed aur availability se chukani padti hai. Kai machines ka ek hi jawab par agree karna consensus kehlaata hai. Kaafi promises isi par tike hain, aur yeh dikhne se kaafi zyada mushkil hai.

Distributed system mein kai cheezein galat ho sakti hain, jaisa Chapter 8 mein dekha. Failure ka sabse simple jawab hai ki poori service fail hone do aur user ko error message dikha do. Agar yeh acceptable nahi hai, toh system ko fault tolerate karna padega. Matlab andar ka koi part toot bhi jaaye, tab bhi system sahi tarah se kaam karta rahe.

Is chapter mein fault-tolerant distributed systems banane ke algorithms aur protocols dekhenge. Hum maan ke chalte hain ki Chapter 8 ki har problem ho sakti hai. Packets lost, reorder, duplicate ho sakte hain, ya kisi bhi arbitrary time tak delay ho sakte hain. Clocks zyada se zyada approximate hi hoti hain. Nodes (system ki individual machines) pause ho sakte hain, jaise garbage collection ke dauraan, ya kisi bhi waqt crash ho sakte hain.

Fault-tolerant system banane ka sabse achha tarika yeh hai ki general-purpose abstractions dhoondho jinki guarantees kaam ki hon, unhe ek baar implement karo, aur applications ko un par rely karne do. Chapter 7 mein transactions ke liye yahi idea use hua tha. Transaction ke andar application aise pretend kar sakti hai ki crashes hote hi nahi (atomicity), koi aur usi waqt data ko touch nahi kar raha (isolation), aur disks kabhi fail nahi hoti (durability). Crashes aur disk failures toh hote hain, lekin transaction unhe chhupa leta hai.

Is chapter ka baaki hissa distributed systems ke liye aisi hi abstractions dhoondhta hai. Sabse important abstractions mein se ek hai consensus, yani saare nodes ko kisi baat par agree karwana. Network messages drop kar de aur processes fail ho jaayein, tab bhi consensus tak pahunchna ek hairaan karne wali tricky problem hai.

Consensus ka working implementation mil jaaye, toh applications use kai kaamon ke liye use kar sakti hain. Maan lo ek database hai jisme single-leader replication hai, yani ek node saari writes leta hai aur baaki unhe copy karte hain. Agar leader mar jaaye, toh database ko kisi doosre node par failover karna padega. Bache hue nodes consensus se naya leader elect kar sakte hain. Zaroori hai ki leader sirf ek ho, aur saare nodes agree hon ki woh kaun hai. Agar do nodes dono khud ko leader maanein, toh use split brain kehte hain, aur aksar isse data loss hota hai. Sahi consensus implementations isse bachne mein madad karti hain.

Chapter mein aage, “Distributed Transactions and Consensus” section mein, Kleppmann un algorithms ko dekhte hain jo consensus aur isse jude problems solve karte hain. Lekin pehle woh un guarantees aur abstractions ki range explore karte hain jo ek distributed system de sakta hai. Faults ke hote hue kuch cheezein ho sakti hain aur kuch nahi. In limits ko theory aur practice, dono mein gehraai se study kiya gaya hai. Yeh chapter un limits ka overview deta hai.

Researchers ne yeh topics decades tak study kiye hain, isliye material bahut hai aur yeh chapter sirf upar-upar chhu sakta hai. Book formal models aur proofs mein nahi jaati. Woh informal intuition par tikti hai, aur jo readers aur gehraai chahte hain, unke liye references diye gaye hain.

Consistency Guarantees

Chapter 5 mein replicated database ki timing wali problems dekhi thi, jise replication lag kehte hain. Agar tum ek hi moment par do database nodes ko dekho, toh aksar dono par alag data dikhega. Write requests alag nodes par alag time par pahunchti hain. Yeh kisi bhi replication method mein hota hai: single-leader, multi-leader ya leaderless.

Zyaadatar replicated databases kam se kam eventual consistency deti hain. Matlab agar tum writes rok do aur kaafi der wait karo, toh aakhir mein saari reads same value return karengi. Inconsistency temporary hoti hai aur khud theek ho jaati hai, bas network faults bhi eventually repair ho jaayein. Kleppmann kehte hain ki “convergence” behtar naam hota, kyunki saari replicas ek hi value par converge hoti hain.

Lekin eventual consistency ek bahut weak promise hai. Yeh nahi batati ki replicas kab converge karengi. Tab tak reads lagbhag kuch bhi return kar sakti hain, ya kuch bhi nahi. Jaise, tum ek value write karke turant read karo, toh ho sakta hai tumhe wahi value na dikhe jo abhi likhi thi. Read kisi aisi doosri replica par route ho sakti hai jise write abhi mila hi nahi. Chapter 5 mein ise apni hi writes read karne ki problem kaha tha.

Application developers ke liye eventual consistency mushkil hai, kyunki yeh normal single-threaded program ke variable se bahut alag behave karti hai. Variable mein value assign karke thodi der baad read karo, toh tum naayi value expect karte ho. Purani value ya error expect nahi karte. Database kuch-kuch aise variable jaisa lagta hai jise read aur write kar sakte hain, par uska behavior kaafi zyada complicated hai.

Database sirf weak guarantees de, toh tumhe uski limits ka lagatar dhyaan rakhna padta hai, warna tum anjaane mein zyada assume kar loge. Bugs subtle hote hain aur testing se pakadna mushkil hota hai, kyunki application zyaadatar waqt theek chalti hai. Eventual consistency ke edge cases aksar tab dikhte hain jab koi fault ho, jaise network interruption, ya jab bahut saari requests ek saath aayein.

Is chapter mein un stronger consistency models ko explore karenge jo ek data system de sakta hai. Stronger guarantees free nahi aati. Stronger guarantees wala system weaker guarantees wale system se slow ya kam fault-tolerant ho sakta hai. Phir bhi strong guarantees attractive hain, kyunki unhe sahi tarah se use karna aasaan hota hai. Kuch consistency models dekhne ke baad tum apni zaroorat ke hisaab se sahi model chunne mein behtar honge.

Distributed consistency models aur Chapter 7 ke transaction isolation levels mein kuch similarity hai. Lekin zyaadatar yeh alag concerns hain. Transaction isolation ka main kaam ek saath chalne wali transactions ke beech race conditions se bachna hai. Distributed consistency ka main kaam replicas ko delays aur faults ko ek doosre ke saath sync mein rakhna hai, chaahe delays aur faults hon.

Chapter teen jude hue areas cover karta hai. Shuru linearizability se hota hai, jo common use ke sabse strong consistency models mein se ek hai, aur uske pros aur cons dekhte hain. Phir dekhte hain ki distributed system mein events ki ordering kaise hoti hai, khaaskar causality aur total ordering. Aakhir mein dekhte hain ki distributed transaction ko atomically commit kaise karein. Yeh last topic consensus problem tak le jaata hai.

Linearizability

Eventually consistent database mein tum do replicas se ek hi waqt par ek hi sawaal poocho, toh dono alag jawab de sakti ho. Yeh confusing hai. Kaafi aasaan hota agar database yeh illusion de ki sirf ek replica hai, yani data ki sirf ek copy. Tab har client ko same data dikhta, aur replication lag ki chinta kisi ko nahi karni padti.

Is idea ko linearizability kehte hain. Ise atomic consistency, strong consistency, immediate consistency ya external consistency bhi kaha jaata hai. Exact definition subtle hai, aur is section ka baaki hissa use samjhata hai. Basic idea yeh hai ki system aisa dikhe jaise data ki sirf ek copy hai, aur us copy par har operation atomic hai (sab ek saath ho jaata hai, beech ka partial state kabhi dikhta nahi).

Linearizable system mein, jaise hi ek client ek write successfully khatam karta hai, uske baad padhne wale har client ko abhi likhi hui value dikhni chahiye. Read ki hui value sabse recent honi chahiye. Woh kisi stale cache ya lagging replica se nahi aa sakti. Yani linearizability ek recency guarantee hai. Ab ek aise system ka example dekhte hain jo linearizable nahi hai.

Example

Book mein ek sports website ka example hai jo linearizable nahi thi. Alice aur Bob ek hi kamre mein baithe hain, dono apne phones par 2014 FIFA World Cup final ka result dekh rahe hain. Step by step yeh hota hai:

  1. Final ka score announce hota hai.
  2. Alice apna page refresh karti hai, winner dekhti hai, aur excited hokar Bob ko bata deti hai.
  3. Bob apne phone par reload dabata hai. Uski request ek aisi database replica ke paas jaati hai jo peeche chal rahi hai.
  4. Uske phone par ab bhi game chalta hua dikhta hai.

Agar Alice aur Bob ne bilkul ek hi moment par reload kiya hota, toh do alag results hairaani ki baat nahi hoti, kyunki kisi ko pata nahi ki server ne har request kab handle ki. Lekin Bob ne request Alice ko score bolte sunne ke baad shuru ki. Isliye woh expect karta hai ki uska result kam se kam Alice jitna fresh ho. Uska stale result linearizability tod deta hai.

System ko linearizable kya banata hai?

Basic idea simple hai: system data ki ek single copy jaisa dikhna chahiye. Lekin iska exact matlab pin down karne mein thodi care lagti hai. Ise precise banane ke liye Kleppmann kuch aur examples lete hain.

Maan lo teen clients ek hi key x ko read aur write kar rahe hain. Research literature mein aisi single value ko register kehte hain. Practice mein yeh key-value store ki ek key, relational database ki ek row, ya document database ka ek document ho sakta hai. Book ki picture sirf yeh dikhati hai ki clients ko kya dikhta hai, database ke andar kya hai woh nahi. Har bar ek client request hai. Bar ka left end woh waqt hai jab request bheji gayi, aur right end woh jab reply aaya. Network delays alag-alag hote hain, isliye client ko kabhi exact nahi pata hota ki database ne uski request kab handle ki. Use bas itna pata hai ki handling bhejne aur receive karne ke beech kahin hui.

Register do tarah ke operations support karta hai:

  • read(x) ⇒ v ka matlab hai ki client ne register x padhne ko kaha, aur database ne value v return ki.
  • write(x, v) ⇒ r ka matlab hai ki client ne register x ko value v par set karne ko kaha, aur database ne r se reply kiya, jo ya toh ok hota hai ya error.

Ab ek register x lo jo 0 se start hota hai. Client C value 1 write karta hai. Is dauraan clients A aur B latest value padhne ke liye database ko baar-baar poll karte rehte hain. A aur B ko kya dikh sakta hai?

  • Jo read write shuru hone se pehle khatam ho jaaye, woh purani value, yani 0, return karegi.
  • Jo read write khatam hone ke baad shuru ho, woh naayi value, yani 1, return karegi, agar database linearizable hai. Write apne start aur end ke beech kisi point par handle hua tha. Write ke end ke baad shuru hui read ko write ke baad hi handle hona padega, isliye use nayi value dikhni hi chahiye.
  • Jo reads time mein write ke saath overlap karti hain, woh 0 ya 1 dono mein se kuch bhi return kar sakti hain. Hum nahi bata sakte ki read handle hote waqt write ka asar ho chuka hai ya nahi. Aise reads ko write ke saath concurrent kehte hain.

Yeh abhi bhi kaafi nahi hai. Agar write ke saath overlap karne wali reads purani ya nayi, kuch bhi value return kar sakti hain, toh write chalte hue readers ko value 0 aur 1 ke beech kai baar idhar-udhar hoti dikh sakti hai. Data ki single copy ki nakal karne wale system se hum yeh expect nahi karte. (Aisa register jisme overlapping reads purani ya nayi value return kar sakti hain, regular register kehlaata hai. Yeh linearizable se weak hai.)

Isse theek karne ke liye linearizability ek aur rule jodti hai. Jaise hi koi bhi read naayi value return kar de, uske baad ki har read, chahe usi client ki ho ya kisi aur ki, wahi naayi value return karegi. Socho ki write ke start aur end ke beech kisi moment par x ki value atomically 0 se 1 ho jaati hai. Ek read ne 1 dekh liya, toh us point ke baad ki saari reads ko 1 hi dikhna chahiye, chahe write formally khatam na hua ho.

Yeh aise chalta hai. Client A sabse pehle nayi value 1 padhta hai. A ki read return hote hi client B ek nayi read shuru karta hai. B ki read A ki read khatam hone ke baad shuru hui, isliye B ko bhi 1 return karna hoga, chahe C ka write abhi chal hi raha ho. Yeh bilkul Alice aur Bob wali situation hai. Alice ne naya result dekh liya, toh Bob ko bhi dikhna chahiye.

Asli idea

Linearizability ka matlab hai koi bhi client ek baar naayi value padh le, toh uske baad ki har read ko wahi value ya usse bhi nayi value return karni hogi. System aisa dikhna chahiye jaise data ki sirf ek copy hai.

Agli picture dikhati hai ki har operation exactly kahan effect mein aata hai. Neeche ki timeline wahi idea simple form mein hai. Ek client write karta hai, aur do doosre read karte hain. Jo read kisi aisi read ke baad shuru ho jisne naayi value dekh li hai, woh bhi naayi value hi return karegi. Highlighted bar bura outcome hai.

Phir Kleppmann ek zyada complex case dikhate hain, jisme teesri kism ka operation judta hai: compare-and-set, jo cas(x, vold, vnew) ⇒ r likha jaata hai. Compare-and-set ek atomic operation hai. Agar x ki current value v_old ke barabar hai, toh database use v_new kar deta hai. Agar x, v_old ke barabar nahi hai, toh register ko chhoda jaata hai aur operation error return karta hai. Yahan r database ka reply hai, ok ya error.

Is zyada detailed picture mein har operation par ek marker hai, us moment par jab lagta hai ki woh effect mein aaya. Markers ko order mein jodein, toh result register ke liye ek valid sequence hona chahiye. Har read ko apne se pehle ke sabse recent write ki set ki hui value return karni hogi. Linearizability yeh bhi maangti hai ki jodi hui line hamesha time mein aage badhe, kabhi peeche na jaaye. Yahi recency ki guarantee deta hai: ek baar nayi value write ya read ho jaaye, toh har baad ki read use tab tak dekhti hai jab tak woh overwrite na ho.

Us picture ki kuch details par Kleppmann dhyaan dilate hain:

  • Client B ne apni read pehle bheji. Phir client D ne x ko 0 set karne ki request bheji, aur uske baad client A ne x ko 1 set karne ki. Phir bhi B ki read 1 return karti hai, jo A ne likhi thi. Yeh acceptable hai. Matlab database ne pehle D ka write handle kiya, phir A ka write, phir B ki read. Requests concurrent thi, isliye yeh order allowed hai. Shayad B ki request network mein delay ho gayi aur dono writes ke baad hi database tak pahunchi.
  • B ki read ne 1 tab return kar diya jab A ko apne write ka database se ok abhi mila nahi tha. Yeh bhi theek hai. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki value likhe jaane se pehle padh li gayi. A ko jaane wala ok reply bas wapsi mein delay ho gaya.
  • Yeh model koi transaction isolation assume nahi karta. Doosre clients kisi bhi waqt value badal sakte hain. Jaise, C pehle 1 padhta hai aur phir 2, kyunki B ne C ki do reads ke beech value badal di. Compare-and-set check kar sakta hai ki value tumhare neeche se badli nahi hai. B aur C ke compare-and-set requests succeed hote hain. D ka fail hota hai, kyunki database ne jab use handle kiya tab x ab 0 nahi tha.
  • B ki last read, jo shaded bar mein dikhayi gayi hai, linearizable nahi hai. Woh C ke compare-and-set ke saath overlap karti hai, jo x ko 2 se 4 karta hai. Koi aur request na hoti, toh B ki read ka 2 return karna theek hota. Lekin client A B ki read shuru hone se pehle hi naayi value 4 padh chuka hai. Isliye B A ke dekhe se purani value return nahi kar sakta. Yeh phir se Alice aur Bob wali situation hai.

Linearizability ke peeche ki intuition yahi hai, aur formal definition ise aur precise banati hai. Real system linearizably behave karta hai ya nahi, yeh test karna possible hai, par mehenga hai. Tum har request aur reply ki timing record karte ho, phir check karte ho ki unhe ek valid sequential order mein arrange kiya ja sakta hai ya nahi.

Linearizability aur Serializability mein fark

Linearizability ko Chapter 7 ki serializability se confuse karna aasaan hai. Dono words ka matlab kuch aisa lagta hai ki “operations ko ek sequential order mein arrange kiya ja sakta hai.” Lekin yeh do alag guarantees hain, aur fark matter karta hai.

Serializability transactions ki ek isolation property hai. Ek transaction kai objects, jaise rows, documents ya records, read aur write kar sakta hai. Serializability guarantee deti hai ki transactions aise behave karein jaise ek ke baad ek chale, har ek agle ke shuru hone se pehle poora complete ho. Serial order us order se alag ho sakta hai jisme transactions actually chali thi.

Linearizability ek single object, yani ek register, ki reads aur writes par recency guarantee hai. Yeh operations ko transactions mein group nahi karti. Isliye yeh write skew jaisi problems nahi rokti, jo Chapter 7 mein bataye the, jab tak tum conflicts ko materialize karne jaise extra steps na lo.

Database dono properties de sakta hai, aur is combination ko strict serializability ya strong one-copy serializability (strong-1SR) kehte hain. Two-phase locking par ya actual serial execution par based serializability implementations aam taur par linearizable hoti hain. Serializable snapshot isolation linearizable nahi hai. Woh readers aur writers ke beech lock contention se bachne ke liye ek consistent snapshot se padhta hai. Snapshot ka poora point yeh hai ki usme snapshot se nayi writes shamil nahi hoti. Isliye snapshot se hui reads linearizable nahi hoti.

Trade-offs
PropertySerializabilityLinearizability
Kis par lagu hoti haiAisi transactions jo kai objects touch karti hainEk register (ek object) ki reads aur writes
GuaranteeResults transactions ke kisi ek-ek karke wale order se match karte hain. Woh order real order se alag ho sakta hai.Har operation ek point in time par effect mein aata hai, real time order mein, isliye reads ko latest write dikhta hai
Khud se write skew rokti haiHaan, jab true serializability ke taur par implement hoNahi, kyunki yeh operations ko transactions mein group nahi karti
Typical implementationsTwo-phase locking aur actual serial execution aam taur par linearizable hote hain. Serializable snapshot isolation nahi hota.Consensus-based coordination services aur leader se hone wali single-leader reads

Linearizability par rely karna

Linearizability ki zaroorat asal mein kab padti hai? Sports match ka final score check karna ek halka example hai. Kuch seconds purana result shayad hi koi nuksaan kare. Lekin kuch areas hain jahan system ke sahi kaam karne ke liye linearizability zaroori hai.

Locking aur leader election. Single-leader replication wale system ko pakka karna hota hai ki sach mein sirf ek leader hai, kai nahi. Leader elect karne ka ek tarika lock use karna hai. Jo bhi node start hota hai, woh lock acquire karne ki koshish karta hai, aur jo succeed hota hai woh leader ban jaata hai. Lock chahe jaise bhi implement ho, woh linearizable hona chahiye. Saare nodes agree hon ki lock kis node ke paas hai, warna lock bekaar hai. Apache ZooKeeper aur etcd jaisi coordination services aksar distributed locks aur leader election ke liye use hoti hain. Yeh consensus algorithms se fault-tolerant tarike mein linearizable operations deti hain. Consensus is chapter mein aage cover hoga. Locks aur leader election ko sahi implement karne mein ab bhi kaafi subtle details hote hain, jaise Chapter 8 mein bataya fencing issue. Apache Curator jaisi libraries ZooKeeper ke upar higher-level recipes deti hain. Phir bhi in kaamon ki basic foundation ek linearizable storage service hi hai.

Kuch distributed databases mein locks ka use bahut finer level par bhi hota hai. Oracle Real Application Clusters (RAC) har disk page ke liye ek lock use karta hai, jisme kai nodes same disk storage share karte hain. Yeh linearizable locks har transaction ke critical path par hote hain, isliye RAC deployments mein aam taur par database nodes ke beech dedicated network hota hai.

Constraints aur uniqueness guarantees. Databases mein uniqueness constraints common hain. Ek username ya email address sirf ek hi user ko identify karna chahiye. File storage service mein do files ka path aur name same nahi ho sakta. Agar tum yeh data likhte waqt hi enforce karna chahte ho, taaki do log ek saath same name ka user ya file banayein toh ek ko error mile, toh tumhe linearizability chahiye. Yeh lock jaisa hai. Koi username register karta hai, toh woh us name par lock acquire karne jaisa hai. Yeh atomic compare-and-set jaisa bhi hai: username ko is user ke ID par set karo, bas agar woh pehle se liya hua na ho.

Yahi issue doosre rules mein bhi aata hai. Bank account ka balance kabhi negative nahi hona chahiye. Warehouse mein jitna stock hai usse zyada items nahi bechne chahiye. Do log flight ya theater mein ek hi seat book nahi kar sakte. In har rule ko ek single, up-to-date value chahiye, jaise account balance, stock level ya seat occupancy, jis par saare nodes agree hon.

Real applications mein kabhi-kabhi in rules ko loosely handle kiya jaata hai. Flight overbook ho jaaye, toh airline customers ko doosri flight par shift kar sakti hai aur compensation offer kar sakti hai. Us case mein linearizability ki zaroorat nahi bhi ho sakti.
