Aise loosely enforced rules par Kleppmann timeliness aur integrity ki discussion mein wapas aate hain. Lekin hard uniqueness constraint, jaisa relational database enforce karta hai, uske liye linearizability chahiye. Doosre constraints, jaise foreign key references ya simple attribute checks, linearizability ke bina bhi implement ho sakte hain.

Cross-channel timing dependencies. Football wale example ko dobara dekho. Bob ko pata sirf isliye chala ki uska result stale hai kyunki communication ka ek doosra channel tha: Alice ki awaaz. Alice kuch na bolti, toh Bob dobara refresh karta aur aakhir mein final score dekh leta. Violation isliye noticed hua kyunki ek second channel tha.

Computer systems mein bhi yahi pattern hota hai. Maan lo ek website hai jahan users photos upload karte hain, aur ek background process photos ko chhote thumbnails mein resize karta hai taaki woh jaldi download hon. Web server image resizer ko message queue ke through instruct karta hai (queues Chapter 11 mein cover hongi). Web server poori photo queue par nahi daalta, kyunki zyaadatar message brokers chhote messages ke liye bane hote hain, aur ek photo kai megabytes ki ho sakti hai. Iske bajaye photo pehle file storage service mein likhi jaati hai. Woh write complete hone ke baad resize karne ka instruction queue par jaata hai.

File storage service linearizable hai, toh system theek chalta hai. Agar nahi hai, toh race ho sakti hai. Message queue, yani steps 3 aur 4, storage service ke andar ki internal replication se tez ho sakti hai. Step 5 mein resizer image fetch kare, toh use photo ka purana version dikh sakta hai, ya koi photo hi nahi. Agar woh purana version resize kar de, toh storage mein full-size image aur thumbnail hamesha ke liye inconsistent ho jaate hain.

Yeh problem isliye hoti hai kyunki do communication channels hain: file storage aur message queue. Linearizability ki recency guarantee ke bina yeh dono channels race kar sakte hain. Yeh wahi race hai jo Alice aur Bob ke example mein thi, jahan database replication aur Alice ki awaaz do channels the.

Linearizability akela fix nahi hai, lekin samajhne mein sabse aasaan hai. Extra channel tumhare control mein ho, jaise message queue hai par Alice ki awaaz nahi, toh tum doosre approaches use kar sakte ho. Yeh Chapter 5 ke apni hi writes padhne wale ideas jaise hain, lekin inme complexity badh jaati hai.

Linearizable systems implement karna

Ab jab humne dekh liya ki linearizability kahan kaam aati hai, toh aisa system kaise banayein jo use de? Sabse simple jawab, kyunki linearizability ka matlab hai “aise behave karo jaise data ki ek hi copy hai”, yeh hai ki sach mein sirf ek copy rakho. Lekin single copy faults tolerate nahi kar sakti. Jis node par woh hai woh fail ho jaaye, toh data lost ho jaata hai, ya kam se kam node wapas aane tak unavailable rehta hai.

System ko fault-tolerant banane ka aam tarika replication hai, jisme data ki copies kai nodes par rehti hain. Kleppmann Chapter 5 ke replication methods ko compare karte hain ki kaun se linearizable bane ja sakte hain.

Single-leader replication: potentially linearizable. Single-leader system mein leader ke paas woh primary copy hoti hai jo writes ke liye use hoti hai, aur followers backup copies rakhte hain. Tum leader se padho, ya aise followers se jo synchronously update hote hain, toh reads ke linearizable hone ka potential hai. Lekin har single-leader database linearizable nahi hota. Kuch design se hi nahi hote, jaise jo snapshot isolation use karte hain. Kuch concurrency bugs ki wajah se fail hote hain. Leader se padhne mein yeh bhi assume hota hai ki tumhe pakka pata hai ki leader kaun hai. Ek node sochta hai ki woh leader hai jabki woh nahi hota. Agar woh galat-fehmi wala leader requests serve karta raha, toh linearizability tootne ke chances kaafi hain. Asynchronous replication ke saath failover committed writes bhi kho sakta hai, jisse durability aur linearizability dono toot jaati hain.

Consensus algorithms: linearizable. Kuch consensus algorithms, jo is chapter mein aage aayenge, single-leader replication se kaafi milte-julte lagte hain. Lekin consensus protocols mein split brain aur stale replicas se bachne ke measures hote hain. In details ki wajah se consensus algorithms linearizable storage ko safely implement kar sakte hain. ZooKeeper aur etcd aise hi kaam karte hain.

Multi-leader replication: not linearizable. Multiple leaders wale systems writes ko kai nodes par concurrently process karte hain aur asynchronously replicate karte hain. Isse conflicting writes ban sakti hain jinhe resolve karna padta hai. Yeh conflicts isliye hote hain kyunki data ki single copy nahi hai, isliye system linearizable nahi hota.

Leaderless replication: probably not linearizable. Dynamo-style leaderless systems mein kuch log kehte hain ki quorum reads aur writes maang kar “strong consistency” possible hai, jahan w + r, n se bada ho. (Yahan n replicas ka count hai, w woh kitne replicas hain jinhe write confirm karna hai, aur r woh kitne jinhe read ka jawab dena hai.) Exact quorum setup aur tum strong consistency ko kaise define karte ho, uske hisaab se yeh claim bilkul sahi nahi hai. Time-of-day clocks par based last-write-wins conflict resolution, jaisa Cassandra mein hai, lagbhag pakka linearizable nahi hai, kyunki clock timestamps ke events ke real order se match karne ki guarantee nahi di ja sakti. Sloppy quorums bhi linearizability ko rule out kar dete hain. Strict quorums bhi non-linearizable ho sakte hain, jaisa agla example dikhata hai.

Linearizability aur Quorums

Intuitively, Dynamo-style system mein strict quorum reads aur writes linearizable hone chahiye. Lekin network delays alag-alag hon toh race conditions aa sakti hain. Book ke example mein yeh steps hain:

  1. Register x 0 se start hota hai. Ek writer client x ko 1 set kar raha hai, write ko teeno replicas ko bhejkar (n = 3, w = 3).
  2. Usi waqt client A do nodes ke quorum se read karta hai (r = 2). Un nodes mein se ek par use nayi value 1 dikhti hai.
  3. Usi waqt client B do nodes ke ek alag quorum se read karta hai. Use dono se purani value 0 milti hai.

Quorum condition poori hoti hai, kyunki w + r, n se bada hai. Phir bhi yeh execution linearizable nahi hai. B ki request A ki request khatam hone ke baad shuru hui, phir bhi B purani value return karta hai jabki A ne nayi value return ki thi. Yeh phir se Alice aur Bob hai.

Dynamo-style quorums ko linearizable banana possible hai, lekin speed ki keemat par. Reader ko result return karne se pehle read repair synchronously karna padta hai (read repair ek fix-up hai jo sabse nayi value ko stale replicas par wapas likhta hai). Writer ko apna write bhejne se pehle nodes ke quorum se latest state padhni padti hai. Lekin Riak performance penalty ki wajah se synchronous read repair nahi karta. Cassandra quorum reads par read repair khatam hone ka wait karta hai. Phir bhi, jab ek hi key par kai writes concurrently hoti hain tab woh linearizability kho deta hai, kyunki woh last-write-wins conflict resolution use karta hai.

Saath hi, is tarike se sirf linearizable reads aur writes hi ban sakte hain. Linearizable compare-and-set nahi ban sakta, kyunki uske liye consensus algorithm chahiye. Isliye sabse safe assumption yeh hai ki Dynamo-style replication wala leaderless system linearizability nahi deta.

Linearizability ki keemat

Kuch replication methods linearizability de sakte hain aur kuch nahi. Linearizability ki costs ko aur closely dekhna worth hai. Chapter 5 mein multi-leader replication ko multi-datacenter setups ke liye achha choice bataya tha, jahan har datacenter ke paas data ki apni copy hoti hai. Neeche ka example dikhata hai ki datacenters ke beech ke links fail hone par linearizability ka kya hota hai.

Socho ki dono datacenters ke beech ka network interrupt ho jaaye toh kya hoga. Maan lo har datacenter ke andar ka network ab bhi chal raha hai, aur clients apne local datacenter tak pahunch sakte hain, lekin dono datacenters aapas mein connect nahi ho paate.

Multi-leader database mein har datacenter normal tarike se kaam karta rehta hai. Ek datacenter ki writes doosre mein asynchronously replicate hoti hain, isliye woh bas queue mein lagi rehti hain aur connection wapas aane par exchange ho jaati hain.

Single-leader replication mein leader kisi ek datacenter mein hona chahiye. Saari writes aur saari linearizable reads usi leader ke paas jaani chahiye. Isliye follower datacenter se connected client ko apni requests network ke across leader ke datacenter tak synchronously bhejni padti hain. Datacenters ke beech ka network cut ho jaaye, toh follower ke paas wale clients leader tak nahi pahunch sakte. Woh write nahi kar sakte, aur linearizable reads bhi nahi kar sakte. Woh apne local follower se abhi bhi padh sakte hain, lekin woh data stale ho sakta hai, yani linearizable nahi hoga. Agar application ko linearizable reads aur writes chahiye, toh link repair hone tak woh follower datacenter mein unavailable ho jaati hai. Jo clients leader ke datacenter tak pahunch sakte hain, unpar koi asar nahi padta.

CAP Theorem

Yeh issue sirf single-leader aur multi-leader replication ki khaasiyat nahi hai. Koi bhi linearizable database ise face karta hai, chahe woh kaise bhi bana ho. Yeh sirf multi-datacenter setups tak bhi limited nahi hai. Yeh kisi bhi unreliable network par ho sakta hai, ek datacenter ke andar bhi. Trade-off aisa dikhta hai:

Trade-offs
Jab network replicas ko alag kar deApplication ko linearizability chahiyeApplication ko linearizability nahi chahiye
Cut-off replica kya karti haiUse network theek hone ka wait karna padta hai, ya error return karna padta hai. Dono tarah se woh unavailable hai.Har replica apni requests khud process karti rehti hai, jaise multi-leader setup mein.
Client ko kya milta haiSahi, up-to-date jawab, ya koi jawab nahiEk jawab jo abhi available hai, lekin linearizable nahi hai

Seedhi baat, jin applications ko linearizability nahi chahiye, woh network problems ko zyada tolerate kar sakti hain. Yeh insight popularly CAP theorem ke naam se jaana jaata hai. Iska naam Eric Brewer ke naam par hai, jinhone ise 2000 mein introduce kiya, haalaanki distributed databases ke designers 1970s se yeh trade-off jaante the. Kuch log do choices ko CP (consistent lekin partition ke dauraan available nahi) aur AP (available lekin partition ke dauraan consistent nahi) label karte hain. Kleppmann kehte hain ki us labeling scheme mein kai flaws hain, isliye ise avoid karna behtar hai.

CAP pehle ek rule of thumb ke taur par propose hua tha, precise definitions ke bina, taaki databases ke trade-offs par discussion shuru ho. Us waqt kai distributed databases aise cluster par linearizable behavior dene ki koshish karte the jo storage share karta tha. CAP ne database engineers ko shared-nothing systems ke wider design space ko explore karne ke liye encourage kiya, jahan har node ki apni storage hoti hai. Yeh systems bade web services ke liye zyada suit karte the. Kleppmann is culture change ka credit CAP ko dete hain, jo mid-2000s se aayi nayi database technologies ke explosion mein dikhta hai, jinhe NoSQL kehte hain.

CAP Theorem ki kami

CAP ko aksar teen properties mein summarize kiya jaata hai, consistency, availability aur partition tolerance, jinme se tum do chun sakte ho. Kleppmann kehte hain ki yeh phrasing misleading hai. Network partition ek tarah ka fault hai. Isliye yeh aisi cheez nahi hai jise tum avoid karna choose kar sako. Partitions hongi hi, chahe tumhe pasand ho ya nahi.

Network sahi kaam kar raha ho, toh system consistency (linearizability) aur full availability, dono de sakta hai. Network fault aane par tumhe linearizability aur full availability mein se ek chunni padti hai. CAP ko kehne ka behtar tarika yeh hai: partition hone par system ya toh consistent ho sakta hai ya available. Network zyada reliable ho, toh yeh choice kam baar karni padti hai, lekin kisi na kisi point par yeh choice avoid nahi ho sakti.

Kleppmann yeh bhi batate hain ki CAP ki discussion mein “availability” ki kai contradictory definitions hain. Formal theorem word ke aam matlab se match nahi karta. Khud ko “highly available” kehne wale kai systems CAP ki particular definition poori nahi karte. Isliye CAP ke aas-paas bahut misunderstanding hai. Unka nateeja hai ki yeh systems ko behtar samajhne mein madad nahi karta, aur ise avoid karna hi behtar hai.

Formal CAP theorem bahut narrow hai. Yeh sirf ek consistency model, linearizability, aur ek tarah ka fault, network partitions, ko consider karta hai. Yahan partition ka matlab hai aise nodes jo zinda hain lekin ek doosre se disconnected hain. (Book “partitioning” word ko aur jagah dataset ko chhote pieces mein todne ke liye use karti hai, jo Chapter 6 mein sharding hai. Network partition ek alag cheez hai, lekin CAP ka P wahi word hai.) Formal theorem network delays, dead nodes ya doosre trade-offs ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta. Isliye CAP historically influential raha hai, lekin systems design karne ke liye uski practical value kam hai. Distributed systems mein aur bhi bahut saare impossibility results hain, aur CAP ko ab zyada precise results ne replace kar diya hai. Ab yeh zyaadatar historical interest ka hai.

Linearizability aur Network Delays

Linearizability useful hai, lekin hairaan karne wali baat hai ki bahut kam systems ise actually dete hain. Modern multi-core CPU ki RAM bhi linearizable nahi hai. Ek core par ek thread kisi memory address par write kare, aur doosre core par ek thread thodi der baad wahi address read kare, toh memory barrier (jise fence bhi kehte hain) use kiye bina yeh guarantee nahi ki use abhi likhi hui value dikhegi.

Wajah yeh hai ki har CPU core ka apna cache aur store buffer hota hai. Memory access pehle cache mein jaata hai, aur changes main memory mein asynchronously likhe jaate hain. Cache se padhna main memory se padhne se bahut tez hai, isliye achhi performance ke liye yeh design zaroori hai. Lekin ab data ki kai copies hain, aur woh asynchronously update hoti hain, isliye linearizability chali jaati hai.

Yeh trade-off kyun accept karein? Multi-core memory model ko CAP theorem se justify karna samajh se bahar hai. Ek computer ke andar hum usually reliable communication maan lete hain. Hum expect nahi karte ki ek CPU core computer ke baaki hisse se kat jaaye toh bhi normal kaam karta rahe. Linearizability chhodne ki wajah performance hai, fault tolerance nahi. Yahi baat un kai distributed databases ke liye bhi sach hai jo linearizable guarantees nahi dete. Woh mainly tez hone ke liye aisa karte hain, mainly fault tolerance ke liye nahi. Linearizability slow hai, aur hamesha slow hai, sirf network faults ke dauraan nahi.

Kya linearizable storage banane ka koi tez tarika mil sakta hai? Jawab lagta hai nahi. Attiya aur Welch ne prove kiya ki agar tumhe linearizability chahiye, toh reads aur writes ka response time kam se kam network delays ki uncertainty ke proportional hoga. Jis network mein delays bahut variable hon, jaise zyaadatar computer networks mein, wahan linearizable reads aur writes ka response time high hi rahega. Koi tez linearizable algorithm exist nahi karta. Weaker consistency models kaafi tez ho sakte hain, isliye latency-sensitive systems ke liye yeh trade-off bahut matter karta hai. Chapter 12 mein correctness chhode bina linearizability se bachne ke tarike discuss hote hain.

Ordering Guarantees

Linearizable register aise behave karta hai jaise data ki sirf ek copy ho, aur har operation ek hi point in time par atomically effect karta dikhta hai. Iska matlab hai ki operations kisi well-defined order mein chalte hain. Book ke Figure 9-4 mein yahi dikhaya gaya tha, jahan operations ko usi order mein jod diya gaya jis order mein woh chalte hue lagte hain.

Ordering is book mein baar-baar aayi hai, jisse lagta hai ki yeh ek fundamental idea hai. Chalo dekhte hain ki ordering aur kahan-kahan aayi thi:

  • Chapter 5 mein, single-leader replication mein leader ka main kaam hai replication log mein writes ka order decide karna. Followers writes isi order mein apply karte hain. Single leader na ho, toh concurrent operations conflict kar sakte hain.
  • Chapter 7 ki serializability ka matlab hai ki transactions aise behave karein jaise woh kisi sequential order mein chale hon. Yeh do tarike se ho sakta hai: unhe literally ek ke baad ek chalaya jaye, ya concurrently chalne diya jaye aur conflicts ko locks ya aborts se roka jaye.
  • Chapter 8 mein timestamps aur clocks se is disorderly duniya mein order laaya gaya, jaise yeh decide karne ke liye ki do writes mein se kaun si baad mein hui.

Ordering, linearizability aur consensus ke beech gehre connections hain. Yeh topic baaki book se zyada theoretical hai, lekin isse samajh aata hai ki systems kya kar sakte hain aur kya nahi.

Ordering aur Causality

Ordering baar-baar isliye aati hai kyunki woh causality ko preserve karne mein madad karti hai. Causality matlab cause aur effect ka link: ek cheez doosri ki wajah se hoti hai. Book mein kai examples aaye hain jo dikhate hain ki causality kyun zaroori hai:

  • Answers before questions. Chapter 5 (Figure 5-5) mein ek observer ko question se pehle uska answer dikh gaya. Yeh confusing hai, kyunki answer dene wale ne question pehle dekha hoga. Question aur answer ke beech causal dependency hai.
  • Updates before creation. Figure 5-9 mein teen leaders wale system mein network delays ki wajah se writes ek doosre ko overtake kar gaye. Ek replica ko aise row ka update dikha jo abhi exist hi nahi karti thi. Yahan causality ka matlab hai ki row pehle create honi chahiye, tabhi update ho sakti hai.
  • Concurrent writes. Chapter 5 mein dekha tha ki kisi bhi do operations A aur B ke liye teen possibilities hoti hain. Ya A, B se pehle hua, ya B, A se pehle hua, ya A aur B concurrent hain. “Happened before” relationship causality ko express karne ka hi ek aur tarika hai. Agar A, B se pehle hua, toh B ko A ke baare mein pata ho sakta hai, B A par build kar sakta hai, ya A par depend kar sakta hai. Agar A aur B concurrent hain, toh unke beech koi causal link nahi hai. Kisi ko doosre ke baare mein pata nahi tha.
  • Consistent snapshots. Chapter 7 mein kaha tha ki transaction ek consistent snapshot se read karta hai. Consistent ka matlab hai causality ke saath consistent. Agar snapshot mein koi answer hai, toh jis question ka woh answer hai woh bhi snapshot mein hona chahiye. Poore database ko ek point in time par dekhne se yeh property milti hai: us point se pehle causally jo kuch hua uske effects dikhte hain, aur us ke baad causally jo hua woh kuch nahi dikhta. Read skew, yani Figure 7-6 ke non-repeatable reads, ka matlab hai data ko aisi state mein read karna jo causality tod deti hai.
  • Write skew. Figure 7-8 mein Alice ko off call jaane diya gaya kyunki uske transaction ne dekha ki Bob abhi bhi on call hai, aur Bob ke saath bhi bilkul yahi ulta hua. Off call jaana causally is observation par depend karta hai ki kaun on call hai. Serializable snapshot isolation in transactions ke beech causal dependencies track karke write skew detect karta hai.
  • The football example. Figure 9-1 mein Alice ko score chillate sunne ke baad Bob ko stale result mila. Yeh causality violation hai. Alice ka chillana score ke announcement par depend karta hai, isliye Bob ko bhi score dikhna chahiye tha. Image resizer wale example mein bhi yahi pattern tha.

Causality events par ek order lagati hai. Cause, effect se pehle aata hai. Message receive hone se pehle bheja jaata hai. Question, answer se pehle aata hai. Aur real life ki tarah, ek cheez se doosri cheez nikalti hai. Ek node kuch data read karta hai aur uske result mein kuch likhta hai. Doosra node woh likha hua read karta hai aur badle mein kuch aur likhta hai. Dependent operations ki yeh chains system ka causal order define karti hain, yani yeh record ki kya kis se pehle hua.

Agar koi system causality ke impose kiye hue ordering ko follow karta hai, toh hum use causally consistent kehte hain. Jaise ki snapshot isolation causal consistency deta hai. Jab tum database se read karke koi data dekhte ho, toh tumhe woh sab data bhi dikhna chahiye jo causally us se pehle aaya tha, bas woh data beech mein delete na ho gaya ho.

Causal order total order nahi hota

Total order mein tum kisi bhi do elements ko compare kar sakte ho. Agar tumhe do natural numbers milein, jaise 5 aur 13, toh tum hamesha bata sakte ho ki kaun bada hai. Mathematical sets alag hote hain. Kya set {a, b}, set {b, c} se bada hai? Tum compare nahi kar sakte, kyunki dono mein se koi bhi doosre ka subset nahi hai. Yeh incomparable hain. Isliye sets sirf partially ordered hote hain. Kuch cases mein ek set doosre se bada hota hai, aur kuch cases mein dono compare hi nahi ho sakte.

Total aur partial order ka yeh difference database ke consistency models mein dikhta hai:

  • Linearizability operations ka total order deti hai. Agar system aise behave kare jaise data ki ek hi copy ho, aur har operation atomic ho, toh kisi bhi do operations ke liye tum bata sakte ho ki pehle kaun hua. Pichhle figure ki timeline yahi dikhati hai.
  • Causality partial order deti hai. Do operations concurrent tab hote hain jab koi bhi doosre se pehle na hua ho. Do events tab ordered hote hain jab woh causally related hon, yani ek doosre se pehle hua ho. Agar woh concurrent hain, toh woh incomparable hain. Kuch operations ek doosre ke respect mein ordered hote hain, aur kuch nahi.

Toh is definition ke hisaab se, linearizable datastore mein koi concurrent operations nahi hote. Ek hi timeline hoti hai jis par saare operations totally ordered hote hain. Requests handle hone ke liye line mein wait kar sakti hain, lekin store har request ko ek single point in time par atomically handle karta hai, data ki ek hi copy par kaam karte hue. Concurrency ka matlab hota ki timeline branch ho aur phir dobara merge ho. Alag branches ke operations incomparable hote hain. Chapter 5 ke concurrent operations ka jumble (Figure 5-14) aisa hi hai, jismein arrows causal dependencies dikhate hain. Yeh partial order hai, seedhi line nahi.

Git jaise distributed version control systems bhi isi tarah kaam karte hain. Aksar ek commit doosre ke baad seedhi line mein aata hai. Kabhi branches ban jaati hain, jab kai log ek saath project par kaam karte hain. Jab un concurrent commits ko combine kiya jaata hai, tab merges bante hain. Version history causal dependencies ka ek graph hai.

Linearizability, causal consistency se strong hai

Causal order aur linearizability ka aapas mein kya relation hai? Jawab yeh hai ki linearizability se causality implied hoti hai. Koi bhi linearizable system causality ko sahi tarah se preserve karta hai. Khaaskar, agar system mein kai communication channels hain, jaise photo example mein message queue aur file storage service, toh linearizability causality ko automatically intact rakhti hai. Components ko kaam karwane ke liye ek doosre ko timestamps pass karne ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Isi wajah se linearizable systems samajhna aasaan hota hai aur woh appealing lagte hain. Lekin jaisa pehle dekha, system ko linearizable banane se uski performance aur availability par asar pad sakta hai, khaaskar jab network delays bade hon, jaise geographically distributed systems mein. Isliye kuch distributed data systems ne linearizability chhod di hai. Isse unki performance behtar ho jaati hai, lekin unke saath kaam karna mushkil ho sakta hai.

Achhi khabar yeh hai ki beech ka ek raasta hai. Causality preserve karne ka linearizability akela tarika nahi hai. System linearizability ki performance cost diye bina bhi causally consistent ho sakta hai. Us case mein CAP theorem apply nahi hota. Asal mein, causal consistency sabse strong consistency model hai jo network delays ki wajah se slow nahi hota aur network fail hone par bhi available rehta hai.

Kai cases mein, jin systems ko lagta hai ki unhe linearizability chahiye, unhe asal mein sirf causal consistency chahiye hoti hai, jo provide karna sasta hai. Isi observation par researchers aise naye databases explore kar rahe hain jo causality preserve karte hain, aur jinki performance aur availability eventually consistent systems ke kareeb hai. Yeh research abhi nayi hai, aur isme se bahut kam production tak pahunchi hai. Abhi bhi kuch challenges solve karne hain. Lekin future ke systems ke liye yeh ek promising direction hai.

Causal dependencies capture karna

Book is baare mein poori detail mein nahi jaati ki non-linearizable system causal consistency kaise maintain kar sakta hai. Woh bas kuch key ideas explore karti hai.

Causality maintain karne ke liye tumhe pata hona chahiye ki kaun sa operation kis doosre operation se pehle hua. Yeh partial order hai. Concurrent operations kisi bhi order mein process ho sakte hain, lekin agar ek operation doosre se pehle hua, toh har replica ko unhe usi order mein process karna hoga. Isliye jab replica koi operation process karta hai, toh use pehle yeh pakka karna hoga ki us se causally pehle ke saare operations process ho chuke hain. Agar un pehle ke operations mein se koi missing hai, toh baad wale operation ko wait karna hoga jab tak woh aa na jaye.

Causal dependencies dhoondhne ke liye tumhe yeh describe karne ka tarika chahiye ki node kya “jaanta” hai. Agar node ne write Y issue karte waqt value X pehle se dekh li thi, toh X aur Y causally related ho sakte hain. Yeh analysis fraud investigation jaisa hai: CEO ne decision Y lete waqt kya X ke baare mein jaanta tha?

Kaun sa operation kis se pehle hua yeh dhoondhne ki techniques waisi hi hain jaisi Chapter 5 mein concurrent writes detect karne wale section mein thi. Woh section leaderless store ke baare mein tha, jahan lost updates se bachne ke liye tumhe same key par concurrent writes detect karni padti hain. Causal consistency isse aage jaati hai. Use sirf ek key ke liye nahi, poore database mein causal dependencies track karni padti hain. Version vectors ko generalize karke yeh kiya ja sakta hai.

Causal ordering nikalne ke liye database ko pata hona chahiye ki application ne data ka kaun sa version read kiya tha. Isi wajah se Chapter 5 ke Figure 5-13 mein pehle wale operation ka version number write ke saath database ko wapas bheja jaata hai. Aisa hi ek idea serializable snapshot isolation ke conflict detection mein bhi aata hai. Jab transaction commit karna chahta hai, toh database check karta hai ki jo version of data usne read kiya tha woh abhi bhi up to date hai ya nahi. Yeh karne ke liye database track karta hai ki kaun sa data kis transaction ne read kiya hai.

Sequence number ordering

Causality ek important idea hai, lekin har causal dependency ko actually track karna impractical ho sakta hai. Kai applications mein clients kuch likhne se pehle bahut sara data read karte hain. Phir yeh clear nahi hota ki write us saare data par depend karta hai ya sirf thode se par. Har read ko track karna bahut bada overhead hoga.

Ek behtar tarika hai: events ko order karne ke liye sequence numbers ya timestamps use karo. Timestamp ka time-of-day clock se aana zaroori nahi hai. Chapter 8 mein dekha tha ki physical clocks mein kaafi problems hoti hain. Timestamp ek logical clock se bhi aa sakta hai. Logical clock ek algorithm hai jo operations ko identify karne ke liye numbers ki sequence banata hai, aam taur par har operation ke liye ek counter increment karke.

Aise sequence numbers compact hote hain, aksar sirf kuch bytes ke. Yeh total order bhi dete hain. Har operation ko unique number milta hai, aur tum do numbers compare karke hamesha dekh sakte ho ki kaun sa operation baad mein hua.

Hum aise sequence numbers bhi bana sakte hain jinka total order causality ke saath consistent ho. Promise yeh hai: agar operation A causally B se pehle hua, toh A ka sequence number B se kam hoga. Concurrent operations ko kisi bhi order mein rakha ja sakta hai. Aisa total order causality ki saari information capture karta hai, lekin woh causality ko strictly jitna chahiye us se zyada order bhi lagata hai.

Single-leader replication wale database mein replication log pehle se hi writes ka aisa total order define karta hai jo causality ke saath consistent hai. Leader har operation ke liye ek counter increment karta hai, isliye log ki har entry ko ek badhta hua sequence number milta hai. Agar follower writes ko usi order mein apply karta hai jis order mein woh log mein hain, toh uski state hamesha causally consistent rehti hai, chahe woh leader se peeche hi kyun na chal raha ho.

Noncausal sequence number generators

Agar single leader nahi hai, kyunki tum multi-leader ya leaderless replication use karte ho, ya database partitioned hai, toh sequence numbers kaise generate karo yeh kam clear hai. Book practice mein use hone wale kai methods list karti hai:

  • Separate sets per node. Jaise do nodes ho toh ek node sirf odd numbers generate kare aur doosra sirf even. Aam taur par, tum har number ke kuch bits reserve kar sakte ho jo unique node ID hold karein, taaki do nodes kabhi same number na banayein.
  • Time-of-day timestamps. Tum har operation ke saath physical clock ka timestamp attach kar sakte ho. Aise timestamps sequential nahi hote, lekin agar unki resolution kaafi high ho, toh operations ko totally order karne ke liye shayad kaafi hon. Last-write-wins conflict resolution method yahi use karta hai.
  • Preallocated blocks. Jaise node A numbers ka block 1 se 1,000 claim kar le, aur node B 1,001 se 2,000. Phir har node apne block se numbers assign karta hai, aur supply kam hone par naya block claim karta hai.

Teeno options performance aur scaling mein us tarike se behtar hain jismein har operation ko ek leader se guzaara jaye jo counter increment karta hai. Yeh har operation ke liye unique, lagbhag badhta hua number banate hain. Lekin teeno mein ek problem hai. Unke sequence numbers causality ke saath consistent nahi hote, kyunki woh alag-alag nodes ke operations ka order capture nahi karte:

  • Har node ek second mein alag number of operations handle kar sakta hai. Agar ek node even numbers aur doosra odd numbers generate kare, toh even counter odd counter se peeche reh sakta hai, ya ulta. Ek odd-numbered aur ek even-numbered operation mil jaye, toh tum accurately nahi bata sakte ki causally kaun pehle hua.
  • Physical clock timestamps mein clock skew ki problem hoti hai, jisse woh causality ke saath inconsistent ho sakte hain. Figure 8-3 mein ek case dikhaya tha jahan jo operation causally baad mein hua use kam timestamp mil gaya. (Physical timestamps ko causality ke saath consistent banana possible hai. Google ka Spanner expected clock skew estimate karta hai aur write commit karne se pehle uncertainty interval ka wait karta hai, taaki causally baad wali transaction ko hamesha bada timestamp mile. Lekin zyadatar clocks woh uncertainty figure nahi de sakte jo is method ko chahiye.)
  • Block allocator ke saath ek operation ko 1,001 se 2,000 range ka number mil sakta hai, jabki causally baad wale operation ko 1 se 1,000 ka number mil jaye. Phir se numbers causality ke khilaf chale jaate hain.

Book yeh bhi batati hai ki jo total order causality ko ignore karta hai woh banana aasaan hai, lekin zyada useful nahi hai. Jaise, tum har operation ko ek random UUID de sakte ho aur UUID se sort kar sakte ho. Yeh valid total order hai, lekin UUIDs yeh nahi batate ki asal mein kaun sa operation pehle hua, ya do operations concurrent the ya nahi.

Lamport timestamps

Causality ke saath consistent sequence numbers generate karne ka ek simple method hai. Ise Lamport timestamp kehte hain. Leslie Lamport ne ise 1978 mein propose kiya tha, ek aise paper mein jo ab distributed systems ke sabse zyada cited papers mein se ek hai.

Har node ka ek unique identifier hota hai, aur har node ek counter rakhta hai ki usne kitne operations process kiye hain. Lamport timestamp (counter, node ID) ka ek pair hota hai. Do nodes ki counter value kabhi-kabhi same ho sakti hai, lekin node ID jodne se har timestamp unique ho jaata hai.

Lamport timestamp ka time-of-day clock se koi lena-dena nahi hai, lekin yeh total order deta hai. Agar tumhare paas do timestamps hain, toh jiska counter bada ho woh bada timestamp hai. Agar counters barabar hain, toh jiska node ID bada ho woh bada hai.

Ab tak yeh lagbhag wahi hai jo upar even aur odd counters mein bataya tha. Lamport timestamps ko causality ke saath consistent banane wali key idea yeh hai: har node aur har client ab tak dekhi hui maximum counter value track karta hai, aur har request mein woh maximum bhejta hai. Jab koi node aisi request ya response receive karta hai jiska maximum counter uske apne counter se bada ho, toh woh turant apna counter us maximum tak badha leta hai.

Figure 9-8 yahi dikhata hai. Client A ko node 2 se counter value 5 milti hai. Phir woh 5 ka maximum node 1 ko bhej deta hai. Us waqt node 1 ka counter sirf 1 hai. Lekin use turant 5 tak aage badha diya jaata hai. Isliye node 1 ke agle operation ko incremented counter 6 milta hai.

Jab tak maximum counter value har operation ke saath travel karti rahe, yeh scheme Lamport ordering ko causality ke saath consistent rakhti hai. Har causal dependency se timestamp badhta hai.

Lamport timestamps ko kabhi-kabhi version vectors se confuse kar liya jaata hai, jo Chapter 5 mein cover hue the. Dono mein kuch similarities hain, lekin purpose alag hain. Version vectors bata sakte hain ki do operations concurrent hain ya ek causally doosre par depend karta hai. Lamport timestamps hamesha total order enforce karte hain. Lamport timestamps ke total order se tum nahi bata sakte ki do operations concurrent hain ya causally dependent. Version vectors ke mukaable Lamport timestamps ka advantage yeh hai ki woh zyada compact hote hain.

Timestamp ordering kaafi nahi hai

Lamport timestamps aisa total order define karte hain jo causality ke saath consistent hai. Lekin distributed systems ki kai common problems solve karne ke liye woh poore kaafi nahi hain.

Maan lo ek system ko pakka karna hai ki ek username exactly ek user account ko identify kare. Agar do users ek saath same username se account banane ki koshish karein, toh ek ko succeed hona chahiye aur doosre ko fail. Chapter 8 mein leader aur lock wale section mein is problem ko chhua tha.

Pehli nazar mein Lamport timestamps jaisa total order kaafi lagta hai. Agar same username ke do accounts ban jayein, toh jiska timestamp kam ho use winner chuno, kyunki usne naam pehle pakda. Bade timestamp wale ko fail hone do. Timestamps totally ordered hain, isliye comparison hamesha valid hota hai.

Yeh baad mein winner decide karne ke liye kaam karta hai. Jab tum system ke saare username-creation operations collect kar lete ho, tab tum unke timestamps compare kar sakte ho. Lekin yeh tab kaam nahi karta jab kisi node ko abhi-abhi username create karne ki request mili ho aur use abhi decide karna ho ki woh succeed hogi ya nahi. Us waqt node ko nahi pata ki koi aur node concurrently same naam se account bana raha hai ya nahi, aur woh doosra node kaun sa timestamp assign karega.

Yeh pakka karne ke liye ki koi aur node kam timestamp ke saath same username nahi bana raha, tumhe har doosre node se poochna padega ki woh kya kar raha hai. Agar un nodes mein se koi fail ho gaya ho, ya network problem ki wajah se reach na ho paye, toh system ruk jayega. Humein aisa fault-tolerant system nahi chahiye.

Root problem yeh hai ki operations ka total order tabhi banta hai jab tum sabhi operations collect kar lete ho. Agar kisi doosre node ne aise operations generate kiye hain jo tumne abhi dekhe nahi, toh tum final order nahi bana sakte. Woh unknown operations total order mein alag-alag positions par insert karne pad sakte hain.

Conclusion yeh hai. Username uniqueness constraint jaisi cheez enforce karne ke liye total order kaafi nahi hai. Tumhe yeh bhi pata hona chahiye ki order kab final hai. Agar tumhare paas username create karne ka operation hai, aur tumhe pakka pata hai ki koi aur node tumhare operation se pehle same naam ka claim nahi ghusa sakta, toh tum apne operation ko safely successful declare kar sakte ho. Total order kab final hai yeh jaanne wala idea total order broadcast ke topic mein capture hota hai.

Try karo

Do nodes ko lagbhag ek hi samay par same username register karne ki request milti hai. Node 1 apni request par Lamport timestamp (4, node 1) lagata hai, aur node 2 apni request par (4, node 2). Kaun si request ka timestamp kam hai? Phir socho ki node 1 ko safely apni request ko winner declare karne se pehle abhi bhi kya nahi pata.

Total order broadcast

Agar tumhara program ek single CPU core par chalta hai, toh operations ka total order define karna aasaan hai. Bas wahi order jisme CPU ne unhe chalaya. Distributed system mein saare nodes ko ek total order par agree karwana tricky hai. Is section mein pehle humne timestamps aur sequence numbers se ordering dekhi, aur paaya ki woh single-leader replication se weak hai. Agar tum uniqueness constraint enforce karne ke liye timestamp ordering use karte ho, toh tum koi bhi fault tolerate nahi kar sakte.

Single-leader replication operations ka total order aise decide karta hai ki ek node ko leader chun leta hai, aur saare operations us leader ke CPU par sequence mein chalata hai. Challenge do hisson mein hai. Pehla, agar load ek leader sambhal na sake, toh system ko scale kaise karein. Doosra, agar leader fail ho jaye toh failover kaise karein (Chapter 5 mein node outages handle karna cover hua tha). Research literature mein is problem ko total order broadcast ya atomic broadcast kehte hain.

Dhyaan do

Ordering guarantee ka scope. Jin partitioned databases mein har partition ka ek leader hota hai, woh aam taur par order sirf har partition ke andar rakhte hain. Isliye woh aise guarantees nahi de sakte jo partitions ke aar-paar jaate hon, jaise consistent snapshots ya partitions ke beech foreign key references. Saare partitions ka total order possible hai, lekin uske liye extra coordination chahiye.

Total order broadcast ko aam taur par nodes ke beech messages pass karne ke protocol ki tarah describe kiya jaata hai. Informally, ise har waqt do safety properties satisfy karni hoti hain:

  • Reliable delivery. Koi message lost nahi hota. Agar message ek node tak deliver hota hai, toh woh saare nodes tak deliver hota hai.
  • Totally ordered delivery. Messages har node tak same order mein deliver hote hain.

Correct algorithm ko dono properties true rakhni hoti hain, chahe koi node ya network faulty ho. Jab network cut hota hai tab messages deliver nahi honge. Lekin algorithm retry karta reh sakta hai, taaki network repair hone par messages pahunch jayein, aur unhe phir bhi sahi order mein pahunchna chahiye.

Total order broadcast ka use

Consensus services ZooKeeper aur etcd asal mein total order broadcast implement karti hain. Yeh total order broadcast aur consensus ke beech strong connection ka hint hai, jo chapter aage explore karta hai.

Database replication ko exactly total order broadcast hi chahiye. Agar har message database ka ek write hai, aur har replica same writes ko same order mein process karta hai, toh replicas ek doosre ke saath consistent rehte hain, temporary replication lag ko chhodkar. Is principle ko state machine replication kehte hain. Chapter 11 mein yeh dobara aayega.

Isse serializable transactions bhi implement ho sakte hain. Chapter 7 mein actual serial execution describe hua tha. Agar har message ek deterministic transaction hai, yani aisa jo stored procedure ki tarah chalta hai aur jiska result predictable hota hai, aur har node messages ko same order mein process karta hai, toh database ke partitions aur replicas ek doosre ke saath consistent rehte hain.

Total order broadcast ki ek important property yeh hai ki order delivery ke time par fix ho jaata hai. Agar baad ke messages already deliver ho chuke hain, toh node kisi message ko retroactively pehle ki position par insert nahi kar sakta. Isi wajah se total order broadcast timestamp ordering se strong hai.

Total order broadcast ko dekhne ka ek aur tarika hai ki yeh log banane ka tarika hai, jaise replication log, transaction log, ya write-ahead log. Message deliver karna log mein append karne jaisa hai. Kyunki saare nodes same messages same order mein deliver karte hain, woh sab log read karke messages ki same sequence dekh sakte hain.

Total order broadcast us lock service ke liye bhi useful hai jo fencing tokens deta hai (Chapter 8 mein inhe explain kiya tha). Lock acquire karne ki har request log mein ek message ki tarah append hoti hai. Saare messages ko log mein unke aane ke order mein number diye jaate hain. Woh sequence number fencing token ka kaam kar sakta hai, kyunki woh hamesha badhta hai. ZooKeeper is sequence number ko zxid kehta hai.

Total order broadcast se linearizable storage banana

Figure 9-4 ne dikhaya tha ki linearizable system mein operations ka total order hota hai. Toh kya linearizability aur total order broadcast ek hi cheez hain? Bilkul nahi, lekin dono closely linked hain.

Total order broadcast asynchronous hai. Messages reliably ek fixed order mein deliver hote hain, lekin kisi message ke kab pahunchne ka koi guarantee nahi hota. Ek recipient doosron se peeche reh sakta hai. Linearizability iske ulta ek recency guarantee hai: read ko latest likhi hui value dikhni chahiye.

Phir bhi, agar tumhare paas total order broadcast hai, toh tum uske upar linearizable storage bana sakte ho. Jaise, tum pakka kar sakte ho ki usernames accounts ko uniquely identify karein. Socho ki har possible username ke liye ek linearizable register hai jo atomic compare-and-set support karta hai. Har register null value se start hota hai, jiska matlab hai ki naam free hai. Username claim karne ke liye tum us naam ke register par compare-and-set chalate ho, use user ki account ID par set karte hue, is condition par ki current value null ho. Agar kai users ek saath same naam lene ki koshish karein, toh sirf ek compare-and-set succeed hoga. Baaki ko linearizability ki wajah se null se alag value dikhegi.

Book dikhati hai ki total order broadcast ko append-only log ki tarah use karke aisa linearizable compare-and-set kaise implement karein:

  1. Log mein ek message append karo, jo tentatively batata hai ki tum kaun sa username claim karna chahte ho.
  2. Log read karo, aur wait karo jab tak tumhara append kiya hua message tumhe wapas deliver na ho jaye.
  3. Log mein aise messages check karo jo same username claim karte hain. Agar aisa pehla message tumhara apna hai, toh tum succeed ho gaye. Tum claim commit kar sakte ho, shayad ek aur message append karke, aur client ko bata sakte ho. Agar us username ka pehla message kisi aur user ka hai, toh operation abort kar do.

Kyunki log entries saare nodes ko same order mein deliver hoti hain, agar kai writes concurrent hain, toh saare nodes agree karte hain ki kaun pehle aaya. Pehli conflicting write jeetti hai aur baad wali abort ho jaati hain. Isliye saare nodes is par agree karte hain ki har write commit hua ya abort. Aisa hi approach log ke upar serializable multi-object transactions implement karne ke liye bhi use ho sakta hai.

Yeh procedure linearizable writes ensure karta hai. Yeh linearizable reads guarantee nahi karta. Agar tum aise store se read karte ho jo log se asynchronously update hota hai, toh value stale ho sakti hai. Precisely kahein toh, yeh procedure sequential consistency deta hai, jise timeline consistency bhi kehte hain, jo linearizability se thodi weak hai. Reads ko linearizable banane ke liye teen options hain:

  • Reads ko log ke through sequence karo. Ek message append karo, log read karo, aur jab tumhara message tumhe wapas deliver ho tab actual read karo. Log mein message ki position us point in time ko define karti hai jahan read hota hai. etcd ke quorum reads kuch aise hi kaam karte hain.
  • Agar log tumhe apne latest message ki position linearizable tarike se fetch karne deta hai, toh woh position query karo, wait karo jab tak us position tak ki saari entries tumhe deliver na ho jayein, aur phir read karo. ZooKeeper ke sync() operation ke peeche yahi idea hai.
  • Aise replica se read karo jo writes par synchronously update hota hai, aur isliye pakka up to date hota hai. Yeh technique chain replication mein use hoti hai.

Linearizable storage se total order broadcast banana

Pichhle section mein dikhaya tha ki total order broadcast se linearizable compare-and-set kaise banate hain. Book ulta bhi dikhati hai. Agar maan lo ki linearizable storage hai, toh tum usse total order broadcast bana sakte ho.

Sabse aasaan tarika yeh hai ki maan lo ek linearizable register hai jo integer store karta hai aur atomic increment-and-get operation support karta hai. Atomic compare-and-set se bhi kaam ho jaata.

Algorithm simple hai. Total order broadcast se bhejne wale har message ke liye tum linearizable integer par increment-and-get chalate ho. Jo value wapas mili use sequence number ki tarah message ke saath attach kar dete hain. Phir message ko saare nodes ko bhejte hain, aur jo lost ho jaye use dobara bhejte hain. Recipients messages ko unke sequence numbers ke order mein deliver karte hain.

Lamport timestamps se key difference dhyaan rakhein. Linearizable register ko increment karke jo numbers milte hain woh bina gaps ki sequence banate hain. Isliye agar node ne message 4 deliver kar diya aur phir use message 6 mila, toh use pata hai ki message 6 deliver karne se pehle use message 5 ka wait karna hoga. Lamport timestamps ke saath aisa nahi hota. Total order broadcast aur timestamp ordering ke beech yahi key difference hai.

Atomic increment-and-get wala linearizable integer banana kitna mushkil hai? Agar kabhi kuch fail na hota, toh aasaan hota: integer ko ek node par variable mein rakh lo. Asli problem yeh hai ki us node ka network connection toot jaye toh kya karein, aur node fail ho jaye toh value restore kaise karein. Kleppmann ka point hai ki agar tum linearizable sequence number generators ke baare mein kaafi gehrai se sochoge, toh tum aakhir mein consensus algorithm hi bana loge.

Yeh coincidence nahi hai. Yeh prove kiya ja sakta hai ki linearizable compare-and-set register (ya increment-and-get register) aur total order broadcast dono consensus ke equivalent hain. Agar tum in problems mein se ek solve kar sakte ho, toh us solution ko baaki problems ke solution mein badal sakte ho. Book ise kaafi profound aur surprising insight kehti hai.

Ab consensus problem ko seedhe tackle karne ka waqt aa gaya hai.

Distributed Transactions aur Consensus

Consensus distributed computing ki sabse important aur fundamental problems mein se ek hai. Upar se dekhein toh yeh simple lagti hai. Seedhi baat, goal yeh hai ki kai nodes kisi cheez par agree kar jaayein. Tum soch sakte ho ki yeh itna mushkil nahi hoga. Lekin kaafi broken systems isi galat soch par bane hain ki yeh problem aasaan hai.

Consensus book mein der se aata hai, kyunki yeh topic subtle hai aur ise samajhne ke liye background knowledge chahiye. Researchers ko bhi consensus saaf samajhne mein decades lag gaye, aur raaste mein kaafi galatfehmiyan hui. Ab tak book replication (Chapter 5), transactions (Chapter 7), failure ke system models (Chapter 8), linearizability aur total order broadcast cover kar chuki hai. Isliye ab consensus ko tackle karne ka time hai.

Kai situations mein nodes ko agree karna padta hai. Inmein se do yahan important hain:

  • Leader election. Single-leader replication wale database mein saare nodes ko agree karna hota hai ki leader kaun sa node hai. Agar network fault ki wajah se kuch nodes doosron se baat nahi kar paate, toh leadership par jhagda ho sakta hai. Bad failover se bachne ke liye consensus chahiye, warna split brain ho jaata hai. Do leaders honge toh dono writes accept karenge, unka data alag-alag direction mein chala jaayega, aur nateeja inconsistency aur data loss hoga.
  • Atomic commit. Jo database kai nodes ya partitions par phaile transactions support karta hai, wahan transaction kuch nodes par fail ho sakta hai aur kuch par succeed. ACID transactions ki atomicity bachane ke liye saare nodes ko outcome par agree karna hoga. Ya toh sab abort karein, agar kuch bhi galat hua, ya sab commit karein, agar sab theek raha. Consensus ke is instance ko atomic commit problem kehte hain. Atomic commit ko consensus se thoda alag tarah formalize kiya jaata hai. Atomic commit tabhi succeed hota hai jab har participant commit ke liye vote kare, jabki consensus us value par decide kar sakta hai jo koi bhi ek participant propose kare. Lekin dono problems ek doosre mein reduce ho sakti hain. Non-blocking atomic commit consensus se zyada mushkil hai, aur book isse baad mein three-phase commit ke under discuss karti hai.

Consensus ka impossible hona

Tumne FLP result ke baare mein suna hoga, jo uske authors Fischer, Lynch aur Paterson ke naam par hai. Yeh prove karta hai ki aisa koi algorithm nahi hai jo hamesha consensus tak pahunche, agar kisi node ke crash hone ka risk ho. Distributed system mein hume maanna padta hai ki nodes crash ho sakte hain. Toh reliable consensus impossible lagta hai. Phir bhi book aise algorithms discuss karti rahi hai jo consensus achieve karte hain. Toh yeh ho kya raha hai?

Iska jawab yeh hai ki FLP result asynchronous system model mein prove hua hai, aur woh model kaafi restrictive hai. Usmein maana jaata hai ki algorithm deterministic hai aur koi clocks ya timeouts use nahi kar sakta. Agar algorithm ko timeouts use karne ki ijaazat ho, ya kisi aur tarike se un nodes ko pehchaanne ki jinpar crash ka shak ho (chahe shak kabhi galat bhi ho), toh consensus solvable ho jaata hai. Algorithm ko random numbers use karne dena bhi impossibility result ko bypass karne ke liye kaafi hai.

Isliye FLP result theory ke hisaab se bahut important hai, lekin practice mein distributed systems aam taur par consensus achieve kar lete hain.

Is section ka baaki plan yeh hai. Pehle book atomic commit ko detail mein dekhti hai. Khaas taur par two-phase commit (2PC) algorithm, jo atomic commit solve karne ka sabse common tarika hai. Yeh kai databases, messaging systems aur application servers mein built-in aata hai. Pata chalta hai ki 2PC ek tarah ka consensus algorithm hai, lekin bahut achha nahi. 2PC se seekhkar book behtar consensus algorithms ki taraf badhti hai, jaise ZooKeeper (Zab) aur etcd (Raft) mein use hone wale.

Atomic Commit aur Two-Phase Commit (2PC)

Chapter 7 mein bataya gaya tha ki transaction atomicity ka purpose yeh hai ki kai writes ke beech mein kuch galat ho jaaye toh semantics simple rahein. Transaction do tarah se khatam hota hai. Ya toh woh commit hota hai, jisse uski saari writes permanent ho jaati hain, ya woh abort hota hai, jisse saari writes rollback ho jaati hain, yani undo ya discard ho jaati hain.

Atomicity ki wajah se failed transactions database mein adhoore results aur half-updated state nahi chhodte. Yeh multi-object transactions ke liye sabse zyada matter karta hai, aur un databases ke liye jo secondary indexes maintain karte hain. Secondary index main data se alag structure hota hai. Isliye agar tum koi data change karo, toh index mein bhi matching change karna padta hai. Atomicity index ko main data ke saath consistent rakhti hai. Jo index data se match na kare, woh kaafi kaam ka nahi hoga.

Single-Node se Distributed Atomic Commit tak

Jo transaction ek hi database node par chalta hai, uski atomicity aam taur par storage engine deta hai. Jab client node ko commit karne ko kehta hai, database transaction ki writes ko durable banata hai, typically write-ahead log mein, aur phir disk par log mein ek commit record append karta hai. Agar isi beech database crash ho jaaye, toh node restart hone par transaction log se recover hota hai. Agar crash se pehle commit record disk par sahi se likh diya gaya tha, toh transaction committed maana jaata hai. Nahi, toh uski writes rollback ho jaati hain.

Toh single node par transaction commit hoga ya nahi, yeh is par depend karta hai ki data disk tak kis order mein pahunchta hai: pehle data, phir commit record. Key moment woh hai jab disk commit record likhna khatam karta hai. Us moment se pehle crash transaction ko abort kar sakta hai. Uske baad transaction committed hai, chahe database crash ho jaaye. Zaroori baat yeh hai ki ek hi device, yani ek node se jude ek disk ka controller, commit ko atomic banata hai.

Lekin agar ek transaction mein kai nodes involved hon toh? Maan lo tumhare paas partitioned database mein multi-object transaction hai, ya term-partitioned secondary index hai, jahan index entry primary data se alag node par rehti hai. Zyada-tar NoSQL distributed datastores aise distributed transactions support nahi karte. Kuch clustered relational systems karte hain, aur book unhe baad mein discuss karti hai.

In cases mein har node ko commit request bhej dena aur har ek par alag se commit kar lena kaafi nahi hai. Commit aasaani se kuch nodes par succeed aur kuch par fail ho sakta hai, jisse atomicity toot jaayegi. Aisa teen tarah se ho sakta hai:

  • Kuch nodes ko constraint violation ya conflict detect ho sakta hai, isliye unhe abort karna padta hai, jabki doosre nodes successfully commit kar sakte hain.
  • Kuch commit requests network mein kho sakti hain, aur timeout ki wajah se aakhir mein abort ho jaati hain, jabki doosri commit requests pahunch jaati hain.
  • Kuch nodes commit record poora likhne se pehle crash ho sakte hain. Woh recover hone par rollback kar dete hain, jabki doosre nodes successfully commit kar lete hain.

Agar kuch nodes commit karein aur kuch abort, toh nodes ek doosre se inconsistent ho jaate hain, bilkul Chapter 7 ke inconsistent replicas ki tarah. Aur ek baar transaction ek node par commit ho gaya, toh use baad mein wapas nahi liya ja sakta, chahe pata chale ki woh doosre node par abort ho gaya tha. Isliye node tabhi commit kare jab use pakka pata ho ki transaction ke baaki saare nodes bhi commit karenge.

Asli idea

Commit irrevocable hona chahiye. Ek baar commit ho gaya, toh use retract nahi kiya ja sakta. Doosre clients shayad pehle se committed data par depend kar rahe hon, aur node tabhi commit kare jab transaction ke baaki saare nodes ka commit karna pakka ho.

Is rule ki wajah yeh hai ki data commit hote hi doosre transactions ko dikhne lagta hai, aur doosre clients us par depend karna shuru kar sakte hain. Chapter 7 ka read committed isolation level isi par based hai. Agar commit ke baad bhi transaction abort ho sakta, toh jis transaction ne uska data padha tha, woh aise data par based hota jise baad mein "kabhi tha hi nahi" declare kar diya gaya. Un transactions ko bhi revert karna padta.

Committed transaction ke effects ko baad mein ek doosra, compensating transaction undo kar sakta hai. Lekin database ke point of view se woh ek alag transaction hai. Isliye transactions ke beech faile correctness rules application ki problem ban jaate hain.

Two-Phase Commit ka Introduction

Two-phase commit kai nodes par atomic transaction commit karne ka algorithm hai. Yeh guarantee deta hai ki ya toh saare nodes commit karenge ya saare abort. Distributed databases mein yeh ek classic algorithm hai. Kuch databases ise internally use karte hain, aur applications ke liye yeh XA transactions ke through available hai, jinhe Java Transaction API support karta hai, ya SOAP web services ke liye WS-AtomicTransaction ke through.

Single-node transaction ki tarah ek commit request ke bajaay, 2PC mein commit ya abort ka process do phases mein baant diya jaata hai. Isi se naam aaya hai. Book ka Figure 9-9 ek successful run dikhata hai. Neeche wali picture uska simplified version hai.

Dhyaan do

2PC aur 2PL ko confuse na karein. Two-phase commit (2PC) aur two-phase locking (2PL, Chapter 7 se) do bilkul alag cheezein hain. 2PC distributed database mein nodes ke beech atomic commit deta hai. 2PL serializable isolation deta hai. Behtar yahi hai ki dono ko poori tarah alag ideas maanein aur naamon ki is unfortunate similarity ko ignore karein.

2PC ek aisa component use karta hai jo single-node transactions mein aam taur par nahi dikhta: coordinator, jise transaction manager bhi kehte hain. Coordinator aksar usi application process ke andar ek library hota hai jo transaction request karta hai, jaise Java EE container mein embedded. Yeh ek alag process ya service bhi ho sakta hai. Book coordinators ke examples mein Narayana, JOTM, BTM aur MSDTC ginati hai.

2PC transaction ki shuruaat aise hoti hai ki application normal tarike se kai database nodes par data read aur write karta hai. In nodes ko participants kehte hain. Jab application commit ke liye ready hota hai, coordinator phase 1 shuru karta hai. Woh har participant ko ek prepare request bhejta hai aur poochta hai ki kya woh commit kar sakta hai. Phir coordinator jawab track karta hai:

  • Agar har participant yes bolta hai, yani woh commit ke liye ready hai, toh coordinator phase 2 mein commit request bhejta hai, aur commit ho jaata hai.
  • Agar koi bhi participant no bolta hai, toh coordinator phase 2 mein saare nodes ko abort request bhejta hai.
Example

Book is process ki tulna ek traditional wedding ceremony se karti hai. Minister dulhan aur dulhe se ek-ek karke poochta hai ki kya woh doosre se shaadi karna chahta hai. Aam taur par dono yes bolte hain. Jaise hi minister ko dono jawab mil jaate hain, woh unhe married declare kar deta hai. Ab marriage committed hai, aur khabar wahan present sabko announce ho jaati hai. Agar dulhan ya dulha mein se koi yes nahi bolta, toh ceremony cancel ho jaati hai.

Promises ka System

Is chhote description se saaf nahi hota ki two-phase commit atomicity kyun ensure karta hai jabki kai nodes par one-phase commit nahi karta. Two-phase mein bhi prepare aur commit requests utni hi aasaani se kho sakti hain. Toh 2PC mein alag kya hai? Yeh kaise kaam karta hai, yeh samajhne ke liye process ko aur detail mein dekhna padega:

  1. Jab application distributed transaction shuru karna chahta hai, woh coordinator se ek transaction ID maangta hai. Yeh ID globally unique hoti hai.
  2. Application har participant par ek single-node transaction shuru karta hai, aur usmein woh global transaction ID attach kar deta hai. Saari reads aur writes in single-node transactions mein hoti hain. Is stage par kuch galat ho jaaye, jaise node crash ho jaaye ya request timeout ho jaaye, toh coordinator ya koi bhi participant abort kar sakta hai.
  3. Jab application commit ke liye ready hota hai, coordinator har participant ko prepare request bhejta hai, jis par global transaction ID tagged hoti hai. Agar inmein se koi request fail ya timeout ho jaaye, toh coordinator us transaction ID ke liye saare participants ko abort request bhej deta hai.
  4. Jab participant ko prepare request milti hai, use pakka karna hota hai ki woh har haalat mein transaction ko definitely commit kar sakta hai. Isme transaction ka saara data disk par likhna shaamil hai, taaki baad mein commit se mana karne ke liye crash, power failure ya disk space khatam hona koi acceptable bahana na rahe. Conflicts aur constraint violations check karna bhi isi mein aata hai. Agar woh yes bolta hai, toh woh promise karta hai ki poocha jaane par transaction ko bina error ke commit karega. Yani participant abort karne ka apna right chhod deta hai, lekin abhi commit nahi kiya hota.
  5. Jab coordinator ko apni prepare requests ke saare jawab mil jaate hain, woh ek definitive decision leta hai. Woh tabhi commit karta hai jab har participant ne yes vote kiya ho. Coordinator ko yeh decision apne transaction log mein disk par likhna hota hai, taaki baad mein crash ho toh use outcome pata rahe. Is write ko commit point kehte hain.
  6. Decision disk par aa jaane ke baad commit ya abort request saare participants ko bheji jaati hai. Agar woh request fail ya timeout ho, toh coordinator ko succeed hone tak forever retry karna padta hai. Wapas jaane ka koi raasta nahi hai. Decision commit ka tha, toh use carry out karna hi hoga, chahe kitne bhi retries lagein. Agar beech mein koi participant crash ho gaya, toh us participant ke recover hone par transaction commit ho jaayega. Usne yes vote kiya tha, isliye wapas aane par woh commit se mana nahi kar sakta.

Protocol mein do crucial points of no return hain. Jab participant yes vote karta hai, toh woh promise karta hai ki baad mein woh definitely commit kar paayega, halanki coordinator phir bhi abort karne ka faisla le sakta hai. Aur coordinator ke decide karte hi decision irrevocable ho jaata hai. Yahi do promises 2PC ki atomicity guarantee karte hain. Single-node atomic commit mein yeh dono events ek ho jaate hain: transaction log mein commit record likhna.

Marriage wali analogy yahan bhi fit hoti hai. Yes bolne se pehle har insaan no bolkar wedding abort karne ke liye free hai. Yes bolne ke baad koi use retract nahi kar sakta. Maan lo yes bolte hi tum behosh ho gaye, aur minister ka pronouncement nahi sun paaye, tab bhi marriage ho chuki hai. Hosh aane par tum minister se apni global transaction ID ka status poochkar pata kar sakte ho ki tum married hain ya nahi. Ya phir minister ke commit request retry karne ka wait kar sakte hain, kyunki tumhare behosh rehte hue bhi retries chalte rahe.

Coordinator Failure

Book bata chuki hai ki 2PC ke dauran participant ya network fail ho jaaye toh kya hota hai. Agar koi prepare request fail ya timeout ho jaaye, toh coordinator transaction abort kar deta hai. Agar koi commit ya abort request fail ho jaaye, toh coordinator use indefinitely retry karta hai. Lekin yeh kam saaf hai ki coordinator khud crash ho jaaye toh kya hoga.

Agar coordinator prepare requests bhejne se pehle fail ho jaaye, toh participant safely transaction abort kar sakta hai. Lekin jab participant ko prepare request mil chuki ho aur usne yes vote kar diya ho, tab woh apne aap abort nahi kar sakta. Use coordinator se sunne ke liye wait karna padta hai ki transaction commit hua ya abort. Agar is point par coordinator crash ho jaaye ya network fail ho jaaye, toh participant wait ke alawa kuch nahi kar sakta. Is state mein participant ko in doubt ya uncertain kehte hain.

Agli picture is case ko dikhati hai. Coordinator ne commit karne ka decision liya, aur database 2 ko commit request mil gayi. Lekin coordinator database 1 ko commit request bhejne se pehle crash ho gaya. Isliye database 1 ko pata nahi ki commit karna hai ya abort. Timeout se bhi madad nahi milti. Agar database 1 timeout ke baad khud abort kar de, toh woh database 2 se inconsistent ho jaayega, jisne commit kar liya hai. Isi tarah database 1 ka khud commit kar dena bhi safe nahi hai, kyunki ho sakta hai koi aur participant abort kar chuka ho.

Coordinator se sune bina participant ko pata hi nahi chal sakta ki commit karna hai ya abort. Principle mein participants aapas mein baat karke pata kar sakte hain ki kisne kya vote kiya, aur ek agreement par pahunch sakte hain. Lekin yeh 2PC protocol ka hissa nahi hai.

Isliye 2PC complete hone ka ekmaatra tarika yeh hai ki coordinator ke recover hone ka wait kiya jaaye. Isi wajah se coordinator ko commit ya abort requests bhejne se pehle apna decision disk par transaction log mein likhna padta hai. Recover hone par coordinator apna log padhkar har in-doubt transaction ka status pata karta hai. Jis transaction ka coordinator ke log mein commit record nahi hota, use abort kar diya jaata hai. Toh 2PC ka commit point coordinator par ek regular single-node atomic commit hi ban jaata hai.

Try karo

Two-phase commit ke do moments compare karein. Pehle mein coordinator koi bhi prepare request bhejne se pehle crash ho jaata hai. Doosre mein participant pehle hi yes bol chuka hai, aur uske baad coordinator crash hota hai. Kis case mein participant khud abort kar sakta hai, aur jawab badalta kyun hai?

Three-Phase Commit

Two-phase commit ko blocking atomic commit protocol kehte hain, kyunki 2PC coordinator ke recover hone ka wait karte hue atak sakta hai. Theory mein atomic commit protocol ko non-blocking banana possible hai, taaki node fail hone par woh atke nahi. Practice mein ise kaam karwana seedha nahi hai.

Ek alternative, three-phase commit (3PC), propose kiya gaya hai. Lekin 3PC maanta hai ki network mein delay bounded hai aur nodes ke response times bounded hain. Zyada-tar practical systems mein network delay unbounded hota hai aur process pauses hote hain, jaisa Chapter 8 mein dikha, isliye unmein 3PC atomicity guarantee nahi kar sakta.

Aam taur par non-blocking atomic commit ke liye perfect failure detector chahiye, yani yeh pata karne ka reliable tarika ki node crash hua hai ya nahi. Unbounded delay wale network mein timeout reliable failure detector nahi hai, kyunki request network problem ki wajah se bhi timeout ho sakti hai, chahe koi node crash na hua ho. Isi wajah se coordinator failure ki known problem hai, phir bhi 2PC ka use chalta rehta hai.

Distributed Transactions practice mein

Distributed transactions, khaas kar jo two-phase commit par bane hote hain, unki reputation mixed hai. Ek taraf, maana jaata hai ki yeh ek zaroori safety guarantee dete hain, jo warna achieve karna mushkil hota. Doosri taraf, inki criticism hoti hai ki yeh operational problems create karte hain, performance kharab karte hain, aur jitna promise karte hain utna deliver nahi karte. Bahut saari cloud services operational problems ki wajah se distributed transactions implement hi nahi karti.

Kuch implementations mein performance ka bahut bada penalty hota hai. Jaise, MySQL mein distributed transactions single-node transactions se 10 guna se bhi zyada slow report kiye gaye hain. Isliye agar log inhe use karne se mana karte hain, toh surprise ki baat nahi. 2PC ka zyada performance cost do jagah se aata hai: crash recovery ke liye extra disk flushes (fsync), aur extra network round trips.

Lekin Kleppmann kehte hain ki distributed transactions ko poori tarah dismiss nahi karna chahiye. Inme important lessons hain. Sabse pehle, yeh clear hona zaroori hai ki “distributed transaction” ka matlab kya hai. Do bilkul alag types aksar confuse ho jaate hain:

  • Database-internal distributed transactions. Kuch distributed databases, jo apne standard setup mein replication aur partitioning use karte hain, apne hi nodes ke beech transactions support karte hain. VoltDB aur MySQL Cluster ka NDB storage engine iske examples hain. Yahan transaction ke saare nodes same database software chalate hain.
  • Heterogeneous distributed transactions. Yahan participants do ya zyada alag technologies hoti hain. Yeh alag vendors ke do databases ho sakte hain, ya message broker jaisa koi non-database system bhi. In systems ke across distributed transaction ko phir bhi atomic commit ensure karna padta hai, chahe systems andar se bilkul alag hon.

Database-internal transactions ko kisi doosre system ke saath compatible hone ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Isliye woh koi bhi protocol use kar sakte hain aur us ek technology ke hisaab se optimizations laga sakte hain, aur aksar kaafi achha kaam karte hain. Heterogeneous transactions kaafi zyada challenging hote hain.

Exactly-Once Message Processing

Heterogeneous distributed transactions se alag-alag systems ko powerful tarike se combine kiya ja sakta hai. Jaise, message queue ke message ko “processed” tabhi acknowledge kiya jaa sakta hai jab usse process karne wala database transaction successfully commit ho gaya ho. Iske liye message acknowledgment aur database writes ko ek hi atomic transaction mein saath commit kiya jaata hai. Distributed transaction support ho, toh yeh tab bhi possible hai jab message broker aur database bilkul alag technologies hon aur alag machines par chal rahe hon.

Message delivery ya database transaction, dono mein se koi bhi fail ho, toh dono abort ho jaate hain. Isliye message broker baad mein message ko safely redeliver kar sakta hai. Message aur uske processing ke side effects ko atomically commit karne se message effectively exactly once process hota hai, chahe succeed hone se pehle kuch retries lage ho. Abort se us adhoori attempt ke saare side effects discard ho jaate hain.

Example

Maan lo message process karne mein email bhejna bhi shaamil hai, aur email server two-phase commit support nahi karta. Agar processing fail hui aur retry hui, toh email do-teen baar ja sakta hai. Lekin agar transaction abort hone par message processing ke saare side effects rollback ho jaayein, toh processing step ko safely retry kiya jaa sakta hai, jaise kuch hua hi nahi. Catch yeh hai ki transaction se affected har system ko same atomic commit protocol use karne ke layak hona chahiye.

Exactly-once message processing par book Chapter 11 mein dobara aati hai. Pehle hum us atomic commit protocol ko dekhte hain jo aise heterogeneous distributed transactions possible banata hai.

XA Transactions

X/Open XA (eXtended Architecture ka short form) heterogeneous technologies ke across two-phase commit implement karne ka ek standard hai. Yeh 1991 mein aaya tha aur kaafi widely implement hua hai. Bahut se traditional relational databases XA support karte hain, jaise PostgreSQL, MySQL, DB2, SQL Server aur Oracle. Support karne wale message brokers mein ActiveMQ, HornetQ, MSMQ aur IBM MQ aate hain.

XA koi network protocol nahi hai. Yeh ek C API hai jo transaction coordinator se interface karne ke liye hai. Doosri languages ke liye bhi bindings available hain. Java EE world mein XA transactions Java Transaction API (JTA) ke through milte hain. JTA ko Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) use karne wale databases ke drivers support karte hain, aur Java Message Service (JMS) use karne wale message brokers ke drivers bhi.

XA maanta hai ki tumhari application participant databases ya messaging services se baat karne ke liye ek network driver ya client library use karti hai. Agar driver XA support karta hai, toh woh XA API call karke pata lagata hai ki koi operation distributed transaction ka hissa hona chahiye ya nahi. Agar haan, toh woh zaroori information database server ko bhej deta hai. Driver callbacks bhi expose karta hai, jinke through coordinator participant se prepare, commit ya abort karne ko keh sakta hai.

Transaction coordinator XA API implement karta hai. Standard yeh nahi batata ki ise kaise implement karna hai. Practice mein coordinator aksar bas ek library hoti hai, jo usi process mein load hoti hai jisme woh application chal rahi hai jo transaction issue karti hai. Yeh koi alag service nahi hoti. Yeh transaction ke participants ka track rakhta hai. Prepare karne ko kehne ke baad driver ke callback ke through unke responses collect karta hai. Aur local disk par ek log rakhta hai, jisme har transaction ka commit ya abort decision record hota hai.

Agar application process crash ho jaaye, ya jis machine par woh chal raha hai woh mar jaaye, toh coordinator bhi saath chala jaata hai. Jin participants ke paas prepared lekin uncommitted transactions hain, woh phir in doubt mein atak jaate hain. Coordinator ka log application server ki local disk par hota hai, isliye us server ko restart karna padega. Coordinator library ko log padhna padega taaki har transaction ka outcome recover ho sake. Tabhi woh driver ke XA callbacks use karke participants ko commit ya abort karne ko keh sakti hai. Database server coordinator se directly contact nahi kar sakta, kyunki saari communication uski client library se hokar jaati hai.

In doubt mein locks pakad kar rakhna

Hume itna fikr kyun hai ki transaction in doubt mein atka hua hai? Baaki system aage badh kar us in-doubt transaction ko ignore kyun nahi kar sakta, jo eventually clean up ho hi jaayega?

Problem locking ki hai. Chapter 7 mein samjhaya tha ki database transactions aam taur par jis bhi row ko modify karte hain, us par exclusive lock lete hain, taaki dirty writes na hon. Agar tumhe serializable isolation chahiye, toh two-phase locking use karne wale database ko transaction jo rows padhta hai un par bhi shared lock lena padta hai.

Database in locks ko tab tak release nahi kar sakta jab tak transaction commit ya abort na ho jaaye. Book ke Figure 9-9 mein yeh shaded area hai. Isliye two-phase commit mein transaction jab tak in doubt hai, tab tak apne locks pakde rakhta hai. Agar coordinator crash hota hai aur dobara start hone mein 20 minute lagte hain, toh woh locks 20 minute tak held rahenge. Agar coordinator ka log poori tarah lost ho gaya, toh locks hamesha ke liye held reh sakte hain, ya kam se kam tab tak jab tak koi administrator situation ko haath se resolve na kare.

Jab tak locks held hain, koi aur transaction un rows ko modify nahi kar sakta. Database ke hisaab se, doosre transactions ko unhe padhne se bhi roka jaa sakta hai. Matlab doosre transactions bas aage nahi badh sakte. Agar unhe wahi data chahiye, toh woh blocked ho jaate hain. Isse application ke bade hisse tab tak unavailable ho sakte hain jab tak in-doubt transaction resolve na ho.

Coordinator failure se recover karna

Theory mein, agar coordinator crash hoke restart hota hai, toh use apne log se cleanly recover karke saare in-doubt transactions resolve kar dene chahiye. Practice mein orphaned in-doubt transactions hote hain. Yeh woh transactions hain jinka outcome coordinator kisi wajah se decide nahi kar paata, jaise transaction log lost ho gaya ya software bug se corrupt ho gaya. Aise transactions automatically resolve nahi ho sakte. Yeh database mein hamesha pade rehte hain, locks pakde hue aur doosre transactions ko block karte hue.

Database servers reboot karne se bhi yeh theek nahi hota. 2PC ki sahi implementation ko in-doubt transaction ke locks restarts ke across bhi rakhne padte hain. Warna atomicity todne ka risk hoga. Yeh ek sticky situation hai.

Bahar nikalne ka ek hi tarika hai: administrator haath se decide kare ki aise har transaction ko commit karna hai ya rollback. Administrator ko har in-doubt transaction ke participants check karne padte hain, dekhna padta hai ki kisi participant ne pehle hi commit ya abort kar diya hai ya nahi, aur phir wahi outcome baaki sab par apply karna padta hai. Isme kaafi manual mehnat lag sakti hai. Yeh aksar kisi serious production outage ke dauraan bahut stress aur time pressure mein hota hai. Warna coordinator itni buri halat mein kyun hota?

Bahut si XA implementations mein ek emergency escape hatch hota hai jise heuristic decisions kehte hain. Inse participant coordinator ke decision ke bina khud hi in-doubt transaction ko commit ya abort karne ka decision le sakta hai. Yahan “heuristic” word ek polite tarika hai yeh kehne ka ki decision shayad atomicity tod dega, kyunki yeh two-phase commit ke promises ke khilaaf jaata hai. Heuristic decisions sirf catastrophic situations se nikalne ke liye hain, regular use ke liye nahi.

Distributed Transactions ki limitations

XA transactions ek real aur important problem solve karte hain: kai participant data systems ko ek-doosre ke saath consistent rakhna. Lekin jaisa humne dekha, inke saath major operational problems bhi aati hain. Key realization yeh hai ki transaction coordinator khud ek tarah ka database hai, kyunki woh transaction outcomes store karta hai. Isliye use bhi utni hi care chahiye jitni kisi aur important database ko. Isse kai problems nikalti hain:

  • Single point of failure. Agar coordinator replicated nahi hai, aur sirf ek machine par chalta hai, toh woh poore system ke liye single point of failure hai. Uske fail hone se doosre application servers in-doubt transactions ke locks par block ho jaate hain. Surprising baat yeh hai ki bahut si coordinator implementations by default highly available nahi hoti, ya unme sirf basic replication support hota hai.
  • Application servers stateless nahi rehte. Bahut si server-side applications stateless model follow karti hain, jo HTTP ko pasand hai. Unka saara durable state database mein hota hai, isliye application servers apni marzi se add aur remove kiye jaa sakte hain. Lekin jab coordinator application server ke andar chalta hai, toh deployment ki nature badal jaati hai. Coordinator ke logs durable state ka crucial hissa ban jaate hain, databases jitne hi important, kyunki crash ke baad in-doubt transactions recover karne ke liye unki zaroorat padti hai. Aise application servers ab stateless nahi rehte.
  • Lowest common denominator. XA ko data systems ki badi range ke saath kaam karna padta hai, isliye woh sirf wahi offer kar sakta hai jo un sab mein common ho. Jaise, woh alag-alag systems ke across deadlocks detect nahi kar sakta, kyunki iske liye ek standard protocol chahiye jisme systems yeh information exchange karein ki har transaction kaun se locks ka wait kar raha hai. Yeh serializable snapshot isolation ke saath bhi kaam nahi karta, kyunki iske liye alag-alag systems ke across conflicts identify karne ka protocol chahiye.
  • Database-internal transactions kam limited hote hain. Ek single distributed database ke andar ke transactions mein limits utni severe nahi hoti. Jaise, serializable snapshot isolation ka distributed version possible hai. Lekin ek basic problem phir bhi rehti hai. 2PC mein transaction commit hone ke liye har participant ko respond karna zaroori hai. Isliye agar system ka koi bhi hissa broken hai, toh transaction bhi fail ho jaata hai. Distributed transactions failures ko amplify karte hain. Yeh fault-tolerant systems banane ke goal ke khilaaf jaata hai.

Kya in baaton ka matlab hai ki hume kai systems ko ek-doosre ke saath consistent rakhne ki koshish chhod deni chahiye? Bilkul nahi. Aise aur tarike hain jo heterogeneous distributed transactions ki takleef ke bina wahi kaam karte hain. Inpar Kleppmann Chapters 11 aur 12 mein wapas aate hain. Lekin pehle consensus ka topic poora karte hain.

Fault-Tolerant Consensus

Simple words mein, consensus ka matlab hai kai nodes ko kisi cheez par agree karwana. Jaise, kai log ek saath airplane ya theater ki aakhri seat book karne ki koshish karein, ya wahi username register karne ki koshish karein. Consensus algorithm decide kar sakta hai ki in aapas mein incompatible operations mein se kaun jeetega.

Problem ko aam taur par aise formalize kiya jaata hai. Ek ya zyada nodes values propose kar sakte hain, aur algorithm unmein se ek par decide karta hai. Seat-booking example mein, customer ki request handle karne wala har node us customer ki ID propose kar sakta hai jise woh serve kar raha hai. Decision phir batata hai ki seat kis customer ko mili.

Is formal version mein consensus algorithm ko chaar properties satisfy karni padti hain:

  • Uniform agreement. Koi bhi do nodes alag decide nahi karte.
  • Integrity. Koi node do baar decide nahi karta.
  • Validity. Agar koi node value v decide karta hai, toh v kisi node ne propose ki thi.
  • Termination. Jo bhi node crash nahi hota, woh eventually koi value decide kar leta hai.

Book batati hai ki is version ko uniform consensus kehte hain, aur asynchronous systems mein unreliable failure detectors ke saath yeh ordinary consensus ke equivalent hai. Yeh “nodes” word bhi use karti hai jahan academic papers “processes” likhte hain.

Pehli do properties, agreement aur integrity, consensus ka core hain. Sab ek hi outcome par decide karte hain, aur decision ho jaane ke baad koi apna mind change nahi kar sakta. Validity property mainly trivial solutions ko rule out karne ke liye hai. Jaise, jo algorithm proposed value kuch bhi ho, hamesha null decide kare, woh agreement aur integrity satisfy kar dega. Lekin validity satisfy nahi karega.

Agar tumhe fault tolerance ki parwah nahi hai, toh pehli teen properties aasaan hain. Tum ek node ko dictator hardcode kar sakte ho, aur saare decisions wahi node le. Lekin agar woh ek node fail ho jaaye, toh system koi decision nahi le sakta. Two-phase commit mein bilkul yahi hua tha. Coordinator fail ho jaaye, toh in-doubt participants decide nahi kar sakte ki commit karna hai ya abort.

Termination property fault tolerance ko formalize karti hai. Yeh kehti hai ki consensus algorithm bas baithe-baithe hamesha kuch na karta rahe, aisa nahi ho sakta.
