Use progress karna hi padega, aur kuch nodes fail bhi ho jaayein, toh baaki nodes ko phir bhi decision tak pahunchna hoga. Book ki terminology mein, termination ek liveness property hai: kuch achha eventually hota hai. Baaki teen safety properties hain: kuch bura kabhi nahi hota. (Book safety aur liveness ki baat apne system models wale chapter mein karti hai.)

Consensus ka system model maanta hai ki jab koi node crash hota hai, toh woh achanak gayab ho jaata hai aur kabhi wapas nahi aata. Socho ki ek earthquake aaya jisne tumhare node wale datacenter ko tabah kar diya, aur node 30 feet kichad ke neeche dab gaya, ab woh kabhi online nahi aayega. Is model mein, jo bhi algorithm kisi node ke recover hone ka wait karta hai woh termination satisfy nahi kar sakta. Khaas taur par, two-phase commit termination ki requirements poori nahi karta.

Waise, agar har node crash ho jaaye aur koi bhi chal nahi raha, toh koi algorithm kuch decide nahi kar sakta. Algorithm kitni failures tolerate kar sakta hai, uski ek limit hoti hai. Yeh prove kiya jaa sakta hai ki termination guarantee karne ke liye kisi bhi consensus algorithm ko kam se kam nodes ka majority sahi se kaam karta hua chahiye. Woh majority safely ek quorum bana sakti hai, jo Chapter 5 mein describe kiya tha.

Isliye termination property tabhi hold karti hai jab maana jaaye ki aadhe se kam nodes crashed ya unreachable hain. Lekin zyadatar consensus implementations safety properties (agreement, integrity aur validity) tab bhi rakhti hain jab nodes ka majority fail ho jaaye ya serious network problem ho. Bada outage system ko requests process karne se rok sakta hai. Lekin woh consensus system ko corrupt karke invalid decisions nahi karwa sakta.

Zyadatar consensus algorithms yeh bhi maante hain ki Byzantine faults nahi hain. Byzantine fault woh hota hai jisme node protocol ko sahi tarah follow nahi karta, jaise alag-alag nodes ko contradictory messages bhejna. Aisa hua toh safety properties toot sakti hain. Consensus ko Byzantine faults ke against robust banana possible hai, jab tak ek-tihaai se kam nodes Byzantine-faulty hon. Lekin un algorithms ko detail mein discuss karne ki book ke paas jagah nahi hai.

Consensus Algorithms aur Total Order Broadcast

Sabse mashhoor fault-tolerant consensus algorithms hain Viewstamped Replication (VSR), Paxos, Raft aur Zab. Inme bahut similarities hain, lekin yeh same nahi hain. Book har ek ki poori detail mein nahi jaati. Agar tum khud consensus system implement nahi kar rahe, toh unke shared high-level ideas jaanna kaafi hai. Book aisa karne se mana karti hai, kyunki yeh bahut mushkil hai.

In mein se zyadatar algorithms formal model ko directly use nahi karte. Woh model ek single value propose karta hai aur uspar decide karta hai, saath mein chaar properties satisfy karta hai. Iske bajaye, yeh values ke ek sequence par decide karte hain. Isse yeh total order broadcast algorithms ban jaate hain, jo is chapter mein pehle cover hue the.

Total order broadcast mein zaroori hai ki messages exactly once, same order mein, saare nodes ko deliver hon. Yeh consensus ke kai rounds chalane ke equivalent hai. Har round mein nodes woh message propose karte hain jo woh agla bhejna chahte hain, aur phir total order mein deliver hone wale agle message par decide karte hain. Matlab total order broadcast consensus ke baar-baar rounds ke equivalent hai, jahan har consensus decision ek message delivery ke barabar hai. Properties aage carry hoti hain:

  • Consensus agreement ki wajah se, saare nodes same messages same order mein deliver karte hain.
  • Integrity ki wajah se, messages duplicate nahi hote.
  • Validity ki wajah se, messages corrupt nahi hote aur hawa se nahi banaye jaate.
  • Termination ki wajah se, messages lost nahi hote.

Viewstamped Replication, Raft aur Zab total order broadcast ko directly implement karte hain. Yeh har value ke liye alag consensus round chalane se zyada efficient hai. Paxos ke case mein is optimization ko Multi-Paxos kehte hain.

Single-Leader Replication aur Consensus

Chapter 5 mein single-leader replication describe kiya tha. Woh saare writes leader ko bhejta hai aur followers par same order mein apply karta hai, jisse replicas up to date rehte hain. Kya yeh essentially total order broadcast hi nahi hai? Agar hai, toh Chapter 5 mein hum consensus ki fikr kiye bina kaise kaam chala gaye?

Jawab is baat mein hai ki leader kaise chuna jaata hai. Agar leader haath se chuna jaata hai, operations team ke log use configure karte hain, toh tumhare paas dictatorial kism ka consensus algorithm hai. Sirf ek node ko writes accept karne ki ijazat hai, aur wahi replication log mein writes ka order decide karta hai. Agar woh node down ho jaaye, toh jab tak operators haath se koi aur leader configure na karein, system writes accept nahi kar sakta. Yeh practice mein achha chal sakta hai. Lekin yeh consensus ki termination property satisfy nahi karta, kyunki progress se pehle kisi insaan ko intervene karna padta hai.

Kuch databases automatic leader election aur failover karte hain. Agar purana leader fail ho jaaye, toh woh kisi follower ko naya leader promote kar dete hain, jaisa Chapter 5 mein discuss hua. Isse hum fault-tolerant total order broadcast ke kareeb pahunchte hain, aur isliye consensus solve karne ke bhi.

Lekin ek problem hai. Pehle humne split brain ki baat ki thi, aur kaha tha ki saare nodes ko agree karna hoga ki leader kaun hai. Warna do nodes dono khud ko leader maan sakte hain aur database ko inconsistent state mein pahuncha sakte hain. Toh leader elect karne ke liye hume consensus chahiye. Lekin upar describe kiye consensus algorithms total order broadcast algorithms hain. Total order broadcast single-leader replication jaisa hai, aur single-leader replication ko leader chahiye. Toh hum atak gaye lagte hain. Leader elect karne ke liye pehle leader chahiye. Consensus solve karne ke liye pehle consensus solve karna padega.

Is loop se bahar kaise nikalein? Iska jawab epoch numbering hai, jo aage describe hai.

Epoch Numbering aur Quorums

Ab tak discuss hue saare consensus protocols kisi na kisi form mein leader use karte hain, lekin woh guarantee nahi dete ki leader har waqt unique hai. Iske bajaye woh weaker guarantee dete hain. Protocols ek epoch number define karte hain, jise Paxos mein ballot number, Viewstamped Replication mein view number, aur Raft mein term number kehte hain. Har epoch ke andar protocol guarantee deta hai ki sirf ek leader hai.

Jab bhi lagta hai ki current leader dead hai, nodes ke beech naya leader elect karne ke liye vote start hota hai. Us election ko ek naya, bada epoch number milta hai. Isliye epoch numbers totally ordered hote hain aur hamesha badhte hain. Agar do alag epochs ke do alag leaders mein conflict ho, shayad isliye ki pehla leader asal mein dead nahi tha, toh jis leader ka epoch number zyada hai woh jeet jaata hai.

Leader ko kuch bhi decide karne se pehle check karna padta hai ki koi aur higher epoch number wala leader conflicting decision lene ke kareeb toh nahi hai. Leader ko kaise pata chale ki kisi aur node ne use hata nahi diya? Chapter 8 mein yeh idea aaya tha ki sach majority se define hota hai. Node apne judgment par poora bharosa nahi kar sakta. Node ka khud ko leader sochna kaafi nahi hai, doosre nodes bhi use leader maanein, yeh zaroori hai.

Isliye leader ko nodes ke quorum se votes collect karne padte hain. Leader jo bhi decision lena chahta hai, uske liye woh proposed value doosre nodes ko bhejta hai aur quorum ke favor mein respond karne ka wait karta hai. Quorum aam taur par, par hamesha nahi, nodes ka majority hota hai. Node kisi proposal ke favor mein tabhi vote karta hai jab use higher epoch wale kisi aur leader ka pata na ho.

Yani voting ke do rounds hain. Ek vote leader chunta hai. Doosra vote leader ke proposal ko approve karta hai. Key insight yeh hai ki in dono votes ke quorums overlap karne chahiye. Agar kisi proposal par vote succeed hota hai, toh jin nodes ne uske liye vote diya unmein se kam se kam ek ne sabse recent leader election mein bhi hissa liya hoga. Isliye agar proposal par vote kisi higher epoch number ko reveal nahi karta, toh current leader conclude kar sakta hai ki higher epoch wala koi leader election nahi hua. Use yakeen ho sakta hai ki leadership abhi bhi uske paas hai, aur phir woh proposed value ko safely decide kar sakta hai.

Neeche ki picture is rule ka ek simplified view hai, teen nodes ke saath. Epoch 1 mein node A leader hai. Jab baaki nodes epoch 2 mein election start karte hain, toh node A leader nahi rehta. Node B election start karta hai, node C B ko vote deta hai, aur B leader ban jaata hai. A ka ek stale message, jisme abhi bhi epoch 1 hai, un nodes se refuse kar diya jaata hai jo epoch 2 dekh chuke hain.

Yeh voting process two-phase commit jaisa dikhta hai. Lekin bade differences hain. 2PC mein coordinator elect nahi hota. Fault-tolerant consensus algorithms ko sirf nodes ke majority se votes chahiye, jabki 2PC ko har participant se yes vote chahiye. Neeche ki table comparison summarize karti hai. Consensus algorithms ek recovery process bhi define karte hain, jisse naya leader elect hone ke baad nodes consistent state mein pahunchte hain. Isse safety properties hamesha meet hoti hain. Yahi differences consensus ki correctness aur fault tolerance ki key hain.

Trade-offs
AspectTwo-phase commitFault-tolerant consensus
Decide kaun karta haiPehle se fixed coordinator, elected nahiVote se chuna gaya leader, jo epoch number se pehchana jaata hai
Kitne votes chahiyeHar participant se yesNodes ka majority
Failure ke baad recoveryProtocol define nahi karta. Participants coordinator ka wait karte hain, aur locks der tak pakde reh sakte hain.Protocol define karta hai. Naya leader nodes ko consistent state mein laata hai, aur majority chal raha ho tab tak progress jaari rehta hai.

Consensus ki Limitations

Consensus algorithms distributed systems ke liye bahut badi breakthrough hain. Yeh un systems mein concrete safety properties (agreement, integrity aur validity) laate hain jahan baaki sab kuch uncertain hota hai. Aur yeh fault-tolerant bhi rehte hain, matlab jab tak nodes ka majority chal raha hai aur reachable hai, woh progress karte rehte hain. Yeh total order broadcast dete hain, isliye linearizable atomic operations ko bhi fault-tolerant tarike se implement kar sakte hain.

Phir bhi inhe har jagah use nahi kiya jaata, kyunki inke benefits ki ek keemat hoti hai:

  • Synchronous replication. Proposal decide hone se pehle nodes jo voting karte hain, woh ek tarah ki synchronous replication hai. Databases aksar asynchronous replication ke liye configure hote hain. Asynchronous replication mein failover par kuch committed data lost ho sakta hai. Lekin bahut log better performance ke liye yeh risk accept kar lete hain.
  • Strict majority. Consensus systems ko kaam karne ke liye hamesha strict majority chahiye. Ek failure tolerate karne ke liye kam se kam teen nodes chahiye, kyunki teen mein se bache hue do majority banate hain. Do failures tolerate karne ke liye kam se kam paanch nodes chahiye, kyunki paanch mein se bache hue teen majority banate hain. Agar network failure kuch nodes ko baaki se kaat de, toh sirf majority wala hissa progress kar sakta hai. Baaki block ho jaata hai.
  • Fixed membership. Zyadatar consensus algorithms maante hain ki vote karne wale nodes ka ek fixed set hai. Tum seedha nodes add ya remove nahi kar sakte. Membership ko time ke saath badalne dene wale extensions hain, lekin woh kaafi kam samjhe gaye hain.
  • Timeouts par nirbhar rehna. Consensus systems aam taur par failed nodes detect karne ke liye timeouts par depend karte hain. Jin environments mein network delays bahut variable hote hain, khaas kar geographically distributed mein, wahan node temporary network issue ki wajah se galti se maan sakta hai ki leader fail ho gaya. Isse safety ko nuksaan nahi hota. Lekin frequent leader elections se performance bahut kharab ho jaata hai, kyunki system useful kaam karne se zyada waqt leader chunne mein lagata hai.
  • Kharab links ke prati sensitivity. Kuch consensus algorithms network problems ke prati bahut sensitive hote hain. Book Raft ko unpleasant edge cases wala batati hai. Agar poora network sahi chal raha ho, sirf ek link consistently unreliable ho, toh leadership do nodes ke beech bounce karti reh sakti hai, ya current leader ko baar-baar resign karne par majboor kiya jaa sakta hai. Phir system effectively kabhi progress nahi karta. Doosre consensus algorithms mein bhi aisi hi problems hain, aur aise algorithms design karna jo unreliable networks ko better handle karein, abhi bhi ek open research problem hai.

Membership aur Coordination Services

ZooKeeper ya etcd jaise projects ko aksar “distributed key-value stores” ya “coordination and configuration services” kaha jaata hai. Inka API database jaisa hi lagta hai. Tum kisi key ki value read aur write kar sakte ho, aur keys par iterate kar sakte ho. Toh agar yeh basically databases hain, toh yeh consensus algorithm implement karne ki mehnat kyun karte hain? Yeh doosre databases se alag kyun hain?

Yeh samajhne ke liye dekhna madad karta hai ki ZooKeeper jaisi service use kaise hoti hai. Application developer ke taur par tum ZooKeeper ko shayad hi directly use karoge, kyunki yeh general-purpose database ke roop mein achha fit nahi hai. Zyada chance hai ki tum use indirectly, kisi aur project ke through use karenge. HBase, Hadoop YARN, OpenStack Nova aur Kafka sab background mein chal rahe ZooKeeper par depend karte hain. Toh in projects ko isse milta kya hai?

ZooKeeper aur etcd chhota data hold karne ke liye design kiye gaye hain, jo poora memory mein fit ho jaaye, halanki durability ke liye woh phir bhi disk par likhte hain. Tum apni application ka saara data wahan store nahi karna chahoge. Yeh chhota data saare nodes par fault-tolerant total order broadcast algorithm se replicate hota hai. Jaisa pehle discuss hua, total order broadcast bilkul wahi hai jo database replication ko chahiye. Agar har message ek write hai, toh same writes same order mein apply karne se replicas consistent rehte hain.

ZooKeeper Google ki Chubby lock service ke model par bana hai. Yeh total order broadcast implement karta hai, aur isliye consensus bhi. Yeh kai aur features bhi deta hai jo distributed systems banate waqt bahut useful nikalte hain:

  • Linearizable atomic operations. Atomic compare-and-set se tum lock implement kar sakte ho. Agar kai nodes ek saath wahi operation try karein, toh sirf ek succeed hota hai. Consensus protocol guarantee deta hai ki operation atomic aur linearizable hai, chahe kisi bhi point par node fail ho ya network interrupt ho. Distributed lock aam taur par lease ke roop mein implement hota hai, jisme expiry time hota hai, taaki client fail ho toh woh eventually release ho jaaye. Chapter 8 process pauses cover karta hai, isi wajah se leases zaroori hain.
  • Operations ki total ordering. Jaisa Chapter 8 mein discuss hua, jab koi resource lock ya lease se protected ho, toh process pause ke baad clients ko ek-doosre se conflict karne se rokne ke liye fencing token chahiye. Fencing token ek number hota hai jo har baar lock acquire hone par badhta hai. ZooKeeper yeh saare operations ko totally order karke deta hai. Har operation ko ek monotonically badhta transaction ID (zxid) aur version number (cversion) milta hai.
  • Failure detection. Clients ZooKeeper servers par ek long-lived session rakhte hain. Client aur server heartbeats exchange karke check karte hain ki doosra abhi alive hai. Agar connection thodi der ke liye interrupt ho, ya ek ZooKeeper node fail ho jaaye, toh session active rehta hai. Lekin agar heartbeats session timeout se zyada der tak ruk jaayein, toh ZooKeeper session ko dead declare kar deta hai. Us session ke held locks ko aise set kiya jaa sakta hai ki session timeout hone par woh automatically release ho jaayein. ZooKeeper inhe ephemeral nodes kehta hai.
  • Change notifications. Ek client doosre client ke banaye locks aur values padh sakta hai, aur unme changes ke liye watch bhi kar sakta hai. Isliye client ko pata chal sakta hai ki doosra client cluster mein kab join hua, kyunki us client ne ek value likhi thi. Use yeh bhi pata chal sakta hai ki doosra client kab fail hua, kyunki uska session timeout hota hai aur uske ephemeral nodes gayab ho jaate hain. Notifications subscribe karke client changes check karne ke liye baar-baar polling karne se bach jaata hai.

In features mein se sirf linearizable atomic operations ko sach mein consensus chahiye. Lekin yeh sab ka combination hi hai jo ZooKeeper jaise systems ko distributed coordination ke liye itna useful banata hai.

Nodes ko work allocate karna

ZooKeeper aur Chubby ka model ek common case mein achha kaam karta hai. Tumhare paas kisi process ya service ke kai instances hain, aur unmein se ek ko leader, ya primary, chunna hai. Agar leader fail ho jaaye, toh koi aur node take over kare. Yeh single-leader databases ke liye useful hai. Yeh job schedulers aur aise hi stateful systems ke liye bhi useful hai.

Ek aur example partitioned resource ka hai, jaise database, message streams, file storage ya distributed actor system. Tumhe decide karna hota hai ki kaun si partition kis node ko jaaye. Jab naye nodes cluster mein join karte hain, toh load rebalance karne ke liye kuch partitions existing nodes se naye nodes par move karni padti hain. Jab nodes remove hote hain ya fail hote hain, toh doosre nodes ko unka kaam sambhalna padta hai.

Yeh tasks ZooKeeper mein atomic operations, ephemeral nodes aur notifications ke careful use se kiye jaa sakte hain. Sahi tarah kiya jaaye toh application human intervention ke bina faults se automatically recover kar sakti hai. Lekin yeh aasaan nahi hai, chahe Apache Curator jaisi libraries hon jo ZooKeeper client API ke upar higher-level tools deti hain. Phir bhi, zaroori consensus algorithms ko scratch se implement karne se yeh kaafi behtar hai, jiska success record kharab hai.

Ek application ek single node par shuru ho sakti hai aur eventually hazaaron nodes tak badh sakti hai. Hazaaron nodes ke across majority votes karna bahut inefficient hoga. Isliye ZooKeeper nodes ki ek fixed count par chalta hai, aam taur par teen ya paanch. Woh apne majority votes un thode nodes ke beech karta hai, aur saath mein potentially bahut saare clients ko support karta hai. Is tarah ZooKeeper nodes ko coordinate karne ka kuch kaam, jaise consensus, operation ordering aur failure detection, ek external service ko outsource kar deta hai.

ZooKeeper jo data manage karta hai woh normally slow-changing hota hai. Usme aise facts hote hain jaise “falaana IP address par chal raha node partition 7 ka leader hai.” Aise facts minutes ya hours mein badal sakte hain. ZooKeeper application ka runtime state store karne ke liye nahi bana, jo har second hazaaron ya millions baar badal sakta hai. Agar application state ko ek node se doosre node par replicate karna ho, toh Apache BookKeeper jaise doosre tools use kiye jaa sakte hain.

Service Discovery

ZooKeeper, etcd aur Consul aksar service discovery ke liye bhi use hote hain. Matlab woh IP address dhoondhna jisse connect karke tum kisi particular service tak pahunch sako. Cloud datacenters mein virtual machines lagatar aate-jaate rehte hain, isliye tumhe aksar apni services ke IP addresses pehle se nahi pata hote. Iske bajaye, jab koi service start hoti hai, woh apne network endpoints ek service registry mein register karti hai, jahan doosri services use dhoondh sakti hain.

Lekin yeh kam clear hai ki service discovery ko sach mein consensus chahiye. DNS service name ka IP address lookup karne ka traditional tarika hai. Yeh achhi performance aur availability ke liye caching ki kai layers use karta hai. DNS se reads definitely linearizable nahi hote, aur DNS query ke results thode stale hon toh aam taur par problem nahi maani jaati. Zyada zaroori yeh hai ki DNS reliably available ho aur network interruptions ke against robust ho.

Isliye service discovery ko consensus nahi chahiye, lekin leader election ko chahiye. Agar tumhare consensus system ko pehle se pata hai ki leader kaun hai, toh us information ko doosri services ko leader dhoondhne mein madad karne ke liye use karna samajhdaari ho sakti hai. Is kaam ke liye kuch consensus systems read-only caching replicas support karte hain. Yeh replicas saare decisions ka log asynchronously receive karte hain, lekin voting mein hissa nahi lete. Woh aisi read requests serve kar sakte hain jinhe linearizable hone ki zaroorat nahi.

Membership Services

ZooKeeper aur aise tools ko membership services par research ki lambi history ka hissa maana jaa sakta hai, jo 1980s tak jaati hai. Membership services highly reliable systems banane ke liye important rahi hain, jaise air traffic control mein.

Membership service batati hai ki abhi kaun se nodes active hain aur cluster ke live members hain. Jaisa Chapter 8 mein dikhaya, unbounded network delays ki wajah se yeh reliably detect karna possible nahi hai ki doosra node fail hua hai ya nahi. Lekin agar tum failure detection ko consensus ke saath jodte ho, toh nodes is baat par agree kar sakte ho ki kin nodes ko alive maana jaaye.

Phir bhi aisa ho sakta hai ki consensus ne kisi node ko galti se dead declare kar diya, jabki woh alive hai. Lekin phir bhi system ke liye yeh agree karna bahut useful hai ki current membership kin nodes se banti hai. Jaise, leader chunne ka matlab ho sakta hai current members mein sabse kam number wale ko chun lena. Yeh approach tab fail ho jaayegi jab alag-alag nodes ki alag raay ho ki current members kaun hain.

Summary

Short mein
  • Linearizability replicated data ko aisa dikhata hai jaise ek hi copy ho, aur har operation ko atomically act karwata hai. Yeh isliye appealing hai kyunki samajhna aasaan hai: yeh database ko single-threaded program ke variable ki tarah behave karwata hai. Iski downside yeh hai ki yeh slow hai, khaas kar jab network delays bade hon.
  • Causality events ko cause aur effect ke hisaab se order karti hai: kya kis se pehle hua. Yeh linearizability se weaker model hai. Ek seedhi timeline ki jagah version history branch aur merge ho sakti hai, kyunki kuch events concurrent hote hain. Causal consistency linearizability ka coordination overhead avoid karti hai aur network problems ke prati bahut kam sensitive hai.
  • Lamport timestamps counters aur node IDs se causal order capture karte hain. Lekin causal ordering ke baad bhi kuch problems is tarah solve nahi ho sakti. Maan lo ek username unique hona chahiye, jahan concurrent registrations reject honi chahiye. Jo node registration accept karta hai, use kisi tarah pata hona chahiye ki koi aur node usi waqt wahi naam register nahi kar raha. Yeh problem consensus tak le jaati hai.
  • Consensus ka matlab hai aise decide karna ki saare nodes agree hon ki kya decide hua, aur decision irrevocable ho. Bahut si problems consensus mein reduce ho jaati hain aur ek-doosre ke equivalent hain, is sense mein ki ek ka solution baaki ka solution bana diya jaa sakta hai:
    • Linearizable compare-and-set registers, jinhe current value ke basis par decide karna hota hai ki value set karni hai ya nahi.
    • Atomic transaction commit, jahan database ko decide karna hota hai ki distributed transaction commit karni hai ya abort.
    • Total order broadcast, jahan messaging system ko decide karna hota hai ki messages kis order mein deliver hon.
    • Locks aur leases, jahan clients lock grab karne ki race lagayein, toh lock decide karta hai ki kise milega.
    • Membership aur coordination, jahan timeouts jaise failure detector ke diye hue, system ko decide karna hota hai ki kaun se nodes alive hain.
    • Uniqueness constraints, jahan transactions concurrently conflicting records banayein, toh constraint decide karta hai ki kise allow karna hai.
  • Ek single node in sab ko aasaan bana deta hai, ya tum decision lene ki power ek node ko de sakte ho. Single-leader database yahi karta hai. Decide karne ki saari power leader ke paas hoti hai, isliye woh linearizable operations, uniqueness constraints aur totally ordered replication log de sakta hai. Lekin agar leader fail ho jaaye, ya network problem se woh unreachable ho jaaye, toh system progress nahi kar sakta. Isse handle karne ke teen tarike hain:
    1. Leader ke recover hone ka wait karein, aur maan lein ki is dauraan system blocked rahega. Bahut se XA aur JTA transaction coordinators yahi choose karte hain. Yeh consensus ko poori tarah solve nahi karta, kyunki agar leader kabhi recover nahi hua, toh system hamesha ke liye blocked reh sakta hai.
    2. Manually failover karein, yani log naya leader chunein aur system reconfigure karein. Bahut se relational databases yahi karte hain. Yeh “act of God” wala consensus hai, aur yeh insaano ke act karne ki speed se limited hai.
    3. Naya leader automatically chunne ke liye algorithm use karein. Iske liye consensus algorithm chahiye, aur samajhdaari yeh hai ki aisa proven algorithm use karein jo bad network conditions ko sahi se handle karta ho.
  • Ek single leader har write par consensus chalaye bina linearizability de sakta hai. Lekin apni leadership maintain karne aur leaders badalne ke liye use phir bhi consensus chahiye. Isliye leader rakhna bas problem ko aage taal deta hai. Consensus ki zaroorat abhi bhi hai, bas alag jagah aur kam baar.
  • Coordination tools jaise ZooKeeper “outsourced” consensus, failure detection aur membership dete hain. Inhe use karna aasaan nahi hai. Lekin Chapter 8 ki har problem ko jhelne wale apne algorithms banane se yeh kaafi behtar hain. Agar tumhe kuch chahiye jo consensus mein reduce hota ho aur fault-tolerant hona zaroori ho, toh ZooKeeper jaisa tool use karna samajhdaari hai.
  • Har system ko consensus nahi chahiye. Leaderless aur multi-leader replication aam taur par global consensus use nahi karte. Unse jo conflicts aate hain, woh leaders ke across consensus na hone ka nateeja hain. Shayad yeh theek ho. Ho sakta hai hume bas linearizability ke bina jeena aur aise data ke saath kaam karna seekhna ho jiski version histories branch aur merge hoti hain.

Yeh chapter distributed systems ki theory ki research ke bade hisse par based hai. Theoretical papers aur proofs padhna hamesha aasaan nahi hota, aur kabhi-kabhi woh unrealistic assumptions bhi lete hain. Lekin yeh bahut valuable hain. Yeh hume reason karne mein madad karte hain ki kya ho sakta hai aur kya nahi, aur woh counterintuitive tarike dikhate hain jinme distributed systems aksar flawed hote hain. Chapter 110 numbered references ke saath khatam hota hai. Yeh retelling unhe reproduce nahi karti, lekin jinke paas waqt hai unke liye inhe explore karna kaafi worth it hai.

Yahan Part II khatam hota hai. Is part mein replication (Chapter 5), partitioning (Chapter 6), transactions (Chapter 7), distributed systems ke failure models (Chapter 8), aur aakhir mein consistency aur consensus (yeh chapter) cover hue. Theory ki is foundation ke baad, Part III zyada practical systems ki taraf jaata hai, aur is par ki heterogeneous building blocks se powerful applications kaise banayein.

Check yourself

  1. Ek web server photo ko file storage mein save karta hai, phir message queue mein ek resize job daalta hai. Image resizer job milne par photo fetch karta hai. Agar file storage linearizable nahi hai, toh thumbnail permanently galat kyun reh sakta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Queue message photo write ke har replica tak pahunchne se pehle aa sakta hai. Resizer phir photo ki purani copy fetch kar sakta hai, ya kuch bhi nahi, aur galat version resize kar deta hai. Full-size image aur thumbnail inconsistent reh jaate hain, kyunki unhe koi dobara check nahi karta. Storage aur queue, yeh do channels ek-doosre se race karte hain.

  2. Ek single-leader database ka leader datacenter 1 mein hai, aur datacenter 2 ka network link cut ho gaya hai. Datacenter 2 ke clients linearizably na write kar sakte hain na read, kyun? Multi-leader setup kaam karta kyun rahega?

    Jawab dekho

    Writes aur linearizable reads ko leader tak pahunchna padta hai, jo cut hue link ke us paar hai, isliye woh fail hote hain ya wait karte hain. Multi-leader setup mein har datacenter writes locally accept kar sakta hai aur link wapas aane tak replication ko queue kar sakta hai. Isse system available rehta hai, lekin behavior linearizable nahi hota. Yeh wahi trade-off hai jo CAP theorem describe karta hai.

  3. Ek node ka Lamport counter 1 hai. Use maximum counter value 5 wala message milta hai. Uske agle operation ko kaun sa counter milega, aur maximum har message ke saath kyun jaana chahiye?

    Jawab dekho

    Agle operation ko counter 6 milta hai. Maximum receive karne par node apna counter 5 tak badhata hai, phir use increment karta hai. Maximum har message ke saath jaata hai, isliye har causal dependency ka timestamp bada hota hai, aur ordering causality ke saath consistent rehti hai.

  4. Two-phase commit mein ek participant ne yes vote de diya, aur phir coordinator use commit ya abort request bhejne se pehle crash ho gaya. Participant khud se safely commit ya abort kyun nahi kar sakta?

    Jawab dekho

    Yes vote ek promise hai ki poochne par commit karega, lekin participant ko pata nahi ki coordinator ne kya decide kiya. Ho sakta hai kisi aur participant ne commit kar diya ho, ya abort kar diya ho. Khud commit karna kahin aur hue abort se contradict kar sakta hai, aur abort karna commit se. Isliye use coordinator ke recover hone aur apne log se uska decision padhne ka wait karna padega. Ek hi aur option, heuristic decision, atomicity todne ka risk rakhta hai.

Part III

Derived Data

Part III dekhta hai ki alag-alag strengths wale kai data systems, jaise databases, caches, indexes aur analytics tools, ek hi application mein kaise combine kiye ja sakte hain. Shuruaat Chapter 10 ke batch processing se hoti hai, phir streams ki baat aati hai.

Yeh Kleppmann ke part introduction ka paraphrase hai: zyaadatar applications ko ek saath kai data systems chahiye hote hain, aur system of record ko derived data se alag rakhne se data ka flow samajhna aasaan ho jaata hai.

Part III · Chapter 10

Batch Processing

Seedhi baat: ek batch job input files ka fixed set padhta hai aur apne input ko badle bina nayi output files likhta hai. Is simple rule se jobs ko dobara run karna, debug karna aur rollback karna aasaan ho jaata hai. Jo design ideas Unix tools mein kaam karte the, wahi hazaaron machines tak scale ho jaate hain.

Part I aur II mein humne pehle ek database ko dekha, phir distributed databases ko, aur hamesha yeh maana ki application mein sirf ek hi database hai. Real systems itne simple kam hi hote hain. Ek bada application aksar ek hi data ko kai alag tareeke se access aur process karta hai, aur koi ek database un sab ko achhe se handle nahi kar paata. Isliye woh datastores, indexes, caches aur analytics systems ka mix use karta hai, saath mein aisa code bhi jo data ko ek store se doosre mein move karta hai.

Part III dekhta hai ki in alag-alag systems ko, jinka apna data model aur access pattern hota hai, ek coherent architecture mein kaise fit karein. Kleppmann ke hisaab se is kaam ko aksar ignore kiya jaata hai, khaaskar un vendors ki taraf se jo promise karte hain ki unka product tumhari saari zarooratein poori kar dega. Practice mein, alag-alag systems ko jodna kisi bhi serious application ke sabse zaroori kaamon mein se ek hai.

Systems of Record aur Derived Data

Data store aur process karne wale systems do bade groups mein aate hain.

Ek system of record, jise source of truth bhi kehte hain, data ka authoritative version rakhta hai. Jab naya data aata hai, jaise user input, toh woh sabse pehle yahin likha jaata hai. Har fact sirf ek baar represent hota hai, aur usually normalized form mein (data ko tables mein baant dena taaki information repeat na ho). Agar koi doosra system system of record se match nahi karta, toh definition ke hisaab se system of record hi sahi hai.

Ek derived data system mein woh data hota hai jo kisi doosre system ke existing data ko transform ya process karke banaya gaya ho. Derived data kho jaaye, toh tum use source se dobara bana sakte ho. Cache iska classic example hai. Application jab ho sake cache se padhta hai, aur cache mein cheez na mile toh underlying database par fall back karta hai. Denormalized values (data ki copies jo tez reads ke liye arrange ki gayi hon), indexes aur materialized views (pehle se compute karke store kiye gaye results) bhi derived data hain. Recommendation system mein predicted summaries aksar user activity ke logs se derive hote hain.

Derived data redundant hota hai, kyunki woh aisi information repeat karta hai jo pehle se present hai. Phir bhi fast read queries ke liye yeh bahut zaroori hai, aur yeh aksar denormalized hota hai. Ek hi source se tum kai alag datasets derive kar sakte ho, jisse tum same data ko kai nazariyon se dekh paate ho.

Har system mein system of record aur derived data ke beech saaf line nahi hoti, lekin yeh farq bahut kaam ka hai. Isse pata chalta hai ki system ke kaun se hisse ke kya inputs aur outputs hain, aur woh ek doosre par kaise depend karte hain. Kleppmann yeh bhi batate hain ki zyaadatar databases, storage engines aur query languages khud se na system of record hote hain, na derived data. Database bas ek tool hai. Tumhara application use kaise karta hai, yeh decide karta hai ki uska data kaun sa role nibhayega.

Asli idea

System of record aur derived data ke beech ki line is par depend karti hai ki tum tool ko kaise use karte ho, tool khud kya hai yeh nahi. Yeh saaf rakhna ki kaun sa data kis doosre data se derive hua hai, ek uljhe hue architecture mein order le aata hai.

Chapters ka overview

Part III ka roadmap chhota hai. Chapter 10 batch-oriented dataflow systems, jaise MapReduce, se shuru hota hai, aur dikhata hai ki large-scale data systems banane ke liye woh kaun se tools aur principles dete hain. Chapter 11 wahi ideas data streams par le jaata hai, jinse tum similar kaam kam delay ke saath kar sakte ho. Chapter 12 book ko is sawaal par khatam karta hai ki in tools se hum future mein reliable, scalable aur maintainable applications kaise bana sakte hain.

Chapter 10 Donald Knuth ke ek quote se shuru hota hai. Short mein, koi system tab success nahi ho sakta jab ek hi insaan ka us par zyaada asar ho, kyunki asli test tab aata hai jab alag-alag nazariye wale kai log apne experiments chalate hain.

Aaj ka zyaadatar software request aur response style mein kaam karta hai. Tum kuch maangte ho, ya koi instruction bhejte ho, aur kuch der baad system tumhe jawab deta hai. Databases, caches, search indexes aur web servers sab aise hi kaam karte hain. Web aur kai HTTP-based APIs ne is style ko itna common bana diya hai ki yeh bhool jaana aasaan hai ki yeh sirf ek option hai. Kleppmann teen tarah ke systems mein farq karte hain.

  • Services (online systems) client ki request ka wait karte hain, use jitni jaldi ho sake handle karte hain, aur response bhej dete hain. Performance ka main measure response time hai, aur availability bahut matter karti hai, kyunki agar client service tak pahunch na paaye toh woh apne user ko error dikhata hai.
  • Batch processing systems (offline systems) bahut saara input data lete hain, us par ek job chalate hain, aur output data banate hain. Jobs kuch minutes se lekar kai din tak le sakti hain, isliye koi user unke khatam hone ka wait nahi kar raha hota. Inhe aksar regularly run karne ke liye schedule kiya jaata hai, jaise din mein ek baar. Inka main measure throughput hai, yani ek given size ka input nipatane mein kitna time lagta hai.
  • Stream processing systems (near-real-time systems) in dono ke beech mein aate hain. Batch systems ki tarah yeh bhi requests ka jawab dene ke bajay input consume karte hain aur output produce karte hain. Lekin yeh data ke fixed set par kaam karne ke bajay events par unke hone ke thodi der baad hi kaam karte hain. Isse inki latency kam hoti hai. Stream processing batch processing par hi build hoti hai, isliye Chapter 11 mein uski baat hogi.

Batch processing reliable, scalable aur maintainable applications ka ek important building block hai. MapReduce, jo 2004 mein publish hua ek batch processing algorithm hai, ko shayad zyada hi josh mein “the algorithm that makes Google so massively scalable” kaha gaya tha. Baad mein ise Hadoop, CouchDB aur MongoDB jaise open source systems mein implement kiya gaya.

Data warehouses jo parallel processing systems saalon se use kar rahe the, unke mukable MapReduce kaafi low-level programming model hai. Lekin commodity hardware kitne bade scale par processing handle kar sakta hai, is mamle mein yeh ek bada kadam tha. Kleppmann ke hisaab se MapReduce ki importance ab ghat rahi hai, phir bhi ise samajhna zaroori hai, kyunki isse saaf pata chalta hai ki batch processing kyun aur kaise kaam aati hai.

Batch processing bahut purani bhi hai. Programmable computers aane se pehle punch card tabulating machines, jaise 1890 US Census mein use hui Hollerith machines, ek semi-mechanized tarah ki batch processing karti thi, taaki bade inputs se totals nikale ja sakein. MapReduce un electromechanical IBM card-sorting machines se bhi milta-julta hai jo businesses 1940s aur 1950s mein use karte the. Book ke words mein, history apne aap ko dohraati rehti hai.

Chapter Unix tools se shuru hota hai. Unix ke ideas aur lessons bade, mixed distributed data systems par bhi lagu hote hain, isliye shuruaat ke liye yeh achhi jagah hai.

Unix tools se Batch Processing

Chalo ek simple example se shuru karte hain. Maan lo ek web server har request serve karne par log file mein ek line append karta hai. Default nginx access log format mein ek line neeche wale example jaisi dikhti hai. Book ne padhne ke liye ise kai lines mein tod diya hai, lekin file mein yeh ek hi line hoti hai.

216.58.210.78 - - [27/Feb/2015:17:55:11 +0000] "GET /css/typography.css HTTP/1.1"
200 3377 "http://martin.kleppmann.com/" "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X
10_9_5) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/40.0.2214.115
Safari/537.36"

Is line ko samajhne ke liye tumhe log format ki definition chahiye, jo yeh hai:

$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request"
$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" "$http_user_agent"
Example

Sample line ko field by field padhein, toh yeh pata chalta hai:

  • Client ka IP address 216.58.210.78 hai.
  • User logged in nahi tha, isliye remote user field mein hyphen hai.
  • Request 27 February 2015 ko 17:55:11 UTC par aayi thi.
  • Request ne file /css/typography.css maangi thi.
  • Response status 200 tha, matlab success, aur response 3,377 bytes ka tha.
  • Browser ko jis page ne refer kiya woh http://martin.kleppmann.com/ tha, yani browser ne stylesheet isliye load ki kyunki us page ne use use ki thi.
  • Browser Chrome 40 tha, Mac par.

Simple Log Analysis

Log files ko website traffic ki achhi-achhi reports mein badalne ke liye kaafi tools hain. Exercise ke liye hum basic Unix tools se apna khud ka tool banate hain. Maan lo tumhe apni site ke sabse popular paanch pages nikaalne hain. Unix shell mein tum yeh aise kar sakte ho:

cat /var/log/nginx/access.log |
awk '{print $7}' |
sort |
uniq -c |
sort -r -n |
head -n 5

Har command ek chhota sa step karti hai:

  1. cat log file padhta hai. (Kuch log kehte hain ki cat strictly zaroori nahi hai, kyunki awk file seedha padh sakta hai. Book ise rakhti hai kyunki tab pipeline left se right padhne mein saaf lagti hai.)
  2. awk har line ko whitespace se alag karke fields mein todta hai, aur sirf saatva field print karta hai, jo requested URL hota hai. Sample line mein yeh /css/typography.css hai.
  3. sort URLs ko alphabetical order mein laga deta hai. Agar koi URL n baar request hua tha, toh ab woh URL lagaataar n baar aata hai.
  4. uniq -c dekhta hai ki do adjacent lines same hain ya nahi, aur repeated lines hata deta hai. -c option ek counter jodta hai, isliye har distinct URL ke liye pata chal jaata hai ki woh kitni baar aaya.
  5. Doosra sort us number ke hisaab se sort karta hai (-n), ulte (-r) order mein, taaki sabse bada count sabse pehle aaye.
  6. head -n 5 pehli paanch lines output karta hai aur baaki phenk deta hai.

Output kuch aisa dikhta hai:

4189 /favicon.ico
3631 /2013/05/24/improving-security-of-ssh-private-keys.html
2124 /2012/12/05/schema-evolution-in-avro-protocol-buffers-thrift.html
1369 /
915 /css/typography.css

Agar tumhe Unix tools nahi aate, toh yeh command line obscure lagti hai, lekin yeh bahut powerful hai. Yeh gigabytes ki log files seconds mein process kar deti hai, aur analysis badalna bhi aasaan hai. Report se CSS files hatani hain, toh awk argument ko '$7 !~ /\.css$/ {print $7}' kar do. Top pages ki jagah top client IP addresses count karne hain, toh use '{print $1}' kar do. Aur aise hi aage.

Try karo

Upar wali pipeline mein awk argument mein kaunsa ek change karne se top client IP addresses mil jaayenge? Phir sort aur uniq steps ke baare mein socho. Kya unhe kuch badalna padega, aur kyun?

Book ke paas Unix tools ko detail mein explore karne ki jagah nahi hai, lekin inhe seekhna worth it hai. Hairaani ki baat hai ki kaafi saare data analyses awk, sed, grep, sort, uniq aur xargs ke kisi combination se kuch minutes mein ho jaate hain, aur yeh tools perform bhi bahut achha karte hain.

Commands ki chain versus custom program

Unix commands ki chain ki jagah tum wahi kaam karne ke liye ek simple program bhi likh sakte ho. Ruby mein yeh kuch aisa dikh sakta hai:

counts = Hash.new(0)
File.open('/var/log/nginx/access.log') do |file|
  file.each do |line|
    url = line.split[6]
    counts[url] += 1
  end
end
top5 = counts.map{|url, count| [count, url] }.sort.reverse[0...5]
top5.each{|count, url| puts "#{count} #{url}" }

Ise step by step padhte hain:

  1. counts ek hash table hai jo har URL ke liye ek counter rakhta hai. Counter by default zero se shuru hota hai.
  2. Log ki har line ke liye URL saatva whitespace-separated field hai. Index 6 isliye hai kyunki Ruby arrays zero se ginti shuru karte hain.
  3. Us URL ka counter ek se badh jaata hai.
  4. Table ko counter value ke hisaab se sort kiya jaata hai, sabse bada pehle, aur top paanch entries rakh li jaati hain.
  5. Un paanch entries ko print kar diya jaata hai.

Yeh program Unix pipes ki chain jitna concise nahi hai, lekin kaafi readable hai. Dono mein se tumhe kaunsa pasand aayega, yeh kaafi had tak taste ki baat hai. Asli fark is mein hai ki bade file par yeh kaise chalte hain.

Sorting versus in-memory aggregation

Ruby script memory mein ek hash table rakhti hai jisme har URL ki ek entry hoti hai. Unix pipeline mein aisa koi table nahi hota. Woh ek aisi list sort karti hai jisme ek URL ki har request ek repeated line hoti hai, aur phir paas-paas baithi repeats ko count karti hai.

Kaunsa approach behtar hai, yeh is par depend karta hai ki tumhare paas kitne alag-alag URLs hain. Zyadatar chhoti aur mid-sized websites ke liye, har distinct URL aur uska counter laptop par bhi lagbhag 1 GB memory mein fit ho jaata hai. Ek job ko random access ke liye jitni memory chahiye, book use uska working set kehti hai. Yahan working set sirf distinct URLs ki ginti par depend karta hai. Agar ek URL log mein ek million baar bhi aaye, toh table mein uski sirf ek entry aur ek counter rehta hai. Agar working set itna chhota hai ki memory mein aa jaaye, toh in-memory hash table ekdum theek kaam karta hai.

Jab working set memory se bada ho, tab sorting approach ka fayda hota hai, kyunki woh disks ko efficiently use kar sakta hai. Yeh wahi principle hai jo book ne Chapter 3 mein SSTables aur LSM-Trees ke liye bataya tha. Data ke chunks memory mein sort hote hain aur segment files ki tarah disk par likhe jaate hain, phir kai sorted segments ko merge karke ek bada sorted file banaya jaata hai. Merging mein har file order mein padhi jaati hai, jo sequential access pattern hai aur disks ise achhe se handle karte hain. Chapter 3 mein sequential I/O ke liye optimize karne par zor diya gaya tha, aur wahi pattern yahan phir dikhta hai.

GNU Coreutils (Linux ke standard tools) ki sort utility memory se bade datasets ko disk par spill karke handle karti hai. Yeh apne aap kai CPU cores bhi use karti hai. Isliye commands ki simple chain bade datasets tak scale ho jaati hai, aur memory khatam nahi hoti. Bottleneck shayad input file ke disk se padhe jaane ki speed hogi.

The Unix Philosophy

Yeh koi ittefaq nahi hai ki log file ko commands ki chain se analyze karna aasaan tha. Yeh Unix ke key design ideas mein se ek tha, aur aaj bhi bahut relevant hai. Unix pipes Doug McIlroy ne invent kiye the, aur unhone inhe 1964 mein pehli baar describe kiya. Unhone programs ki tulna garden hoses se ki: data ko kisi aur tarah se massage karna ho, toh ek aur segment screw kar do. Plumbing wali yeh analogy chal padi, aur programs ko pipes se jodne ka idea us cheez ka hissa ban gaya jise aaj Unix philosophy kehte hain. 1978 mein is philosophy ko chaar principles mein describe kiya gaya:

  1. Har program ko ek hi kaam achhe se karne do. Naya kaam karna ho toh naya program banao, purane programs mein naye features jod kar unhe complicated mat karo.
  2. Maan kar chalo ki har program ka output kisi aur, abhi tak anjaan, program ka input banega. Output ko extra information se clutter mat karo. Strictly columnar ya binary input formats se bacho. Interactive input par zor mat do.
  3. Software, yahan tak ki operating systems bhi, aise design aur build karo ki unhe jaldi try kiya ja sake, ideally weeks ke andar. Clumsy hisson ko phenk kar dobara banane mein hichkichao mat.
  4. Programming task halka karne ke liye unskilled help ki jagah tools use karo, chahe tools banane ke liye detour lena pade aur yeh pata ho ki kuch tools use ke baad phenkne padenge.

Kleppmann ka kehna hai ki yeh approach, apni automation, rapid prototyping, incremental iteration, experimentation ke saath friendliness, aur bade projects ko manageable chunks mein todne ke saath, aaj ke Agile aur DevOps movements jaisi lagti hai. Chaar dashakon mein hairaani ki baat hai ki bahut kam badla hai.

Sort tool pehle principle ka achha example hai. Yeh shayad zyadatar programming languages ki standard libraries se behtar sorting implementation hai, kyunki un libraries mein aam taur par disk spill ya multiple threads ka use nahi hota. Phir bhi sort akele kaafi kaam ka nahi hai. Yeh tabhi powerful banta hai jab doosre tools, jaise uniq, ke saath combine hota hai.

A uniform interface

Agar ek program ka output doosre program ka input banana hai, toh dono programs ko data format par agree karna padega. Agar kisi bhi program ka output kisi bhi doosre program ke input se jud sakta hai, toh har program ko same input aur output interface use karna hoga. Unix mein woh interface ek file hai, ya zyada sahi kahein toh ek file descriptor. File bytes ka ek ordered sequence hoti hai. Kyunki interface itna simple hai, isliye kai alag-alag cheezein ise use kar sakti hain: disk par ek aam file, kisi doosre process se communication channel (Unix socket, standard input ya standard output), audio device ya printer jaisa device driver, ya network par TCP connection. Yeh bilkul alag-alag cheezein ek hi interface share karti hain, isliye aasaani se plug ho jaati hain. Book ise remarkable kehti hai.

Convention ke hisaab se, kaafi (sab nahi) Unix programs us byte sequence ko ASCII text maante hain. Log analysis mein yahi fact use hua. awk, sort, uniq aur head, sab apne input ko newline character se alag kiye hue records ki list maante hain. Newline ka choice thoda arbitrary hai. ASCII record separator character shayad behtar choice hota, kyunki woh isi kaam ke liye bana hai. Phir bhi, kyunki saare programs ek hi separator par agree karte hain, woh saath mein kaam kar paate hain.

Web mein bhi aisa hi uniform interface hai. URL ek particular resource ka naam hota hai, aur tum kisi bhi doosri website se kisi bhi URL ko link kar sakte ho, chahe servers bilkul unrelated organizations ke hon. Book isse bulletin board systems (BBSs) ke daur se compare karti hai, jahan har system ka apna phone number aur modem settings hoti thi. Ek BBS se doosre BBS ka reference phone number aur modem configuration ke roop mein likhna padta tha. User ko hang up karna padta, doosre system ko dial karna padta, aur information haath se dhoondhni padti thi. Tum kisi doosre BBS ke andar ke content ke piece ko seedha link nahi kar sakte the.

Har record ko parse karna itna uniform nahi hai. Unix tools aksar line ko whitespace ya tab characters se fields mein todte hain, lekin CSV, pipe-separated aur doosre encodings bhi common hain. Xargs jaise simple tool mein bhi input parse karne ko control karne ke liye lagbhag aadha darjan command-line options hain. Aur uniform interface khoobsurat bhi nahi hai. URL nikaalne wala expression {print $7} padhna mushkil hai. Ideal duniya mein yeh kuch aisa hota {print $request_url}. Book is idea par chapter mein aage phir aati hai.

Phir bhi, Unix ka uniform text interface dashakon baad bhi remarkable hai. Bahut kam software tools itni achhi tarah compose hote hain. Tum apni email aur online shopping history ko custom analysis tool se pipe karke spreadsheet mein daal do aur results social network par post kar do, yeh aasaani se nahi kar sakte. Same data model wale databases mein bhi ek se doosre mein data move karna aksar mushkil hota hai. Book integration ki is kami ko data ka Balkanization kehti hai.

Logic aur wiring ko alag rakhna

Unix tools ki ek aur khaasiyat hai standard input (stdin) aur standard output (stdout) ka use. Default mein stdin keyboard se aata hai aur stdout screen par jaata hai. Tum input file se bhi le sakte ho aur output file mein bhi bhej sakte ho. Ek pipe ek process ke stdout ko doosre process ke stdin se jodta hai, ek chhote in-memory buffer ke through. Poora intermediate stream kabhi disk par nahi likha jaata.

Zaroorat ho toh program files ko seedha padh aur likh bhi sakta hai. Lekin Unix approach tab best chalta hai jab program particular file paths ko ignore karke sirf stdin aur stdout use kare. Phir shell chalane wala person decide karta hai ki inputs aur outputs kaise wire hon. Program ko pata nahi hota aur na hi parwah hoti hai ki input kahan se aa raha hai ya output kahan ja raha hai. Book ise loose coupling, late binding ya inversion of control kehti hai. Wiring ko program logic se alag rakhne se chhote tools ko jodkar bade systems banana aasaan ho jaata hai.

Tum apne khud ke programs bhi likhkar operating system ke saath aane wale tools se jod sakte ho. Pipeline mein hissa lene ke liye program ko bas stdin padhna aur stdout likhna hai. Log example mein tum ek aisa tool likh sakte ho jo user-agent strings ko sensible browser names mein badal de, ya ek jo IP addresses ko country codes mein badal de, aur use seedha pipeline mein plug kar do. Sort program ko farak nahi padta ki uska padosi operating system ka hissa hai ya tumhara khud ka likha code.

Lekin limits bhi hain. Jin programs ko kai inputs ya outputs chahiye, woh possible hain par tricky. Tum kisi program ke output ko seedha network connection mein pipe nahi kar sakte. Uske liye netcat ya curl jaisa alag tool chahiye. (Unix ne shuru mein sab kuch files ke roop mein represent kiya tha, lekin BSD sockets API ne is pattern ko tod diya. Research systems Plan 9 aur Inferno zyada consistent hain, aur TCP connection ko file ke roop mein represent karte hain.) Agar program khud files kholta hai, subprocesses start karta hai ya network connections kholta hai, toh wiring woh khud karta hai. Use phir bhi command-line options se configure kiya ja sakta hai, lekin shell user ke paas use rewire karne ki azaadi kam hoti hai.

Transparency aur experimentation

Unix tools ke itne successful hone ki ek wajah yeh hai ki inme dekhna aasaan hota hai ki kya chal raha hai. Book teen wajah gaati hai:

  • Unix commands ke input files aam taur par immutable maane jaate hain, matlab unhe kabhi badla nahi jaata. Tum command jitni baar chaho chala sakte ho, alag-alag options try kar sakte ho, aur input kharaab nahi hota.
  • Tum pipeline ko kisi bhi jagah rok sakte ho, output less mein bhej sakte ho, aur dekh sakte ho ki woh expected form mein hai ya nahi. Isse debugging aasaan ho jaati hai.
  • Tum ek stage ka output file mein likhkar us file ko agle stage ka input bana sakte ho. Phir poori pipeline dobara chalaye bina tum baad wala stage restart kar sakte ho.

Unix tools kaafi blunt hote hain, relational database ke query optimizer ke saamne simple, lekin experimentation ke liye phir bhi gazab ke kaam ke hain. Inki sabse badi limitation yeh hai ki yeh ek hi machine par chalte hain. Yahin Hadoop jaise tools kaam aate hain.

MapReduce aur Distributed Filesystems

MapReduce kaafi had tak Unix tools jaisa hai, bas yeh shayad hazaaron machines par distributed hota hai. Unix tools ki tarah yeh bhi ek kaafi blunt, brute-force approach hai, phir bhi hairaani ki baat hai ki bahut effective hai. Ek MapReduce job ek Unix process jaisa hota hai: yeh ek ya zyada inputs leta hai aur ek ya zyada outputs produce karta hai.

Zyadatar Unix tools ki tarah, MapReduce job chalane se aam taur par uska input modify nahi hota, aur output produce karne ke alawa koi side effect nahi hota. Output files ek baar, sequentially likhi jaati hain, aur likhne ke baad file ka koi existing hissa kabhi change nahi hota. Jahan Unix tools stdin aur stdout use karte hain, wahan MapReduce jobs distributed filesystem mein files padhte aur likhte hain. Hadoop ki implementation mein woh filesystem HDFS hai, yani Hadoop Distributed File System. HDFS Google ke File System (GFS) ka open source reimplementation hai. Doosre distributed filesystems mein GlusterFS aur Quantcast File System (QFS) hain. Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage aur OpenStack Swift jaisi object storage services bhi kai tarah se similar hain. Yeh chapter HDFS ko running example ki tarah use karta hai, lekin principles kisi bhi distributed filesystem par lagu hote hain.

HDFS shared-nothing principle follow karta hai, jo Part II ke introduction mein describe hua tha. Yeh network attached storage (NAS) aur storage area networks (SAN) ke shared-disk approach se alag hai. Shared-disk storage ek centralized storage appliance hota hai, jo aksar custom hardware aur Fibre Channel jaise special network infrastructure se bana hota hai. Shared-nothing system ko special hardware nahi chahiye, bas normal datacenter network se jude computers chahiye.

HDFS har machine par ek daemon process chalata hai. Daemon ek network service expose karta hai jisse doosre nodes us machine par stored files access kar sakte hain. Yeh isliye kaam karta hai kyunki datacenter ki har general-purpose machine mein kuch disks lage hote hain. NameNode naam ka ek central server track karta hai ki kaunse file blocks kaunsi machine par stored hain. Is tarah HDFS ek bada conceptual filesystem present karta hai, jo daemon chalane wali har machine ka disk space use karta hai.

Machine aur disk failures tolerate karne ke liye file blocks ko kai machines par replicate kiya jaata hai. Replication ka matlab simply kai copies rakhna ho sakta hai. Yeh erasure coding scheme bhi ho sakti hai, jaise Reed–Solomon codes, jo full copies se kam storage overhead mein lost data recover kar sakte hain. Yeh techniques RAID jaisi hain, jo ek machine se jude kai disks ko protect karta hai. Fark yeh hai ki distributed filesystem mein file access aur replication ek aam datacenter network par hota hai, bina kisi special hardware ke.

HDFS ne achhi tarah scale kiya hai. Likhte waqt, sabse bade HDFS deployments das hazaar machines par chalte the, aur unki combined storage sau petabytes mein thi. Yeh isliye viable ho paya kyunki commodity hardware aur open source software ke saath HDFS par data store aur access karna, dedicated storage appliance par utni hi capacity se kaafi sasta padta hai.

MapReduce Job Execution

MapReduce ek programming framework hai, jisse HDFS jaise distributed filesystem mein stored bade datasets ko process karne ka code likha jaata hai. Ise samajhne ka sabse aasaan tarika hai web server log example par wapas jaana. Data processing pattern kaafi similar hai:

  1. Input files ka ek set padho aur unhe records mein todo. Log example mein har record ek line hai, isliye newline record separator hai.
  2. Mapper function call karo, jo har record se ek key aur ek value nikaalta hai. Example mein mapper awk '{print $7}' hai. Yeh URL ko key ki tarah nikaalta hai aur value khaali chhod deta hai.
  3. Saare key-value pairs ko key ke hisaab se sort karo. Log example mein yeh pehli sort command karti hai.
  4. Reducer function call karo, jo sorted pairs par iterate karta hai. Agar same key kai baar aaye, toh sorting ne un occurrences ko paas-paas la diya hota hai, isliye memory mein zyada state rakhe bina unhe combine karna aasaan hota hai. Example mein reducer uniq -c hai, jo same key wale adjacent records ko count karta hai.

Yeh chaaron steps ek hi MapReduce job kar sakta hai. Steps 2 (map) aur 4 (reduce) mein tum apna data processing code likhte ho. Step 1, files ko records mein todna, input format parser handle karta hai. Step 3, sort, MapReduce mein implicit hai. Ise tum kabhi likhte nahi, kyunki mapper output reducer ko dene se pehle hamesha sorted hota hai.

Log example mein step 5 mein ek doosra sort tha, jo URLs ko unki requests ki ginti ke hisaab se rank karta tha. MapReduce mein doosra sorting stage chahiye ho, toh tum doosra job likhte ho aur pehle job ke output ko doosre job ka input bana dete ho. Is nazariye se dekhein toh mapper ka role data ko sorting ke layak form mein taiyaar karna hai, aur reducer ka role sort hone ke baad data ko process karna.

MapReduce job banane ke liye tum do callback functions implement karte ho, mapper aur reducer. Yeh aise behave karte hain (book isse Chapter 2 ki MapReduce querying se bhi jodti hai):

  • Mapper. Mapper har input record ke liye ek baar call hota hai, aur uska kaam us record se key aur value nikaalna hai. Har input ke liye yeh koi bhi number mein key-value pairs emit kar sakta hai, zero bhi. Yeh ek record se doosre record tak koi state nahi rakhta, isliye har record apne aap handle hota hai.
  • Reducer. Framework mappers ke key-value pairs leta hai, same key ki saari values collect karta hai, aur us collection par ek iterator ke saath reducer ko call karta hai. Reducer output records produce kar sakta hai, jaise ek URL ke occurrences ki ginti.

Hadoop MapReduce mein mapper aur reducer dono ek Java class hote hain jo ek particular interface implement karti hai. MongoDB aur CouchDB mein yeh JavaScript functions hote hain. Standard Unix tools bhi distributed computation mein mapper aur reducer ka kaam kar sakte hain, halaanki yeh kam common hai.

MapReduce ka distributed execution

Unix commands ki pipeline se main fark yeh hai ki MapReduce computation ko kai machines par phaila sakta hai, aur parallelism handle karne ke liye tumhe koi code nahi likhna padta. Mappers aur reducers ek time par ek record par kaam karte hain. Unhe pata hona zaroori nahi ki input kahan se aa raha hai ya output kahan ja raha hai, isliye machines ke beech data move karne ka complicated kaam framework sambhal leta hai.

Parallelization partitioning par based hai. Job ka input aam taur par HDFS ki ek directory hoti hai. Har file, ya bade file ka har block, ek partition hai, aur ek alag map task use process karta hai. Book ka Figure 10-1 teen mappers aur teen reducers wala ek job dikhata hai. Neeche wala diagram wahi idea draw karta hai.

Input files aam taur par har ek sau megabytes ki hoti hain. MapReduce scheduler koshish karta hai ki har mapper ko aisi machine par chalaye jisme input file ki ek replica stored ho, bas us machine ke paas task chalane ke liye kaafi spare RAM aur CPU ho. Is principle ko computation ko data ke paas rakhna kehte hain. Isse input ko network par copy karna bach jaata hai, network load kam hota hai aur locality improve hoti hai. Zyadatar cases mein mapper ka application code assigned machine par pehle se nahi hota, isliye framework pehle code (jaise Java program ke JAR files) sahi machines par copy karta hai. Phir woh map task start karta hai aur input file ko ek time par ek record ke hisaab se mapper ko deta hai. Mapper ka output key-value pairs ka ek set hota hai.

Reduce side bhi partitioned hoti hai. Map tasks ki ginti input file blocks ki ginti se decide hoti hai. Reduce tasks ki ginti job ka author decide karta hai, aur woh map tasks ki ginti se alag ho sakti hai. Yeh pakka karne ke liye ki same key wale saare key-value pairs same reducer par pahunchein, framework key ko hash karke decide karta hai ki har pair kaunse reduce task ko jaayega.

Pairs sorted hone chahiye, lekin dataset aam taur par itna bada hota hai ki ek machine par normal algorithm se sort nahi ho sakta. Isliye sorting stages mein hoti hai. Pehle, har map task apne output ko key ke hash ke hisaab se reducer ke basis par partition karta hai. Har partition mapper ki local disk par ek sorted file mein likha jaata hai, jo Chapter 3 mein discuss hue SSTables jaisi technique se hota hai.

Jab mapper apna input padhna aur sorted files likhna khatam kar leta hai, tab scheduler reducers ko batata hai ki ab woh us mapper ka output fetch karna shuru kar sakte hain. Har reducer har mapper se connect hota hai aur apne partition ki sorted files download karta hai. Reducer ke hisaab se partition karna, sort karna, aur data ko mappers se reducers tak copy karna, is poore process ko shuffle kehte hain. Book maanti hai ki yeh naam confusing hai, kyunki taash ke patte shuffle karne ke ulat, MapReduce mein koi randomness nahi hoti.

Reduce task mappers ki files leta hai aur sort order banaye rakhte hue unhe merge karta hai. Agar alag-alag mappers ne same key wale records banaye hon, toh merged input mein woh records ek-doosre ke paas aa jaate hain. Reducer ko ek key aur ek iterator ke saath call kiya jaata hai, jo us key ke saare records scan karta hai. Ho sakta hai woh saare records memory mein fit na hon, isliye iterator unhe dheere-dheere padhta hai. Reducer koi bhi logic laga sakta hai, aur kitne bhi output records produce kar sakta hai. Inhe distributed filesystem ki ek file mein likha jaata hai, aam taur par ek copy reducer ki machine ki local disk par aur replicas doosri machines par.

MapReduce workflows

Ek single MapReduce job se jitne problems solve ho sakte hain, woh limited hain. Log example mein ek job har URL ke page views count kar sakta hai. Lekin sabse popular URLs nikaalne ke liye sorting ka doosra round chahiye. Isliye MapReduce jobs ko workflows mein chain karna bahut common hai, jahan ek job ka output agle job ka input ban jaata hai.

Hadoop ke MapReduce framework mein workflows ke liye koi special support nahi hai. Chaining directory ke naam se implicitly hoti hai. Pehle job ko configure kiya jaata hai ki woh apna output HDFS ki ek designated directory mein likhe, aur doosre job ko configure kiya jaata hai ki woh usi directory se padhe. Framework ke liye yeh do independent jobs hain.

Isliye chained MapReduce jobs Unix pipelines jaise kam dikhte hain, jo output ko ek chhote buffer se seedha agle process tak pass karti hain. Woh un commands ke sequence jaise zyada lagte hain jisme har command apna output ek temporary file mein likhti hai aur agli command use padhti hai. Is design ke advantages aur disadvantages ki baat book chapter mein aage materialization wale section mein karti hai.

Batch job ka output tabhi valid maana jaata hai jab job successfully complete ho jaaye. MapReduce failed job ka partial output discard kar deta hai. Isliye koi job tabhi start ho sakta hai jab uski input directories banane wale jobs successfully complete ho chuke hon. In dependencies ko manage karne ke liye Hadoop ke kai workflow schedulers hain, jaise Oozie, Azkaban, Luigi, Airflow aur Pinball. Yeh management features bhi dete hain jo batch jobs ka bada collection maintain karte waqt matter karte hain. Recommendation systems banate waqt 50 se 100 MapReduce jobs ke workflows common hain, aur bade organization mein kai teams aise jobs chala sakti hain jo ek-doosre ka output padhte hain. Tool support bahut zaroori ho jaata hai.

Hadoop ke higher-level tools, jaise Pig, Hive, Cascading, Crunch aur FlumeJava, bhi kai MapReduce stages ke workflows set up karte hain aur unhe apne aap wire kar dete hain.

Reduce-Side Joins aur Grouping

Chapter 2 mein humne data models aur query languages ke context mein joins ki baat ki thi, lekin yeh nahi bataya tha ki joins asal mein implement kaise hote hain. Chalo ab woh baat aage badhate hain.

Kaafi datasets mein ek record doosre record se associated hota hai. Yeh relational model mein foreign key ho sakta hai, document model mein document reference, ya graph model mein edge. Jab bhi kisi code ko is association ke dono taraf ke records access karne hon, tab join chahiye hota hai. Denormalization se joins ki zaroorat kam ho sakti hai, par aam taur par poori khatam nahi hoti. Is book mein jo joins discuss hue hain, woh zyadatar equi-joins hain. Inmein ek record un doosre records se associate hota hai jinki kisi particular field (jaise ID) mein bilkul same value ho. Kuch databases doosre tarah ke joins bhi support karte hain, par book unhe cover nahi karti.

Database mein agar query sirf kuch records se related hai, toh woh aam taur par index use karke unhe jaldi dhoondh leti hai. Query mein joins hon, toh kai index lookups lag sakte hain. MapReduce mein indexes ka koi concept nahi hota, jaise hum aam taur par samajhte hain. Jab MapReduce job ko input ke taur par files ka set diya jaata hai, toh woh un sab files ka poora content padhta hai. Database ki language mein ise full table scan kehte hain. Sirf kuch records padhne hon, toh index lookup ke mukable full scan bahut hi zyada expensive hai. Lekin analytic queries ko aksar bahut saare records par aggregates chahiye hote hain. Aise mein poora input scan karna theek ho sakta hai, khaaskar jab processing kai machines par phaili ho.

Batch processing mein joins ka matlab hota hai ek dataset ke andar ek association ke saare occurrences resolve karna. Jaise, job saare users ka data ek saath process karta hai, kisi ek particular user ka data alag se lookup nahi karta. Doosra tarika index ke saath kaafi zyada efficient hota.

Example: user activity events ka analysis

Example

Book ke Figure 10-2 mein jo example hai, usmein do inputs hain. Left mein activity events ka log hai, yani website par logged-in users ne jo kiya uska clickstream. Right mein users ka database hai. Ise star schema (Chapter 3 dekhein) ka hissa samajh sakte hain: events ka log fact table hai, aur user database ek dimension hai.

Maan lo ek analyst activity ko profile information se correlate karna chahta hai. Profile mein user ki age ya date of birth ho, toh analyst pata laga sakta hai ki kaun se pages kaun si age groups mein sabse popular hain. Lekin har activity event mein sirf user ID hota hai, poora profile nahi. Har event mein profile embed karna wasteful hoga, isliye events ko user database ke saath join karna padta hai.

Sabse simple implementation yeh hai ki events ek-ek karke dekhein aur har user ID ke liye remote server par user database ko query karein. Yeh possible hai, par performance kharab hoti hai. Throughput database server tak ke round-trip time se limited ho jaata hai. Local cache utna hi help karta hai jitna data ka distribution allow kare. Aise kai queries parallel mein chalane se database aasaani se overwhelm ho sakta hai.

Batch process mein achha throughput chahiye, toh computation jitna ho sake ek machine ke local rehna chahiye. Har record ke liye network par random-access requests karna bahut slow hai. Remote database ko query karne se batch job nondeterministic bhi ho jaata hai, kyunki job chalte waqt us database ka data badal sakta hai. Behtar tarika yeh hai ki user database ki ek copy le lein, jaise database backup se ETL (extract, transform, load) process ke zariye, aur use activity log wale hi distributed filesystem mein rakh dein. Phir user database files ke ek set mein hota hai aur activity records doosre set mein, aur MapReduce relevant records ko efficiently ek jagah la sakta hai.

Sort-merge joins

Yaad rakhein ki mapper ka kaam har input record se key aur value nikalna hai. Is join mein key user ID hai. Mappers ka ek set activity events par jaata hai aur user ID ko key aur event ko value bana kar emit karta hai. Mappers ka doosra set user database par jaata hai aur user ID ko key aur date of birth ko value bana kar emit karta hai. Figure 3 yahi dikhata hai.

Framework jab mapper output ko key ke hisaab se partition aur sort karta hai, toh same ID wale activity events aur user record reducer input mein ek-doosre ke bagal mein aa jaate hain. Job sort aise bhi arrange kar sakti hai ki reducer ko hamesha user record pehle mile, aur uske baad us user ke events timestamp order mein. Is technique ko secondary sort kehte hain.

Ab reducer join karta hai. Uska function har user ID ke liye ek baar call hota hai. Secondary sort ki wajah se pehli value user database ka date-of-birth record hoti hai. Reducer date of birth ko ek local variable mein rakhta hai, phir same user ID wale activity events par iterate karta hai, aur viewed URL aur viewer ki age (years mein) ke pairs output karta hai. Baad ke MapReduce jobs har URL ke liye viewer ages ka distribution calculate kar sakte hain, aur URLs ko age group ke hisaab se cluster kar sakte hain.

Reducer ek user ID ke saare records ek hi baar mein process karta hai, isliye use memory mein ek time par sirf ek user record rakhna padta hai. Use kabhi network request nahi karni padti. Is algorithm ko sort-merge join kehte hain, kyunki mapper output key ke hisaab se sorted hota hai, aur phir reducers join ke dono taraf ke records ki sorted lists ko merge karte hain.

Related data ko ek hi jagah laana

Sort-merge join mein mappers aur sorting process yeh pakka karte hain ki ek user ID ke liye zaroori saara data ek hi jagah aa jaye: reducer ki ek single call. Data pehle se line up hone ki wajah se reducer ek simple, single-threaded program ho sakta hai, jo high throughput aur low memory overhead ke saath records chalata jaata hai.

Ise aise bhi dekh sakte hain ki mappers reducers ko messages bhejte hain. Mapper jab key-value pair emit karta hai, toh key value ke destination address jaisi kaam karti hai. Key bas ek arbitrary string hai, IP address aur port number jaisa network address nahi. Phir bhi woh address ki tarah behave karti hai, kyunki same key wale saare pairs same destination par pahunchte hain, yani reducer ki ek call par.

Yeh model physical network communication (data ko sahi machine tak pahunchana) ko application logic (data milne ke baad usse process karna) se alag kar deta hai. Typical database use mein aisa nahi hota, wahan data ki request aksar application code ke andar kahin gehraai mein hoti hai. MapReduce saari network communication khud sambhalta hai, isliye application code ko partial failures (jaise kisi doosre node ka crash) ki fikar nahi karni padti. Framework failed tasks ko transparently retry kar leta hai, aur application logic par koi asar nahi padta.

GROUP BY

Joins ke alawa, related data ko ek hi jagah laane wale pattern ka ek aur common use hai records ko kisi key se group karna, jaise SQL ka GROUP BY clause. Same key wale saare records ek group banate hain. Aksar agla step har group ke andar aggregate karna hota hai. Common examples yeh hain:

  • Har group ke records count karna. SQL mein yeh COUNT(*) aggregation hai, jaise har URL ke page views count karna.
  • Kisi ek field ki values ko add karna, jaise SUM(fieldname) mein.
  • Kisi ranking function ke hisaab se top k records chunna.

MapReduce se grouping implement karne ka sabse simple tarika yeh hai ki mappers aise set up karein ki unke key-value pairs mein grouping key use ho. Phir partitioning aur sorting same key wale saare records ko same reducer tak le aati hai. Isi wajah se MapReduce par bane grouping aur joining kaafi similar dikhte hain.

Grouping ka ek aur common use hai sessionization: ek user session ke saare activity events ikattha karna, taaki us user ne kaun se actions kis sequence mein kiye woh pata chale. Aisi analysis se jawab mil sakta hai ki jin users ne tumhari website ka naya version dekha woh purane version wale users se zyada kharidne ke chance mein hain ya nahi (yeh A/B testing hai), ya marketing campaign apni cost ke laayak hai ya nahi. Agar tum kai web servers chalate ho, toh ek user ke events shayad kai servers ki log files mein bikhre honge. Session cookie, user ID ya aisi kisi identifier ko grouping key bana kar tum sessionization implement kar sakte ho. Isse ek user ke saare events ek jagah aa jaate hain, aur alag-alag users alag-alag partitions mein phail jaate hain.

Skew ko handle karna

Same key wale saare records ko ek hi jagah laane wala pattern tab toot jaata hai jab bahut bada data kisi ek key se related ho. Social network mein zyadatar users ke kuch sau connections hote hain, par kuch celebrities ke karodon followers ho sakte hain. Is tarah ke disproportionately active records ko linchpin objects ya hot keys kehte hain.

Dhyaan do

Kisi celebrity ki saari activity (jaise unki ek post ke replies) ek hi reducer mein ikattha karne se skew hota hai, jise hot spot bhi kehte hain. Ek reducer ke paas baaki sabse kahin zyada records aa jaate hain. MapReduce job tabhi complete hoti hai jab uske saare mappers aur reducers khatam ho jaayein, isliye aage ke saare jobs us sabse slow reducer ka intezaar karte hain.

Join input mein hot keys hon, toh compensate karne ke liye kai algorithms hain:

  • Pig ka skewed join pehle ek sampling job chalata hai, taaki pata chale kaun si keys hot hain. Join karte waqt mappers hot key ke records ko kai reducers mein se kisi ek ko random tarike se bhejte hain. Normal MapReduce key ke hash se reducer deterministically chunta hai. Doosre input ke liye, hot key ke records ko un saare reducers tak copy karna padta hai jo us key ko handle karte hain.
  • Crunch ka sharded join similar tarike se kaam karta hai, lekin hot keys ko sampling se dhoondhne ke bajaye explicitly specify karna padta hai.
  • Hive ke skewed join mein hot keys ko table metadata mein name karna padta hai. Woh un keys ke records ko baaki records se alag files mein store karta hai. Us table ko join karte waqt woh hot keys ke liye map-side join (neeche describe kiya gaya hai) use karta hai.

Yeh techniques hot key ka kaam kai reducers mein baant deti hain, jisse parallelism behtar hoti hai. Iski cost yeh hai ki doosre join input ko kai reducers tak replicate karna padta hai. Randomization ka yahi idea partitioned databases mein hot spots ko kam karne ke liye bhi use hota hai, jo Chapter 6 mein cover hua hai.

Hot key se grouping aur aggregation do stages mein bhi ho sakti hai. Pehla MapReduce stage records ko random reducers ko bhejta hai, toh har reducer hot key ke records ka sirf ek subset group karta hai aur ek zyada compact partial result output karta hai. Phir doosra MapReduce job pehle-stage ke saare reducers ke partial results ko combine karke har key ki ek value bana deta hai.

Try karo

Socho ek reduce-side join hai jismein ek key ke records baaki saari keys ke records ko milakar bhi kahin zyada hain. Upar ki skew techniques mein se tum kaun si chunoge, aur doosre join input par uski kya cost aayegi?

Map-Side Joins

Pichhle section ke join algorithms asli join logic reducers mein chalate hain, isliye unhe reduce-side joins kehte hain. Mappers input taiyaar karte hain: woh har record se key aur value nikalte hain, pairs ko reducer partitions mein assign karte hain, aur key ke hisaab se sort karte hain.

Reduce-side approach ka ek bada fayda hai. Tumhe input data ke baare mein koi assumptions nahi lene padte. Uski properties aur structure kuch bhi ho, mappers use joining ke liye taiyaar kar sakte hain. Nuksaan yeh hai ki woh saari sorting, reducers tak copying aur merging kaafi expensive ho sakti hai. Available memory buffers par depend karta hai, lekin MapReduce ke stages se guzarte hue data kai baar disk par likha ja sakta hai.

Agar tum apne input ke baare mein kuch assumptions le sakte ho, toh map-side join se joins ko tez bana sakte ho. Is approach mein ek cut-down MapReduce job hota hai, jismein na reducers hote hain na sorting. Har mapper distributed filesystem se ek input file block padhta hai aur ek output file likhta hai. Bas itna hi.

Broadcast hash joins

Sabse simple map-side join tab lagta hai jab ek bade dataset ko ek chhote dataset ke saath join karna ho. Chhota dataset itna chhota hona chahiye ki har mapper mein poora memory mein load ho sake. Maan lo Figure 10-2 ka user database memory mein fit ho jaata hai. Mapper start hote hi pehle distributed filesystem se user database ko in-memory hash table mein padhta hai. Phir woh activity events scan karta hai aur har event ki user ID us hash table mein lookup karta hai. (Yahan maana gaya hai ki har key ki exactly ek entry hai, jo user database ke liye shayad sahi hai, kyunki user ID ek hi user ko identify karti hai. Aam taur par ek key ki kai entries ho sakti hain, aur join saare matches output karta hai.)

Phir bhi kai map tasks ho sakte hain, bade input ke har file block ke liye ek. Figure 10-2 mein activity events bada input hain. In mappers mein se har ek chhote input ko poora memory mein load karta hai. Is simple lekin effective algorithm ko broadcast hash join kehte hain. Broadcast word yeh batata hai ki bade input ke ek hisse ka har mapper poora chhota input padhta hai, yani chhota input effectively bade input ke har partition ko bhej diya jaata hai. Hash word hash table ke use ko dikhata hai. Pig is join ko replicated join naam se support karta hai. Hive ise MapJoin kehta hai, aur Cascading, Crunch aur Impala query engine bhi ise use karte hain.

Chhote input ko in-memory hash table mein load karne ke bajaye ek alternative yeh hai ki use local disk par read-only index mein store kar dein. Us index ke frequently used hisse operating system ke page cache mein rehte hain, toh lookups lagbhag in-memory hash table jitne tez ho sakte hain. Isme poora dataset memory mein fit hone ki zaroorat bhi nahi padti.

Partitioned hash joins

Map-side join ke inputs agar same tarike se partitioned hain, toh hash join har partition par independently apply ho sakta hai. Figure 10-2 ke liye tum activity events aur user database dono ko user ID ke aakhri decimal digit se partition kar sakte ho, yani har side par 10 partitions. Phir mapper 3 pehle un saare users ko hash table mein load karta hai jinki ID 3 par khatam hoti hai. Uske baad woh un saare users ke activity events scan karta hai jinki ID 3 par khatam hoti hai.

Partitioning sahi ho, toh jo bhi record join ho sakta hai woh same numbered partition mein hota hai. Isliye har mapper ko har input dataset se sirf ek partition padhna padta hai. Fayda yeh hai ki har mapper apne hash table mein kam data load karta hai.

Yeh approach tabhi chalti hai jab dono inputs ke partitions ki ginti same ho, aur records same key aur same hash function se partitions mein assign hue hon. Agar inputs pehle ke MapReduce jobs ne generate kiye hain jo yeh grouping already kar chuke hain, toh yeh assumption theek ho sakta hai. Hive ise bucketed map joins kehta hai.

Map-side merge joins

Ek aur variant tab lagta hai jab input datasets sirf same tarike se partitioned hi nahi, balki same key par sorted bhi hon. Aise mein farak nahi padta ki inputs memory mein fit hone laayak chhote hain ya nahi. Mapper wahi merge kar sakta hai jo normally reducer karta. Woh dono input files ko incrementally, ascending key order mein padhta hai, aur same key wale records ko match karta hai.

Map-side merge join possible ho, toh shayad pehle ke MapReduce jobs ne inputs ko isi partitioned aur sorted form mein banaya hoga.
