Principle mein, join us pehle wale job ke reduce stage mein bhi ho sakta tha. Lekin merge join ko alag map-only job ki tarah chalana phir bhi worth it ho sakta hai, jaise jab partitioned aur sorted datasets doosre kaamon ke liye bhi chahiye hon.

Map-side joins wale MapReduce workflows

MapReduce join ka output jab aage ke jobs use karte hain, tab map-side ya reduce-side join ka choice output ka structure badal deta hai. Reduce-side join ka output join key ke hisaab se partitioned aur sorted hota hai. Map-side join ka output bade input jaise hi partitioned aur sorted hota hai. Wajah yeh hai ki join ke bade input ke har file block ke liye ek map task start hota hai, chahe join partitioned ho ya broadcast.

Map-side joins apne inputs ke size, sorting aur partitioning ke baare mein zyada assumptions bhi lete hain. Isliye join strategies optimize karte waqt tumhe distributed filesystem mein datasets ka physical layout pata hona chahiye. Sirf encoding format aur directory ka naam jaanna kaafi nahi hai. Tumhe partitions ki ginti, aur woh keys bhi pata honi chahiye jinse data partitioned aur sorted hai. Hadoop ecosystem mein yeh metadata aksar HCatalog aur Hive metastore mein rakha jaata hai.

Trade-offs
Join methodKya chahiyeKis mein achhaCost
Sort-merge (reduce-side)Inputs ke baare mein kuch special nahiKisi bhi input par chalta hai, uska structure kuch bhi hoHar record ko network par sort, copy aur merge karna, aur data kai baar disk par likha ja sakta hai
Broadcast hash (map-side)Ek input itna chhota ki har mapper mein memory mein fit ho jayeNa sort, na reduce stage. Bada input wahin padha jaata hai jahan woh rakha haiChhota input har mapper tak copy hota hai. Chhota side fit na ho toh method toot jaata hai
Partitioned hash (map-side)Dono inputs same tarike se partitioned, same key, hash function aur partitions ki ginti ke saathHar mapper har input ka sirf ek slice load karta haiPartitioning pehle se sahi honi chahiye, aur aam taur par pehle ke jobs ise set up karte hain
Map-side merge (map-side)Dono inputs same key par partitioned aur sortedMap-only job, na sorting na reducers. Input ka size matter nahi kartaSorted, partitioned inputs pehle se present hone chahiye, yani aam taur par pehle ke kisi job ne unhe banaya ho

Batch Workflows ka Output

Is chapter mein humne MapReduce jobs ke workflows chalane ke algorithms dekhe, lekin ek zaroori sawaal abhi nahi poochha. Saari processing khatam hone par uska result kya hota hai? Yeh jobs chalate hi kyun hain?

Database queries ke liye book transaction processing (OLTP) aur analytic purposes mein farak karti hai. OLTP queries aam taur par indexes use karke key se kuch hi records lookup karti hain, taaki unhe user ko dikha sakein, jaise web page par. Analytic queries aksar bahut saare records scan karti hain, unhe group aur aggregate karti hain, aur report banati hain. Report time ke saath kisi metric ka graph, top 10 ranking, ya kisi quantity ka subcategories mein breakdown ho sakti hai. Uska consumer aksar ek analyst ya manager hota hai jise business decisions lene hote hain.

Batch processing kahan fit hoti hai? Yeh na transaction processing hai na analytics, halanki analytics ke zyada kareeb hai, kyunki batch process aam taur par apne input ke bade hisse scan karta hai. Lekin MapReduce jobs ka workflow analysis ke liye use hone wali SQL query jaisa nahi hota. Batch process ka output aksar report hota hi nahi. Woh kisi aur tarah ka structure hota hai.

Search indexes banana

Google ne MapReduce pehli baar apne search engine ke indexes banane ke liye use kiya tha, aur woh kaam 5 se 10 MapReduce jobs ka workflow tha. Google baad mein is kaam ke liye MapReduce se hat gaya, phir bhi search index banane ke nazariye se MapReduce ko samajhna madad karta hai. Aaj bhi Lucene aur Solr ke indexes banane ka Hadoop MapReduce ek achha tarika hai.

Chapter 3 mein humne briefly dekha tha ki Lucene jaisa full-text search index kaise kaam karta hai. Yeh ek file hai, jise term dictionary kehte hain, jismein tum efficiently kisi keyword ko lookup karke un saare document IDs ki list pa sakte ho jinmein woh keyword hai. Is list ko postings list kehte hain. Book ise bahut simplified view kehti hai. Asli index ko results ko relevance se rank karne, spelling galtiyan sudharne, synonyms resolve karne wagairah ke liye aur data bhi chahiye. Lekin principle wahi rehta hai.

Documents ke ek fixed set par full-text search chalani ho, toh indexes banane ke liye batch process bahut effective tarika hai. Mappers zaroorat ke hisaab se documents ke set ko partition karte hain, har reducer apne partition ka index banata hai, aur index files distributed filesystem mein likh di jaati hain. Document-partitioned indexes banana, jo Chapter 6 mein cover hua hai, bahut achhe se parallelize hota hai.

Keyword se search index ko query karna read-only operation hai, isliye index files ek baar ban jaayein toh immutable hoti hain. Documents ka set badle, toh ek option yeh hai ki poora indexing workflow time-time par dobara chalayein, aur khatam hone par purani index files ko naye wali se wholesale replace kar dein. Sirf kuch documents badle hon toh yeh computationally expensive ho sakta hai. Lekin is approach ko samajhna aasaan hai: documents andar, indexes bahar. Doosra option index ko incrementally banana hai. Chapter 3 mein jaisa dekha, Lucene mein documents add, remove ya update karne par woh nayi segment files likhta hai aur background mein asynchronously segment files ko merge aur compact karta hai. Incremental processing ke baare mein aur Chapter 11 mein hai.

Batch process ke output ke taur par key-value stores

Search indexes batch workflow ke output ka sirf ek example hain. Batch processing ka ek aur common use machine learning systems banana hai, jaise spam filters, anomaly detection aur image recognition ke classifiers, aur recommendation systems jo aise logon ko suggest karte hain jinhe tum jaante ho honge, aise products jinmein tumhe interest ho sakta hai, ya related searches. Un jobs ka output aksar ek database hota hai. Jaise, ek database ko user ID se query karke us user ke suggested friends mil sakte hain. Doosre ko product ID se query karke related products ki list mil sakti hai.

In databases ko woh web application query karti hai jo user requests handle karti hai, aur woh aam taur par Hadoop infrastructure se alag hoti hai. Toh output wapas aisi database mein kaise pahunche jise web application query kar sake?

Sabse obvious choice yeh hai ki apne pasandida database ki client library ko seedhe mapper ya reducer ke andar use karein, aur batch job se seedhe database server mein ek-ek record likhein. Yeh chal sakta hai, bas shart yeh hai ki tumhare firewall rules Hadoop environment se production databases tak direct access allow karo. Lekin book ise kai wajahon se bura idea kehti hai:

  1. Joins ke time jaisa dekha, har ek record ke liye network request karna batch task ke normal throughput se orders of magnitude slow hai. Client library batching support kare, tab bhi performance kharab hone ki possibility hai.
  2. MapReduce jobs aksar kai tasks parallel mein chalate hain. Agar woh sab usi rate par ek hi output database mein likhein jis rate par batch process produce kar sakta hai, toh database overwhelm ho sakta hai, aur queries ke liye uski performance kharab ho jaati hai. Isse system ke doosre hisson mein operational problems ho sakti hain.
  3. Normally MapReduce job output ke liye saaf all-or-nothing guarantee deta hai. Job succeed ho jaye, toh result wahi hota hai jo har task ko exactly ek baar chalane se aata, chahe kuch tasks fail hue ho aur retry hue ho. Poori job fail ho jaye, toh koi output nahi banta. Lekin external system mein likhne se side effects hote hain jinhe is tarah chhupaya nahi ja sakta. Adhoori job ke partial results doosre systems ko dikh sakte hain. Tumhe Hadoop task attempts aur speculative execution (jismein slow task ki doosri copy start ho sakti hai) ki complexities bhi handle karni padti hain.
Asli idea

Kahin behtar solution yeh hai ki naya database batch job ke andar hi banayein aur use files ki tarah likh dein job ki output directory mein, bilkul search indexes ki tarah. Files likhne ke baad immutable hoti hain, aur unhe bulk mein un servers mein load kiya ja sakta hai jo read-only queries handle karte hain.

Kai key-value stores MapReduce jobs ke andar database files banane ko support karte hain. Inmein Voldemort, Terrapin, ElephantDB aur HBase bulk loading shaamil hain. Yeh files banana MapReduce ke liye achha fit hai. Mapper key nikalta hai, aur us key par sorting index banane ke zaroori kaam ka kaafi bada hissa pehle hi hai. In key-value stores mein se zyadatar load hone ke baad read-only hote hain, kyunki files sirf batch job likh sakta hai aur phir woh immutable hoti hain. Matlab unke data structures kaafi simple ho sakte hain. Jaise, unhe write-ahead log (WAL) nahi chahiye, jo changes ka woh log hai jo databases crashes se recover karne ke liye use karte hain.

Voldemort mein data load karte waqt server purani data files se requests serve karta rehta hai, jabki nayi files distributed filesystem se server ki local disk par copy hoti hain. Copy poori hone par server atomically nayi files ko query karne par switch ho jaata hai. Kuch galat ho jaye, toh woh aasaani se purani files par wapas switch kar sakta hai, kyunki woh abhi bhi wahin hain aur immutable hain.

Batch process outputs ki philosophy

Unix philosophy dataflow ko bahut explicit bana kar experimentation ko encourage karti hai. Program apna input padhta hai aur output likhta hai. Input badalta nahi, pichhla koi bhi output poori tarah replace ho jaata hai, aur koi aur side effects nahi hote. Tum command ko jitni baar chaho dobara chala sakte ho, tweak ya debug karte hue, system ki state bigade bina.

MapReduce bhi yahi philosophy follow karta hai. Inputs ko immutable maan kar aur external databases mein writes jaise side effects se bach kar, batch jobs ko achhi performance milti hai aur unhe maintain karna kahin aasaan hota hai:

  • Bugs ko roll back karna. Tum bug laa do aur output galat ya corrupt ho jaye, toh code ke pichhle version par roll back karke job dobara chala sakte ho. Output phir sahi ho jaayega. Ya isse bhi aasaan, purana output kisi alag directory mein rakhein aur wapas usi par switch kar lein. Read-write database yeh nahi deta. Buggy code ne database mein kharab data likh diya ho, toh code roll back karne se data theek nahi hota. Buggy code se recover karne ki is ability ko book human fault tolerance kehti hai.
  • Tez development. Galtiyan undo karna aasaan hai, isliye feature development us environment se tez chal sakta hai jahan galtiyon se irreversible nuksaan ho sakta hai. Irreversibility kam karne ke is principle ko Kleppmann Agile software development se jodte hain.
  • Automatic retries. Map ya reduce task fail ho jaye, toh framework use reschedule karke same input par dobara chalata hai. Failure kisi bug ki wajah se ho, toh task baar-baar crash karta rehta hai aur kuch attempts ke baad job fail ho jaati hai. Failure transient ho, toh fault tolerate ho jaata hai. Automatic retry tabhi safe hai kyunki inputs immutable hain aur failed tasks ke outputs discard ho jaate hain.
  • Shared inputs. Files ka wahi set kai alag-alag jobs ka input ho sakta hai. Isme woh monitoring jobs bhi aate hain jo metrics calculate karte hain aur check karte hain ki job ke output ki expected characteristics hain ya nahi, jaise use pichhle run ke output se compare karke.
  • Logic wiring se alag. Unix tools ki tarah MapReduce jobs logic ko wiring se alag rakhte hain, yani input aur output directories configure karna. Is separation of concerns se code reusable banta hai. Ek team aisi job par focus kar sakti hai jo ek kaam achhe se karti hai, jabki doosri teams decide karti hain ki use kahan aur kab chalana hai.

Unix aur Hadoop kuch tarikon se alag bhi hain. Zyadatar Unix tools untyped text files maante hain, isliye unhe input parsing bahut karni padti hai. Log example mein URL nikalne ke liye {print $7} use hua tha. Hadoop par aise kuch low-value syntactic conversions zyada structured file formats use karke bach jaate hain. Avro aur Parquet aksar use hote hain. Avro efficient schema-based encoding deta hai aur schema ko time ke saath evolve hone deta hai, jaisa Chapter 4 mein discuss hua hai. Parquet column-oriented format hai, jo Chapter 3 mein cover hua tha.

Hadoop aur Distributed Databases ki tulna

Hadoop kuch-kuch Unix ke distributed version jaisa hai. HDFS filesystem hai, aur MapReduce Unix process ka ek quirky implementation hai jo apne map phase aur reduce phase ke beech hamesha sort utility chalata hai. Pichhle sections mein dikhaya gaya ki in primitives ke upar join aur grouping operations kaise implement hote hain.

MapReduce paper publish hua tab ek lihaaz se uske ideas naye nahi the. Pichhle kuch sections mein jo processing aur parallel join algorithms discuss hue, woh massively parallel processing (MPP) databases mein dus saal se zyada pehle hi implement ho chuke the. Gamma database machine, Teradata aur Tandem NonStop SQL is area ke pioneers the.

Sabse bada farak focus ka hai. MPP databases machines ke cluster par analytic SQL queries ke parallel execution par concentrate karte hain. MapReduce aur distributed filesystem ka combination kahin zyada general-purpose operating system jaisa kuch deta hai, jo arbitrary programs chala sakta hai.

Storage mein diversity

Databases tumse data ko kisi particular model, jaise relational ya document, ke hisaab se structure karwate hain. Distributed filesystem ki files bas byte sequences hoti hain, jinhe kisi bhi data model aur kisi bhi encoding se likha ja sakta hai. Woh database records ke collections ho sakte hain, par utni hi aasaani se text, images, videos, sensor readings, sparse matrices, feature vectors, genome sequences ya kisi aur tarah ka data bhi ho sakte hain.

Book simple words mein kehti hai: Hadoop ne data ko bina soche-samjhe HDFS mein dump karna aur baad mein sochna ki use process kaise karna hai, possible bana diya. MPP databases aam taur par chahte hain ki data ko database ke proprietary storage format mein import karne se pehle, data aur query patterns ki careful up-front modeling ho. Purist ke nazariye se yeh careful modeling achhi hai, kyunki database ke users ko behtar quality ka data milta hai. Lekin practice mein, data ko jaldi available kara dena, chahe woh raw aur awkward format mein ho, aksar pehle se ideal data model decide karne se zyada valuable hota hai.

Yeh data warehouse jaisa hai, jahan bade organization ke kai hisson se data ek jagah laana valuable hai, kyunki isse un datasets ke across joins ho sakte hain jo pehle alag-alag the. MPP database jis careful schema design ki maang karta hai, woh is central collection ko slow kar deta hai. Data ko raw form mein collect karna aur schema ki chinta baad mein karna collection ko tez kar deta hai. Is idea ko kabhi-kabhi data lake ya enterprise data hub kehte hain.

Bina soche-samjhe data dump karne se data ko interpret karne ka bojh shift ho jaata hai. Dataset ke producer ko use standardized format mein convert karne par majboor karne ke bajaye, interpretation consumer ki problem ban jaati hai. Yeh schema-on-read approach hai, jise Chapter 2 mein document model ke saath discuss kiya tha. Jab producer aur consumers alag teams ho aur unki priorities alag hon, tab yeh advantage ho sakta hai. Shayad ek ideal data model ho hi nahi. Data ke alag-alag views alag-alag purposes ke liye suit kar sakte hain, aur data ko raw form mein dump karne se aisi kai transformations ho sakti hain. Book ise sushi principle kehti hai, yani raw data behtar hai.

Isliye Hadoop aksar ETL ke liye use hua hai. Transaction processing systems ka data kisi raw form mein distributed filesystem mein dump hota hai. Phir MapReduce jobs us data ko clean karte hain, relational form mein transform karte hain, aur analysis ke liye MPP data warehouse mein import kar dete hain. Data modeling ab bhi hoti hai, lekin woh ek alag step hai, data collection se decoupled. Yeh decoupling isliye chalti hai kyunki distributed filesystem data ko kisi bhi format mein accept karta hai.

Processing models mein diversity

MPP databases monolithic, tightly integrated software hote hain. Woh disk par storage layout, query planning, scheduling aur execution sab sambhalte hain. Kyunki yeh saare components database ki zaroorat ke hisaab se tune ho sakte hain, poora system un queries par bahut achha perform kar sakta hai jinke liye woh bana tha. SQL query language bhi bina code likhe expressive queries aur clean semantics deti hai, jisse woh business analysts ke graphical tools (jaise Tableau) ke liye accessible ho jaati hai.

Har processing ko SQL queries mein sensibly express nahi kiya ja sakta. Tum machine learning ya recommendation systems, relevance ranking models wale full-text search indexes, ya image analysis bana rahe hain, toh shayad tumhe data processing ka zyada general model chahiye. Is tarah ki processing aksar kisi application ke liye bahut specific hoti hai. Examples hain machine learning ke liye feature engineering, machine translation ke liye natural language models, aur fraud prediction ke liye risk estimation functions. Inmein code likhna anivaarya hai, sirf queries kaafi nahi.

MapReduce ne engineers ko bade datasets par apna code aasaani se chalane ki ability di. Tumhare paas HDFS aur MapReduce ho, toh tum unke upar SQL query execution engine bana sakte ho, aur Hive project ne yahi kiya. Lekin tum aur bhi kai tarah ke batch processes likh sakte ho jo SQL query mein express hone ke liye suit nahi karte.

Baad mein logon ne paaya ki kuch tarah ki processing ke liye MapReduce bahut limiting aur bahut slow hai, toh Hadoop ke upar doosre processing models develop hue. Do processing models, SQL aur MapReduce, kaafi nahi the, aur zyada ki zaroorat thi. Hadoop ke open hone ki wajah se aise kai approaches implement karna feasible tha jo monolithic MPP database ki seemaon mein fit nahi hote.

Yeh saare processing models machines ke ek single shared-use cluster par chal sakte hain, aur sab distributed filesystem ki same files access karte hain. Alag-alag tarah ki processing ke liye data ko kai specialized systems mein import karne ki zaroorat nahi. System itna flexible hai ki ek hi cluster mein diverse workloads support kar sake. Data ko idhar-udhar move na karna padne se usse value nikalna kahin aasaan hota hai, aur naye processing models ke saath experiment karna bhi.

Hadoop ecosystem mein random-access OLTP databases, jaise HBase (Chapter 3 mein SSTables aur LSM-Trees ki discussion dekhein), aur MPP-style analytic databases, jaise Impala, dono hain. Na HBase MapReduce use karta hai na Impala, lekin dono storage ke liye HDFS use karte hain. Data access aur process karne ke yeh bahut alag tarike hain, phir bhi woh ek hi system mein saath reh sakte hain aur integrate ho sakte hain.

Frequent faults ke liye design

MapReduce aur MPP databases ko compare karte hue design ke do aur farak dikhte hain: har ek faults ko kaise handle karta hai, aur memory aur disk ko kaise use karta hai. Batch processes online systems se kam fault-sensitive hote hain. Fault ka users par turant asar nahi padta, aur job hamesha dobara chalayi ja sakti hai.

Query chalte waqt koi node crash ho jaye, toh zyadatar MPP databases poori query abort kar dete hain. Woh ya toh user ko query dobara submit karne dete hain ya khud automatically dobara chala dete hain. Queries normally zyada se zyada seconds ya minutes chalti hain, isliye errors handle karne ka yeh tarika acceptable hai, kyunki retry karna bahut expensive nahi hota. MPP databases yeh bhi pasand karte hain ki jitna ho sake data memory mein rahe, jaise hash joins use karke, taaki disk se padhne ki cost bache.

MapReduce kisi map ya reduce task ke fail hone ko poori job par asar ke bina tolerate kar sakta hai, kyunki woh kaam ko individual task ki granularity par retry karta hai. Woh data ko disk par likhne ke liye bhi kaafi eager hai. Yeh ek hisse mein fault tolerance ke liye hai, aur ek hisse mein is liye ki woh maanta hai ki dataset waise bhi memory mein fit hone ke liye bahut bada hoga.

MapReduce approach bade jobs ke liye suit karti hai: aise jobs jo itna data process karte hain aur itni der chalte hain ki beech mein kam se kam ek task failure hone ki possibility ho. Aise mein ek task failure ki wajah se poori job dobara chalana wasteful hoga. Task ki granularity par recovery se fault-free processing slow ho jaaye, tab bhi task failures ka rate kaafi high ho toh yeh reasonable trade-off ho sakta hai.

Lekin yeh assumptions kitne realistic hain? Zyadatar clusters mein machine failures hoti hain, par kam, isliye zyadatar jobs ko machine failure ka saamna nahi karna padega. Kya fault tolerance ke liye itna significant overhead dena sach mein worth it hai?

MapReduce ke memory ke careful use aur task-level recovery ko samajhne ke liye dekhein ki use kis environment ke liye design kiya gaya tha. Google mixed-use datacenters chalata tha, jahan online production services aur offline batch jobs same machines par chalte the. Har task ka ek resource allocation (CPU cores, RAM, disk space wagairah) hota tha jo containers enforce karte the. Har task ki ek priority bhi hoti thi. Higher-priority task ko zyada resources chahiye hon, toh same machine ke lower-priority tasks ko terminate, yani preempt, kiya ja sakta tha, taaki resources free ho jaayein. Priority se computing resources ki price bhi tay hoti thi. Teams ko jo use karti thi uska paisa dena padta tha, aur higher-priority processes zyada mehnge the.

Is architecture mein non-production, low-priority resources ko overcommit karna possible hai, kyunki system jaanta hai ki zaroorat padne par woh unhe wapas le sakta hai. Overcommit karne se machines ka use zyada poori tarah hota hai, aur yeh un systems se zyada efficient hai jo production aur non-production kaam ko alag rakhte hain. Lekin MapReduce jobs low priority par chalte hain, isliye kisi bhi waqt preempt hone ka risk rehta hai jab koi higher-priority process unke resources maange. Batch jobs effectively wahi computing resources use karte hain jo high-priority processes ke apna hissa lene ke baad bach jaate hain.

Google mein ek ghanta chalne wale MapReduce task ke higher-priority process ke liye jagah banane ke chakkar mein terminate hone ka risk lagbhag 5% hota hai. Yeh rate hardware problems, machine reboots ya doosri wajahon se hone wale failures ke rate se ek order of magnitude se zyada hai. Is rate par, 100 tasks wali job, jinmein har task 10 minute chalta hai, mein is baat ka risk 50% se zyada hai ki khatam hone se pehle kam se kam ek task terminate ho jaayega.

Isi wajah se MapReduce ko frequent, unexpected task termination tolerate karne ke liye design kiya gaya hai. Aisa isliye nahi ki hardware khaas taur par unreliable hai. Aisa isliye kyunki kisi bhi waqt processes terminate karne ki azaadi se poore cluster mein resources ka behtar utilization hota hai.

Open source cluster schedulers mein preemption kam use hota hai. YARN ka CapacityScheduler queues ke beech resources balance karne ke liye preemption support karta hai. Lekin book likhe jaane ke waqt YARN, Mesos ya Kubernetes mein general priority preemption support nahi tha. Jis environment mein tasks aksar terminate nahi hote, wahan MapReduce ke design decisions kam sense banate hain. Agla section kuch aise alternatives dekhta hai jo alag decisions lete hain.

MapReduce ke aage

2000s ke end mein MapReduce kaafi popular hua aur uska bahut hype bhi raha. Lekin distributed systems ke liye yeh bas ek programming model hai, aur bhi kaafi options hain. Data ki volume, uska structure aur processing ka type dekhkar, kabhi doosre tools computation express karne ke liye zyada sahi hote hain.

Is chapter ne MapReduce par kaafi time lagaya, kyunki yeh seekhne ke liye ek achha tool hai. Yeh distributed filesystem ke upar ek saaf aur simple abstraction hai. Simple is matlab mein ki tum samajh sakte ho ki woh kya kar raha hai, yeh matlab nahi ki use karna aasaan hai. Raw MapReduce APIs se complex processing job implement karna actually kaafi mushkil aur thakaane wala kaam hai. Jaise, koi bhi join algorithm tumhe shuru se khud implement karna padega.

Isi wajah se MapReduce ke upar higher-level programming models bane, jaise Pig, Hive, Cascading aur Crunch. Agar tumhe MapReduce ka kaam samajh aata hai, toh inhe seekhna kaafi aasaan hai, aur inke higher-level constructs se bahut saare common batch tasks implement karna kaafi simple ho jaata hai.

Lekin MapReduce ke execution model mein hi kuch problems hain, aur ek aur abstraction layer lagane se woh theek nahi hoti. Kuch tarah ki processing mein yeh poor performance ke roop mein dikhti hain. MapReduce bahut robust hai. Tum almost kitna bhi bada data ek unreliable, multi-tenant system par process kar sakte ho, jahan tasks baar-baar terminate hote rehte hain, aur phir bhi job poora ho jayega, bhale hi dheere. Doosri taraf, kuch tools kuch tarah ki processing mein orders of magnitude tak faster hote hain.

Chapter ka baaki hissa inhi mein se kuch alternatives dekhta hai. Chapter 11 mein hum stream processing par jaayenge, jise batch processing ko tez karne ka ek aur tarika maana ja sakta hai.

Intermediate state ka materialization

Har MapReduce job doosre sabhi jobs se independent hota hai. Job ka baaki duniya se main contact uske input aur output directories hain, jo distributed filesystem mein hoti hain. Agar tum chahte ho ki ek job ka output doosre job ka input bane, toh doosre job ki input directory ko pehle job ki output directory ke barabar set karna padega. Phir ek external workflow scheduler doosra job tabhi start karega jab pehla complete ho chuka ho.

Yeh setup tab theek hai jab pehle job ka output ek aisa dataset ho jo tum apne organization mein sabke liye publish karna chahte ho. Tab doosre jobs, doosri teams ke likhe hue jobs bhi, usse naam se refer karke reuse kar sakte hain. Data ko ek well-known location par publish karne se loose coupling milti hai, yani jobs ko yeh pata hona zaroori nahi ki unka input kaun produce karta hai ya output kaun consume karta hai.

Lekin kaafi cases mein tumhe pata hota hai ki ek job ka output sirf ek doosre job ke input ke taur par use hota hai, aur dono ek hi team maintain karti hai. Tab distributed filesystem ki files bas intermediate state hoti hain, yani ek job se doosre job tak data pahunchane ka zariya. Recommendation systems banane ke liye 50 ya 100 MapReduce jobs ke complex workflows mein aisi intermediate state bahut hoti hai.

Is intermediate state ko files mein likhne ke process ko materialization kehte hain. Yeh term Chapter 3 mein materialized views ke saath bhi aaya tha. Matlab kisi operation ka result pehle se compute karke likh dena, bajaye ismein ki jab koi maange tab on demand compute karein.

Chapter ke start mein log analysis ke liye Unix pipes use hue the, jo ek command ka output agli command ke input se jodte hain. Pipes intermediate state ko poori tarah materialize nahi karte. Woh output ko input tak incrementally stream karte hain, aur sirf ek chhota sa in-memory buffer use karte hain. Unix pipes ke comparison mein, MapReduce ka intermediate state ko poori tarah materialize karne wala approach teen downsides rakhta hai:

  • MapReduce job tabhi start ho sakta hai jab pichhle jobs ke woh saare tasks complete ho jayein jo uske inputs generate karte hain. Unix pipe se jude processes sab ek saath start hote hain, aur har process output aate hi consume kar leta hai. Skew, yani alag-alag machines par uneven load, ki wajah se job mein aksar kuch straggler tasks hote hain jo baaki se bahut zyada time lete hain. Pichhle job ke saare tasks ka wait karne se poora workflow slow ho jaata hai.
  • Mappers aksar redundant hote hain. Woh bas wahi file wapas read karte hain jo reducer ne abhi likhi thi, aur use partitioning aur sorting ke agle stage ke liye taiyaar karte hain. Kaafi cases mein mapper ka kaam pichhle reducer ka hi hissa ban sakta hai. Agar reducer output bhi mapper output ki tarah hi partitioned aur sorted hota, toh reducers ko seedha chain kiya ja sakta tha, beech mein mapper stages ke bina.
  • Intermediate state ko distributed filesystem mein rakhne ka matlab hai ki files kai nodes par replicate hoti hain. Temporary data ke liye yeh aksar overkill hota hai.

Dataflow engines

MapReduce ki in problems ko theek karne ke liye distributed batch computations ke kai naye execution engines bane. Sabse jaane-maane hain Spark, Tez aur Flink. Inka design alag hai, lekin ek idea sabme common hai: woh poore workflow ko ek hi job ki tarah handle karte hain, use independent subjobs mein todne ke bajaye.

Kyunki yeh systems data ke kai processing stages se guzarne ka flow explicitly model karte hain, inhe dataflow engines kehte hain. MapReduce ki tarah, yeh bhi ek user-defined function ko baar-baar call karke, ek single thread par ek time mein ek record process karte hain. Yeh apne inputs ko partition karke kaam parallelize karte hain, aur ek function ka output network ke through copy karke doosre function ka input bana dete hain.

MapReduce se alag, in functions ko map aur reduce ke alternating strict roles mein rehna zaroori nahi hai. Unhe kaafi flexible tarike se jod sakte hain. Book inhe operators kehti hai. Dataflow engine ek operator ke output ko doosre ke input se jodne ke kai options deta hai:

  • Records ko key ke hisaab se repartition aur sort karna, jaise MapReduce shuffle mein hota hai. Isse sort-merge joins aur grouping possible hote hain, bilkul MapReduce ki tarah.
  • Kai inputs lekar unhe ek hi tarike se partition karna, lekin sorting skip kar dena. Isse partitioned hash joins mein mehnat bachti hai. Wahan records ka order matter nahi karta, kyunki hash table banate waqt woh waise bhi randomize ho jaata hai.
  • Broadcast hash joins ke liye, ek operator ka wahi output join operator ke saare partitions ko bhej dena.

Is tarah ka processing engine Dryad aur Nephele naam ke research systems par based hai. MapReduce model ke mukable ismein kai advantages hain:

  • Sorting jaisa mehnga kaam sirf wahin karna padta hai jahan sach mein zaroori ho. Yeh har map aur reduce stage ke beech default mein nahi hota.
  • Koi unnecessary map tasks nahi hote. Mapper ka kaam aksar pichhle reduce operator mein hi fold ho sakta hai, kyunki mapper dataset ke partition hone ka tarika nahi badalta.
  • Workflow ke saare joins aur data dependencies explicitly declare hote hain, isliye scheduler ko pata hota hai ki kaun sa data kahan chahiye. Isliye woh locality optimizations kar sakta hai. Jaise, jo task kuch data consume karta hai use usi machine par rakh sakta hai jahan woh data produce karne wala task chal raha hai, taaki data network par copy hone ke bajaye ek shared memory buffer se guzar jaye.
  • Operators ke beech ki intermediate state memory mein rakhi ja sakti hai ya local disk par likhi ja sakti hai. Isme HDFS mein likhne se kam I/O lagta hai, kyunki HDFS mein use kai machines par replicate karna padta hai aur har replica par disk par likhna padta hai. MapReduce mapper output ke liye yeh trick pehle se use karta hai, aur dataflow engines ise saari intermediate state par apply karte hain.
  • Operators apna input ready hote hi execute karna shuru kar sakte hain. Poore pichhle stage ke khatam hone ka wait karne ki zaroorat nahi.
  • Naye operators chalane ke liye existing Java Virtual Machine (JVM) processes ko reuse kiya ja sakta hai. Isse startup overhead kam hota hai, jabki MapReduce har task ke liye naya JVM launch karta hai.

Dataflow engines se tum wahi computations implement kar sakte ho jo MapReduce workflows karte hain, aur in optimizations ki wajah se woh aam taur par kaafi tez chalte hain. Operators map aur reduce ka generalization hain, isliye wahi processing code dono engines par chal sakta hai. Pig, Hive ya Cascading mein likhe workflows ko ek simple configuration change se MapReduce se Tez ya Spark par switch kar sakte hain, code badle bina.

Tez ek kaafi patli library hai jo nodes ke beech data copy karne ke liye YARN shuffle service par depend karti hai. Spark aur Flink bade frameworks hain. Inme apni network communication layer, scheduler aur user-facing APIs hote hain, jinke baare mein chapter thodi der mein wapas aayega.

Dataflow engines mein fault tolerance

Intermediate state ko distributed filesystem mein poori tarah materialize karne ka ek fayda yeh hai ki state durable hoti hai. Isse MapReduce mein fault tolerance kaafi aasaan ho jaati hai. Agar koi task fail ho jaye, toh use doosri machine par restart kar sakte hain, aur woh wahi input filesystem se dobara read kar sakta hai.

Spark, Flink aur Tez intermediate state ko HDFS mein likhne se bachte hain, isliye unka approach alag hai. Agar koi machine fail ho jaye aur us par rakhi intermediate state kho jaye, toh khoya hua data kisi aur available data se dobara recompute hota hai. Framework agar pichhla intermediate stage available ho toh use leta hai. Nahi toh original input data par wapas jaata hai, jo aam taur par HDFS mein hota hai.

Recomputation possible banane ke liye framework ko track rakhna padta hai ki data ka har hissa kaise compute hua tha. Yani usne kaun se input partitions use kiye aur us par kaun se operators apply hue. Spark data ki ancestry track karne ke liye resilient distributed dataset (RDD) abstraction use karta hai. Flink operator state ke checkpoints leta hai, taaki chalte waqt fault mein phans gaye operator ko wapas resume kar sake.

Recomputation determinism par depend karta hai. Yani same input data milne par kya operators hamesha same output dete hain? Yeh sawal tab matter karta hai jab kuch khoya hua data pehle hi downstream operators ko bheja ja chuka ho. Agar operator restart ho aur recompute kiya data original khoye hue data se alag ho, toh downstream operators ke liye purane aur naye data ka contradiction suljhana bahut mushkil ho jaata hai. Nondeterministic operators ka solution aam taur par yeh hota hai ki downstream operators ko bhi kill karke naye data par dobara chalaya jaye.

Aise cascading faults se bachne ke liye operators ko deterministic banana behtar hai. Lekin nondeterminism galti se bhi ghus sakta hai. Kai programming languages hash table ke elements par iterate karte waqt koi particular order guarantee nahi karti. Kai probabilistic aur statistical algorithms random numbers par depend karte hain. System clock ya external data sources ka koi bhi use bhi nondeterministic hota hai. Faults se reliably recover karne ke liye in sabhi causes ko hatana padta hai. Ek tarika yeh hai ki pseudorandom numbers ek fixed seed se generate karein, taaki har baar wahi sequence aaye.

Recomputation se recover karna hamesha sahi jawab nahi hota. Agar intermediate data source data se bahut chhota ho, ya computation bahut CPU-intensive ho, toh shayad intermediate data ko files mein materialize karna recompute karne se sasta padega.

Materialization par charcha

Wapas Unix analogy par aate hain. MapReduce aisa hai jaise har command ka output ek temporary file mein likhna. Dataflow engines Unix pipes jaise kaafi zyada lagte hain. Khaas kar Flink pipelined execution ke around bana hai, matlab ek operator ka output doosre operators ko incrementally pass karna, input poora hone ka wait kiye bina use process karna shuru karna.

Sorting operation ko output dene se pehle apna poora input consume karna hi padta hai. Mumkin hai ki sabse last input record ka key sabse chhota ho, aur isliye woh sabse pehla output record hona chahiye. Isliye jis bhi operator ko sorting chahiye, use kam se kam kuch der ke liye state accumulate karni padti hai. Lekin workflow ke kaafi doosre hisse pipelined tarike se chal sakte hain.

Job complete hone par uska output kisi durable jagah jaana chahiye, jahan users use dhoondh kar use kar sakein. Sabse zyada chance hai ki use dobara distributed filesystem mein likha jaye. Isliye dataflow engine use karne par bhi HDFS ke materialized datasets aam taur par job ke inputs aur final outputs hi rehte hain. MapReduce ki tarah, inputs immutable hote hain aur output poori tarah replace ho jaata hai. MapReduce se improvement yeh hai ki ab saari intermediate state bhi filesystem mein likhni nahi padti.

Graphs aur Iterative Processing

Chapter 2 mein data model karne ke liye graphs aur unke edges aur vertices traverse karne ke liye graph query languages ki baat hui thi. Woh discussion OLTP-style use par thi, jahan queries jaldi chalakar kuch criteria se match karne wale chhote number ke vertices dhoondhe jaate hain.

Graphs ko batch context mein dekhna bhi interesting hai, jahan goal poore graph ka offline process ya analysis hota hai. Yeh zaroorat aksar machine learning mein aati hai, jaise recommendation engines aur ranking systems mein. Sabse famous graph algorithms mein se ek PageRank hai, jo estimate karta hai ki ek web page kitna popular hai, is basis par ki kaun se doosre pages use link karte hain. Yeh us formula ka hissa hai jo tay karta hai ki search engines results kis order mein dikhaye.

Yahan naming ka ek trap hai. Spark, Flink aur Tez jaise dataflow engines job ke operators ko directed acyclic graph (DAG) mein arrange karte hain. Yeh graph processing jaisa nahi hai. Dataflow engine mein ek operator se doosre tak data ka flow graph ki tarah structured hota hai, lekin data khud aam taur par relational-style tuples hota hai. Graph processing mein data khud graph ki shakal mein hota hai. Book ise ek aur unfortunate naming confusion kehti hai.

Kai graph algorithms ek time par ek edge traverse karke kaam karte hain. Woh ek vertex ko uske adjacent vertex se join karte hain taaki koi information propagate ho, aur yeh tab tak repeat karte hain jab tak koi condition poori na ho. Jaise, algorithm tab ruk sakta hai jab follow karne ke liye aur edges na bachein, ya jab koi metric converge ho jaye. Chapter 2 mein iska ek example tha, jisme database mein North America ki saari locations ki list banayi gayi thi, un edges ko baar-baar follow karke jo batate hain ki kaun si location kis doosri location ke andar hai. Is tarah ke algorithm ko transitive closure kehte hain.

Graph ko tum distributed filesystem mein files ki tarah store kar sakte ho, jinme vertices aur edges ki lists hon. Lekin repeat until done wala idea plain MapReduce mein express nahi ho sakta, kyunki MapReduce data par sirf ek single pass karta hai. Isliye is tarah ka algorithm aksar iterative style mein implement hota hai:

  1. Ek external scheduler algorithm ka ek step calculate karne ke liye batch process chalata hai.
  2. Batch process complete hone par scheduler completion condition ke basis par check karta hai ki algorithm khatam hua ya nahi. Jaise, aur edges follow karne ke liye nahi bache, ya pichhli iteration se change kisi threshold se kam hai.
  3. Agar khatam nahi hua, toh scheduler step 1 par wapas jaata hai aur ek aur round chalata hai.

Yeh approach kaam karta hai, lekin ise MapReduce se implement karna aksar bahut inefficient hota hai. MapReduce ko pata hi nahi ki algorithm iterative hai. Woh hamesha poora input dataset read karta hai aur bilkul naya output dataset banata hai, chahe pichhli iteration ke baad graph ka sirf ek chhota hissa hi badla ho.

Pregel processing model

Graphs ki batch processing ke optimization ke taur par bulk synchronous parallel (BSP) model of computation popular ho gaya hai. Ise Apache Giraph, Spark ke GraphX API aur Flink ke Gelly API ne implement kiya hai. Ise Pregel model bhi kehte hain, kyunki Google ke Pregel paper ne graph processing ke liye is approach ko popular banaya.

Yaad karein ki MapReduce mein mappers conceptually reducer ki kisi particular call ko message bhejte hain, kyunki framework same key wale saare mapper outputs ko ek saath collect kar deta hai. Pregel bhi isi tarah ke idea par chalta hai. Ek vertex doosre vertex ko message bhej sakta hai, aur aam taur par messages graph ke edges ke saath-saath travel karte hain. Har iteration mein har vertex ke liye ek function call hota hai, aur use us vertex ko bheje gaye saare messages diye jaate hain, bilkul reducer ki call ki tarah. Fark yeh hai ki Pregel model mein vertex apni state ek iteration se doosri tak memory mein yaad rakhta hai. Isliye function ko sirf naye incoming messages process karne padte hain. Agar graph ke kisi hisse mein koi message nahi bheja ja raha, toh wahan koi kaam karne ki zaroorat nahi.

Agar tum har vertex ko ek actor maano, toh yeh model kuch-kuch actor model jaisa hai, jo distributed actor frameworks book mein pehle discuss hue the. Lekin kuch differences hain. Vertex state aur vertices ke beech ke messages fault-tolerant aur durable hote hain. Communication fixed rounds mein hota hai. Har iteration mein framework pichhli iteration mein bheje gaye saare messages deliver karta hai. Actors mein aam taur par aisi timing guarantee nahi hoti.

Pregel mein fault tolerance

Vertices sirf messages pass karke communicate kar sakte hain, ek-doosre ko seedha query karke nahi. Isse performance ko help milti hai, kyunki messages ko batch kiya ja sakta hai aur communication ka wait kam hota hai. Wait sirf iterations ke beech hota hai. Pregel guarantee deta hai ki ek iteration mein bheje gaye saare messages agli iteration mein deliver honge, isliye pichhli iteration poori tarah khatam honi chahiye, aur uske saare messages network par copy ho jaane chahiye, tabhi agli iteration start ho sakti hai.

Underlying network messages ko drop, duplicate ya arbitrarily delay kar sakta hai, jaisa Chapter 8 ke unreliable networks section mein discuss hua tha. Phir bhi Pregel implementations guarantee dete hain ki agli iteration mein messages apne destination vertex par exactly once process honge. MapReduce ki tarah, framework faults se transparently recover karta hai, jisse Pregel par bane algorithms ka programming model simple ho jaata hai.

Yeh fault tolerance checkpointing se aati hai. Iteration ke end mein saare vertices ki state periodically durable storage mein likhi jaati hai. Agar koi node fail ho jaye aur uski in-memory state kho jaye, toh sabse simple solution hai poori graph computation ko last checkpoint par rollback karke wahin se restart karna. Agar algorithm deterministic hai aur messages log hote hain, toh sirf khoye hue partition ko recover karna bhi possible hai, jaisa dataflow engines ke liye discuss hua tha.

Parallel execution

Vertex ko yeh jaanne ki zaroorat nahi ki woh kaun si physical machine par chal raha hai. Jab woh doosre vertices ko messages bhejta hai, toh woh bas ek vertex ID ko bhej deta hai. Framework tay karta hai ki kaun sa vertex kaun si machine par chalega, aur messages ko network par kaise route karna hai taaki woh sahi jagah pahunchein.

Programming model ek time par ek vertex ko deal karta hai, ise kabhi vertex ki tarah sochna kaha jaata hai, isliye framework graph ko arbitrary tarike se partition kar sakta hai. Ideal toh yeh hai ki jo vertices zyada communicate karte hain unhe ek hi machine par colocate kiya jaye. Lekin aisa optimized partitioning dhoondhna mushkil hai. Practice mein graph ko aksar bas arbitrarily assign kiye gaye vertex ID se partition kar dete hain, related vertices ko ek saath group karne ki koshish kiye bina.

Isliye graph algorithms mein aksar cross-machine communication ka overhead kaafi hota hai. Intermediate state, yani nodes ke beech bheje gaye messages, aksar original graph se bhi bada hota hai. Network par messages bhejne ka overhead distributed graph algorithms ko kaafi slow kar sakta hai.

Isliye, agar tumhara graph ek computer ki memory mein fit ho jaata hai, toh single-machine algorithm (shayad single-threaded bhi) distributed batch process se kaafi behtar chalega. Graph memory se bada ho lekin ek computer ki disks mein fit ho jaye, tab bhi GraphChi jaise framework se single-machine processing ek achha option hai. Agar graph ek machine ke liye bahut bada hai, toh Pregel jaisa distributed approach avoid nahi kiya ja sakta. Graph algorithms ko efficiently parallelize karna abhi bhi ongoing research ka area hai.

High-Level APIs aur Languages

MapReduce ke popular hone ke baad ke saalon mein distributed batch processing ke execution engines mature ho gaye hain. Infrastructure ab itna robust hai ki 10,000 se zyada machines ke clusters par kai petabytes data store aur process kar sakta hai. Itne bade scale par batch processes ko physically operate karna ab lagbhag solved maana jaata hai. Ab dhyaan doosri cheezon par gaya hai: programming model behtar banana, processing ki efficiency badhana, aur jin problems ko yeh technologies solve kar sakti hain unka daayra badhana.

Jaisa pehle discuss hua, Hive, Pig, Cascading aur Crunch jaisi higher-level languages aur APIs isliye popular hui kyunki MapReduce jobs haath se program karna thakaane wala kaam hai. Tez aane par in languages ko ek extra fayda mila: job code dobara likhe bina naye dataflow engine par chalna. Spark aur Flink ke apne high-level dataflow APIs bhi hain, jo aksar FlumeJava se inspired hain.

Yeh dataflow APIs aam taur par computation express karne ke liye relational-style building blocks use karte hain. Tum field ki value par datasets join kar sakte ho, tuples ko key se group kar sakte ho, kisi condition se filter kar sakte ho, aur counting, summing ya doosre functions se tuples aggregate kar sakte ho. Andar se yeh operations wahi join aur grouping algorithms karte hain jinke baare mein is chapter mein bataya gaya.

Kam code ke alawa, high-level interfaces interactive use bhi allow karte hain. Tum shell mein analysis code thoda-thoda karke likh sakte ho aur use baar-baar chalakar dekh sakte ho ki woh kya kar raha hai. Dataset explore karte waqt aur use process karne ke alag-alag tarike try karte waqt development ka yeh style bahut kaam aata hai. Yeh Unix philosophy jaisa bhi hai. Yeh interfaces system use karne wale logon ko zyada productive banate hain, aur machine level par job execution ki efficiency bhi badhate hain.

Declarative query languages ki taraf badhna

Joins ko relational operators ki tarah specify karna, join karne wala code khud likhne ke bajaye, ek fayda deta hai. Framework join inputs ki properties analyze karke automatically decide kar sakta hai ki task ke liye kaun sa join algorithm sahi hai. Hive, Spark aur Flink ke paas cost-based query optimizers hain jo yeh karte hain. Woh joins ka order bhi badal sakte hain, taaki intermediate state ki matra kam se kam rahe.

Join algorithm ka choice batch job ki performance mein bada fark la sakta hai, aur yeh convenient hai ki is chapter ke saare join algorithms samajhna aur yaad rakhna na pade. Yeh tab chalta hai jab joins declarative tarike se declare kiye jaate hain. Application batati hai ki use kaun se joins chahiye, aur query optimizer tay karta hai ki unhe sabse achhe se kaise execute karein. Chapter 2 mein data ke query languages ki baat karte waqt yeh idea introduce hua tha.

Kuch doosre tarikon se MapReduce aur uske dataflow successors SQL ke fully declarative model se alag hain. MapReduce callback functions ke around bana tha. Har record ya records ke group ke liye ek user-defined function, yani mapper ya reducer, call hota hai, aur woh kuch bhi arbitrary code chalane ke liye free hai ki kya output karna hai. Iska fayda yeh hai ki tum parsing, natural language analysis, image analysis aur numerical ya statistical algorithms ke liye existing libraries ke bade ecosystem ka use kar sakte ho.

Arbitrary code chalane ki yahi freedom MapReduce heritage wale batch systems ko MPP databases se lambe samay se alag karti aayi hai. Databases mein user-defined functions ki facilities hoti hain, lekin unhe use karna aksar jhanjhat ka hota hai, aur woh un package managers aur dependency systems ke saath achhe se integrated nahi hote jo zyadatar programming languages use karti hain, jaise Java ke liye Maven, JavaScript ke liye npm aur Ruby ke liye RubyGems.

Dataflow engines ko joins ke alawa doosre areas mein bhi declarative features jodne se fayde mile hain. Agar callback function mein bas ek simple filtering condition ho, ya woh record se sirf kuch fields select kare, toh har record par function call karne ki ek real CPU cost hoti hai. Agar aisi simple filtering aur mapping declarative tarike se declare ho, toh query optimizer column-oriented storage layouts ka fayda utha sakta hai aur disk se sirf zaroori columns read kar sakta hai. Hive, Spark DataFrames aur Impala vectorized execution bhi use karte hain. Matlab data par ek tight inner loop mein iterate karna, jo CPU caches ke liye friendly ho aur function calls se bachaye. Spark iske liye JVM bytecode generate karta hai, aur Impala un inner loops ke liye LLVM se native code generate karta hai.

Apne high-level APIs mein declarative aspects jodkar, aur aise query optimizers rakhkar jo unhe use kar sakein, batch processing frameworks MPP databases jaise dikhne lagte hain, aur comparable performance tak pahunch sakte hain. Kyunki woh abhi bhi arbitrary code chala sakte hain aur arbitrary formats mein data read kar sakte hain, unka flexibility wala advantage bana rehta hai.

Alag-alag domains ke liye specialization

Arbitrary code chalane ki ability kaam ki hai, lekin kai common processing patterns baar-baar aate hain. Isliye common building blocks ki reusable implementations rakhna worth it hai. MPP databases traditionally business intelligence analysts aur business reporting ke kaam aate rahe hain. Lekin batch processing jin kai domains mein use hoti hai, yeh unme se bas ek hai.

Statistical aur numerical algorithms tezi se zaroori hote ja rahe hain, kyunki classification aur recommendation systems jaisi machine learning applications ko inki zaroorat hoti hai. Reusable implementations ab aa rahi hain. Jaise, Mahout MapReduce, Spark aur Flink ke upar machine learning algorithms implement karta hai. MADlib similar functionality ek relational MPP database, Apache HAWQ, ke andar implement karta hai.

Spatial algorithms bhi kaam ke hain. Book k-nearest neighbors ko example ke taur par deti hai. Yeh kisi multi-dimensional space mein ek diye gaye item ke paas wale items dhoondhta hai, jo ek tarah ki similarity search hai. Genome analysis mein bhi approximate search matter karti hai, jahan algorithms ko aise strings dhoondhne padte hain jo similar hon lekin bilkul identical nahi.

Jaise-jaise batch engines mein built-in functions aur declarative operators aa rahe hain, aur MPP databases zyada programmable aur flexible ho rahe hain, dono ek-doosre jaise dikhne lage hain. Aakhir mein, yeh sab data store aur process karne ke systems hi hain.

Summary

Short mein
  • Unix ke lessons. Chapter awk, grep, sort aur uniq se shuru hua tha. Inke design ideas MapReduce aur naye dataflow engines tak chalte hain. Inputs immutable hote hain, outputs kisi baad ke program ka input banne ke liye hote hain, aur complex problems ko chhote tools compose karke solve kiya jaata hai jo har ek ek hi kaam achhe se karta hai.
  • Interface. Unix duniya mein uniform interface, jo ek program ko doosre ke saath compose hone deta hai, files aur pipes hain. MapReduce mein yeh distributed filesystem hai. Dataflow engines pipe-jaisa transport jodte hain, taaki intermediate state ko filesystem mein likhna na pade. Job ka initial input aur final output aam taur par ab bhi HDFS hi hota hai.
  • Partitioning. MapReduce mein mappers input file block ke hisaab se partitioned hote hain. Unka output repartition, sort aur merge hokar reducer partitions ki ek configurable count mein jaata hai, taaki related data (same key wale saare records) ek hi jagah pahunche. Dataflow engines jab tak zaroorat na ho sorting avoid karte hain, lekin partitioning ka approach unka mota-mota similar hi hai.
  • Fault tolerance. MapReduce disk par bahut baar likhta hai. Isse ek failed task ko job restart kiye bina recover karna aasaan ho jaata hai, lekin jab kuch fail nahi hota tab execution slow hota hai. Dataflow engines kam materialize karte hain aur zyada memory mein rakhte hain, isliye node fail hone par unhe zyada recompute karna padta hai. Deterministic operators recompute hone wale data ki matra kam karte hain.
  • Join algorithms. Sort-merge joins mein har input ek mapper se guzarta hai jo join key nikalta hai, phir partition, sort aur merge hota hai taaki same key wale saare records ek hi reducer call tak pahunchein. Broadcast hash joins ek chhote input ko har mapper ke hash table mein load karte hain. Partitioned hash joins hash table approach ko do inputs ke har matching partition par apply karte hain. Inme se zyadatar MPP databases aur dataflow engines ke andar bhi use hote hain.
  • Ek restricted model. Batch callback functions se maana jaata hai ki woh stateless hon aur apne designated output ke alawa unka koi externally visible side effect na ho. Isse framework tasks ko safely retry kar sakta hai aur failed tasks ka output discard kar sakta hai. Framework guarantee de sakta hai ki final output wahi hoga jaise koi fault aaya hi nahi. Yeh guarantees un online services se kaafi strong hain jo request handle karte waqt side effect ke taur par databases mein likhti hain.
  • Bounded input. Batch job input read karta hai aur input ko modify kiye bina output produce karta hai. Input bounded hota hai, matlab uska size known aur fixed hota hai, jaise kisi ek point of time par log files ka set ya database ka snapshot. Isliye job ko pata hota hai ki woh kab khatam hua aur aakhir mein complete ho jaata hai. Chapter 11 stream processing par jaata hai, jahan input unbounded hota hai, isliye job kabhi complete nahi hota.

Chapter ke end mein 81 sources ki ek numbered References list hai, jisme MapReduce paper, Hadoop aur Spark ki books, aur Pregel paper shamil hain. Yeh retelling us list ko reproduce nahi karti.

Khud check karein

  1. Ruby program aur Unix pipeline dono same top five pages dete hain. Sort-based pipeline kab behtar choice hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Jab working set memory se bada ho, jaise ek aisi site jisme bahut saare distinct URLs hain. Sort utility disk par spill karti hai, chunks sort karti hai, aur unhe sequential reads se merge karti hai, isliye woh wahan bhi chalti rehti hai jahan hash table ki memory khatam ho jaati.

  2. Reduce-side sort-merge join mein reducer ko ek time par memory mein sirf ek user record kyun rakhna padta hai, aur secondary sort kaise help karta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Reducer har user ID ke liye ek baar call hota hai, aur secondary sort ke saath user record sabse pehle aata hai. Reducer us ek date of birth ko ek variable mein rakh sakta hai aur user ke events ke upar stream karta rehta hai. Use memory mein koi aur record ya koi network request nahi chahiye.

  3. Batch job ke liye apne results ko production database mein ek-ek record karke likhna bura idea kyun hai, aur book iske bajaye kya suggest karti hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Har record ke liye ek slow network request lagti hai, kai parallel writers database ko overwhelm kar sakte hain, aur agar job fail ho jaye toh external system par hue side effects chhupaye nahi ja sakte. Book suggest karti hai ki job ke andar hi naye database files banayein, unhe output directory mein likhein, aur read-only servers mein bulk mein load karein.

  4. Dataflow engine khoyi hui machine se recover karne ke liye HDFS copy padhne ke bajaye uska data recompute karta hai. Operators ka deterministic hona kyun zaroori hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Agar recompute kiya hua result us khoye hue result se alag ho jo downstream pehle hi bheja ja chuka hai, toh downstream operators ke saamne contradictory data aa jaata hai. Operators ko deterministic banane se yeh nahi hota, aur sirf khoya hua data hi recompute karna padta hai.

Part III · Chapter 11

Stream Processing

Seedhi baat: stream woh data hai jo kabhi aana band nahi hota. Jab tum changes ko events ke log ki tarah dekhte ho, toh database, cache aur search index, teeno ek hi log se current rakhe ja sakte ho. Aur jo process hamesha chalta rehta hai, usse time, joins aur recovery ke liye apne alag tools chahiye.

Chapter ki shuruaat John Gall ki book Systemantics ki ek line se hoti hai: jo complex system kaam karta hai, woh hamesha kisi simple system se grow hua hota hai jo kaam karta tha, aur jo complex system scratch se design kiya jaata hai woh kabhi kaam nahi karta. Yeh yaad rakhein, kyunki chapter kaafi complicated ideas ko ek-ek step karke build karta hai.

Chapter 10 mein batch processing thi. Batch job input files ka ek set padhta hai aur output files ka naya set likhta hai. Iska output derived data hota hai, matlab job dobara chalakar usse kabhi bhi dobara bana sakte hain. Batch processing search indexes, recommendation systems aur analytics banane ke liye use hoti thi.

Lekin Chapter 10 ne ek badi assumption li thi. Usne maana tha ki input bounded hai, yani uska size known aur finite hai. Isliye batch job ko pata hota hai ki usne sab kuch padh liya hai aur woh finish kar sakta hai. Yeh baat dikhne se zyada important hai. Sorting ko lo, jo MapReduce ke center mein hai. Sort ko output likhne se pehle poora input padhna padta hai, kyunki aakhri record ki key sabse chhoti ho sakti hai, aur tab usse sabse pehle aana hoga. Tum jaldi likhna shuru nahi kar sakte.

Real mein bahut sa data unbounded hota hai. Woh dheere-dheere aata rehta hai. Tumhare users ne kal bhi data banaya, aaj bhi banaya, aur kal bhi banayenge. Jab tak business band nahi hota, dataset kisi meaningful tarike se kabhi complete nahi hota. Isliye batch systems ko is endless flow ko fixed length ke chunks mein kaatna padta hai, jaise har din ke end par ek din ka data, ya har ghante ke end par ek ghante ka data.

Problem yeh hai ki daily batch run ka matlab hai ki input mein change output mein ek din baad hi dikhta hai. Impatient users ke liye yeh bahut slow hai. Tum chunks chhote kar sakte ho, jaise har second ke end par us second ka data process karna. Ya phir chunks hata hi dein aur har event ko hote hi process kar lein. Yeh doosra option hi stream processing ka idea hai.

Aam taur par stream woh data hai jo time ke saath thoda-thoda karke available hota hai. Yeh idea kaafi jagah dikhta hai: Unix programs ka standard input aur output, kuch programming languages ki lazy lists, Java ke FileInputStream jaise file APIs, TCP connections, aur internet par audio aur video ki delivery.

Chapter event streams ko data manage karne ka ek tarika maanta hai. Event stream pichhle chapter ke batch data ka unbounded, step-by-step version hai. Isme teen cheezein aati hain. Pehla, streams ko kaise represent, store aur network par send karte hain. Doosra, streams ka databases se kya relation hai. Teesra, streams ko continually kaise process karein aur isse kaunsi applications ban sakti hain.

Event streams ko transmit karna

Batch world mein job ke inputs aur outputs files hoti hain, shayad kisi distributed filesystem par. Streaming mein iska equivalent kya hai?

Jab input file hoti hai, toh pehla step aam taur par usse records ki sequence mein parse karna hota hai. Streaming mein record ko zyada tar event kehte hain. Cheez wahi hai: ek chhota, self-contained, unchangeable object jisme kisi point in time par jo hua uski details hoti hain. Event mein aam taur par ek timestamp hota hai, jo time-of-day clock se liya jaata hai aur batata hai ki event kab hua.

Jo hua woh user ka koi action ho sakta hai, jaise page dekhna ya purchase karna. Woh kisi machine se bhi aa sakta hai, jaise sensor ki temperature reading ya CPU usage ka measurement. Batch chapter ki web server log lines bhi events hi thi.

Event ko text, JSON ya compact binary form mein encode kar sakte hain, jaisa Chapter 4 mein discuss hua tha. Is encoding se tum event ko store kar sakte ho, jaise usse file mein append karke, relational table mein insert karke, ya document database mein likhkar. Isse tum event ko network par doosri machine ko process hone ke liye bhi bhej sakte ho.

Batch processing mein file ek baar likhi jaati hai aur phir kai jobs usse padh sakte hain. Streaming mein yahi pattern naye words mein bolte hain. Event ek producer ek baar produce karta hai, jise publisher ya sender bhi kehte hain. Phir usse kai consumers process kar sakte hain, jinhe subscribers ya recipients bhi kehte hain. Filesystem mein file ka naam related records ko group karta hai. Streaming system mein related events ko ek topic ya stream mein group karte hain.

Principle mein producers aur consumers ko jodne ke liye ek file ya database kaafi hai. Producer har event ko datastore mein likh deta hai. Har consumer time-time par datastore ko poll karta hai ki pichhli baar dekhne ke baad koi naya event aaya ya nahi. Batch job jab din mein ek baar chalta hai, toh bilkul yahi karta hai.

Jab tumhe low delay ke saath continual processing chahiye, toh polling mehengi ho jaati hai, agar datastore us ke liye design nahi hua. Jitni zyada baar poll karein, utne kam requests mein kuch naya milta hai, aur overhead badhta hai. Behtar yeh hai ki naye events aane par consumers ko notify kiya jaaye. Relational databases mein triggers hote hain, jo naye row jaise change par react kar sakte hain, lekin book ke hisaab se woh bahut limited hain aur kaafi samay se kuch-kuch afterthought rahe hain. Isliye event notifications deliver karne ke liye specialized tools banaye gaye.

Messaging systems

Consumers ko notify karne ka ek common tarika messaging system hai. Producer ek message bhejta hai, jisme event hota hai, aur system woh message consumers ko push kar deta hai. Chapter ne Chapter 4 mein message-passing dataflow wale section mein iska zikr pehle hi kiya tha, aur yahan woh isse detail mein dekhta hai.

Sabse simple messaging system ek direct channel hai, jaise Unix pipe ya producer aur consumer ke beech TCP connection. Lekin pipes aur TCP bas ek sender ko ek recipient se jodte hain. Messaging system isse aage jaata hai. Woh kai producers ko ek hi topic par messages bhejne deta hai, aur kai consumers ko us topic ke messages receive karne deta hai.

Is publish and subscribe model ke andar systems kaafi alag-alag approaches lete hain, aur koi bhi har purpose ke liye sahi nahi hai. Kleppmann do sawal batate hain jinse systems ko alag pehchaana ja sakta hai.

  1. Agar producers messages itni tezi se bhejein ki consumers handle na kar paayein, toh kya hota hai? Teen basic options hain. System messages ko drop kar sakta hai. Unhe queue mein buffer kar sakta hai. Ya backpressure laga sakta hai, jise flow control bhi kehte hain, yani consumer ke catch up karne tak producer ko aur bhejne se block kar dena. Unix pipes aur TCP backpressure use karte hain. Unka buffer chhota aur fixed size ka hota hai, aur jab woh bhar jaata hai toh sender block ho jaata hai jab tak receiver data bahar na nikaal le. Agar system messages ko queue mein buffer karta hai, toh tumhe pata hona chahiye ki queue jab memory mein fit nahi hoti tab kya hota hai. System crash ho jaata hai, ya messages disk par likh deta hai? Aur woh disk access performance par kaisa asar daalta hai?

  2. Agar nodes crash ho jaayein ya offline chale jaayein, toh kya hota hai? Kya koi message lost hota hai? Durability, yani accept kiya hua data rakhne ka promise, aam taur par disk par likhne, doosri machines par replicate karne, ya dono se aati hai. In sab ki ek cost hoti hai. Agar tum kuch messages lose karna afford kar sakte ho, toh usi hardware se aksar higher throughput aur lower latency mil sakti hai.

Messages lose hona acceptable hai ya nahi, yeh application par depend karta hai. Sensor readings aur metrics lo jo regularly bheje jaate hain. Ek data point missing ho toh aam taur par koi harm nahi, kyunki jaldi hi naya value aa jaata hai. Lekin agar bahut sare messages drop ho jaayein, toh metrics kisi ke dhyaan mein aaye bina galat ho sakte hain. Agar tum events count kar rahe ho, toh baat alag hai. Har lost message ka matlab galat counter, isliye reliable delivery bahut zaroori hai.

Chapter 10 ke batch systems mein yahan ek kaam ki property thi. Woh strong reliability guarantee dete hain. Failed tasks automatically retry hote hain, aur failed task ka partial output phenk diya jaata hai. Isliye output aisa dikhta hai jaise koi failure hua hi nahi, aur programming model simple rehta hai. Is chapter mein aage Kleppmann dekhte hain ki streaming setting mein aisi hi guarantees kaise milein.

Producers se consumers ko direct messaging

Kuch messaging systems beech mein kisi middleman ke bina producers aur consumers ke beech seedha messages bhejte hain. Book kuch examples gaati hai.

  • UDP multicast finance mein stock market prices jaise feeds ke liye kaafi use hota hai, jahan low latency sabse zaroori hai. UDP khud unreliable hai, isliye application protocol ko lost packets recover karne padte hain. Producer ko bheje hue packets yaad rakhne padte hain taaki request par dobara bhej sake.
  • Brokerless libraries jaise ZeroMQ aur nanomsg bhi kuch aisa hi approach lete hain. Woh central server ke bina TCP ya IP multicast par publish and subscribe implement karte hain.
  • StatsD aur Brubeck network ki har machine se metrics unreliable UDP messages se collect karte hain. StatsD protocol mein counters tabhi sahi hote hain jab har message pahunche. UDP messages lose kar sakta hai, isliye counts zyada se zyada approximate hote hain.
  • Webhooks ek pattern hai jisme ek service doosri service ke paas ek callback URL register karti hai. Jab bhi koi event hota hai, doosri service us URL par request karti hai. Yeh producer se consumer ko direct push hai, aam taur par HTTP ya RPC par.

Yeh systems un situations mein achha kaam karte hain jinke liye bane the. Lekin aam taur par application code ko pata hona chahiye ki messages lost ho sakte hain. Woh sirf limited faults tolerate karte hain. Protocol network se lost packets detect karke dobara bhej bhi de, tab bhi yeh systems maante hain ki producers aur consumers hamesha online rehte hain. Agar consumer offline hai, toh jab woh unreachable tha tab bheje gaye messages use miss ho jaate hain. Kuch protocols producer ko failed deliveries retry karne dete hain, lekin agar producer crash ho jaaye aur retry hone wale messages ka buffer kho de, toh yeh kaam nahi karta.

Message brokers

Ek widely used alternative message broker hai, jise message queue bhi kehte hain. Broker essentially ek database hai jo message streams handle karne ke liye optimize kiya gaya hai. Woh server ki tarah chalta hai, aur producers aur consumers usse clients ki tarah connect hote hain. Producers broker ko messages likhte hain, aur consumers broker se padhte hain.

Data ek central jagah rakha jaata hai, isliye broker un clients ko aasaani se handle kar leta hai jo aate-jaate rehte hain, yani connect, disconnect aur crash hote hain. Durability broker ke paas chali jaati hai. Kuch brokers messages sirf memory mein rakhte hain. Baaki, configuration ke hisaab se, unhe disk par likhte hain taaki broker crash ke baad bhi bache rahein. Jab consumers slow hote hain, toh zyada tar brokers messages drop karne ya backpressure lagane ke bajaye queue ko unbounded badhne dete hain. Yeh choice bhi configuration par depend kar sakti hai.

Iska ek consequence hai. Consumers aam taur par asynchronous hote hain. Producer jab message bhejta hai, toh woh normally sirf broker ke confirm karne ka wait karta hai ki usne message store kar liya. Woh consumers ke process karne ka wait nahi karta. Consumer tak delivery baad mein kisi point par hoti hai. Aksar yeh second ke ek hisse mein ho jaata hai, lekin agar queue mein backlog ho toh kaafi zyada time lag sakta hai.

Message brokers aur databases ki tulna

Kuch message brokers XA ya JTA use karke two-phase commit protocols mein hissa le sakte hain, jo Chapter 9 mein covered transaction standards hain. Isse woh nature mein databases jaise ban jaate hain. Lekin Kleppmann chaar practical differences batate hain.

  • Data ki lifetime. Databases data tab tak rakhte hain jab tak koi explicitly delete na kare. Zyada tar brokers message successfully deliver hote hi usse automatically delete kar dete hain. Isliye woh long-term storage ke liye suitable nahi hain.
  • Working set ka size. Brokers messages jaldi delete karte hain, isliye woh maante hain ki unka working set chhota hai aur queues chhoti hain. Agar consumers slow hain aur broker ko bahut kuch buffer karna padta hai, shayad messages disk par spill karke, toh har message ko handle karne mein zyada time lagta hai aur overall throughput gir sakta hai.
  • Data select karne ke tarike. Databases aksar secondary indexes aur search ke kai tarike support karte hain. Brokers aksar consumer ko un topics par subscribe karne dete hain jo kisi pattern se match karte hain. Mechanisms alag hain, lekin dono mein client apne kaam ka data choose kar sakta hai.
  • Queries aur notifications. Database query ek moment ka result return karti hai. Agar baad mein koi doosra client data change kare, toh pehle client ko nahi bataya jaata ki uska result ab stale hai, jab tak woh dobara na pooche ya poll na kare. Brokers arbitrary queries support nahi karte, lekin naye messages aane par clients ko notify zaroor karte hain.

Message brokers ka yeh traditional view hai. Yeh JMS (Java Message Service) aur AMQP (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) jaise standards mein captured hai. Aur yeh RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, HornetQ, Qpid, TIBCO Enterprise Message Service, IBM MQ, Azure Service Bus aur Google Cloud Pub/Sub jaise software mein implement hai.

Multiple consumers

Jab kai consumers ek hi topic se padhte hain, toh do main patterns use hote hain. Book ka Figure 11-1 dono dikhata hai.

  • Load balancing. Har message consumers mein se kisi ek ko deliver hota hai, isliye consumers kaam share karte hain. Broker messages ko consumers ko kisi bhi tarike se assign kar sakta hai. Yeh pattern tab useful hai jab har message process karna mehenga ho, kyunki tum zyada consumers add karke zyada parallel process kar sakte ho. AMQP mein is effect ke liye kai clients ek hi queue se consume karte hain. JMS ise shared subscription kehta hai.
  • Fan-out. Har message saare consumers ko deliver hota hai. Kai independent consumers ek hi broadcast par tune in kar sakte hain bina ek-doosre par asar daale. Yeh kai batch jobs ke ek hi input file padhne ka streaming version hai. JMS ise topic subscriptions se deta hai, aur AMQP exchange bindings se.

Dono patterns ko combine kiya ja sakta hai. Maan lo consumers ke do groups ek hi topic par subscribe karte hain. Har group ko poora ka poora har message milta hai, lekin har group ke andar sirf ek node ko har message milta hai.

Acknowledgments aur redelivery

Consumers kabhi bhi crash ho sakte hain. Isliye ho sakta hai broker kisi consumer ko aisa message deliver kare jo woh kabhi finish na kare, ya crash hone se pehle sirf thoda hi process kare. Message lost na ho, iske liye brokers acknowledgments use karte hain, jinhe aam taur par acks kehte hain. Consumer ko explicitly broker ko batana padta hai ki usne message process kar liya. Tabhi broker message ko queue se hatata hai.

Agar broker ko ack milne se pehle consumer ka connection band ho jaaye ya timeout ho jaaye, toh broker maan leta hai ki message process nahi hua. Phir woh message doosre consumer ko dobara deliver karta hai. Kleppmann ek subtle case batate hain. Ho sakta hai message poora process ho chuka ho, lekin ack network par lost ho gaya. Is case ko handle karne ke liye atomic commit protocol chahiye, jo distributed transactions wala chapter cover karta hai.

Redelivery ka ordering par ek surprising side effect hota hai. Book ise aise samjhati hai.

Example

Producer 1 ek topic ko m3, m4 aur m5 messages isi order mein bhejta hai, aur us topic ke do consumers hain. Consumers normally messages ko usi order mein handle karte hain jisme woh bheje gaye.

  1. Consumer 2 ko m3 milta hai aur woh usse process karna shuru karta hai.
  2. Usi time consumer 1 m4 process kar raha hai.
  3. Consumer 2 m3 ko acknowledge karne se pehle crash ho jaata hai.
  4. Broker ko ack nahi dikha, toh woh m3 ko baad mein consumer 1 ko redeliver karta hai.
  5. Isliye consumer 1 messages ko m4, m3, m5 order mein handle karta hai.

Nateeja yeh hai ki m3 aur m4 ab us order mein process nahi hue jisme producer ne bheje the. Book ka Figure 11-2 is sequence ko draw karta hai.

Broker messages ko order mein rakhne ki koshish kare, jo JMS aur AMQP dono standards us se chahte hain, tab bhi load balancing aur redelivery milkar messages ko reorder kar hi dete hain. Isse bachne ka ek tarika hai har consumer ke liye alag queue use karna, taaki load balancing na ho. Jab messages poori tarah independent hon toh reordering se farak nahi padta. Lekin jab messages ke beech causal dependencies hon toh padta hai, jaisa chapter aage dikhata hai.

Partitioned logs

Network par packet bhejna, ya kisi network service ko request karna, aam taur par ek short-lived action hota hai jo koi lasting record nahi chhodta. Tum usse packet capture aur logging se record kar sakte ho, lekin aam taur par koi aisa sochta nahi. Jo message brokers messages disk par likhte bhi hain, woh bhi delivery ke baad unhe jaldi delete kar dete hain. Woh messaging ke transient view par bane hain.

Databases aur filesystems ka view ulta hai. Database ya file mein jo bhi likha jaata hai, woh tab tak recorded rehna expected hai jab tak koi deliberately delete na kare. Mindset ka yeh farak derived data banane par bada asar daalta hai.

Chapter 10 ke batch jobs ki ek key property yeh hai ki tum unhe baar-baar chala sakte ho, alag-alag processing steps try karke, aur input ko koi risk nahi, kyunki input read-only hai. AMQP- aur JMS-style messaging mein yeh sach nahi hai. Agar acknowledgment broker se message delete kar deta hai, toh message receive karna destructive hai. Tum wahi consumer dobara chalakar wahi result expect nahi kar sakte.

Messaging system mein naya consumer add karne ki bhi ek limit hai. Naye consumer ko normally sirf woh messages milte hain jo uske register hone ke baad bheje gaye. Purane messages pehle hi chale gaye hote hain. Iske ulta, file ya database ka naya client past mein kisi bhi time likha hua data padh sakta hai, jab tak application ne usse overwrite ya delete na kiya ho.

Toh sawal yeh banta hai: dono ko combine kyun na karein? Database ki durable storage aur messaging system ki low-latency notification, dono ek saath mil sakti hain. Yahi log-based message brokers ka idea hai.

Message storage ke liye logs ka use

Log disk par records ki append-only sequence hota hai. Pichhle chapters mein logs log-structured storage engines aur write-ahead logs (Chapter 3) mein, aur replication (Chapter 5) mein mile the. Wahi structure messages bhi carry kar sakta hai. Producer message ko log ke end mein append karke bhejta hai. Consumer log mein order se aage badhte hue messages padhta hai. Jab consumer end par pahunchta hai, toh woh notification ka wait karta hai ki ek aur message append hua. Unix tool tail -f, jo file ko watch karta hai aur naye lines add hote hi print karta hai, kaafi hadd tak aise hi kaam karta hai.

Ek disk ki capacity se aage jaane ke liye log ko partitioned kiya ja sakta hai, Chapter 6 ke partitioning idea se. Har partition ek alag log hota hai, aur alag partitions alag machines par reh sakte hain. Har partition ko doosron se independent padha aur likha ja sakta hai. Topic phir partitions ka ek group hota hai jo sab ek hi type ke messages carry karte hain. Figure 1 yeh idea dikhata hai.

Har partition ke andar broker har message ko ek number deta hai jo hamesha badhta rehta hai, jise offset kehte hain. Offset ek sequence number hai. Partition append-only hai, isliye uske messages ek single, fixed order mein hote hain. Alag partitions ke beech koi ordering guarantee nahi hai.

Apache Kafka, Amazon Kinesis Streams aur Twitter ka DistributedLog aise log-based message brokers hain jo isi tarah kaam karte hain. Google Cloud Pub/Sub bhi milte-julte lines par bana hai, lekin woh log interface ke bajaye JMS-style interface deta hai. Yeh brokers har message disk par likhte hain, phir bhi millions of messages per second ka throughput hasil karte hain. Woh partitions ko kai machines par failaakar yeh karte hain, aur messages ko doosri machines par replicate karke fault tolerance paate hain.

Logs aur traditional messaging ki tulna

Log-based approach mein fan-out aasaan ho jaata hai. Kai consumers log ko independently padh sakte hain, aur message padhne se woh delete nahi hota. Load balancing alag tarike se hoti hai. Individual messages baantne ke bajaye broker poore partitions consumer group ke nodes ko assign karta hai. Phir har consumer apne partitions ke saare messages padhta hai, aam taur par order mein aur single thread par.

Is coarse load balancing ke do downsides hain, jo Kleppmann batate hain.

  • Ek topic ka kaam jitne nodes share kar sakte hain, woh zyada se zyada us topic ke partitions ki count ke barabar hai. Ek partition ke messages hamesha ek hi node ko jaate hain.
  • Agar ek message process hone mein slow hai, toh woh usi partition ke apne peeche ke saare messages ko rok deta hai. Yeh wahi head-of-line blocking hai jo pehle Chapter 1 mein describe hui thi.

Book ek workaround batati hai. Do consumers ek partition share kar sakte hain agar dono poore messages padhein, lekin ek sirf even-numbered offsets handle kare aur doosra sirf odd wale. Ek aur option hai ek consumer ke andar thread pool. Lekin book har partition ki single-threaded processing prefer karti hai, kyunki thread pool se consumer offsets track karna mushkil ho jaata hai. Parallelism phir zyada partitions add karke badhaya jaata hai.

Kaunsa style behtar hai, yeh kaam par depend karta hai. Neeche ka table trade-off ka summary hai.

Trade-offs
StyleKahan achha haiCost
AMQP ya JMS-style brokerMehenge messages ko parallel mein ek-ek karke handle karna, jab order kam matter karta ho. Task queues ke liye achha.Redelivery ke baad messages reorder ho sakte hain. Acknowledge hote hi messages delete ho jaate hain, isliye unhe replay nahi kar sakte.
Log-based brokerFast messages ke saath high throughput jahan order matter karta hai. Kai independent readers. Purane messages replay karna.Consumer group ke andar parallelism partition count se capped hoti hai. Ek slow message apne partition ke baaki messages ko rok deta hai.

Consumer offsets

Partition ko order mein padhne se yeh dekhna aasaan ho jaata hai ki kya process ho chuka hai. Consumer ke current offset se chhote offset wale har message ko handle kiya ja chuka hai. Bade offset wale har message ko abhi dekha nahi gaya. Isliye broker ko har ek message ka acknowledgment track karne ki zaroorat nahi. Use bas time-time par har consumer ka offset record karna hota hai. Kam bookkeeping ka matlab batching aur pipelining ke liye zyada gunjaish, jo throughput mein help karti hai.

Kleppmann ke hisaab se yeh offset database replication ke log sequence number jaisa hi hai. Replication mein sequence number se follower disconnect hone ke baad apne leader se dobara connect hokar bina koi write skip kiye aage badh sakta hai. Yahan bhi wahi idea use hota hai. Broker leader database ka role nibhata hai, aur har consumer follower ka.

Agar koi consumer node fail ho jaaye, toh group ka koi doosra node failed consumer ke partitions ko le leta hai. Woh last recorded offset se padhna shuru karta hai. Failed consumer ne apne last recorded offset ke baad jo bhi messages process kiye the, woh doosri baar process honge. Is se kaise deal karein, yeh chapter aage batata hai.

Disk space ka use

Agar log sirf badhta hi rahe, toh akhir mein disk space khatam ho jayegi. Isliye log ko segments mein baant diya jaata hai. Time-time par purane segments delete ya archive storage mein move kar diye jaate hain. Space free karne ka ek zyada refined tarika chapter mein aage aata hai.

Slow consumers ke liye iska ek consequence hai. Agar koi consumer itna peeche reh jaaye ki uska offset ek deleted segment ko point kare, toh woh messages miss kar dega.
