  1. Do clients lagbhag ek hi waqt par same item par write karte hain, aur database aur search index un writes ko ulte order mein receive karte hain. Koi error nahi hua, phir bhi yeh dono systems hamesha ke liye alag kyun ho jaate hain?

    Jawab dekho

    Har system ne writes ko usi order mein apply kiya jis order mein usne receive kiye. Database mein us write ki value rehti hai jo usne aakhir mein dekha, aur search index mein bhi us write ki value rehti hai jo usne aakhir mein dekha, aur yeh dono alag hain. Writes ko order karne ke liye single leader ya version detection na ho, toh kisi ko conflict ka pata hi nahi chalta.

  2. Ek topic mein 4 partitions hain, aur ek consumer group mein 6 consumers hain. Ek saath kitne consumers kaam ke hain, aur kyun?

    Jawab dekho

    Sirf 4. Ek partition ke messages hamesha same consumer ko jaate hain, isliye group mein har partition ek hi consumer ko diya ja sakta hai. Baaki 2 consumers ke paas padhne ko kuch nahi hota. Zyada parallelism ke liye zyada partitions chahiye.

  3. Ek 5-minute tumbling window aur ek 5-minute sliding window, dono events dekhte hain. Events 10:03:39 aur 10:08:12 par aate hain. Yeh dono events same sliding window mein kyun hain lekin same tumbling window mein kyun nahi?

    Jawab dekho

    Events ke beech 4 minute 33 second ka gap hai, jo 5 minutes se kam hai, isliye sliding window dono ko cover kar sakti hai. Tumbling windows ki boundaries fixed hoti hain, aur 10:03:39 aur 10:08:12 alag-alag fixed 5-minute windows mein aate hain, isliye woh saath group nahi hote.

  4. Fail hui batch job ko bas shuru se restart kiya ja sakta hai, lekin saalon se chal rahi stream job ke saath shayad aisa na ho. Stream processors uski jagah kya use karte hain, aur output processor se bahar ja chuka ho toh yeh kyun matter karta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Woh microbatching, checkpoints, atomic commits aur idempotent writes jaise mechanisms use karte hain, jinse shuru se start kiye bina kisi recent known point se recover kiya ja sakta hai. Output agar kisi outside system ko already bhej diya gaya ho, jaise database ya email service, toh processor use discard nahi kar sakta. Tab restart us side effect ko repeat kar sakta hai, jab tak external write idempotent ya kisi aur tarah se coordinated na ho.

Part III · Chapter 12

Data systems ka future

Seedhi baat: koi ek tool har kaam achhe se nahi karta, isliye achhe systems kai tools ko combine karte hain. Data ek tool se doosre tool tak changes ke ordered log ki tarah flow karta hai, jisse har copy sahi rehti hai aur aasaani se dobara ban sakti hai. Author yeh bhi kehte hain ki jo log aise systems banate hain, unhe yeh sochna chahiye ki system un logon par kya asar daalta hai jinka data unke paas hai.

Ab tak book ne mostly yeh bataya ki cheezein abhi kaisi hain. Yeh last chapter aage dekhta hai aur poochta hai ki cheezein kaisi honi chahiye. Author kuch ideas rakhte hain, jinse unke hisaab se applications ka design aur build karna behtar ho sakta hai. Predictions toh opinion ki baat hoti hain, isliye jahan bhi woh apni raay de rahe hain, wahan first person mein likhte hain. Tum unse disagree kar sakte ho. Yeh ideas discussion ki shuruaat ke liye hain, aur un terms ko clear karne ke liye jinhe log aksar mix kar dete hain.

Chapter 1 mein book ka goal yeh tha ki aise applications banana explore karein jo reliable, scalable aur maintainable hon. Yeh chapter un sab themes ko ek jagah laata hai. Fault-tolerance algorithms reliability badhate hain, partitioning scalability badhati hai, aur evolution aur abstraction ke mechanisms maintainability badhate hain. Ab aim yeh hai ki aaj ke applications se behtar design banayein: robust, correct, badalne mein aasaan, aur aakhir mein logon ke liye achhe.

Chapter ki shuruaat St. Thomas Aquinas ke ek quote se hoti hai, jo ek ship ke captain ke baare mein hai. Captain ka final aim ship ko harbor mein safe rakhna nahi hota, kyunki ship sail karne ke liye hi bana hota hai. Book yeh quote epigraph ki tarah deti hai aur ise detail mein explain nahi karti. Ek reasonable matlab yeh ho sakta hai ki system ko is baat se judge karna chahiye ki woh kis kaam ke liye hai, is baat se nahi ki woh change se kitna bachta hai.

Data Integration

Book mein ek theme baar-baar aaya hai: har problem ke kai solutions hote hain, aur har ek ke apne pros, cons aur trade-offs hote hain. Chapter 3 mein log-structured storage, B-trees aur column-oriented storage ko compare kiya tha. Chapter 5 mein single-leader, multi-leader aur leaderless replication compare hue. Agar tumhari problem bas itni hai ki kuch data store karein aur baad mein wapas dhoondh lein, toh koi ek sahi jawab nahi hai. Har approach alag circumstances ke liye theek baithta hai.

Ek software ko aam taur par ek hi approach choose karni padti hai. Ek code path ko robust aur fast banana hi kaafi mushkil hai, aur ek hi program mein sab kuch karne ki koshish se lagbhag pakka hai ki woh har kaam kharab karega. Isliye sahi tool circumstances par depend karta hai. Jise general-purpose database kehte hain, woh bhi kisi ek particular use pattern ke liye design hota hai.

Isse do challenges aate hain. Pehla, yeh jaanna ki kaunsa product kin circumstances mein fit hota hai. Vendors yeh batane se hichkichate hain ki unka software kaunse workloads achhe se handle nahi karta, toh tumhe lines ke beech padhna padta hai, pichhle chapters ke trade-off wale sawaal use karke. Doosra challenge yeh hai ki complex applications ek hi data ko kai alag tarah se use karte hain. Koi ek program in sab uses ke liye fit nahi hota. Aam taur par ek application ke features dene ke liye kai software ko combine karna padta hai. Book ise data integration problem kehti hai.

Specialized tools ko data derive karke combine karna

Ek common example hai OLTP database ko full-text search index ke saath combine karna. OLTP ka matlab hai online transaction processing, yani bahut saare chhote reads aur writes ka workload, jo zyadatar application databases handle karte hain. Full-text index se users text mein koi bhi keyword search kar sakte hain. Kuch databases, jaise PostgreSQL, mein basic full-text feature hota hai jo simple applications ke liye kaafi hai. Zyada sophisticated search ke liye dedicated information retrieval tools chahiye. Lekin search indexes aam taur par system of record (yani woh authoritative jagah jahan data rakha jaata hai) ke roop mein achhe nahi hote. Isliye kai applications ko do tools chahiye: ek data ko reliably store karne ke liye, aur ek usse achhe se search karne ke liye.

Data ki har nayi representation ke saath integration problem badhti jaati hai. Database aur search index ke alawa, tumhe yeh bhi karna pad sakta hai:

  • analytics systems mein copies rakhna, jaise data warehouses ya batch aur stream processing systems;
  • caches maintain karna, ya original data se derived objects ke denormalized versions (aisi copies jo data ko repeat karke aisi shape mein rakhti hain jisse reads tez ho jaayein) banana;
  • data ko machine learning, classification, ranking ya recommendation systems se guzaarna;
  • data change hone par notifications bhejna.

Author ne engineers ko yeh kehte suna hai ki 99% logon ko kisi technology ke features ka sirf ek chhota subset chahiye. Unka maanna hai ki aisi baatein bolne waale ke experience ke baare mein zyada batati hain, technology ki asli usefulness ke baare mein kam. Jo cheez ek insaan ko obscure lagti hai, woh kisi doosre ki central requirement ho sakti hai. Integration ki zaroorat aam taur par tab dikhti hai jab tum zoom out karke poore organization ke dataflows dekhte ho.

Dataflows ke baare mein sochna. Jab ek hi data ko alag-alag access patterns serve karne ke liye kai storage systems mein rakhna padta hai, toh inputs aur outputs ke baare mein clear hona zaroori hai. Data sabse pehle kahan likha jaata hai? Kaunsi representations kin sources se derive hoti hain? Aur har change sahi format mein un sabhi jagahon tak kaise pahunchta hai jahan use pahunchna chahiye?

Database aur search index wale example ko lo. Tum data pehle ek system-of-record database mein likh sakte ho, phir us database mein hue changes ko capture kar sakte ho. Isse change data capture, ya CDC, kehte hain, yani database ka change log padhkar har change aage bhej dena. Phir yeh changes search index par usi order mein apply hote hain. Agar index sirf CDC se hi update hota hai, toh index poori tarah database se derived hai, aur isliye woh database ke saath consistent rehta hai, bas software mein koi bug na ho. Tab database mein likhna hi system mein naya input aane ka ekmaatra tarika hota hai.

Doosra tarika yeh hai ki application seedha database aur search index, dono mein likhe. Isse wahi problem aati hai jo book ne Figure 11-4 mein dikhayi hai, aur jiska description agle paragraph mein hai.

Dual-writes problem. Maan lo do clients ek hi record par ek saath conflicting writes bhejte hain. Application database mein aur search index mein, ek ke baad ek, likhta hai. Dono systems writes ko alag order mein process kar sakte hain. Ho sakta hai database client 1 ka write pehle aur client 2 ka baad mein apply kare, jabki search index unhe ulte order mein apply kare. Order tay karne ki zimmedari kisi ek system ki nahi hai, isliye woh contradictory faisle le sakte hain aur hamesha ke liye ek doosre se inconsistent rah sakte hain.

Try karo

Do clients ek aisi app ke through conflicting values likhte hain jo database aur search index ko seedha update karti hai. Ek aisa design change batayein jisse ek hi system writes ka order decide kare. Phir batayein ki iske badle tum kya khote ho, extra delay aur naye bottleneck ke baare mein sochkar.

Ek total order decide karna. Agar har user input ek hi system se guzre jo saare writes ka ek order tay kare, toh problem khatam ho jaati hai. Baaki representations phir writes ko usi order mein process karke derive ho sakti hain. Yeh Chapter 9 ka state machine replication approach hai, jisme har copy wahi operations wahi sequence mein apply karti hai. Author ke hisaab se yeh itna zaroori nahi ki tum CDC use karo ya event sourcing log (aisa log jo har change ko permanent history ki tarah record karta hai), zaroori yeh hai ki tum total order decide karo. Event log se derived system ko update karna deterministic aur idempotent bhi banaya ja sakta hai. Deterministic ka matlab hai ki same input hamesha same output deta hai, aur idempotent ka matlab hai ki ek step do baar chalane ka wahi effect hota hai jo ek baar chalane ka. Dono properties faults se recovery ko kaafi aasaan bana deti hain.

Derived data versus distributed transactions. Kai data systems ko consistent rakhne ka classic tarika distributed transaction hai, yani ek transaction jo ek se zyada systems par phaili ho aur ek unit ki tarah succeed ya fail ho. Toh derived data use karna isse kaise compare hota hai?

Abstract level par dono ka goal ek hi hai, bas tarike alag hain. Distributed transactions writes ka order locks se decide karte hain, jo do transactions ko ek hi data ek saath chhune se rokte hain. Logs order tay karte hain events ko sequence mein record karke. Distributed transactions atomic commit use karte hain, ek protocol jo change ko ya toh har jagah effect mein laata hai ya kahin nahi, taaki har change exactly once apply ho. Log-based systems iski jagah deterministic retries aur idempotence par rely karte hain, jisse dohraya gaya step koi extra nuksaan nahi karta.

Sabse bada fark timing ka hai. Transaction systems aam taur par linearizability dete hain, ek strong guarantee ki jaise hi write complete hota hai, har agla read use dekhta hai. Isse kaam ki properties milti hain, jaise apne hi writes padhna: tum kuch save karo toh tumhara agla read use dikhata hai. Derived data systems aam taur par asynchronously update hote hain, matlab update thodi der baad hota hai aur bhejne waala wait nahi karta. Isliye woh by default wahi timing guarantees nahi dete.

Distributed transactions limited environments mein kaamyaabi se use hue hain, jo unki cost accept karte hain. Lekin author ka maanna hai ki XA, jo alag-alag products ke beech distributed transactions ka ek standard hai, ki fault tolerance aur performance kharab hai, jisse uski usefulness bahut limited ho jaati hai. Shayad koi behtar protocol possible ho, par use widely adopt karwana aur existing tools mein build karwana mushkil hoga aur jaldi hone ki ummeed nahi hai. Tab tak, unke hisaab se log-based derived data systems ko integrate karne ka sabse promising tarika hai. Unhe nahi lagta ki sabko yeh kehna madad karta hai ki eventual consistency (copies sirf kuch der baad agree karti hain) avoidable nahi hai aur bas ise jhelna padega, kam se kam achhi guidance ke bina toh nahi. Chapter is baat par wapas aata hai jab woh correctness ke aim ki baat karta hai, jahan woh asynchronous systems ke upar stronger guarantees banane ko dekhta hai.

Total ordering ki limits. Chhote systems ke liye ek totally ordered event log banana aasaan hai. Single-leader databases bilkul yahi karte hain, kyunki unka replication log writes ka total order hota hai. Jaise-jaise systems bade aur complex workloads tak badhte hain, limits saamne aati hain:

  • Total order ke liye aam taur par saare events ko ek leader node se guzarna padta hai jo order decide kare. Agar event rate ek machine ke handle karne se zyada ho, toh log ko machines par partitions mein baantna padta hai. Phir do partitions ke beech ka order undefined hota hai.
  • Jo servers kai datacenters mein phaile hote hain, jaise ek poora datacenter offline hone par bhi survive karne ke liye, unmein aam taur par har datacenter mein ek leader hota hai. Network delays ki wajah se har write ko datacenters ke beech coordinate karna bahut slow hota hai, isliye jo events do datacenters mein shuru hote hain unka koi defined order nahi hota.
  • Microservices mein aksar har service ki apni durable state hoti hai, aur services ke beech koi state share nahi hoti. Tab alag services ke events ka koi defined order nahi hota.
  • Kuch applications client-side state ko turant update karte hain, aur offline bhi kaam karte hain. Tab clients aur servers ko events alag orders mein dikhne ki possibility hoti hai.

Events ka total order decide karna total order broadcast kehlata hai, aur yeh consensus ke barabar hai, yani kai nodes ko ek value par agree karwane ki problem. Zyadatar consensus algorithms maante hain ki ek node events ki poori stream handle kar sakta hai, aur woh ordering ka kaam kai nodes mein share karne ka koi tarika nahi dete. Author ke hisaab se aise consensus algorithms design karna jo ek node ki throughput se aage scale karein aur poori duniya mein achhe se chalein, abhi bhi ek open research problem hai.

Causality capture karne ke liye events ko order karna. Jab do events ke beech koi causal link nahi hota, toh total order na hone se farak nahi padta, kyunki concurrent events ko kisi bhi tarah order kiya ja sakta hai. Kuch cases aasaan hain. Agar kai updates ek hi object ko chhute hain, toh us object ID ke saare updates ko ek hi log partition par route kar sakte hain, jisse woh order mein rehte hain. Causal dependencies kabhi zyada subtle tarike se bhi aa sakti hain, aur tab order matter karta hai.

Example

Unfriend aur message. Ek social network par do purane partners ka abhi breakup hua hai. Ek doosre ko friend list se hata deta hai, aur phir apne baaki friends ko ex-partner ke baare mein shikayat wali post karta hai. Post karne waale ka irada yeh hai ki ex-partner use na dekhe, kyunki post friendship khatam hone ke baad bheji gayi thi. Lekin maan lo friend status ek jagah store hai aur messages doosri jagah. Tab dono events ka order kho sakta hai. Naye messages ki notifications bhejne waali service message ko unfriend event se pehle process kar sakti hai. Phir woh galti se ex-partner ko notify kar degi.

Yahan notifications asal mein messages aur friend list ke beech ek join hain, isliye yeh joins ke saath timing problem hai, jaise book mein pehle discuss hui thi. Author kehte hain ki iska koi simple jawab nahi hai. Shuruaat ke liye yeh options hain:

  • Logical timestamps, jo coordination ke bina total order dete hain, isliye jahan total order broadcast feasible nahi hai wahan kaam aa sakte hain. Lekin tab recipients ko out-of-order aaye events handle karne padte hain, aur events ke saath extra metadata bhejna padta hai.
  • Ek aisa event log karna jo record kare ki user ne decision lene se pehle kaunsi state dekhi thi, aur us event ko ek unique ID dena. Baad ke events us ID ko refer karke dependency record kar sakte hain. Book is idea par reads being events wale section mein wapas aati hai.
  • Conflict resolution algorithms, jo tab madad karte hain jab events unexpected order mein aate hain. Woh state maintain karne mein madad karte hain, lekin tab nahi jab action ka koi external side effect ho, jaise notification bhejna.

Author ko ummeed hai ki aise patterns saamne aayenge jo causal dependencies ko efficiently capture karein aur derived state ko correct rakhein, bina har event ko total order broadcast ke bottleneck se guzaare.

Batch aur Stream Processing

Data integration ka goal batana aasaan hai: data sahi form mein, saari sahi jagahon par pahunche. Wahan tak pahunchne ke liye inputs consume karne, unhe transform karne, join karne, filter aur aggregate karne, models train karne, results evaluate karne aur outputs likhne padte hain. Batch aur stream processors is kaam ke tools hain. Unke outputs derived datasets hote hain, jaise search indexes, materialized views (precomputed query results jo data ki tarah store hote hain), users ke liye recommendations, aur aggregate metrics.

Chapters 10 aur 11 ne dikhaya ki batch aur stream processing kai principles share karte hain. Main fark yeh hai ki stream processors unbounded datasets par kaam karte hain, jo kabhi khatam nahi hote, jabki batch job ek known, finite size ka input padhta hai. Engines alag tarah se bane hote hain, aur yeh farq ab dhundhle hone lage hain. Spark batch engine ke upar stream processing karta hai, stream ko chhote batches mein kaatkar jinhe microbatches kehte hain. Apache Flink stream engine ke upar batch processing karta hai. Principle mein har style ko doosre se imitate kiya ja sakta hai, lekin performance alag hoti hai. Jaise microbatching hopping ya sliding windows ke saath, jo overlap karne waale time windows hain, kharab perform kar sakti hai.

Derived state maintain karna. Batch processing ka flavor kaafi functional hota hai, chahe code functional language mein na likha ho. Woh deterministic, pure functions ko favor karta hai. Pure function ka output sirf uske inputs par depend karta hai, aur uske explicit outputs ke alawa koi side effects nahi hote. Inputs ko immutable (kabhi change nahi hote) maana jaata hai, aur outputs append-only (sirf jode jaate hain) hote hain. Stream processing bhi wahi style follow karti hai, lekin managed, fault-tolerant state add karti hai, jise framework crashes ke baad bhi safe rakhta hai.

Pure functions fault tolerance ke liye achhe hain, kyunki unhe dobara chalana safe hota hai. Woh organization ke dataflows ko samajhna bhi aasaan banate hain. Derived data chahe search index ho, statistical model ho ya cache, data pipelines ke roop mein sochna madad karta hai jo ek cheez se doosri cheez derive karte hain. Ek system mein state change application functions se guzarta hai, aur uske effects derived systems par apply hote hain.

Principle mein derived systems ko synchronously bhi update kiya ja sakta hai, jaise relational database table write ke same transaction mein secondary index (column par ek extra lookup structure, jo main table se alag rakha jaata hai) update karta hai. Book ka kehna hai ki asynchrony hi log-based systems ko robust banati hai. Isse ek hisse ka fault wahin local rehta hai. Iske ulta, distributed transactions tab abort ho jaate hain jab koi ek participant fail ho, isliye woh failure ko baaki system mein phailane ki taraf jaate hain.

Secondary indexes wale partitioned systems mein ek related issue aata hai. Chapter 6 ne dikhaya tha ki secondary index aksar partition boundaries cross karta hai. Agar index term-partitioned hai, yani index indexed value ke hisaab se split hai, toh writes ko kai partitions mein jaana padta hai. Agar woh document-partitioned hai, yani har partition apne hi documents index karta hai, toh reads ko saare partitions mein jaana padta hai. Dono cases mein cross-partition communication sabse reliable aur scalable tab hoti hai jab index asynchronously maintain ho.

Application evolution ke liye data reprocess karna. Stream processing se input ke changes derived views mein kam delay ke saath dikh jaate hain. Batch processing se tum jama hui bahut saari history reprocess karke existing data se naye views derive kar sakte ho. Dono derived data maintain karne ke liye useful hain.

Reprocessing system ko evolve karne ka bhi achha tarika hai, taaki woh naye features aur requirements support kare. Iske bina schema evolution (stored data ka structure badalna) sirf simple changes tak limited rehta hai, jaise ek naya optional field ya naya record type add karna. Yeh tab bhi sach hai jab database schema ko write ke time check kare ya sirf read ke time. Reprocessing ke saath tum poore dataset ko ek bilkul alag model mein restructure kar sakte ho jo nayi requirements ke liye fit ho.

Example

Railways par schema migrations. Book batati hai ki bade migrations computing ke bahar bhi hote hain. Unnisvin sadi ke England mein railway building ke shuruaati dinon mein alag-alag track gauges the, yani do rails ke beech ki doori. Ek gauge ke liye bani train doosre gauge ke track par nahi chal sakti thi, jisse network ke jodne par limit lagti thi. 1846 mein ek single standard gauge tay hua, lekin phir baaki tracks ko convert karna pada. Ek line ko mahino ya saalon ke liye band karna koi option nahi tha.

Solution yeh tha ki track ko pehle dual ya mixed gauge mein convert karein, ek teesri rail jodkar. Phir dono gauges ki trains us line par chal sakti thi, teen mein se do rails use karke. Jab har train standard gauge mein convert ho gayi, toh nonstandard rail hata di gayi. Purane track ko is tarah reprocess karna, purane aur naye ko saath-saath rakhkar, change ko saalon mein dheere-dheere hone deta tha. Yeh ab bhi mehenga hai, isliye kuch nonstandard gauges bache hue hain. Jaise San Francisco Bay Area ka BART system US ke zyadatar hisse se alag gauge use karta hai.

Derived views se gradual evolution. Dataset ko restructure karne ke liye achanak switch ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Tum purana schema aur naya schema, dono ko ek hi underlying data ke do independently derived views ki tarah rakh sakte ho. Shuruaat mein kuch hi users ko naye view par route karein, uski performance test karne aur bugs dhoondhne ke liye, jabki zyadatar users purane par rahein. Phir naye view par users ka hissa badhayein, aur aakhir mein purana drop kar dein. Har stage ko reverse kiya ja sakta hai agar kuch galat ho jaaye, kyunki wapas jaane ke liye ek chalta hua system hamesha present rehta hai. Author kehte hain ki irreversible damage ka risk kam karne se teams ka confidence badhta hai, aur woh tezi se aage badh sakti hain.

Lambda architecture. Agar batch processing history reprocess karti hai aur stream processing recent updates handle karti hai, toh dono ko combine kaise karein? Lambda architecture ek proposal hai jisne kaafi attention paya. Iska core idea yeh hai ki incoming data ko ek badhte hue dataset mein immutable events append karke record kiya jaata hai, event sourcing jaisa. In events se read-optimized views derive hote hain. Lambda architecture do systems parallel chalata hai: ek batch system, jaise Hadoop MapReduce, aur ek alag stream system, jaise Storm.

Dono layers ek specific tarike se saath kaam karti hain. Stream processor events ko jaldi consume karke view ka approximate update banata hai. Baad mein batch processor wahi events consume karke derived view ka corrected version banata hai. Reasoning yeh hai ki batch processing simple hai aur usme bugs kam hote hain, jabki stream processors ko kam reliable aur fault-tolerant banana mushkil maana jaata tha. Stream side fast approximate algorithms bhi use kar sakti hai, jabki batch side slower exact algorithms.

Author kehte hain ki lambda architecture ne data systems ko behtar banaya, mainly is principle ko popular karke ki views ko immutable events ki streams se derive karein aur zaroorat padne par un events ko reprocess karein. Lekin unhe kai practical problems dikhti hain:

  • Wahi logic batch framework aur stream framework, dono mein chalana kaafi extra kaam hai. Summingbird jaisi libraries ek computation ko dono contexts mein chalne deti hain, lekin do systems ko debug, tune aur maintain karne ki operational complexity rehti hai.
  • Dono pipelines alag outputs banati hain, aur user requests ka jawab dene ke liye unhe merge karna padta hai. Tumbling window (ek fixed, non-overlapping time slice) par simple aggregation ke liye merge kaafi aasaan hai. Joins ke saath, sessionization (ek user ke events ko sessions mein group karna) ke saath, ya jab output time series na ho, tab yeh bahut mushkil ho jaata hai.
  • Bade datasets par poori history reprocess karna mehenga hai. Isliye batch side aksar incremental batches process karne ke liye set hoti hai, jaise har ghante ke end par ek ghante ka data. Isse woh timing problems aati hain jo book ke reasoning about time wale section mein discuss hui thi, jaise stragglers (der se aane waale events) aur woh windows jo batch boundaries cross karti hain. Batch job ko incremental banana use streaming layer jaisa bana deta hai, jo batch layer ko simple rakhne ke goal ke khilaaf jaata hai.

Batch aur stream processing ko unify karna. Naya kaam tumhe lambda architecture ke fayde uske nuksaan ke bina deta hai. Yeh batch computations, jo history reprocess karti hain, aur stream computations, jo events ko aate hi handle karti hain, dono ko ek hi system mein chalata hai. Author teen features batate hain jo isse possible banate hain, aur kehte hain ki woh ab widely available ho rahe hain:

  • Historical events ko usi engine se replay karne ki ability jo recent events handle karta hai. Log-based message brokers messages replay kar sakte hain, aur kuch stream processors distributed filesystem, jaise HDFS, se input padh sakte hain.
  • Stream processors ke liye exactly-once semantics. Iska matlab hai ki output waisa hi hota hai jaise koi fault hua hi nahi, chahe kuch faults hue hon. Batch processing ki tarah, iske liye failed tasks ka partial output discard karna padta hai.
  • Processing time ki jagah event time ke hisaab se windowing. Event time woh hai jab cheez asal mein hui. Processing time woh hai jab system ne use handle kiya. Purane events replay karte waqt processing time ka koi matlab nahi hota. Apache Beam aise computations ke liye ek API deta hai, jo Apache Flink ya Google Cloud Dataflow par chal sakta hai.

Databases ko unbundle karna

Sabse abstract level par databases, Hadoop aur operating systems ka basic kaam ek hi hai. Woh kuch data store karte hain, aur use process aur query karne dete hain. Database records ko kisi data model mein store karta hai, jaise tables ki rows, documents, ya graph ke vertices. Operating system ka filesystem data ko files mein store karta hai. Core mein dono information management systems hain. Chapter 10 ne kaha tha ki Hadoop ecosystem kuch had tak Unix ka distributed version hai. Real practical differences hain. Kai filesystems ek directory mein 10 million chhoti files ko achhe se handle nahi kar paate, jabki database mein 10 million chhote records hona aam baat hai. Phir bhi, dono ko compare karna useful hai.

Unix aur relational databases ne bahut alag philosophies apnayi. Unix ka aim programs ko hardware ka logical lekin kaafi low-level view dena tha. Relational databases ka aim application programmers ko high-level abstraction dena tha jo on-disk data structures, concurrency, crash recovery aur bahut kuch ki complexity chhupata hai. Unix ne pipes aur files diye jo bas bytes ki sequences hain. Databases ne SQL aur transactions diye.

Kaunsa behtar hai, yeh is par depend karta hai ki tumhe kya chahiye. Ek tarah se Unix simple hai, kyunki woh hardware ke upar ek patla wrapper hai. Doosri tarah se relational databases simple hain. Ek chhoti declarative query, jo batati hai ki tumhe kya result chahiye, yeh nahi ki use compute kaise karna hai, bahut saari machinery use kar sakti hai, jaise query optimization, indexes, join methods, concurrency control aur replication, aur query likhne waale ko details jaanne ki zaroorat nahi padti. Unix aur relational model dono 1970 ke shuruaati saalon mein aaye, aur unke beech ka tension dashakon se chala aa raha hai. Author NoSQL movement ko Unix style ki low-level abstractions ko distributed OLTP storage par laagu karne ki koshish ki tarah dekhte hain. Woh kehte hain ki woh dono philosophies mein reconcile karne ki koshish karenge, taaki dono ka best mil sake.

Data storage technologies ko compose karna

Poori book mein humne databases ke kai features dekhe. Secondary indexes hain, jo field ki value se records jaldi dhoondhne dete hain. Materialized views hain, jo query results ke precomputed caches hain. Replication logs hain, jo doosre nodes par data ki copies up to date rakhte hain. Aur full-text search indexes hain, jo kuch relational databases mein hote hain. Chapters 10 aur 11 ne milte-julte themes dikhaye: batch jobs mein full-text indexes banana, stream processing mein materialized views maintain karna, aur CDC se database ke changes ko derived systems tak replicate karna.

Toh databases mein bane features aur un derived systems ke beech parallels hain jo log batch aur stream processors se banate hain. Author unme se kai parallels ko saamne laate hain.

Index banana. Socho jab tum relational database par CREATE INDEX chalate ho toh kya hota hai. Database table ke ek consistent snapshot (table ka ek frozen view, jaisa woh kisi ek moment par tha) ko scan karta hai aur jis field ko index karna hai uski values nikaalta hai. Woh unhe sort karta hai aur index likh deta hai. Phir snapshot ke baad hue writes ka backlog process karta hai, kyunki table locked nahi tha aur writes chalti rah sakti thi. Uske baad woh har write par index ko up to date rakhta hai.

Yeh process naya follower replica set up karne se kaafi milta-julta hai, jo snapshot leta hai, changes ke saath catch up karta hai, aur phir saath-saath follow karta rehta hai. Yeh streaming system mein CDC shuru karne se bhi bahut milta hai, jo ek initial snapshot se shuru hota hai. Matlab CREATE INDEX chalana existing dataset ko reprocess karna hai aur index ko uske upar ek naye view ki tarah derive karna hai. Existing data shayad current state ka snapshot ho, past changes ka poora log nahi, lekin dono closely related hain.

Sab cheezon ka meta-database. Author ka suggestion hai ki poore organization ka dataflow ek vishaal database jaisa dikhne lagta hai. Jab bhi koi batch job, stream job ya ETL process (extract, transform aur load: ek system se data ko doosre system mein reshaped form mein copy karna) data ko ek jagah aur form se doosre mein le jaata hai, woh wahi kar raha hota hai jo database andar se karta hai jab woh indexes ya materialized views ko up to date rakhta hai. Is nazariye se, batch aur stream processors database triggers (code jo data change hone par apne aap chalta hai), stored procedures (code jo database ke andar rakha aur chalaya jaata hai) aur materialized view maintenance routines ke elaborate versions hain. Jo derived systems woh maintain karte hain woh alag-alag index types jaise hain. Ek relational database B-tree indexes, hash indexes aur spatial indexes support kar sakta hai. Ubharte hue architecture mein, yeh facilities ek integrated product ke features nahi hain. Woh alag software dete hain, alag machines par, alag teams ke chalaye hue.

Author is premise se shuru karte hain ki koi ek data model ya storage format har access pattern ke liye fit nahi hota. Phir woh andaza lagate hain ki alag storage aur processing tools ko ek cohesive system mein compose karne ke do tarike hain.

Federated databases: reads ko unify karna. Tum kai underlying storage engines aur processing methods ke upar ek unified query interface de sakte ho. Ise federated database, ya polystore, kehte hain. Jaise PostgreSQL ka foreign data wrapper feature isi pattern ko follow karta hai. Jin applications ka specialized data model ya query interface hai, woh phir bhi underlying engines tak seedha pahunch sakti hain. Jinhe bikhri hui jagahon se data combine karna hai, woh federated interface se aasaani se kar sakte hain. Federated query interface relational tradition ko follow karta hai: ek integrated system, high-level language aur elegant semantics, lekin uski implementation complicated hoti hai.

Unbundled databases: writes ko unify karna. Federation kai systems mein read-only querying ko address karta hai. Systems ke beech writes ko sync mein rakhne ka uske paas koi achha jawab nahi hai. Ek single database ke andar consistent index banana built-in feature hai. Jab tum kai storage systems compose karte ho, toh wahi guarantee chahiye: har data change ko har sahi jagah pahunchna chahiye, faults hone par bhi. Storage systems ko reliably plug karna aasaan banana, jaise CDC aur event logs se, database ke index-maintenance features ko unbundle karne jaisa hai taaki woh alag technologies ke beech writes synchronize kar sakein. Yeh Unix tradition ko follow karta hai: chhote tools jo har ek ek hi kaam achhe se karte hain, ek uniform low-level interface (pipes) se baat karte hain, aur ek higher-level language, shell, se compose ho sakte hain.

Unbundling ko kaam karwana

Federation aur unbundling ek hi sikke ke do pehlu hain: alag-alag hisson se ek reliable, scalable aur maintainable system compose karna. Read-only federated querying ke liye ek data model ko doosre par map karna padta hai. Isme sochna padta hai, lekin aakhir mein yeh ek manageable problem hai. Author ko lagta hai ki kai storage systems mein writes ko sync mein rakhna zyada mushkil engineering problem hai, isliye woh usi par focus karte hain.

Writes synchronize karne ka traditional tarika heterogeneous storage systems, yani alag-alag kism ke systems, ke beech distributed transactions use karta hai. Author ke hisaab se yeh galat solution hai. Ek storage ya stream system ke andar transactions feasible hain. Lekin jab data technologies ki boundary cross karta hai, toh unka maanna hai ki idempotent writes ke saath ek asynchronous event log kaafi zyada robust aur practical approach hai.

Stream processors exactly-once semantics paane ke liye andar se distributed transactions already use karte hain, aur yeh achhe se kaam kar sakta hai. Lekin jab transaction mein alag-alag logon ke likhe systems shaamil hon, jaise ek stream processor jo distributed key-value store ya search index mein likh raha ho, toh standard transaction protocol na hone se integration bahut mushkil ho jaata hai. Events ka ordered log, jise idempotent consumers consume karein, kaafi simple abstraction hai, aur alag systems ke beech banana kaafi zyada feasible hai.

Log-based integration components ke beech loose coupling deta hai. Yeh do tarah se dikhta hai.

  1. System level par, asynchronous event streams poore system ko ek component ke outages ya slowdowns ke prati zyada robust banati hain. Agar koi consumer slow chale ya fail ho, toh log messages ko buffer karta hai, aur producer aur baaki consumers chalte rehte hain. Faulty consumer fix hone ke baad catch up kar leta hai, isliye koi data miss nahi hota, aur fault wahin contained rehta hai. Iske ulta, distributed transactions ki synchronous coupling local fault ko bade scale ki failure mein badalne ki taraf jaati hai.
  2. Human level par, unbundling alag teams ko alag components independently develop, improve aur maintain karne deta hai. Har team ek hi kaam achhe se karne par focus kar sakti hai, doosri teams ke systems ke saath well-defined interfaces ke saath. Event logs itne powerful hain ki strong consistency properties capture kar sakein, kyunki events durable aur ordered hote hain. Woh itne general bhi hain ki lagbhag kisi bhi kism ke data par laagu ho sakein.

Unbundled versus integrated systems. Agar unbundling sach mein future ka tarika ban bhi jaaye, toh woh databases ko unke current form mein replace nahi karegi. Stream processors ke andar state maintain karne ke liye, aur batch aur stream jobs ke output par queries serve karne ke liye databases ki zaroorat rahegi. Specialized query engines bhi important rahenge. Jaise massively parallel processing (MPP) data warehouses ke query engines exploratory analytic queries ke liye optimized hain aur us workload ko bahut achhe se handle karte hain.

Kai kism ka infrastructure chalane ki cost hoti hai. Har piece ka learning curve, configuration issues aur operational quirks hote hain, isliye kam se kam moving parts deploy karna faydemand hai. Ek single integrated product un workloads par behtar aur zyada predictable performance bhi de sakta hai jinke liye woh design hua tha, un systems ke muqable jo kai tools ko application code se jodkar bane hain. Author preface ki ek baat dohraate hain: jis scale ki zaroorat nahi hai uske liye build karna wasted effort hai, aur yeh tumhe ek inflexible design mein phansa sakta hai. Asal mein yeh premature optimization ka ek roop hai.

Isliye unbundling ka goal yeh nahi hai ki particular workloads par individual databases ko performance mein haraaye. Goal yeh hai ki kai databases ko combine karein taaki tumhe kisi bhi single product se kaafi wide range ke workloads par achhi performance mile. Yeh breadth ke baare mein hai, depth ke baare mein nahi. Yeh wahi idea hai jo book mein pehle Hadoop comparison mein storage aur processing models ki diversity ke baare mein tha. Agar ek technology tumhari saari zaroorat poori karti hai, toh aam taur par use use karna hi behtar hai, use lower-level parts se dobara banane se. Composition tabhi faydemand hai jab koi single product tumhari saari requirements poori na kare.

Trade-offs
OptionKisme achhaCost
Ek integrated databaseChalane ke liye ek hi product, aur jin workloads ke liye bana hai unpar predictable performanceTumhe bas wahi milta hai jo woh product deta hai. Zaroorat ke unusual combinations ke liye woh kharab fit ho sakta hai.
Unbundled compositionBreadth: har part apne kaam ke liye best tool ho sakta hai, kai kism ke workloads parBahut saare moving parts, har ek ka apna learning curve aur quirks. Unke beech ka glue code tumhe likhna aur maintain karna padta hai.

Kya missing hai? Data systems compose karne ke tools behtar ho rahe hain, lekin author kehte hain ki ek bada piece abhi bhi missing hai. Hamare paas abhi Unix shell ka unbundled-database equivalent nahi hai, yani ek high-level language jisse storage aur processing systems ko simple, declarative tarike se compose kiya ja sake.

Unhe yeh declare kar paana pasand aayega: mysql | elasticsearch, Unix pipe ke analogy mein. Yeh CREATE INDEX ka unbundled version hota. Yeh MySQL database ke saare documents lekar unhe Elasticsearch cluster mein index kar deta. Phir yeh database ke har change ko capture karta rehta aur use search index par apne aap apply kar deta, bina custom application code ke. Author ko lagta hai ki is tarah ka integration lagbhag kisi bhi storage ya indexing system ke saath possible hona chahiye.

Caches ko bhi isi tarah aasaani se maintain kiya ja sakta hai. Materialized view asal mein ek precomputed cache hi hai. Toh tum socho ki complex queries ke liye materialized views declaratively specify karke cache banaya jaaye. In queries mein graphs par recursive queries (aisi queries jo connected records ke network mein links follow karti hain) aur yahan tak ki application logic bhi ho sakta hai. Author is area mein shuruaati research, jaise differential dataflow, ka zikr karte hain, aur ummeed karte hain ki yeh ideas production systems tak pahunchenge.

Dataflow ke around applications design karna

Database ko unbundle karna, yani specialized storage aur processing systems ko application code ke saath compose karna, ise kabhi-kabhi database inside-out approach kehte hain. Yeh naam author ke 2014 ke ek conference talk ke title se aaya hai. Woh kehte hain ki ise nayi architecture bolna bahut bada claim hoga. Unke hisaab se yeh ek design pattern hai aur discussion ki shuruaat hai. Naam isliye diya taaki log ispar aasaani se baat kar sakein.

Yeh ideas unke apne nahi hain. Yeh doosron ke kaam ka mix hai. Dataflow programming languages jaise Oz aur Juttle, functional reactive programming (FRP) languages jaise Elm, aur logic language Bloom ke saath kaafi overlap hai. Is context mein unbundling term Jay Kreps ne propose kiya tha.

Spreadsheets mein pehle se hi dataflow programming hai, aur woh zyadatar mainstream languages se kaafi aage hai. Tum ek cell mein formula daalte ho, jaise kisi doosre column ke cells ka sum. Formula ka koi bhi input badalta hai, toh result apne aap update ho jaata hai. Data-system level par hum yahi chahte hain. Database mein koi record change ho, toh uska index update ho, aur us par depend karne wale cached views ya totals refresh ho jaayein. Tumhe mechanics manage nahi karne chahiye. Bas yeh bharosa hona chahiye ki refresh sahi tarah se ho jaayega.

Author ka maanna hai ki zyadatar data systems abhi bhi VisiCalc se seekh sakte hain, jo 1979 ka ek spreadsheet program tha. Aaj ke data systems spreadsheets se kai important cheezon mein alag hain. Unhe fault-tolerant, scalable aur durable hona padta hai. Unhe un technologies ko bhi integrate karna padta hai jo alag-alag logon ne alag-alag samay par likhi hain, aur existing libraries aur services reuse karni padti hain. Yeh umeed rakhna realistic nahi hai ki saara software ek hi language, ek hi framework ya tool mein likha jaayega. Is section ka baaki hissa unbundled databases aur dataflow ke around applications banane ke tarike explore karta hai.

Application code ek derivation function ke roop mein

Jab ek dataset doosre se derive hota hai, toh ek transformation function ek ko doosre mein badalta hai. Book mein kai examples hain:

  • Secondary index ek derived dataset hai jisme transformation simple hoti hai. Base table ke har row ya document ke liye woh indexed columns ya fields ki values nikaalta hai aur unke hisaab se sort karta hai. B-tree ya SSTable index, jo Chapter 3 ke hisaab se key ke order mein sorted hote hain, unke liye woh sorting hi index hai.
  • Full-text search index banane ke liye pehle natural language processing lagti hai. Isme language detection, word segmentation (text ko words mein todna, jo un languages mein zaroori hai jinme spaces nahi hote), stemming ya lemmatization (words ko base form mein laana, jaise running se run), spelling correction aur synonym identification aate hain. Phir fast lookups ke liye ek structure banta hai, jaise inverted index, jo har word ko un documents se map karta hai jinme woh word hai.
  • Machine learning system mein model training data se feature extraction aur statistical analysis ke through derive hota hai. Jab model ko naye input par apply karte hain, toh output input aur model se derive hota hai, yani indirectly training data se.
  • Cache mein aksar data us form mein aggregated hota hai jisme user interface use dikhayega. Ise fill karne ke liye pata hona chahiye ki interface kaun se fields use karta hai. Interface badla, toh cache fill karne ka tarika bhi badalna pad sakta hai, aur cache ko rebuild karna padega.

Secondary index ki derivation itni common hai ki kai databases ise built-in dete hain, aur tum bas CREATE INDEX bol kar ise chala sakte ho. Common languages ke basic linguistic features database ke full-text search mein built-in ho sakte hain, lekin zyada sophisticated features ko aksar domain-specific tuning chahiye hoti hai. Machine learning mein feature engineering, yani model kaun se input signals use karega yeh choose karna, application-specific hone ke liye mashhoor hai. Yeh aksar is par depend karta hai ki users app ke saath kaise interact karte hain.

Derived dataset banane wala function jab secondary index jaisa standard, cookie-cutter function nahi hota, toh application ki specific zarooraton ke liye custom code chahiye. Yahin kai databases struggle karte hain. Relational databases triggers, stored procedures aur user-defined functions support karte hain, jo database ke andar application code chala sakte hain. Lekin database design mein yeh zyadatar baad mein jodi gayi cheezein rahi hain.

Application code aur state ko alag rakhna

Theory mein database kisi bhi application code ke liye ek deployment environment ban sakta hai, jaise operating system hota hai. Practice mein databases is kaam ke liye theek nahi nikle. Woh modern application development ki zarooraton ko poora nahi karte, jaise dependency aur package management, version control, rolling upgrades, evolvability, monitoring, metrics, network services ko calls, aur external systems ke saath integration. Clusters chalane ke tools, jaise Mesos, YARN, Docker aur Kubernetes, khaas taur par application code chalane ke liye design hue the. Woh ek hi kaam achhe se karte hain, isliye un databases se kaafi behtar hain jo user-defined functions ko kai features mein se ek feature ki tarah chalate hain.

Isliye author ko lagta hai ki system ke kuch hisse durable data storage mein specialize karein, aur kuch hisse application code chalane mein. Dono aapas mein interact kar sakte hain aur phir bhi independent rehte hain.

Aaj ke zyadatar web applications stateless services ki tarah deploy hote hain. Koi bhi user request kisi bhi application server par route ho sakti hai, aur response bhejne ke baad server request ke baare mein sab bhool jaata hai. Isse servers add ya remove karna aasaan ho jaata hai, lekin state kahin na kahin rehni chahiye, aur woh usually database mein hoti hai. Trend yeh raha hai ki stateless application logic ko state management se alag rakha jaaye: database ke andar koi application logic nahi, aur application ke andar koi persistent state nahi. Author mazaak mein kehte hain ki functional programming community ko yeh kehna pasand hai ki woh Church aur state ke separation mein believe karti hai. Yeh Alonzo Church par pun hai, jo mathematician the aur jinhone lambda calculus banaya. Usme aise variables hi nahi hain jo overwrite ho sakein, isliye mutable state unke kaam se alag rehti hai.

Is typical model mein database ek shared mutable variable ki tarah kaam karta hai, jise application network par synchronously read aur update karti hai. Durability, kuch concurrency control aur fault tolerance database sambhalta hai. Lekin zyadatar programming languages mein tum kisi variable ke changes ko subscribe nahi kar sakte. Bas read kar sakte hain. Spreadsheet cell ke ulat, variable badalne par readers ko notification nahi milta. Tum observer pattern se aisa notification khud bana sakte ho, lekin zyadatar languages mein yeh built-in nahi hota. Databases ko yahi passive approach virasat mein mili hai. Data badla ya nahi, yeh jaanne ke liye aksar tumhe poll karna padta hai, matlab timer par apni query baar-baar chalana. Changes ko subscribe karna ek feature ke roop mein abhi shuru hi ho raha hai.

Dataflow: state changes aur application code ka interplay

Applications ko dataflow ki tarah sochne se application code aur state management ka relationship badal jaata hai. Database ko ek passive variable maan kar application usse manipulate kare, aisa sochne ke bajaye tum state, state changes aur unhe process karne wale code ke interplay par focus karte hain. Application code ek jagah ke state change par react karke doosri jagah ka state change trigger karta hai.

Yeh idea book mein pehle aa chuka hai. Chapter 11 mein database changes ke log ko events ki aisi stream ki tarah dekha gaya tha jise tum subscribe kar sakte ho. Message-passing systems jaise actors, jo Chapter 4 mein aaye the, woh bhi messages ke through events par respond karte hain. 1980s mein tuple spaces ne distributed computations ko aise processes ki tarah describe karne ki koshish ki thi jo state changes ko observe karke un par react karte hain. Database ke andar bhi yahi hota hai jab data change par trigger fire hota hai, ya jab secondary index apni table ke change ko reflect karne ke liye update hota hai. Unbundling is idea ko primary database ke bahar le jaati hai, taaki derived datasets bana sakein, jaise caches, full-text search indexes, machine learning models aur analytics systems. Yeh kaam stream processing aur messaging systems kar sakte hain.

Author zor dete hain ki derived data maintain karna asynchronous job execution jaisa nahi hai, jiske liye messaging systems traditionally bane the. Do farq important hain:

  • Order matter karta hai. Agar kai views ek hi event log se derive ho rahe hain, toh unhe events same order mein process karne honge, tabhi woh aapas mein consistent rahenge. Kai message brokers unacknowledged messages ko redeliver karte waqt woh order preserve nahi karte. Dual writes bhi isliye ruled out hain.
  • Fault tolerance zaroori hai. Ek bhi message lost ho jaaye, toh derived dataset apne source se hamesha ke liye out of sync ho jaata hai. Isliye message delivery aur derived state updates, dono reliable hone chahiye. Kai actor systems default mein actor state aur messages memory mein rakhte hain, toh actor chalane wali machine crash hone par woh lost ho jaate hain.

Stable message ordering aur reliable processing demanding requirements hain. Lekin yeh distributed transactions se kaafi sasti aur operationally zyada robust hain. Modern stream processors yeh guarantees scale par de sakte hain, aur application code ko stream operators ki tarah chalne dete hain. Aise operators woh arbitrary processing kar sakte hain jo built-in derivation functions aksar nahi kar paate. Pipes se jude Unix tools ki tarah, stream operators ko compose karke bade systems bana sakte hain. Har operator state changes ki streams input leta hai, aur state changes ki doosri streams output deta hai.

Stream processors aur services

Application development ka fashionable style functionality ko services mein baant deta hai, jo synchronous network requests, jaise REST APIs, ke through baat karti hain. Ek bade application ke mukable, is service-oriented approach ka main advantage loose coupling se organizational scalability hai. Alag-alag teams alag-alag services par kaam kar sakti hain, jisse teams ke beech coordination kam lagti hai, bas shart yeh hai ki har service independently deploy aur update ho sake.

Stream operators ko compose karke dataflow systems banana microservices approach se kai cheezon mein milta-julta hai. Lekin underlying communication mechanism bahut alag hai. Dataflow synchronous request-response ke bajaye one-directional, asynchronous message streams use karta hai. Book mein pehle jo advantages aaye the, jaise better fault tolerance, unke alawa dataflow systems better performance bhi de sakte hain. Book ek example deti hai. Ek customer ek item khareedta hai jiska price ek currency mein hai, lekin payment doosri currency mein hui. Currency convert karne ke liye system ko current exchange rate chahiye. Iske do tarike hain.

Example

Purchase mein exchange rates. Microservices approach mein purchase process karne wala code har baar exchange-rate service ya database se current rate query karta hai. Dataflow approach mein purchase code pehle se exchange-rate updates ki stream subscribe kar leta hai. Jab bhi rate badalta hai, woh current rate ek local database mein record kar leta hai. Purchase aane par woh sirf us local database ko query karta hai.

Doosre approach mein kisi aur service ko jaane wali synchronous network request ki jagah ek local database ki query aa gayi, jo usi machine par ya usi process mein bhi ho sakta hai. Book yeh bhi kehti hai ki microservices team rates ko locally cache karke network call bacha sakti thi. Lekin us cache ko fresh rakhne ke liye unhe updated rates poll karne padte, ya changes ki stream subscribe karni padti, aur dataflow approach bilkul yahi karta hai.

Dataflow approach faster hai, aur kisi doosri service ke fail hone par bhi zyada robust hai. Sabse fast aur sabse reliable network request woh hai jo hoti hi nahi. RPC call, yani ek program ka network ke zariye doosre program ka function invoke karna, ki jagah system ab purchase events aur exchange-rate update events ke beech stream join karta hai. Yeh join time-dependent hai. Agar purchase events baad mein dobara process kiye jaayein, toh tab tak exchange rate badal chuka hoga. Original output rebuild karne ke liye tumhe purchase ke time ka historical rate chahiye. Chahe tum service query karo ya stream subscribe karo, tumhe is time dependence ko handle karna hi padega.

Abhi bhi kuch open questions hain, jaise time-dependent joins ko kaise handle karein. Lekin author ko lagta hai ki dataflow ke around applications banana ek bahut promising direction hai. Jab bhi current state chahiye tab query karne ke bajaye changes ko subscribe karna hume spreadsheet model of computation ke kareeb le jaata hai: kisi data ka ek hissa badle, toh us se derived har cheez tezi se update ho sakti hai.

Derived state ko observe karna

Pichhle section ke dataflow systems derived datasets banane aur unhe up to date rakhne ka ek process dete hain, jaise search indexes, materialized views aur predictive models. Book is process ko write path kehti hai. Jab bhi koi information likhi jaati hai, woh batch aur stream processing ke kai stages se guzar sakti hai, aur aakhir mein har derived dataset update hokar usse include kar leta hai. Book ka Figure 12-1 yeh idea search index ke saath dikhata hai, jahan ek taraf document updates aur doosri taraf queries milte hain.

Lekin derived dataset banate hi kyun hain? Zyada chance hai ki tum use baad mein query karna chahte ho. Yeh read path hai. Jab user request aati hai, tum derived dataset se read karte ho, results par shayad aur processing karte ho, aur response banate ho. Write path aur read path milkar data ka poora safar cover karte hain, us point se jahan data collect hota hai us point tak jahan woh consume hota hai, shayad kisi aur insaan ke through. Write path woh hissa hai jo data aate hi precompute ho jaata hai, chahe kisi ne use dekhne ko maanga ho ya nahi. Read path tabhi hota hai jab koi poochhta hai. Agar tum functional programming jaante ho, toh dhyaan doge ki write path eager evaluation jaisa hai, aur read path lazy evaluation jaisa.

Derived dataset woh jagah hai jahan write path aur read path milte hain. Yeh is baat ka trade-off hai ki kitna kaam write time par hoga aur kitna read time par.

Materialized views aur caching

Full-text search index ek achha example hai. Write path index update karta hai, aur read path keywords ke liye use search karta hai. Dono taraf kaam hota hai. Writes document mein aane wale har term ke index entries update karte hain. Reads query ke har word ko look up karte hain aur matching documents dhoondhne ke liye Boolean logic lagate hain. AND query mein har word match hona chahiye. OR query mein har word ka koi bhi synonym chal jaata hai.

Index ke bina search ko saare documents scan karne padenge, jaise grep command files scan karta hai. Documents bahut hon toh yeh bahut mehnga ho jaata hai. Index nahi hai matlab write path par kaam kam, kyunki update karne ko kuch hai hi nahi, lekin read path par kaafi zyada kaam.

Tum ulta raasta bhi le sakte ho aur har possible query ke results precompute kar sakte ho. Tab reads sirf ready answers uthayenge, Boolean logic ki zaroorat hi nahi. Lekin write path bahut zyada expensive ho jaayega. Possible queries ka set practically infinite hai, isliye sabko precompute karne ke liye unlimited time aur storage chahiye. Author footnote mein jodte hain: nonempty results wali distinct queries ka set finite hota hai agar collection finite ho, lekin woh terms ki count ke saath exponentially badhta hai, jo phir bhi buri khabar hai.

Beech ka raasta yeh hai ki sirf sabse common queries ke fixed set ke results precompute karein, taaki unhe index tak gaye bina jaldi serve kiya ja sake. Uncommon queries phir bhi index se serve hoti hain. Ise aam taur par common queries ka cache kehte hain. Ise materialized view bhi keh sakte hain, kyunki jab naye documents aate hain jo kisi common query ke results mein aane chahiye, toh use update karna padta hai.

Toh write path aur read path ke beech index hi ek possible boundary nahi hai. Tum common search results cache kar sakte ho, ya jab documents kam hon toh bina index ke scan kar sakte ho. Caches, indexes aur materialized views, sab boundary ko shift karte hain. Woh results precompute karke write path par zyada kaam karne dete hain, taaki read path par mehnat bache.

Yahi shift book ki shuruaat ke Twitter example ka topic tha. Chapter 1 ne numbers diye the. Tweet post karne ka average 4.6k requests per second tha, aur peak 12k se upar. Home timeline dekhna 300k requests per second par chalta tha. Ek typical tweet lagbhag 75 followers tak pahunchta tha, lekin kuch users ke 30 million se zyada followers the.

Example

Twitter timeline, dobara. Book is example par wapas aati hai yeh dikhane ke liye ki alag-alag users ke liye boundary alag tarah se kheenchi ja sakti hai.

  1. Ordinary users: kaam write time par. Jab ordinary user tweet post karta hai, toh system uske followers dhoondhta hai aur tweet ko har follower ke home timeline cache mein copy kar deta hai. Average lagbhag 75 followers par, 4.6k tweets per second lagbhag 345k timeline writes per second ban jaate hain.
  2. Phir reading sasti hoti hai. Jab koi follower apni timeline kholta hai, toh read path us cache mein ek lookup hai. Kaam tweet post hote hi ho chuka tha.
  3. Celebrities: kaam read time par. 30 million se zyada followers wala user, agar fan out kiya jaaye, toh ek tweet ke liye 30 million se zyada writes karwayega. Isliye unke tweets har timeline mein copy nahi hote. Woh ek hi baar store hote hain. Jab koi user apni timeline read karta hai, toh jin celebrities ko woh follow karta hai unke tweets read time par fetch karke merge kar diye jaate hain, jaise read-time approach kaam karta hai.
  4. Result. Ordinary users ka zyadatar kaam write time par hota hai, jahan reads fast hote hain, aur celebrities timeline read hote waqt thoda zyada kaam karke write storm se bach jaate hain. Book ke hisaab se yeh hybrid consistently achhi performance deta hai, aur 500 pages ke baad book ek poora chakkar lagakar wahin aa gayi hai.

Stateful, offline-capable clients

Author ko write path aur read path ke beech boundary wala idea databases se aage bhi kaam ka lagta hai. Ise ek aur setting mein dekhna worth it hai: clients, yani woh programs jo end users ke devices par chalte hain.

Web applications lambe samay se client/server model par bane hain, jisme clients zyadatar stateless hote hain aur data par authority servers ke paas hoti hai. Yeh model itna common hai ki hum lagbhag bhool hi jaate hain ki kuch aur bhi ho sakta hai. Lekin technology aage badhti rehti hai. Traditionally web browsers stateless clients the, jo sirf connected rehne par kaam ke the. Offline tum lagbhag bas pehle se load kiya hua page scroll kar sakte the. Haal ke single-page JavaScript apps ko stateful powers mil gayi hain, jaise client-side interaction aur persistent local storage. Mobile apps device par kaafi state rakh sakte hain aur zyadatar actions ke liye server ka round trip skip kar sakte hain.

Isse offline-first applications mein phir se interest jaaga hai. Yeh jitna ho sake kaam usi device ke local database se karte hain, bina internet connection ke, aur connection milne par background mein remote servers ke saath sync karte hain. Mobile connections aksar slow aur unreliable hote hain. Isliye users ke liye bada fayda hai jab interface network requests ka wait na kare, aur app zyadatar offline kaam kare.

Jab state end-user devices par rehti hai, toh naye options khulte hain. Tum on-device state ko server ki state ka cache maan sakte ho. Screen ke pixels client app ke model objects par ek materialized view hain. Model objects remote datacenter mein rakhi state ki ek local replica hain.

State changes ko clients tak push karna. Typical web page mein, agar page load karne ke baad server par data badal jaaye, toh browser ko tab tak pata nahi chalta jab tak tum reload na karo. Browser data ko ek point in time par read karta hai, use static maan leta hai, aur updates subscribe nahi karta. Toh device par state ek stale cache hai, jo tab tak refresh nahi hota jab tak tum changes ke liye poll na karo. RSS feeds bhi asal mein polling ka ek basic form hain.

Naye protocols HTTP ke basic request-response pattern se aage jaate hain. Server-sent events, jo EventSource API use karte hain, aur WebSockets browser ko server ke saath ek open TCP connection rakhne dete hain. Connection open rehte waqt server jab bhi kuch kehna chahe, browser ko messages push kar sakta hai. Isse server client ko uski state ke changes ke baare mein bata sakta hai, aur client ki state kitni stale hoti hai woh kam hota hai.

Write aur read paths ke terms mein, state changes ko actively client devices tak push karna write path ko end user tak extend karna hai. Client ab bhi apni initial state lene ke liye read path use karta hai. Uske baad woh server se aane wali state changes ki stream par rely kar sakta hai. Stream processing aur messaging ke ideas datacenter tak limited nahi hain. Inhe end-user devices tak extend kiya ja sakta hai.

Devices kabhi-kabhi offline honge aur changes receive nahi kar paayenge. Lekin book ke hisaab se yeh problem pehle hi solve ho chuki hai. Chapter 11 ne bataya tha ki log-based message broker ka consumer fail ya disconnect hone ke baad reconnect kar sakta hai, aur jo messages uske door rehte hue aaye the unme se koi miss nahi hota. Yahi technique individual users ke liye bhi kaam karti hai, jahan har device events ki ek chhoti stream ka chhota subscriber hai.

End-to-end event streams. Stateful clients aur user interfaces banane ke tools, jaise Elm language aur Facebook ka React, Flux aur Redux toolchain, pehle se hi events ki stream subscribe karke client-side state manage karte hain. Events user input ya server ke responses ko represent karte hain, aur structure event sourcing jaisa hai. Is model ko extend karna natural hoga, taaki server state-change events ko usi client-side pipeline mein push kar sake. Tab state changes end to end flow kar sakte hain. Ek device par kiya gaya action event logs, kai derived data systems aur stream processors se guzarega, aur doosre device par dekh rahe insaan ke user interface tak pahunchega. Author ka suggestion hai ki aise changes low delay se aa sakte hain, end to end ek second se bhi kam mein.

Kuch applications, jaise instant messaging aur online games, mein pehle se is tarah ki real-time architecture hai, matlab aisi jisme interactions ka delay kam hota hai. Book batati hai ki yeh real-time ka ek alag matlab hai, pehle discuss kiye gaye response time guarantees se alag. Toh hum saari applications aise kyun nahi banate? Challenge yeh hai ki stateless clients aur request-response interactions ki assumption hamare databases, libraries, frameworks aur protocols mein gehraai se baithi hui hai. Kai datastores aise reads aur writes support karte hain jisme ek request ka ek response aata hai. Bahut kam datastores changes subscribe karne dete hain, yani aisi request jo samay ke saath responses ki stream return kare. Write path ko poori tarah user tak extend karne ke liye hume in mein se kai systems ko dobara sochna padega, request-response se hatkar publish/subscribe dataflow ki taraf jaana hoga, jahan producers events publish karte hain aur interested parties unhe subscribe karte hain. Author ko lagta hai ki responsive interfaces aur offline support ke fayde is mehnat ke laayak honge. Unhe ummeed hai ki designers sirf current state query karne ke saath-saath changes subscribe karne ko bhi ek option ki tarah dimaag mein rakhenge.

Reads bhi events hain

Jab stream processor derived data ko kisi store mein likhta hai, aur user requests us store ko query karti hain, toh store hi write path aur read path ke beech ki boundary hai. Store data par random-access reads allow karta hai, jinke liye warna poora event log scan karna padta.

Aksar data storage streaming system se alag hota hai. Lekin stream processors ko bhi aggregations aur joins ke liye state maintain karni padti hai, jaisa Chapter 11 mein bataya gaya tha. Yeh state usually processor ke andar chhupi rehti hai. Kuch frameworks bahar ke clients ko ise query karne dete hain, jisse stream processor ek simple database ban jaata hai.

Author is idea ko aur aage le jaana chahte hain. Ab tak writes event log se guzarte hain, jabki reads transient network requests hain jo seedhe un nodes ko bheji jaati hain jinke paas data hai. Yeh reasonable hai, lekin yahi akela option nahi hai. Reads ko bhi events ki streams ke roop mein represent kiya ja sakta hai. Tab read events aur write events, dono ek stream processor ke through bheje ja sakte hain, jo har read event ka jawab result ko output stream mein emit karke deta hai. Jab writes aur reads dono events hain, aur same stream operator tak route hote hain, toh tum asal mein read queries ki stream aur database ke beech stream-table join kar rahe hote ho. Read event ko us database partition tak bhejna padta hai jisme data hai, bilkul waise hi jaise batch aur stream processors ko join karte waqt same key wale inputs ko ek jagah laana padta hai.

Requests serve karna aur joins perform karna, in dono ka yeh correspondence fundamental hai. Ek one-off read request join operator se guzarti hai, apna jawab leti hai, aur bhula di jaati hai. Subscribe request ek persistent join hai, jisme join ke doosri taraf past aur future events samay ke saath results produce karte hain.

Read events ka log record karne se poore system mein causal dependencies aur data provenance (data kahan se aaya aur kaise derive hua) track karne mein bhi madad milti hai. Isse tum reconstruct kar sakte ho ki user ne faisla lene se pehle kya dekha tha. Maan lo ek online shop hai, wahan customer ko dikhayi gayi predicted shipping date aur inventory status us ke khareedne ya na khareedne ko affect kar sakte hain. Is connection ko study karne ke liye tumhe yeh record chahiye ki customer ko kya dikhaya gaya tha. Read events ko durable storage mein likhne se causal tracking behtar hoti hai, lekin storage aur I/O ka cost badhta hai, aur us overhead ko kam karna abhi bhi ek open research problem hai. Agar tum operational purposes ke liye read requests ka log pehle se hi rakhte ho, unhe process karne ke side effect ke roop mein, toh us log ko requests ka source bana dena koi bada change nahi hai.

Multi-partition data processing

Jo query sirf ek partition ko touch karti hai, uske liye use stream se bhejna aur responses ki stream collect karna overkill ho sakta hai. Lekin yeh idea un complex queries ke distributed execution ka raasta kholta hai jo kai partitions ka data combine karti hain. Yeh message routing, partitioning aur joining infrastructure reuse karta hai jo stream processors pehle se dete hain. Storm ka distributed RPC feature is pattern ko support karta hai. Ise, jaise, Twitter par yeh count karne ke liye use kiya gaya hai ki kitne logon ne koi URL dekha. Woh count un sabke follower sets ka union hai jinhone woh URL tweet kiya. Kyunki users ka set partitioned hai, ise compute karne ke liye kai partitions ke results combine karne padte hain.

Fraud prevention ek aur example hai. Yeh judge karne ke liye ki koi purchase fraudulent hai ya nahi, tum user ke IP address, email address, billing address, shipping address, waghera ke reputation scores dekh sakte ho. In reputation databases mein se har ek khud partitioned hai. Isliye ek purchase ke scores collect karne ke liye alag-alag tarah se partitioned datasets ke saath joins ka ek sequence chahiye.

MPP databases ke internal query execution graphs mein bhi aisi hi khoobiyan hoti hain. Author kehte hain ki agar tumhe is tarah ka multi-partition join chahiye, toh stream processor par khud banane ke bajaye aisa database use karna shayad zyada simple hoga jo yeh feature deta ho. Phir bhi, queries ko streams ki tarah treat karna un large-scale applications banane ka ek tarika deta hai jo conventional off-the-shelf solutions ki limits se takra jaati hain.

Correctness ki taraf badhna

Jo stateless service sirf data read karti hai, woh bada risk nahi hai. Kuch galat ho jaaye toh tum bug fix karte ho, service restart karte ho, aur sab normal ho jaata hai. Databases jaise stateful systems alag hote hain. Unhe lagbhag hamesha ke liye cheezein yaad rakhne ke liye design kiya jaata hai, isliye galti ka asar bhi hamesha ke liye reh sakta hai. Isliye zyada dhyaan se sochna padta hai.

Hum aisi applications chahte hain jo reliable aur correct hon, yani aise programs jinka behavior well defined aur samjha hua ho, chahe faults aayein. Lagbhag chaar dashakon se atomicity, isolation aur durability ki transaction properties, jo Chapter 7 mein cover hui thi, correct applications banane ke liye pehli pasand ke tools rahe hain. Author kehte hain ki yeh foundations dikhne se zyada kamzor hain. Weak isolation levels ke aas-paas ka confusion ek example hai. Kuch areas mein transactions ko poori tarah chhod diya ja raha hai aise models ke favour mein jo better performance aur scalability dete hain, lekin semantics kaafi messy hoti hai. Leaderless replication ek example hai. Consistency ke baare mein baat bahut hoti hai, lekin yeh poorly defined hai. Kuch log kehte hain ki better availability ke liye hume weak consistency accept kar leni chahiye, bina yeh clear kiye ki practice mein iska matlab kya hai.

Engineering methods bhi utne solid nahi hain jitne hone chahiye. Yeh batana bahut mushkil hai ki koi particular application kisi particular isolation level ya replication setup par safe hai ya nahi. Simple solutions aksar tab kaam karte dikhte hain jab concurrency kam ho aur kuch fail na ho, phir heavier conditions mein unme kai subtle bugs nikalte hain. Kyle Kingsbury ke Jepsen experiments ne kuch products ke claimed safety guarantees aur network problems aur crashes ke dauran unke actual behavior ke beech bade gaps ujagar kiye hain. Infrastructure perfect hota tab bhi application code ko uske features sahi tarah se use karne padte. Jab configuration samajhna mushkil ho, jaise weak isolation levels aur quorum configurations (yani yeh rules ki read ya write par kitne nodes ko agree karna hai) mein hota hai, tab yeh error-prone hai.

Trade-off saaf hai. Agar tumhari application kabhi-kabhi unpredictable tareeke se data corrupt hone ya lose hone ko tolerate kar sakti hai, toh zindagi bahut simple ho jaati hai, aur tum shayad best ki umeed rakhkar kaam chala lo. Agar tumhe stronger assurances chahiye, toh serializability aur atomic commit established approaches hain. Lekin unki ek keemat hai. Yeh typically sirf ek datacenter ke andar kaam karte hain, jisse geographically distributed architectures ruled out ho jaate hain, aur yeh us scale aur fault tolerance ko limit karte hain jo tum achieve kar sakte ho.

Author ko lagta hai ki traditional transaction approach kahin nahi ja rahi, lekin applications ko correct aur faults ke prati resilient banane ka yeh aakhri jawab nahi hai. Is section ka baaki hissa dataflow architectures mein correctness ke baare mein sochne ke tarike suggest karta hai.

Databases ke liye end-to-end argument

Strong safety properties wala data system use karna, jaise serializable transactions, is baat ki guarantee nahi deta ki tumhari application data loss ya corruption se free hai. Agar application mein aisa bug hai jo galat data likhta hai ya data delete karta hai, toh serializable transactions tumhe nahi bacha payenge.

Yeh obvious lag sakta hai, lekin author kehte hain ki application bugs aur human mistakes hoti hain, isliye ise serious lena chahiye. Unhone yeh point pehle immutability ki discussion mein use kiya tha, append-only data ke paksh mein argue karne ke liye. Galtiyon se recover karna aasaan hota hai jab faulty code achhe data ko destroy nahi kar sakta. Lekin immutability sab problems ka ilaaj nahi hai, aur ek subtle kism ka corruption phir bhi ho sakta hai.

Operation ka exactly-once execution. Book mein pehle exactly-once, ya effectively-once, semantics ka idea aaya tha. Message process karte waqt kuch galat ho jaaye, toh tum haar maan sakte ho, jisme message drop hota hai aur data lose hota hai, ya dobara try kar sakte ho. Dobara try karne par risk yeh hai ki operation asal mein pehli baar hi succeed ho gaya tha, bas tumhe pata nahi chala. Tab message do baar process ho jaata hai. Do baar process hona ek tarah ka corruption hai. Ek service ke liye customer se do baar charge lena, ya counter do baar increment karke metric zyada dikhana, undesirable hai. Yahan exactly-once ka matlab hai computation ko aise arrange karna ki uska final effect waisa hi ho jaise koi fault aaya hi na ho, chahe operation retry hua ho.

Sabse effective approaches mein se ek yeh hai ki operation ko idempotent bana dein, taaki uska effect ek baar chalne par aur kai baar chalne par same rahe. Lekin jo operation naturally idempotent nahi hai, use idempotent banane mein mehnat aur dhyaan lagta hai. Tumhe extra metadata chahiye ho sakta hai, jaise un operation IDs ka set jinhone pehle hi kisi value ko update kar diya hai. Tumhe ek node se doosre par failover karte waqt fencing bhi ensure karni hogi, matlab yeh pakka karna ki cluster se kata hua purana node writes karta na reh sake.

Duplicate suppression. Duplicates ko suppress karne ki yahi zaroorat stream processing ke alawa kai jagah dikhti hai. TCP packets par sequence numbers use karta hai taaki recipient par unhe order mein laga sake, aur yeh detect kar sake ki packets lost hue ya duplicate. Lost packets dobara bheje jaate hain, aur duplicates data application tak pahunchne se pehle hata diye jaate hain. Lekin yeh sirf ek TCP connection ke andar kaam karta hai.

Maan lo TCP connection ek client ka database se connection hai, jo abhi ek transaction chala raha hai. Kai databases mein transaction ek client connection se juda hota hai, isliye database ko pata hota hai ki ek hi connection par bheji gayi kai queries ek hi transaction ki hain. Agar client ko COMMIT bhejne ke baad, lekin database ka jawab sunne se pehle, network interruption aur timeout mil jaaye, toh use pata nahi hota ki transaction commit hua ya abort.

Example

Aisa transfer jise retry karna safe nahi hai. Book ka Example 12-1 ek transaction ke andar ek account se doosre mein $11 move karta hai. Yeh atomicity ka standard textbook illustration hai:

BEGIN TRANSACTION;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 11.00 WHERE account_id = 1234;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 11.00 WHERE account_id = 4321;
COMMIT;
Example

Dekhte hain connection fail hone par kya hota hai:

  1. Client transaction bhejta hai. Database account 1234 mein $11 jodta hai aur account 4321 se $11 kaat leta hai.
  2. Database commit kar deta hai. Reply client tak pahunchne se pehle connection timeout ho jaata hai.
  3. Client ko pata nahi ki transfer hua ya nahi. Woh reconnect karta hai aur wahi transaction retry kar deta hai.
  4. Agar pehli attempt commit ho chuki thi, toh retry ek aur $11 move kar deta hai. Jo transfer $11 move karne ke liye tha, usne $22 move kar diye.

Transaction idempotent nahi hai, isliye retry nuksaan do baar kar sakta hai. Author batate hain ki Example 12-1 atomicity ka standard example hai, lekin asal mein woh correct nahi hai, aur real banks aise kaam nahi karte.

Two-phase commit protocols TCP connection aur transaction ke beech ka one-to-one link tod dete hain. Unhe transaction coordinator ko network fault ke baad database se reconnect karne dena hota hai aur use batana hota hai ki in-doubt transaction (jiska outcome abhi pata nahi) ko commit karna hai ya abort. Kya yeh ensure karne ke liye kaafi hai ki transaction sirf ek baar chale? Afsos, nahi. End user ke device aur application server ke beech ka network abhi bhi problem hai. Agar client web browser hai, toh woh shayad HTTP POST request se instruction bhejta hai. Weak cellular connection par ek user POST bhejne mein succeed ho sakta hai, lekin response aane se pehle signal kho sakta hai. Use shayad error dikhega aur woh manually retry kar sakta hai. Browsers poochhte hain ki kya tum form dobara submit karna chahte ho, aur user haan bol deta hai, kyunki woh chahta tha ki operation ho. Post/Redirect/Get pattern normal operation mein woh warning avoid kar deta hai, lekin jab POST timeout ho jaaye toh usse madad nahi milti. Web server ke point of view se retry ek alag request hai. Database ke point of view se woh ek alag transaction hai. Usual deduplication mechanisms se koi madad nahi milti.

Operation identifiers. Network communication ke kai hops ke across operation ko idempotent banane ke liye database ke andar ke transaction mechanism par rely karna kaafi nahi hai. Tumhe request ke end-to-end flow ko dekhna padega. Maan lo tum har operation ke liye ek unique identifier generate karte ho, jaise UUID, aur use client application mein hidden form field ki tarah include karte ho. Ya tum saare relevant form fields ka hash calculate karke operation ID derive kar sakte ho. Browser POST do baar submit kare, toh dono requests mein same operation ID hogi. Tum us ID ko poore raaste database tak pass kar sakte ho, aur check kar sakte ho ki us ID wala sirf ek operation hi kabhi execute ho.

Example

Request ID se duplicates suppress karna. Example 12-2 usi transfer ka book wala version hai, jisme request ID ek aisi table mein store hoti hai jis par uniqueness rule laga hai:

ALTER TABLE requests ADD UNIQUE (request_id);
BEGIN TRANSACTION;
INSERT INTO requests
  (request_id, from_account, to_account, amount)
  VALUES('0286FDB8-D7E1-423F-B40B-792B3608036C', 4321, 1234, 11.00);
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 11.00 WHERE account_id = 1234;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 11.00 WHERE account_id = 4321;
COMMIT;
Example

Example 12-2 mein retry ko step by step dekhte hain:

  1. request_id par unique constraint database ko batata hai ki do rows ek hi ID share nahi kar sakti.
  2. Pehli attempt ID ke saath ek row insert karti hai, phir dono balances update karti hai, aur commit karti hai.
  3. Retry wahi request ID bhejta hai. INSERT fail ho jaata hai kyunki ID pehle se present hai. Isse transaction abort ho jaata hai, toh balances doosri baar touch nahi hote.

Relational databases aam taur par uniqueness constraint ko sahi tarah maintain kar sakte hain, weak isolation levels par bhi. Iske ulat, application-level check-then-insert nonserializable isolation mein fail ho sakta hai, jaisa book mein pehle discuss hua tha. Author yeh bhi batate hain ki requests table ek tarah ke event log ki tarah kaam karti hai, jo event sourcing ki taraf ishaara karti hai. Balance updates ko insert ke saath usi transaction mein hona zaroori nahi hai. Woh redundant hain, kyunki unhe downstream consumer mein request event se derive kiya ja sakta hai, bas shart yeh hai ki woh event exactly once process ho. Yeh bhi request ID se enforce kiya ja sakta hai.

End-to-end argument. Duplicate transactions suppress karna ek zyada general principle ka example hai, jo Saltzer, Reed aur Clark ne 1984 mein articulate kiya tha. Essence mein principle kehta hai ki koi function sirf communication system ke dono endpoints par present applications ki knowledge aur madad se hi poori tarah aur correctly implement ho sakta hai. Isliye us function ko communication system ke khud ke feature ke roop mein dena possible nahi hai. System ke andar diya gaya incomplete version phir bhi performance boost ki tarah useful ho sakta hai.
