Is example mein function duplicate suppression tha. TCP ek connection ke andar duplicate packets suppress karta hai. Kuch stream processors message level par exactly-once semantics dete hain. Lekin in dono mein se koi bhi user ko duplicate request submit karne se nahi rok sakta jab pehli request timeout ho gayi ho. Problem solve karne ke liye end-to-end solution chahiye: ek transaction identifier jo end-user client se database tak poore raaste pass hota hai.

Yahi argument data integrity check karne par bhi lagta hai. Ethernet, TCP aur TLS mein built-in checksums network mein packets ka corruption detect kar sakte hain. Woh connection ke dono taraf ke software ke bugs se hone wala corruption, ya jin disks par data store hai unke corruption ko detect nahi kar sakte. Agar tum corruption ke har possible source ko pakadna chahte ho, toh tumhe end-to-end checksums bhi chahiye.

Encryption par bhi isi tarah ka argument lagta hai. Tumhare ghar ke WiFi network ka password un logon se bachata hai jo tumhara WiFi traffic snoop karte hain, lekin internet par kahin aur baithe attackers se nahi. Tumhare client aur server ke beech TLS ya SSL network attackers se bachata hai, lekin compromised server se nahi. In sabse bachne ke liye sirf end-to-end encryption aur authentication hi kaam karte hain.

Low-level features, jaise TCP duplicate suppression, Ethernet checksums aur WiFi encryption, akele end-to-end properties nahi de sakte. Lekin phir bhi woh useful hain, kyunki woh higher levels par problems ki probability kam karte hain. Agar TCP packets ko sahi order mein wapas na lagaye, toh HTTP requests aksar mangled ho jaayein. Point bas itna hai ki low-level reliability akele end-to-end correctness ensure karne ke liye kaafi nahi hai.

Data systems mein end-to-end thinking lagana. Yeh argument ko author ki original thesis par wapas le aata hai. Sirf is wajah se ki application comparatively strong safety properties wala data system use karti hai, yeh guarantee nahi ho jaati ki application data loss ya corruption se free hai. Application ko khud end-to-end measures lene padte hain, jaise duplicate suppression. Author ise sharm ki baat kehte hain, kyunki fault-tolerance mechanisms ko sahi karna mushkil hota hai. Low-level reliability mechanisms, jaise TCP ke, kaafi achhe se kaam karte hain, isliye baaki bache higher-level faults kaafi rare hain.

Achha hota agar baaki bachi high-level fault-tolerance machinery ko kisi abstraction mein wrap kar diya jaata, taaki application code ko uski chinta na karni pade. Lekin author ko darr hai ki sahi abstraction abhi mila nahi hai. Transactions ko lambe samay se achha abstraction maana gaya hai. Woh possible problems ki badi range, jaise concurrent writes, constraint violations, crashes, network interruptions aur disk failures, ko do outcomes mein collapse kar dete hain: commit ya abort. Yeh programming model ki bahut badi simplification hai, lekin unhe darr hai ki yeh kaafi nahi hai.

Transactions expensive hain, khaaskar heterogeneous storage technologies ke across. Jab hum distributed transactions ko bahut costly hone ki wajah se use karne se mana karte hain, toh hum fault-tolerance mechanisms ko application code mein dobara implement karne lagte hain. Book ne dikhaya hai ki concurrency aur partial failure ke baare mein reason karna mushkil aur counterintuitive hai. Isliye author ko shak hai ki zyadatar application-level mechanisms sahi kaam nahi karte, aur nateeja lost ya corrupted data hota hai. Isliye unka maanna hai ki aise fault-tolerance abstractions explore karna worth it hai jo application-specific, end-to-end correctness properties dena aasaan banayein, aur bade distributed environment mein achhi performance aur operational characteristics bhi banaye rakhein.

Constraints enforce karna

Chalo unbundled databases ke context mein correctness ke baare mein sochte hain. Hum dekh chuke hain ki end-to-end duplicate suppression ek request ID se kaam karta hai jo client se us database tak pass hoti hai jo write record karta hai. Baaki tarah ke constraints ka kya?

Yahan focus uniqueness constraints par hai. Pichhle chapters mein aisi kai applications ke examples aaye the jinhe uniqueness enforce karni padti hai. Username ya email address ko ek hi user identify karna chahiye. File storage service mein same naam ki do files nahi ho sakti. Do log ek hi flight ya theater ki ek hi seat book nahi kar sakte. Baaki constraints bhi isi tarah ke hain. Account balance kabhi negative nahi hona chahiye. Warehouse mein jitne items hain unse zyada nahi bechne chahiye. Meeting room mein overlapping bookings nahi honi chahiye. Jo techniques uniqueness enforce karti hain, woh aksar inke liye bhi use ho sakti hain.

Uniqueness constraints ko consensus chahiye. Chapter 9 ne dikhaya tha ki distributed setting mein uniqueness constraint enforce karne ke liye consensus chahiye. Agar kai concurrent requests ek hi value chahti hain, toh system ko kisi tarah decide karna padta hai ki kaun si operation accept ho aur baaki reject. Is agreement tak pahunchne ka sabse common tarika yeh hai ki ek node ko leader bana dein aur saare decisions use lene dein. Yeh tab tak kaam karta hai jab tak tumhe saari requests ko ek hi node se guzaarne mein dikkat nahi, chahe client duniya ke doosri taraf ho, aur jab tak woh node fail nahi hota. Agar tumhe leader ke fail hone ko tolerate karna hai, toh tum wapas consensus problem par aa jaate ho.

Uniqueness checking ko us value par partition karke scale out kiya ja sakta hai jo unique honi chahiye. Agar tumhe request ID se uniqueness chahiye, toh same ID wali saari requests same partition par route kar sakte hain. Agar tumhe usernames unique chahiye, toh tum username ke hash se partition kar sakte ho. Lekin asynchronous multi-leader replication ruled out hai. Alag-alag leaders concurrently conflicting writes accept kar sakte hain, aur tab values unique nahi rahengi. Agar tum aisi har write ko turant reject karna chahte ho jo constraint violate karegi, toh synchronous coordination se bachna mumkin nahi.

Log-based messaging mein uniqueness. Log ensure karta hai ki saare consumers messages same order mein dekhein. Yeh guarantee total order broadcast hai, jo consensus ke equivalent hai. Log-based messaging wale unbundled approach mein ek bahut milta-julta method uniqueness constraints enforce kar sakta hai. Stream processor ek log partition ke saare messages sequentially, ek single thread par consume karta hai. Agar log ko us value se partition kiya gaya hai jo unique honi chahiye, toh stream processor bina ambiguity ke aur deterministically decide kar sakta hai ki kai conflicting operations mein se kaun si pehle aayi.

Example

Kai users ek hi username claim karte hain. Book yeh steps batati hai:

  1. Username ki har request ek message ke roop mein encode hoti hai, aur username ke hash se tay hue partition mein append hoti hai.
  2. Stream processor log mein requests ko order se padhta hai. Woh ek local database mein track rakhta hai ki kaun se usernames le liye gaye hain. Jo naam available hai, use taken record karta hai aur output stream mein success message emit karta hai. Jo naam pehle se taken hai, uske liye rejection message emit karta hai.
  3. Username maangne wala client output stream ko watch karta hai aur apni request se match karne wale success ya rejection ka wait karta hai.

Kyunki ek username ki saari requests same partition mein jaati hain, aur har partition ek time par ek message handle karta hai, isliye jis naam ki request pehle aayi woh jeet jaati hai. Author batate hain ki yeh basically wahi algorithm hai jo total order broadcast se linearizable storage implement karne ke liye hota hai, jo book mein pehle cover hua tha. Partitions badhakar yeh bade request volume tak scale karta hai, kyunki har partition independently process hota hai.

Yeh approach sirf uniqueness constraints ke liye nahi, balki kai aur tarah ke constraints ke liye bhi kaam karta hai. Iska basic principle yeh hai ki jo bhi writes conflict kar sakti hain, unhe same partition par route karke sequentially process kiya jaata hai. Conflict kya maana jaayega, yeh application par depend karta hai, aur stream processor request validate karne ke liye arbitrary logic use kar sakta hai. Author kehte hain ki yeh 1990s mein Bayou ke through pioneer kiye gaye approach jaisa hai.

Multi-partition request processing. Jab kai partitions involved hon, toh constraints satisfy karte hue operation ko atomic banana zyada interesting ho jaata hai. Example 12-2 mein potentially teen partitions hain: ek jisme request ID hai, ek jisme payee ka account hai, aur ek jisme payer ka account hai. Koi wajah nahi ki yeh teen cheezein ek partition share karein, kyunki yeh ek doosre se independent hain.

Traditional database approach mein is transaction ko teeno partitions ke across atomic commit chahiye hota. Isse woh un partitions ko touch karne wale har doosre transaction ke respect mein total order mein aa jaata hai. Partitions ab coordinate kar rahe hain, isliye unhe independently process nahi kiya ja sakta, aur throughput ko nuksaan hone ki possibility hai. Book kehti hai ki partitioned logs ke saath, bina atomic commit ke, equivalent correctness paayi ja sakti hai.

Example

Partitions ke across paisa transfer karna. Steps yeh hain:

  1. Client account A se account B mein paisa transfer karne ki request ko ek unique request ID deta hai. Woh request ko us ID se chune gaye log partition mein append karta hai.
  2. Ek stream processor requests ka log padhta hai. Har request ke liye woh output streams mein do messages emit karta hai: payer A ke liye debit instruction, jo A se partitioned hai, aur payee B ke liye credit instruction, jo B se partitioned hai. Original request ID dono mein jaati hai.
  3. Aage ke processors credit aur debit instructions ki streams consume karte hain, unhe request ID se deduplicate karte hain, aur changes account balances par apply karte hain.

Pehle do steps important hain. Agar client credit aur debit instructions seedhe bhejta, toh use dono partitions ke across atomic commit chahiye hota, taaki ya toh dono ho jaayein ya koi nahi. Iske bajaye request pehle ek single message ke roop mein log hoti hai, aur credit aur debit instructions us message se derive hote hain. Single-object writes lagbhag saare data systems mein atomic hoti hain, isliye request ya toh log mein aati hai ya nahi aati. Multi-partition atomic commit ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Agar step 2 ka stream processor crash ho jaaye, toh woh apne last checkpoint se resume karta hai, jo log mein ek saved position hai. Woh koi request skip nahi karta. Lekin woh kuch requests ko ek se zyada baar process kar sakta hai, aur duplicate credit aur debit instructions produce kar sakta hai. Kyunki woh deterministic hai, woh wahi instructions dobara produce karta hai. Step 3 ke processors phir unhe end-to-end request ID se deduplicate kar sakte hain.

Agar tum yeh bhi ensure karna chahte ho ki transfer se payer overdrawn na ho, toh tum ek stream processor jod sakte ho, jo payer account number se partitioned ho, jo account balances maintain kare aur transactions validate kare. Tab step 1 mein request log mein sirf valid transactions hi daali jaayengi.

Multi-partition transaction ko do alag-alag partitioned stages mein todkar, aur end-to-end request ID use karke, system wahi correctness property hasil kar leta hai. Har request payer aur payee dono accounts par exactly once apply hoti hai, faults ke hote hue bhi, aur atomic commit protocol ke bina. Author batate hain ki kai alag-alag partitioned stages ka idea pehle discuss kiye gaye multi-partition data processing jaisa hai.

Timeliness aur integrity

Transactions ki ek convenient property yeh hai ki woh typically linearizable hote hain. Writer transaction commit hone tak wait karta hai, aur uske baad uski writes saare readers ko turant dikhti hain. Jab operation stream processing ke kai stages mein faila ho, tab aisa nahi hota. Log ke consumers design se asynchronous hote hain, isliye sender wait nahi karta ki uska message process ho gaya ya nahi. Client phir bhi output stream par message aane ka wait karna choose kar sakta hai, jo username example ne kiya tha jab usne check kiya ki uniqueness constraint satisfy hui ya nahi.

Us example mein uniqueness check ki correctness is par depend nahi karti ki sender wait karta hai ya nahi. Wait karna sirf sender ko synchronously batata hai ki check succeed hua ya nahi. Yeh notification message process karne ke effects se decouple ho sakta hai.

Author kehte hain ki consistency term do alag requirements ko jodta hai, jinhe alag-alag dekhna chahiye.

  • Timeliness ka matlab hai ensure karna ki users system ko up-to-date state mein dekhein. Agar user data ki stale copy se read kare, toh use inconsistent state dikh sakti hai. Lekin woh inconsistency temporary hoti hai, aur agar tum wait karke dobara try karo toh khud hi theek ho jaati hai. CAP theorem consistency ko linearizability ke sense mein use karta hai, jo timeliness achieve karne ka ek strong tarika hai. Weaker timeliness properties, jaise read-after-write consistency (apni hi writes dekhna), bhi useful ho sakti hain.
  • Integrity ka matlab hai corruption ka na hona: koi data loss nahi, aur koi contradictory ya false data nahi. Agar koi derived dataset underlying data par view ki tarah maintain hota hai, toh derivation correct honi chahiye. Database index ko database ke contents ko sahi reflect karna chahiye. Jis index mein kuch records missing hon, woh kaafi useful nahi hota. Agar integrity violate ho jaaye, toh inconsistency permanent hoti hai. Zyadatar cases mein wait karke retry karne se corruption theek nahi hota, isliye explicit checking aur repair chahiye. ACID transactions ke context mein consistency ko usually integrity ka application-specific notion samjha jaata hai, aur atomicity aur durability use preserve karne ke important tools hain.

Slogan ke roop mein, timeliness ki violations eventual consistency hain, jabki integrity ki violations perpetual inconsistency hain.

Author ka kehna hai ki zyadatar applications mein integrity timeliness se kaafi zyada important hai. Timeliness ki violations annoying aur confusing ho sakti hain. Integrity ki violations catastrophic ho sakti hain. Credit card statement ka example lo. Agar pichhle 24 ghanton mein hui purchase abhi statement mein nahi dikh rahi, toh koi hairani ki baat nahi, kyunki banks transactions ko asynchronously reconcile aur settle karte hain, aur wahan timeliness kaafi important nahi hai. Lekin yeh bahut bura hoga agar statement balance previous balance plus transactions ke barabar na ho, jo sums mein error hogi. Yeh bhi bura hoga agar tumse aisi purchase ke paise liye jaayein jo merchant ko kabhi pay hi nahi hui, yani paisa gayab ho jaana. Yeh integrity ki violations hain.

Asli idea

Wait karne se timeliness problems theek ho jaati hain, lekin integrity problems theek nahi hotin. Zyadatar applications mein integrity timeliness se zyada matter karti hai, aur yahi woh property hai jise sabse pehle protect karna chahiye.

Dataflow systems ki correctness. ACID transactions usually timeliness, jaise linearizability, aur integrity, jaise atomic commit, dono dete hain. Isliye agar tum correctness ko ACID transactions ke point of view se dekho, toh dono ke beech ka farq kaafi unimportant hai. Lekin event-based dataflow systems inhe decouple kar dete hain. Jab event streams asynchronously process hoti hain, toh timeliness ki koi guarantee nahi hoti, jab tak tum aise consumers na banao jo return karne se pehle message aane ka wait karein. Lekin integrity streaming systems ke liye central hai. Exactly-once, ya effectively-once, semantics integrity preserve karne ka ek mechanism hai. Agar koi event lost ho jaaye, ya do baar effect kare, toh data system ki integrity violate ho sakti hai. Isliye fault-tolerant message delivery aur duplicate suppression, jaise idempotent operations ke through, integrity maintain karne ke liye important hain.

Reliable stream processing distributed transactions ya atomic commit protocol ke bina integrity preserve kar sakti hai. Matlab woh potentially kaafi better performance aur operational robustness ke saath comparable correctness hasil kar sakti hai. Author kehte hain ki yeh integrity kai mechanisms ke combination se aati hai:

  • Write ka content ek single message ke roop mein represent hota hai, jo atomically likha ja sakta hai. Yeh event sourcing ke saath achhe se fit hota hai.
  • Baaki saare state updates us message se deterministic functions se derive hote hain, stored procedures ki tarah.
  • Client-generated request ID processing ke saare levels se pass hoti hai, jo end-to-end duplicate suppression aur idempotence enable karti hai.
  • Messages immutable hote hain, aur derived data ko time-time par reprocess kiya ja sakta hai, jisse bugs se recover karna aasaan ho jaata hai.

Author is combination ko fault-tolerant applications banane ki ek bahut promising direction maante hain.

Loosely interpreted constraints. Traditional uniqueness constraint enforce karne ke liye consensus chahiye, jo typically ek partition ke saare events ko ek single node se guzaarkar implement hota hai. Constraint ke strict form ke liye yeh unavoidable hai, aur stream processing ise avoid nahi kar sakti. Lekin kai real applications uniqueness ke kaafi weaker notions se kaam chala sakti hain:

  • Agar do log concurrently same username register karo, ya same seat book karo, toh tum ek ko message bhej sakte ho jisme maafi maangi jaaye aur kuch alag choose karne ko kaha jaaye. Is tarah galti sudharne ko compensating transaction kehte hain.
  • Agar customers warehouse mein jitne items hain unse zyada order kar do, toh tum aur stock mangwa sakte ho, delay ke liye maafi maang sakte ho, aur discount offer kar sakte ho. Yahi woh cheez hai jo tumhe tab karni padti jab forklift truck kuch items ke upar se guzar jaata aur tumhare paas socha hua se kam bachta. Isliye apology workflow tumhare business processes ka hissa pehle se hona hi chahiye, aur stock par linearizable constraint shayad zaroori na ho.
  • Kai airlines flights overbook karti hain, yeh maan kar ki kuch passengers apni flight miss kar denge. Kai hotels rooms overbook karte hain, yeh maan kar ki kuch guests cancel kar denge. Ek insaan per seat ka rule business reasons se intentionally toda jaata hai, aur compensation, jaise refunds, upgrades ya paas ke hotel mein room, un cases ko handle karta hai jahan demand supply se zyada ho. Overbooking ke bina bhi flights weather ya staff strikes ki wajah se cancel hoti hain, aur us se recover karna business ka normal hissa hai.
  • Agar koi apne paas se zyada paisa withdraw kar le, toh bank overdraft fee laga sakta hai aur use jo bakaya hai woh wapas dene ko keh sakta hai. Din bhar ke total withdrawals limit karke bank apna risk bound kar leta hai.

Kai business contexts mein kisi constraint ko temporarily violate karna aur baad mein maafi maangkar theek karna acceptable hai. Maafi ki keemat, paise ya reputation mein, alag-alag hoti hai, lekin aksar kam hoti hai. Tum email unsend nahi kar sakte, lekin follow-up correction bhej sakte ho. Agar galti se credit card do baar charge ho jaaye, toh tum ek charge refund kar sakte ho, aur tumhari keemat processing fees aur shayad ek complaint hai. Ek baar ATM se paisa nikal jaaye, toh tum use seedhe wapas nahi le sakte, halaanki principle mein overdrawn customer ke peeche, jo pay nahi karta, debt collectors bhej sakte ho.

Maafi ki keemat acceptable hai ya nahi, yeh ek business decision hai. Agar acceptable hai, toh koi bhi data likhne se pehle saare constraints check karne ka traditional model unnecessarily restrictive hai. Optimistically likhna aur constraint baad mein check karna reasonable ho sakta hai. Tum phir bhi yeh pakka kar sakte ho ki validation aisi kisi cheez se pehle ho jise reverse karna expensive ho, lekin iska matlab yeh nahi ki har write se pehle validate karo. In applications ko integrity chahiye. Tum reservation lose nahi karna chahoge, ya mismatched credits aur debits se paisa gayab nahi hona chahiye. Jo unhe nahi chahiye woh constraint enforce karne mein timeliness hai. Agar tumne warehouse mein jitne items hain unse zyada bech diye hain, toh tum baad mein maafi maangkar problem patch kar sakte ho. Yeh book mein pehle discuss kiye gaye conflict resolution approaches jaisa hai.

Coordination-avoiding data systems. Author do observations karte hain. Pehla, dataflow systems derived data par integrity guarantees atomic commit, linearizability ya synchronous cross-partition coordination ke bina maintain kar sakte hain. Doosra, strict uniqueness constraints ko timeliness aur coordination chahiye, lekin kai applications loose constraints se theek hain jo temporarily violate ho sakte hain aur baad mein fix ho sakte hain, bas shart yeh hai ki integrity poore time preserve rahe.

Dono ko milakar dekhein toh dataflow systems kai applications ko bina coordination ke data management de sakte hain, aur phir bhi strong integrity guarantees de sakte hain. Aise coordination-avoiding data systems mein kaafi appeal hai, kyunki woh un systems se behtar performance aur fault tolerance hasil kar sakte hain jinhe synchronous coordination chahiye. Maan lo ek system kai datacenters mein multi-leader configuration mein chalta hai, aur regions ke beech asynchronously replicate karta hai. Koi bhi ek datacenter independently chalta reh sakta hai, kyunki synchronous cross-region coordination ki zaroorat nahi. Aise system mein timeliness weak hogi. Coordination jode bina woh linearizable nahi ho sakta. Lekin phir bhi uski integrity strong ho sakti hai.

Aise system mein serializable transactions derived state maintain karne ke liye abhi bhi useful hain, lekin woh chhote scope par chal sakte hain jahan woh achhe se kaam karte hain. XA jaise heterogeneous distributed transactions ki zaroorat nahi. Synchronous coordination ko wahan phir bhi introduce kiya ja sakta hai jahan chahiye, jaise kisi aise operation se pehle strict constraint enforce karne ke liye jisse recovery possible nahi hai. Lekin sabko coordination ki keemat chukane ki zaroorat nahi agar application ka sirf ek chhota hissa use maangta hai.

Author trade-off ko dekhne ka ek aur tarika dete hain. Coordination aur constraints inconsistencies ki wajah se tumhe jitni maafi maangni padti hai woh kam karte hain. Lekin woh performance aur availability bhi kam kar sakte hain, jisse outages ki wajah se maafi maangne ki count badh sakti hai. Tum maafi ko zero tak nahi la sakte. Maqsad woh sweet spot dhoondhna hai jahan na bahut zyada inconsistencies hon, na bahut zyada availability problems.

Trade-offs
ApproachKahan achha haiKeemat
Systems ke across distributed transactions (jaise XA)Strong timeliness aur systems ke across atomic changes. Readers ko committed writes turant dikhti hain.Fault tolerance aur performance kamzor. Ek participant ki failure baaki ko stall ya abort kar sakti hai, aur protocol ko har involved system support karna padta hai.
Idempotent consumers ke saath log-based derived dataLoose coupling. Faults contained rehte hain, teams independently kaam karti hain, aur design alag-alag products ke across chalta hai.Updates asynchronous hain, isliye default mein timeliness ki koi guarantee nahi. Tumhe stale reads handle karne padte hain aur idempotence khud banana padta hai.
Constraints baad mein check karein, aur zaroorat par maafi maang leinWrite path par koi coordination nahi, isliye writes fast hain aur partitions ke dauran system available rehta hai.Violations users ko dikhte hain. Maafi aur compensation mein paisa ya reputation lagti hai, aur business ke paas uske liye process hona chahiye.

Trust karo, lekin verify bhi karo

Ab tak hum maan kar chal rahe the ki kuch cheezein galat ho sakti hain aur kuch nahi hongi. Yeh assumptions milkar system model banate hain. Jaise hum maante hain ki process crash ho sakte hain, machine ki power achanak ja sakti hai, aur network message delay ya drop kar sakta hai. Hum yeh bhi maante hain ki fsync (ek command jo data ko zabardasti disk par likhwa deti hai) ke baad disk par likha data lost nahi hota, memory ka data corrupt nahi hota, aur CPU ka multiplication instruction hamesha sahi result deta hai.

Yeh assumptions reasonable hain. Zyada-tar time yeh sahi hote hain, aur agar hum hamesha yahi sochte rahein ki computer galti kar dega, toh kaam hi nahi ho paayega. Traditionally system models faults ko binary tarike se dekhte hain: kuch cheezein ho sakti hain, aur kuch kabhi nahi hoti. Asal mein yeh probabilities ka sawaal hai. Kuch cheezein zyada likely hain, kuch kam. Asli sawaal yeh hai ki hamare assumptions kitni baar tootte hain, kya itni baar ki practice mein hamara unse saamna ho jaaye.

Data disk par pada-pada bhi corrupt ho sakta hai. Network par hui corruption kabhi-kabhi TCP checksums se bhi bach nikalti hai. Shayad is baat ko jitna dhyaan milta hai, usse zyada milna chahiye. Author ek application ka example dete hain jis par woh kabhi kaam kar chuke hain, jo clients se crash reports collect karti thi. Kuch reports ka koi explanation nahi tha, siwaye is ke ki un devices ki memory mein random bit flips hue honge. Yeh unlikely lagta hai, lekin agar tumhara software kaafi saare devices par chal raha hai, toh bahut unlikely cheezein bhi ho jaati hain. Hardware faults ya radiation se hone wali random memory corruption ke alawa, kuch memory access patterns aise bhi hain jo bina fault wali memory mein bhi bits flip kar dete hain. Is effect ko rowhammer kehte hain, aur isse operating systems ke security mechanisms tod diye gaye hain. Dhyaan se dekhein toh hardware utni perfect abstraction nahi hai jitni woh lagti hai.

Author yeh bhi jodte hain ki modern hardware par random bit flips abhi bhi bahut rare hain. Woh bas yeh batana chahte hain ki yeh namumkin nahi hain, isliye thoda dhyaan dena banta hai.

Software bugs ke beech integrity bachana

Hardware problems ke alawa software bugs ka risk hamesha rehta hai. Aise bugs lower-level network, memory ya filesystem checksums se bhi nikal jaate hain. Jo database software bahut use hota hai, usme bhi bugs hote hain. Author ne khud dekha hai ki MySQL ek uniqueness constraint ko sahi se maintain nahi kar paaya. Unhone PostgreSQL ke serializable isolation level mein write skew anomalies bhi dekhi hain, jahan do transactions ek doosre ka badla hua data read karte hain, aur dono commit ho jaate hain. MySQL aur PostgreSQL robust aur well-regarded databases hain, jinhe kaafi saalon se bahut log battle-test kar chuke hain. Kam mature software mein haal shayad aur kharab hoga. Careful design, testing aur review ke baad bhi bugs aa hi jaate hain. Woh rare hote hain, aur aakhir mein pakde aur fix ho jaate hain, lekin ek period aisa hota hai jab woh data corrupt kar sakte hain.

Application code ka review aur testing database code se bahut kam hota hai, isliye author maante hain ki wahan bugs kahin zyada honge. Bahut saari applications toh database ke woh features sahi se use bhi nahi karti jo integrity bachate hain, jaise foreign key ya uniqueness constraints. ACID consistency is idea par based hai ki database ek consistent state se shuru hota hai, aur har transaction use doosri consistent state mein le jaata hai. Yeh tabhi samajh mein aata hai jab transaction bug-free ho. Agar application database ko galat tarike se use karti hai, jaise weak isolation level par unsafe tarike se depend karna, toh database ki integrity guarantee nahi ho sakti.

Jo promise kiya gaya hai, us par andha bharosa mat karo

Hardware aur software dono ideal se kam hain, isliye author ke hisaab se corruption der-saver hogi hi. Toh kam se kam hamare paas yeh pata karne ka tarika hona chahiye ki data corrupt hua hai ya nahi, taaki hum use fix kar sakein aur error ka source dhoondh sakein. Data ki integrity check karne ko auditing kehte hain. Chapter 11 mein immutable events ki baat karte hue dikhaya gaya tha ki auditing sirf financial applications ke liye nahi hai. Lekin finance mein auditability khaas taur par zaroori hai, kyunki sabko pata hai ki galtiyan hoti hain, aur sab maante hain ki problems detect aur fix karne ki ability honi chahiye.

Mature systems aam taur par unlikely cheezein galat hone ka bhi plan rakhte hain. HDFS aur Amazon S3 jaise bade storage systems apni disks par poora bharosa nahi karte. Woh background processes chalate hain jo files ko baar-baar read karke dekhte hain, unhe doosre replicas se compare karte hain, aur files ko ek disk se doosri disk par move karte hain, taaki silent corruption ka risk kam ho. Sabke liye seekh yahi hai. Agar tumhe pakka karna hai ki data abhi bhi present hai, toh tumhe use sach mein read karke check karna padega. Zyada-tar time woh sahi niklega. Lekin agar nahi hai, toh tum chahoge ki jaldi pata chale, der se nahi. Isi logic se, tumhe time-time par apne backups se restore karke dekhna chahiye. Warna ho sakta hai ki backup toot chuka ho aur tumhe tab pata chale jab bahut der ho chuki ho aur data lost ho gaya ho. Bas andhe bharose par mat chalein ki sab kuch theek kaam kar raha hai.

Verification ka culture

HDFS aur S3 jaise systems ko bhi yeh maanna padta hai ki disks zyada-tar time sahi kaam karti hain. Yeh reasonable assumption hai, lekin yeh maanne se alag hai ki woh hamesha sahi kaam karti hain. Bahut kam systems mein yeh trust-but-verify approach hai ki woh khud ko continually audit karein. Kai systems maan lete hain ki correctness guarantees absolute hain, aur rare data corruption ki possibility ke liye koi provision nahi rakhte. Author ko umeed hai ki aage chal kar hum aise zyada self-validating aur self-auditing systems dekhenge jo andhe bharose ke bajaye apni integrity khud continually check karte rahein.

Unhe darr hai ki ACID databases ke culture ki wajah se developers ne applications technology par andhe bharose se bana di, jaise transaction mechanism par, aur is chakkar mein auditability ko ignore kar diya. Technology zyada-tar time kaafi achha kaam karti thi, isliye auditing mein investment karna zaroori nahi laga. Phir database landscape badal gaya. NoSQL ke naam par weaker consistency guarantees aam ho gaye, aur kam mature storage technologies bade level par use hone lagi. Audit mechanisms develop nahi hue the, isliye applications andhe bharose par hi chalti rahi, jo ab pehle se zyada khatarnak ho gaya tha. Isi wajah se auditability ke liye design karne ke baare mein dhyaan se sochna chahiye.

Auditability ke liye design karna

Agar ek transaction database ke kai objects badalta hai, toh baad mein yeh batana mushkil hai ki us transaction ka matlab kya tha. CDC se transaction logs capture kar bhi lein, toh alag-alag tables mein hue inserts, updates aur deletes se zaroori nahi ki yeh pata chale ki yeh changes kyun kiye gaye. Jis application logic ne changes decide kiye, woh transient tha, aur use dobara reproduce nahi kiya ja sakta.

Event-based systems better auditability de sakte hain. Event sourcing mein user input ek single immutable event ke roop mein record hota hai, aur uske baad ke saare state updates usi event se derive hote hain. Is derivation ko deterministic aur repeatable banaya ja sakta hai. Matlab events ka wahi log, derivation code ke wahi version se chalaoge, toh wahi state updates milenge. Book mein pehle batch outputs ki discussion mein dataflow ko explicit rakhne par zor diya gaya tha, aur isse data ki provenance (data kahan se aaya) bahut clear ho jaati hai, jisse integrity checking kaafi feasible ho jaati hai. Event log ke liye tum hashes use karke check kar sakte ho ki event storage corrupt nahi hui. Kisi bhi derived state ke liye tum woh batch aur stream processes dobara chala sakte ho jinhone use event log se derive kiya tha, aur dekh sakte ho ki same result milta hai ya nahi. Tum chaho toh ek redundant derivation parallel mein bhi chala sakte ho.

Deterministic aur well-defined dataflow se system ko debug aur trace karna bhi aasaan ho jaata hai, taaki pata chale ki usne woh kyun kiya. Agar kuch unexpected hua, toh un exact circumstances ko reproduce kar paana bahut valuable hai jinki wajah se woh hua. Author ise ek tarah ki time-travel debugging capability kehte hain.

End-to-end argument phir se

Agar hum poore bharose se nahi keh sakte ki har component corruption-free hai, har disk fault-free hai aur har program bug-free hai, toh kam se kam hamein apne data ki integrity periodically check karni chahiye. Agar hum check nahi karenge, toh corruption ka tab tak pata nahi chalega jab tak woh downstream damage na kar de, aur tab use track karna kahin zyada mushkil aur mehenga hota hai. Integrity checking end to end karna sabse behtar hai, jaisa pehle discuss hua tha. Integrity check jitne zyada systems cover karta hai, utne hi kam chance rehte hain ki corruption kisi stage par unnoticed nikal jaaye. Agar tum check kar sakte ho ki poori derived data pipeline end to end sahi hai, toh raaste ki har disk, network, service aur algorithm apne aap us check mein shaamil ho jaati hai.

Continuous end-to-end integrity checks se tumhe apne systems ke sahi hone par zyada confidence milta hai, aur isse tum tezi se aage badh sakte ho. Automated testing ki tarah auditing bhi bugs jaldi pakde jaane ke chances badhati hai, jisse system mein change ya nayi storage technology se damage hone ka risk kam ho jaata hai. Agar tumhe changes karne se darr nahi lagta, toh badalti requirements ke hisaab se application ko kaafi aasaani se evolve kar sakte hain.

Auditable data systems ke liye tools

Abhi bahut kam data systems auditability ko top-level concern banate hain. Kuch applications apne khud ke audit mechanisms bana leti hain, jaise saare changes ko ek alag audit table mein log karke. Lekin audit log aur database state, dono ki integrity guarantee karna phir bhi mushkil hai. Transaction log ko tamper-proof banaya ja sakta hai, hardware security module (ek tamper-resistant device jisme signing keys rehti hain) se use periodically sign karke. Lekin isse yeh guarantee nahi hoti ki sahi transactions pehli jagah log mein gaye the.

Author ka kehna hai ki cryptographic tools shayad system ki integrity aise prove kar sakein jo hardware aur software ki kaafi saari problems, aur malicious actions ke saamne bhi robust ho. Isi ko explore karne ke liye cryptocurrencies, blockchains aur distributed ledger technologies aaye hain, jaise Bitcoin, Ethereum, Ripple aur Stellar. Author khud ko inhe currency ya contracts par agree karne ke tarike ke roop mein judge karne ke qualified nahi maante. Lekin data systems ke point of view se inme interesting ideas hain. Asal mein yeh distributed databases hain, jinka ek data model aur transaction mechanism hota hai, aur jinke alag-alag replicas aise organizations host kar sakte hain jo ek doosre par trust nahi karte. Replicas ek doosre ki integrity continually check karte hain, aur consensus protocol use karke tay karte hain ki kaun se transactions execute karne hain.

Byzantine fault tolerance wale hisse ko le kar woh thode skeptical hain, jo un nodes ko handle karta hai jo jhooth bolte hain ya malicious tarike se behave karte hain. Proof-of-work technique, jaise Bitcoin mining, unhe bahut zyada wasteful lagti hai. Bitcoin ka transaction throughput bhi kaafi kam hai, jiski wajah mainly political aur economic hai, technical nahi. Lekin integrity-checking wale hisse interesting hain.

Cryptographic auditing aur integrity checking mein aksar Merkle trees use hote hain. Yeh hashes ke trees hote hain jo, aur cheezon ke saath, efficiently prove kar sakte hain ki koi record kisi dataset mein hai. Cryptocurrencies ke hype se bahar, certificate transparency ek security technology hai jo TLS/SSL certificates ki validity check karne ke liye Merkle trees par depend karti hai. Author imagine kar sakte hain ki certificate transparency aur distributed ledgers jaise integrity-checking aur auditing algorithms data systems mein zyada widely use hone lagein. Unhe un systems jitna scalable banane ke liye, jinme cryptographic auditing nahi hai, aur performance penalty kam rakhne ke liye kuch kaam karna padega. Lekin unhe lagta hai ki yeh dekhne laayak interesting area hai.

Sahi kaam karna

Aakhri section mein author thoda peeche hat kar bade picture ko dekhte hain. Poori book mein humne data systems ke liye kaafi alag-alag architectures dekhe, unke pros aur cons tole, aur reliable, scalable aur maintainable applications banane ki techniques explore ki. Lekin discussion ka ek important aur fundamental hissa humne chhod diya, aur woh ab us gap ko bharna chahte hain.

Har system kisi purpose ke liye banta hai, aur har action ke intended aur unintended consequences hote hain. Purpose paise kamane jitna simple ho sakta hai, lekin duniya par uske consequences usse kahin aage tak pahunch sakte hain. Jo engineers yeh systems banate hain, unki zimmedari hai ki woh un consequences ke baare mein dhyaan se sochein, aur soch-samajh kar decide karein ki woh kaisi duniya mein rehna chahte hain.

Hum data ko ek abstract cheez ki tarah baat karte hain. Lekin bahut saare datasets logon ke baare mein hote hain: unka behavior, unki interests aur unki identity. Us data ke saath humein insaniyat aur respect se pesh aana chahiye. Users bhi insaan hain, aur human dignity sabse upar hai.

Software development mein ab zyada se zyada important ethical choices karne padte hain. Engineers ki madad ke liye guidelines available hain, jaise ACM ka Software Engineering Code of Ethics and Professional Practice. Lekin practice mein unki baat kam hoti hai, unhe kam apply kiya jaata hai aur kam enforce kiya jaata hai. Nateeja yeh hai ki engineers aur product managers kabhi-kabhi privacy aur apne products ke possible negative consequences ke prati laparwah rawaiya rakhte hain.

Koi technology apne aap mein achhi ya buri nahi hoti. Matter yeh karta hai ki use kaise use kiya jaata hai aur logon par uska kya asar padta hai. Yeh baat search engine jaise software system par bhi utni hi lagu hoti hai jitni ek weapon par. Author ko lagta hai ki software engineers ka sirf technology par focus karna aur uske consequences ko ignore karna kaafi nahi hai. Ethical responsibility unki bhi hai. Ethics ke baare mein reason karna mushkil hai, lekin yeh itna important hai ki ise ignore nahi kiya ja sakta.

Predictive analytics

Predictive analytics big data hype ka ek bada hissa hai. Data analysis se mausam ya kisi beemari ke phailne ka andaza lagana ek baat hai. Yeh predict karna ki koi convicted insaan dobara jurm karega ya nahi, koi loan applicant default karega ya nahi, ya koi insurance customer mehenge claims karega ya nahi, bilkul doosri baat hai. Yeh predictions seedhe individual logon ki zindagi par asar daalti hain.

Payment networks fraudulent transactions rokna chahte hain. Banks bad loans se bachna chahte hain. Airlines hijackings se bachna chahti hain. Companies ineffective ya untrustworthy logon ko hire karne se bachna chahti hain. Unke nazariye se, ek business opportunity miss hone ki cost kam hai, lekin bad loan ya problematic employee ki cost kahin zyada hai. Isliye organizations ka cautious rehna natural hai. Shak ho toh unke liye no kehna hi behtar hai.

Lekin jaise-jaise algorithmic decision-making failti ja rahi hai, jise algorithm ne risky label kar diya hai, chahe sahi ho ya galat, use kaafi saare no decisions jhelne pad sakte hain. Jobs, air travel, insurance, rental housing, financial services aur society ke doosre key hisson se systematically bahar kar diya jaana personal freedom par bahut bada constraint hai. Is situation ke liye book algorithmic prison term cite karti hai. Jin countries mein human rights ki izzat hoti hai, wahan criminal justice system maanta hai ki jab tak guilt prove na ho, insaan innocent hai. Automated systems kisi ko bina guilt ke proof ke, aur appeal ke bahut kam chance ke saath, society mein hissa lene se rok sakte hain.

Bias aur discrimination. Algorithm ke decisions zaroori nahi ki insaan ke decisions se behtar ya kharab hon. Har insaan mein biases hote hain, chahe woh unhe counter karne ki koshish karein, aur discriminatory practices culturally institutionalized ho sakti hain. Ummeed hai ki subjective aur instinctive judgments ke bajaye data par decisions lene se zyada fair ho sakta hai, aur un logon ko behtar mauka mil sakta hai jinhe traditional system aksar nazarandaaz kar deta hai.

Lekin jab hum predictive analytics systems banate hain, toh hum sirf kisi insaan ke decision ko automate nahi kar rahe hote, yani yeh rules likhkar ki kab yes kehna hai aur kab no. Hum rules ko hi data se infer hone ke liye chhod dete hain. Yeh systems jo patterns seekhte hain, woh opaque hote hain. Data mein koi correlation ho bhi, toh hamein pata nahi hota ki kyun. Agar input mein koi systematic bias hai, toh system bahut zyada chance hai ki us bias ko seekh lega aur apne output mein use amplify kar dega.

Kai countries ke anti-discrimination laws ethnicity, age, gender, sexuality, disability ya beliefs jaise protected traits ke base par logon ke saath alag behavior karne ko mana karte hain. Insaan ke data ke doosre features analyze kiye ja sakte hain, lekin agar woh protected traits se correlated hon toh kya hoga? Racially segregated neighborhoods mein insaan ka postal code, ya uska IP address bhi, race ka strong predictor hota hai. Yeh maanna hi hasyaspad lagta hai ki algorithm biased data input lega aur fair aur impartial output dega. Phir bhi data-driven decision making ke supporters aksar yahi baat imply karte hain. Is attitude ka ek satirical description machine learning ko bias ke liye money laundering se compare karta hai.

Predictive analytics systems bas past se extrapolate karte hain. Agar past discriminatory tha, toh yeh us discrimination ko codify kar dete hain. Agar hum chahte hain ki future past se behtar ho, toh moral imagination chahiye, aur woh sirf insaan de sakte hain. Data aur models hamare tools hone chahiye, hamare maalik nahi.

Responsibility aur accountability. Automated decision making yeh sawaal uthati hai ki zimmedar kaun hai aur kisse jawab maanga ja sakta hai. Agar insaan galti karta hai, toh use accountable thehraya ja sakta hai, aur jis par asar pada woh appeal kar sakta hai. Algorithms bhi galtiyan karte hain, lekin jab woh galat hon toh accountable kaun hai? Jab self-driving car accident kar de, toh zimmedar kaun hai? Agar koi automated credit-scoring algorithm kisi khaas race ya religion ke logon ke saath systematically discriminate karta hai, toh kya koi recourse hai? Agar tumhare machine learning system ka koi decision judicial review mein aa jaaye, toh kya tum judge ko samjha sakte ho ki algorithm us decision tak kaise pahuncha?

Credit rating agencies logon ke baare mein decisions lene ke liye data collect karne ka ek puraana example hain. Bura credit score zindagi mushkil bana deta hai. Lekin credit score aam taur par insaan ki asli borrowing history ke relevant facts par based hota hai, aur record mein koi error ho toh use sahi karwaya ja sakta hai, halaanki agencies aksar ise aasaan nahi banati. Machine learning par based scoring algorithms aam taur par kahin zyada alag-alag inputs use karte hain, aur woh kahin zyada opaque hote hain. Isse yeh samajhna mushkil ho jaata hai ki koi particular decision kaise bana, aur kya kisi ke saath anyay ho raha hai.

Credit score yeh summarize karta hai ki tumne past mein kaise behave kiya. Predictive analytics aksar ek alag basis par kaam karta hai: tumhare jaise kaun log hain, aur tum jaise logon ne kaise behave kiya? Isse doosre logon ke behavior se parallels nikalte hain, jo stereotyping imply karta hai, jaise tum kahan rehte ho uske base par, jo race aur socioeconomic class ka close proxy hai. Jo log galat bucket mein daal diye jaate hain, unka kya? Aur agar data galat hone ki wajah se koi decision incorrect hai, toh recourse lagbhag namumkin hai.

Bahut saara data statistical nature ka hota hai. Poori probability distribution sahi ho, tab bhi individual cases galat ho sakte hain. Agar tumhare country mein average life expectancy 80 saal hai, toh iska matlab yeh nahi ki tum se umeed hai ki tum apne 80ve birthday par mar jaaoge. Average aur distribution se tum yeh nahi keh sakte ki ek particular insaan kitna jiyega. Isi tarah prediction system ka output probabilistic hota hai, aur individual cases mein woh galat ho sakta hai.

Author ke hisaab se, decisions lene ke liye data ki supremacy mein andha vishwas sirf delusional nahi hai. Yeh khatarnak hai. Jaise-jaise data-driven decision making failti hai, humein algorithms ko accountable aur transparent banana hoga, existing biases ko reinforce hone se bachana hoga, aur jab woh galtiyan karein (jo woh karenge hi) toh unhe fix karna hoga. Humein data ko logon ko nuksaan pahunchane ke liye use hone se bhi rokna hoga, aur uski positive potential ko realize karna hoga. Analytics logon ki zindagi ke financial aur social characteristics reveal kar sakta hai. Ek taraf, yeh taakat un logon tak madad pahunchane par focus kar sakti hai jinhe sabse zyada zaroorat hai. Doosri taraf, kabhi-kabhi ise predatory businesses use karte hain jo vulnerable logon ko dhoondhte hain taaki unhe risky products bech sakein, jaise high-cost loans aur bekaar college degrees.

Feedback loops. Jin predictive applications ke effects itne door-door tak nahi jaate, jaise recommendation systems, unmein bhi mushkil issues aate hain. Jab services yeh predict karne mein achhi ho jaati hain ki users kaunsa content dekhna chahte hain, toh ho sakta hai woh logon ko sirf wahi opinions dikhane lagein jinse woh pehle se agree karte hain. Isse echo chambers ban sakte hain, jahan stereotypes, misinformation aur polarization panapte hain. Author kehte hain ki hum election campaigns par social media echo chambers ka asar pehle hi dekh rahe hain.

Jab predictive analytics logon ki zindagi ko affect karta hai, toh self-reinforcing feedback loops khaas taur par pernicious problems khadi kar sakte hain. Maan lo employers potential hires ko evaluate karne ke liye credit scores use karte hain. Ho sakta hai tum achhe worker hon aur tumhara credit score bhi achha ho, aur phir achanak tumhare control se bahar ki kisi museebat ki wajah se tum financial difficulty mein aa jaao. Jaise-jaise tum payments miss karte ho, tumhara score girta hai, aur tumhe kaam milne ke chance kam ho jaate hain. Berozgaari tumhe garibi ki taraf dhakelti hai, jisse score aur kharab hota hai, aur kaam dhoondhna aur mushkil ho jaata hai. Author ise ek downward spiral kehte hain, jo mathematical rigor aur data ke camouflage ke peeche chhupe zehreele assumptions se chalti hai.

Hum hamesha predict nahi kar sakte ki feedback loops kab banenge. Lekin kai consequences pehle se dekhe ja sakte hain, agar hum poore system ke baare mein sochein, sirf uske computerized hisse ke baare mein nahi, balki un logon ke baare mein bhi jo uske saath interact karte hain. Book ise systems thinking kehti hai. Hum samajhne ki koshish kar sakte hain ki data analysis system alag-alag behaviors, structures ya characteristics par kaise respond karta hai. Kya woh logon ke beech ke existing differences ko reinforce aur amplify karta hai, jisse ameer aur ameer, aur gareeb aur gareeb hota hai? Ya woh anyay se ladne ki koshish karta hai? Best intentions ke saath bhi, humein unintended consequences se saavdhaan rehna chahiye.

Privacy aur tracking

Predictive analytics ki problems ke alawa, jo data se logon ke baare mein automated decisions leta hai, data collection mein bhi ethical problems hain. Data collect karne wale organizations aur jin logon ka data collect ho raha hai, unke beech ka relationship kya hai?

Jab koi system sirf wahi data store karta hai jo user ne explicitly enter kiya hai, kyunki woh chahta hai ki system use ek khaas tarike se store aur process kare, toh system user ke liye ek service perform kar raha hai, aur user customer hai. Lekin jab user ki activity uske doosre kaamon ke side effect ke taur par track aur log hoti hai, toh relationship itna clear nahi rehta. Service ab sirf wahi nahi karti jo user use karne ko kehta hai. Uski apni interests ban jaati hain, jo user ki interests se conflict kar sakti hain.

Kai online services ke user-facing features ke liye behavioral data track karna important ho gaya hai. Kaun se search results click hue, yeh track karne se unki ranking improve karne mein madad milti hai. Yeh recommend karna ki jinhe X pasand aaya unhe Y bhi pasand aaya, users ko interesting cheezein discover karne mein madad karta hai. A/B tests aur user flow analysis dikhane mein madad karte hain ki interface kaise behtar ho sakta hai. In features ke liye kuch tracking chahiye, aur users ko unse fayda hota hai.

Lekin company ke business model par depend karte hue, tracking aksar yahin nahi rukti. Agar service advertising se funded hai, toh advertisers hi asli customers hain, aur users ki interests doosre number par aa jaati hain. Tracking aur detailed ho jaati hai, analyses aur door tak jaate hain, aur marketing ke liye har insaan ki detailed profile banane ke liye data lambe time tak rakha jaata hai. Tab company aur user ka relationship kaafi alag dikhne lagta hai. User ko ek free service di jaati hai aur use fusla kar zyada se zyada engage karwaya jaata hai. Tracking individual se zyada un advertisers ke kaam aati hai jo service ko fund karte hain. Author ka argument hai ki is relationship ko best describe karne wala word zyada sinister connotations rakhta hai: surveillance.

Surveillance. Ek thought experiment ke taur par, data word ki jagah surveillance likh kar dekhein aur check karein ki aam phrases ab bhi achhe lagte hain ya nahi. Try karein: hamara surveillance-driven organization real-time surveillance streams collect karta hai, unhe surveillance warehouse mein store karta hai, aur naye insights nikalne ke liye surveillance scientists use karta hai. Author maante hain ki is book ke liye yeh ek unusually polemic tone hai, lekin unhe lagta hai ki apni baat rakhne ke liye strong words zaroori hain.

Software ko duniya par chhane ki apni koshishon mein humne ab tak ka sabse bada mass surveillance infrastructure bana liya hai jo duniya ne dekha hai. Internet of Things ki taraf bhaagte hue, hum tezi se ek aisi duniya ke kareeb pahunch rahe hain jahan har aabaad jagah mein kam se kam ek internet-connected microphone hoga. In devices mein smartphones, smart TVs, voice-controlled assistants, baby monitors, aur bachchon ke woh khilaune bhi shaamil hain jo cloud-based speech recognition use karte hain. In mein se bahut saare devices ka security record bahut kharab hai.

Sabse totalitarian aur repressive regimes bhi bas yeh sapna hi dekh sakte the ki har kamre mein microphone ho, aur har insaan ko aisa device carry karne par majboor kiya jaaye jo uski location aur movements track kare. Phir bhi lagta hai ki hum khud, apni marzi se aur josh ke saath bhi, total surveillance ki is duniya mein kood pade hain. Fark yeh hai ki data government agencies ke bajaye corporations collect karte hain.

Har data collection surveillance nahi hoti, lekin use us nazariye se dekhne se data collector ke saath hamare relationship ko samajhne mein madad milti hai. Hum corporations ki surveillance ko khushi-khushi kyun accept kar lete hain? Ek wajah yeh belief hai ki tumhare paas chhupane ko kuch nahi hai. Author batate hain ki yeh maanna hai ki tum existing power structures ke poori tarah saath hain, tum koi marginalized minority nahi ho, aur tumhe persecution ka darr nahi hai, aur har koi itna kismatwala nahi hota. Ek aur wajah yeh hai ki purpose benign lagta hai. Yeh khuli zabardasti aur conformance nahi hai, bas better recommendations aur zyada personalized marketing hai. Lekin predictive analytics ki discussion ke saath jodein toh yeh fark kaafi kam clear lagta hai.

Car insurance premiums pehle se hi cars ke tracking devices se jude hain, aur kuch health insurance coverage fitness tracker pehenne par depend karti hai. Jab surveillance ka use un cheezon ko tay karne ke liye hota hai jo zindagi ke important hisson par asar rakhti hain, jaise insurance coverage ya employment, toh woh benign kam hi lagti hai. Data analysis kaafi chaunkane wali intrusive cheezein bhi reveal kar sakta hai. Smartwatch ya fitness tracker ka movement sensor use karke kaafi achhi accuracy se pata lagaya ja sakta hai ki tum kya type kar rahe ho, jaise passwords. Aur analysis algorithms aur behtar hi hote jaayenge.

Consent aur freedom of choice. Ek argument yeh hai ki users apni marzi se aisi service use karna chunte hain jo unki activity track karti hai. Unhone uske terms of service aur privacy policy se agree kiya hai, isliye woh data collection ke liye consent dete hain. Kuch log yeh bhi jodte hain ki users ko apne data ke badle mein ek valuable service milti hai, aur woh service dene ke liye tracking zaroori hai. Social networks, search engines aur doosri free online services users ke liye waakai valuable hain. Lekin is argument mein problems hain.

Users ko bahut kam pata hota hai ki woh databases mein kaunsa data daal rahe hain, ya use kaise retain aur process kiya jaata hai. Zyada-tar privacy policies roshni daalne se zyada cheezein dhundhli karti hain. Yeh samjhe bina ki unke data ke saath kya hota hai, users koi meaningful consent nahi de sakte. Aksar ek user ka data un doosre logon ke baare mein bhi cheezein batata hai jo us service ke user nahi hain aur jinhone kisi terms se agree nahi kiya. Book ke is part mein jo derived datasets discuss hue, jahan poore user base ka data behavioral tracking aur external data sources ke saath mila diya jaata hai, woh bilkul aise hi data hain jinhe users meaningfully samajh hi nahi sakte.

Aur toh aur, users se data ek one-way process se nikala jaata hai, na ki true reciprocity wale relationship se, aur na hi fair value exchange se. Koi dialog nahi hota, aur users ke paas yeh negotiate karne ka option nahi hota ki kis service ke badle kitna data dein. Relationship bahut asymmetric hai. Terms service tay karti hai, user nahi.

Jo user surveillance ke liye consent nahi deta, uske paas ek hi asli alternative hai ki woh service use hi na kare. Lekin yeh choice bhi free nahi hai. Agar koi service itni popular hai ki zyada-tar log use basic social participation ke liye zaroori maante hain, toh logon se yeh umeed rakhna ki woh opt out karein reasonable nahi hai. Use karna asal mein mandatory ho jaata hai. Zyada-tar Western social communities mein smartphone rakhna, socializing ke liye Facebook use karna, aur jaankari dhoondhne ke liye Google use karna norm ban gaya hai. Khaaskar jab kisi service mein network effects hon, yani jitne zyada log judte hain woh utni hi zyada useful hoti jaati hai, toh use na chunne ki ek social cost hoti hai.

Tracking ki wajah se kisi service ko use karne se mana kar dena sirf un thode se logon ke liye ek option hai jo itne privileged hain ki unke paas privacy policy samajhne ka time aur knowledge hai, aur jo us social participation ya professional opportunities ke miss hone ka bojh utha sakte hain jo us service ko use karne se mil sakti thi. Jo log kam privileged position mein hain, unke liye koi meaningful freedom of choice nahi hai. Surveillance se bachna namumkin ho jaata hai.

Privacy aur data ka use. Kabhi-kabhi log kehte hain ki privacy mar chuki hai, kyunki kuch users social media par apni zindagi ke har tarah ke baare mein post karne ko tayyar hain, kuch mundane aur kuch bahut personal. Author kehte hain ki yeh claim galat hai, aur yeh privacy word ko galat samajhne par based hai. Privacy hone ka matlab har cheez ko secret rakhna nahi hai. Matlab yeh hai ki tumhe freedom ho ki tum chuno kaunsi cheezein kisko batani hain, kya public karna hai, aur kya secret rakhna hai. Privacy ka right ek decision right hai. Isse har insaan decide kar sakta hai ki har situation mein woh secrecy aur transparency ke spectrum par kahan rehna chahta hai. Yeh insaan ki freedom aur autonomy ka ek important hissa hai.

Jab surveillance infrastructure ke through logon se data nikala jaata hai, toh privacy rights zaroori nahi ki khatam ho jaayein. Woh data collector ko transfer ho jaate hain. Jo companies data acquire karti hain, woh asal mein users se keh rahi hoti hain ki woh us data ke saath unpar bharosa karein. Kya reveal karna hai aur kya secret rakhna hai, yeh decide karne ka right individual se company ke paas chala jaata hai.

Companies badle mein is surveillance ke zyada-tar nateeje ko secret rakhti hain, kyunki use reveal karna creepy lagega aur us business ko nuksaan pahunchayega jo doosri companies se zyada logon ke baare mein jaanne par depend karta hai. Users ke baare mein intimate information sirf indirectly reveal hoti hai, jaise un tools mein jo advertisements ko khaas groups tak target karte hain, jaise kisi khaas beemari se jooojhne wale log. Ad jis group ko target karta hai, usme se kisi particular user ko personally identify na bhi kiya ja sake, tab bhi woh intimate information ke disclosure par apni agency kho chuka hai, jaise ki woh kisi beemari se peedit hai ya nahi. Yeh user nahi decide karta ki kisko kya reveal hoga. Yeh company decide karti hai, apne profit ko maximize karne ke liye privacy right ka use karte hue.

Kai companies creepy dikhne se bachna chahti hain. Woh is par focus karti hain ki user perceptions manage ho jaayein, na ki is par ki unka data collection actually kitna intrusive hai. Un perceptions ko bhi aksar kharab tarike se manage kiya jaata hai. Koi cheez factually sahi ho sakti hai, phir bhi agar woh dardnaak yaadein jaga de, toh ho sakta hai user ko uski yaad na dilayi jaaye. Kisi bhi tarah ke data ke saath humein yeh expect karna chahiye ki woh kisi na kisi tarah galat, undesirable ya inappropriate ho sakta hai, aur humein in failures ko handle karne ke mechanisms banane honge. Koi cheez undesirable ya inappropriate hai ya nahi, yeh human judgment ka matter hai. Algorithms aise notions se anjaan hote hain, jab tak hum unhe explicitly human needs ka respect karne ke liye program na karein. In systems ke engineers ke taur par humein humble rehna hoga aur in failings ke liye plan karna hoga.

Aise privacy settings jinse online service ka user control kar sake ki uske data ke kaun se aspects doosre users dekh sakte hain, kuch control users ko wapas dene ki shuruaat hain. Lekin setting chahe kuch bhi ho, service ko khud us data tak unfettered access rehta hai, aur woh use kisi bhi tarike se use kar sakti hai jo privacy policy permit karti hai. Service yeh promise kare ki woh data third parties ko nahi bechegi, tab bhi aam taur par woh khud ko data ko internally process aur analyze karne ke unrestricted rights de deti hai, aur aksar users ko jo dikhta hai usse kahin aage jaati hai.

Privacy rights ka individuals se corporations ko yeh bade scale ka transfer historically unprecedented hai. Surveillance hamesha se rahi hai, lekin pehle woh mehengi aur manual hoti thi, scalable aur automated nahi. Trust relationships bhi hamesha se rahe hain, jaise patient aur doctor ke beech, ya defendant aur attorney ke beech. Lekin un cases mein data ka use ethical, legal aur regulatory constraints se strictly governed raha hai. Internet services ne meaningful consent ke bina huge amounts of sensitive information jama karna, aur use massive scale par is tarah use karna ki users ko samajh hi na aaye ki unke private data ke saath kya ho raha hai, kahin zyada aasaan bana diya hai.

Data assets aur power ke roop mein. Behavioral data kyunki service ke saath user ke interact karne ka byproduct hai, isliye ise kabhi-kabhi data exhaust kehte hain, jo suggest karta hai ki yeh bekaar kachra hai. Is nazariye se behavioral aur predictive analytics woh material recycle karte hain jo warna phenk diya jaata. Author ka kehna hai ki ulta nazariya zyada sahi hai. Agar targeted advertising se service ka kharcha nikalta hai, toh logon ka behavioral data service ka core asset hai. User jis application ke saath interact karta hai, woh bas ek zariya hai users ko lubha kar surveillance infrastructure mein aur zyada personal information daalne ke liye. Online services mein jo khoobsurat human creativity aur social relationships dikhte hain, is nazariye se unhe ek data extraction machine cynically exploit kar rahi hai.

Personal data ek valuable asset hai, is claim ko data brokers ka hona support karta hai. Yeh ek shady industry hai, jo secrecy mein kaam karti hai, aur intrusive personal data ko khareedti, aggregate karti, analyze karti, infer karti aur dobara bechti hai, zyada-tar marketing ke liye. Startups ki valuation aksar unke user numbers se hoti hai, jiska asal matlab unki surveillance capabilities hai.

Data valuable hai, isliye bahut log use chahte hain. Companies chahti hain, isliye woh use collect karti hain. Governments bhi chahti hain, secret deals, coercion, legal compulsion ya seedhe chori ke zariye. Jab koi company bankrupt hoti hai, toh usne jo personal data collect kiya hota hai woh un assets mein se ek hota hai jo bech diye jaate hain. Data ko secure karna bhi mushkil hai, isliye breaches pareshan karne wali frequency se hote hain.

Critics ne is data ko toxic asset kaha hai, ya kam se kam hazardous material. Hum yeh sochein ki hum abuse rokne mein capable hain, tab bhi jab bhi hum data collect karte hain, humein fayde ko is risk ke saath tolna chahiye ki data galat haathon mein pad sakta hai. Computer systems ko criminals ya hostile foreign intelligence services compromise kar sakti hain. Data insiders leak kar sakte hain. Company aise unscrupulous management ke haath mein ja sakti hai jo hamari values share nahi karta. Poora desh aise regime ke kabze mein ja sakta hai jise humse data hand over karwane mein koi jhijhak nahi.

Isliye jab hum data collect karte hain, toh humein sirf aaj ka political environment nahi, balki future ki saari possible governments ke baare mein sochna chahiye. Is baat ki koi guarantee nahi hai ki aage chunee jaane wali har government human rights aur civil liberties ka respect karegi. Aisi technology install karna jo kabhi police state banane mein madad kar sakti hai, poor civic hygiene hai, jaisa ek commentator ne kaha hai. Author puraani kahavat bhi cite karte hain ki knowledge hi power hai. Doosron ko dekhna aur khud ko dekhe jaane se bachaye rakhna power ke sabse important roopon mein se ek hai. Isi wajah se totalitarian governments surveillance chahti hain: isse unhe population ko control karne ki power milti hai. Aaj ki technology companies khule taur par political power nahi dhoondh rahi. Lekin unhone jo data aur knowledge jama kiya hai, woh phir bhi unhe hamari zindagi par bahut power deta hai, aur uska zyada-tar hissa public oversight se chhupa hai.

Industrial Revolution ko yaad rakhna

Data information age ki defining feature hai. Internet, data storage, processing aur software-driven automation ka global economy aur human society par bada asar hai. Pichhle ek dashak mein hamari rozmarra ki zindagi aur social organization badle hain, aur aane wale dashkon mein shayad bahut zyada badlenge, isliye Industrial Revolution se comparisons dimaag mein aate hain.

Industrial Revolution bade technological aur agricultural advances se aayi, aur lambe time mein usne sustained economic growth aur kahin behtar living standards diye. Usne serious problems bhi laayi. Hawa ka pollution, dhuen aur chemical processes se, aur paani ka pollution, industrial aur human waste se, bhayanak tha. Factory owners shaan se rehte the, jabki shehri workers aksar bahut kharab housing mein rehte the aur kathin conditions mein lambe ghante kaam karte the. Child labor aam tha, jisme mines mein khatarnak aur kam paise wala kaam bhi shaamil tha.

Safeguards aane mein bahut time laga. Unmein environmental protection regulations, workplaces ke liye safety protocols, child labor par pabandi, aur khaane ke liye health inspections shaamil the. Business karne ki cost badh gayi jab factories apna waste nadiyon mein nahi daal sakti thi, milawati khaana nahi bech sakti thi, ya apne workers ka exploit nahi kar sakti thi. Lekin society ko poore taur par bahut fayda hua, aur humme se kam hi log un rules se pehle ke time mein wapas jaana chahenge.

Jaise Industrial Revolution ka ek dark side tha jise manage karna pada, waise hi information age mein transition ki bhi badi problems hain jinka humein saamna karke solve karna hoga. Author maante hain ki data ka collection aur use unhi mein se ek hai. Woh Bruce Schneier ko quote karte hain, jo data ko "the pollution problem of the information age" kehte hain, aur kehte hain ki privacy protect karna environmental challenge hai. Lagbhag har computer information produce karta hai, aur woh aas-paas padi rehti hai, sadti rehti hai. Hum use kaise contain karte hain aur kaise dispose karte hain, yeh information economy ki health ke liye central hai. Schneier ka kehna hai ki aane wali generations humein is baat par judge karengi ki humne data collection aur misuse ko kaise handle kiya, bilkul waise hi jaise hum aaj un shuruaati industrialists ko judge karte hain jinhone pollution ko ignore kiya. Author yeh umeed karte hue ant karte hain ki hum unhe garv ka mauka denge.

Legislation aur self-regulation. Data protection laws individuals ke rights bachane mein madad kar sakte hain. Jaise 1995 ki European Data Protection Directive kehti hai ki personal data specified, explicit aur legitimate purposes ke liye collect hona chahiye, aur un purposes se incompatible tarike se aage process nahi hona chahiye. Woh yeh bhi kehti hai ki data un purposes ke liye adequate, relevant aur excessive nahi hona chahiye.

Author ko shak hai ki is tarah ki legislation aaj ke internet context mein effective hai. Yeh rules big data ki philosophy ke seedhe khilaf jaate hain, jo hai data collection ko maximize karna, use doosre datasets ke saath combine karna, aur naye insights nikalne ke liye experiment karna. Exploration ka matlab hai data ko aise purposes ke liye use karna jinki kisi ne kalpana nahi ki thi, jo un specific, explicit purposes ka ulta hai jiske liye user ne consent diya tha, agar hum consent ki baat meaningfully kar bhi sakte hain. Updated regulations ab develop ho rahe hain.

Jo companies logon ke baare mein bahut data collect karti hain, woh regulation ka virodh karti hain, use ek bojh aur innovation mein rukawat maan kar. Kuch had tak author ko lagta hai ki yeh virodh justified hai. Jaise medical data share karte waqt privacy ke clear risks hain, lekin real opportunities bhi hain. Agar data analysis better diagnostics ya better treatments mein madad kare, toh kitni maut roki ja sakti hain? Over-regulation aise breakthroughs ko rok sakti hai. In opportunities ko risks ke saath balance karna mushkil hai.

Fundamentally, author ko lagta hai ki tech industry ko personal data ke maamle mein culture shift chahiye. Humein users ko optimize karne wale metrics samajhna band karna chahiye, aur yaad rakhna chahiye ki woh insaan hain jo respect, dignity aur agency ke haqdaar hain. Humein apne data collection aur processing ko self-regulate karna chahiye, taaki un logon ka trust ban sake aur bana rahe jo hamare software par depend karte hain. Aur humein khud zimmedari leni chahiye ki end users ko batayein ki unka data kaise use hota hai, na ki unhe andhere mein rakhein.

Humein har individual ko apni privacy banaye rakhne deni chahiye, yani apne data par unka control, aur surveillance ke zariye woh control unse chheenna nahi chahiye. Apne data ko control karne ka hamara individual right ek national park ke natural environment jaisa hai. Agar hum use explicitly protect aur uski dekhbhal nahi karenge, toh woh barbaad ho jaayega. Yeh tragedy of the commons hogi, aur hum sab uske baad bure haal mein honge. Ubiquitous surveillance inevitable nahi hai. Hum ab bhi use rok sakte hain.

Hum yeh exactly kaise achieve kar sakte hain, yeh abhi ek open question hai. Shuruaat ke liye, author kehte hain ki humein data ko hamesha ke liye retain nahi karna chahiye. Jaise hi uski zaroorat khatam ho, use purge kar dena chahiye. Purging immutability ke idea ke khilaf jaati hai, lekin yeh issue solve ho sakta hai. Ek promising approach jo woh dekhte hain, woh hai access control ko sirf policy se nahi, balki cryptographic protocols se enforce karna. Overall, culture aur attitude mein badlav zaroori honge.

Summary

Short mein
  • Data integration. Koi ek tool har use ke liye kaafi nahi hota, isliye applications kai tools combine karti hain. Is chapter ke approach mein kuch systems ko systems of record bana diya jaata hai, aur doosra data unse transformations ke zariye derive hota hai. Indexes, materialized views, machine learning models aur statistical summaries isi tarah maintain hote hain. In derivations ko asynchronous aur loosely coupled rakhne se ek area ki problem system ke unrelated hisson tak nahi phailti.
  • Evolving dataflows. Dataflows ko ek dataset se doosre dataset tak transformations ke roop mein express karne se applications ko evolve karne mein madad milti hai. Agar tum koi processing step badalna chahte ho, jaise index ya cache ka structure, toh naya transformation code poore input par dobara chala kar output rederive kar sakte ho. Kuch galat ho jaaye, toh code fix karke data dobara process karke recover kar sakte hain. Chapter in dataflow applications ko ek unbundled database ke roop mein dekhta hai, yani loosely coupled components ka set jo milkar wahi karte hain jo database andar se karta hai.
  • Observing change. Derived state ko underlying data ke changes observe karke update kiya ja sakta hai, aur derived state ko khud bhi downstream consumers observe kar sakte hain. Dataflow end user ke device tak jaa sakta hai, taaki data badalne par interfaces update hon aur offline bhi kaam karte rahein.
  • Correctness. Asynchronous event processing se bade scale par strong integrity implement ki ja sakti hai. End-to-end operation identifiers operations ko idempotent banate hain, aur constraints asynchronously check hote hain. Clients ya toh check pass hone ka wait karte hain, ya bina wait kiye aage badh jaate hain aur violation ke liye apologize karne ka risk lete hain. Yeh distributed transactions se zyada scalable aur robust hai, aur practice mein kai business processes jaise chalte hain, usse match karta hai.
  • Auditing. Audits data ki integrity verify karte hain aur corruption detect karte hain. End-to-end checks pipeline ke har component ko ek saath cover kar lete hain, raaste ki disks, networks, services aur algorithms sab shaamil.
  • Ethics. Data ka use achhe kaam ke liye ho sakta hai, lekin woh significant nuksaan bhi kar sakta hai. Woh aise decisions chala sakta hai jo logon ki zindagi par gehra asar daalte hain aur jinke khilaf appeal karna mushkil hai, discrimination aur exploitation ko badhava de sakta hai, surveillance ko normal bana sakta hai, aur intimate information expose kar sakta hai. Achhi niyat se kiye gaye use mein bhi breaches aur unintended consequences real risks hain. Engineers ki zimmedari hai ki woh aisi duniya ki taraf kaam karein jo logon ke saath insaaniyat aur respect se pesh aaye.

Chapter ke end mein papers, talks aur posts ki ek numbered references list hai jo uske claims ko support karti hai, aur yeh retelling us list ko reproduce nahi karti.

Khud check karein

  1. Do clients ek hi record mein conflicting values likhte hain. Ek write database mein jaata hai aur doosra seedha search index mein. Dono systems permanently alag kyun ho sakte hain, aur kaun sa ek change is problem ko fix karta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Writes ka order koi bhi system decide nahi karta, isliye dono unhe alag-alag order mein process kar sakte hain aur alag values par khatam ho sakte hain. Fix yeh hai ki saara input ek aise system se bhejein jo total order decide kare, aur index ko changes ki us ordered stream se derive karein, jaise CDC ya event log se.

  2. Example 12-1 mein, ek client COMMIT ka reply kho dene ke baad transfer retry karta hai. $11 ke bajaye $22 kyun move ho sakte hain, aur Example 12-2 ise kaise rokta hai?

    Jawab dekho

    Ho sakta hai pehla attempt commit ho chuka ho, isliye retry transfer ko dobara kar deta hai. Example 12-2 mein har transfer ke saath ek request ID hoti hai jis par uniqueness rule lagta hai. Retry ka INSERT fail ho jaata hai kyunki ID pehle se present hai, jisse repeat abort ho jaata hai. Request ID ek end-to-end operation identifier hai, isliye yeh har retry mein same logical operation ko pehchaan leta hai.

  3. Overbooked flight ko apology se theek kiya ja sakta hai, lekin jo bank statement ka hisaab na mile use nahi. Book ki do requirements, timeliness aur integrity, ke through is fark ko samjhayein.

    Jawab dekho

    Overbooking timeliness ya constraint ki problem hai. Yeh ek temporary breach hai jise business process compensate karke fix kar sakta hai, jaise refund ya upgrade se. Jis statement ke sums galat hain, woh integrity violation hai. Woh permanent rehta hai jab tak koi use explicitly detect karke repair na kare, aur intezaar karne se kuch nahi hota. Book ka argument hai ki zyada-tar applications mein integrity timeliness se zyada important hai.

  4. Ek predictive model past loan decisions par train hua hai. Sirf data se bana hone ki wajah se model ko fair kyun nahi kaha ja sakta? Chapter se do wajah dein.

    Jawab dekho

    Inme se koi bhi do: model apne input ke patterns seekhta hai, systematic bias bhi, aur use amplify karta hai. Postal code jaise proxies race jaise protected traits ki jagah le sakte hain. Seekhe hue patterns opaque hote hain aur output probabilistic hota hai, isliye individual decisions galat ho sakte hain aur unhe explain ya appeal karna mushkil hota hai. Feedback loops bhi ek bure decision ko downward spiral bana sakte hain.

Back matter

Glossary

Seedhi baat: yeh book ke glossary ka aasaan Hinglish version hai. Har term ka chhota sa matlab diya hai, aur yeh bhi ki book mein woh chapter kaun sa hai jahan us term ko poori detail mein samjhaya gaya hai. Book khud kehti hai ki uski definitions chhoti hain, isliye zyada detail chahiye toh un chapters ko dekhein.

TermMatlab
asynchronousKisi cheez ke khatam hone ka wait na karna, jaise network par doosri machine ko data bhejna. Sender yeh assume nahi karta ki ismein kitna time lagega. Synchronous aur asynchronous replication ke liye Chapter 5 dekhein, aur networks aur system model ke liye Chapter 8.
atomicIske do matlab hain. Ek saath chal rahe operations ke liye: aisa operation jo aisa lage jaise ek hi instant mein ho gaya, yani koi aur process use aadha-adhoora na dekh sake. Isolation dekho. Transactions ke liye: writes ka ek group jo ya toh sab save hon ya sab undo ho jaayein, chahe fault ho jaaye. Atomicity ke liye Chapter 7 dekhein, aur atomic commit aur two-phase commit ke liye Chapter 9.
backpressureData bhejne wale ko slow down karwana, kyunki receiver utni speed se handle nahi kar pa raha. Ise flow control bhi kehte hain. Messaging systems ke liye Chapter 11 dekho.
batch processAisa computation jo input data ka ek fixed, aam taur par bada, set padhta hai aur naya output banata hai, input ko badle bina. Chapter 10 dekho.
boundedJiski ek known upper limit ya size ho. Book ise network delay ke liye use karti hai (timeouts aur unbounded delays ke liye Chapter 8 dekhein) aur datasets ke liye bhi (Chapter 11 ki shuruaat dekhein).
Byzantine faultAisa node jo kisi bhi arbitrary tarike se galat behave kare, jaise doosre nodes ko contradictory ya malicious messages bhejna. Byzantine faults ke liye Chapter 8 dekho.
cacheAisa component jo haal hi mein use hua data yaad rakhta hai, taaki usi data ki aage ki reads fast ho jaayein. Yeh aam taur par complete nahi hota. Agar koi item missing ho, toh use neeche ke slower storage se laana padta hai, jahan poori copy rehti hai.
CAP theoremEk aisa result jise log kaafi galat samajhte hain aur, book ke hisaab se, practice mein kaam ka nahi hai. CAP theorem ke liye Chapter 9 dekho.
causalityEvents ke beech ka woh link jahan ek cheez doosri se pehle hoti hai, aur baad wali cheez pehle wali ka response hoti hai, ya usi par build hoti hai, ya use pehle wali ke context mein samajhna padta hai. Happens-before relationship aur concurrency ke liye Chapter 5 dekhein, aur ordering aur causality ke liye Chapter 9.
consensusKai nodes ko kisi baat par agree karwana, jaise database cluster ko kaun sa node lead karega. Yeh pehli nazar mein jitna lagta hai, usse kaafi zyada mushkil hai. Fault-tolerant consensus ke liye Chapter 9 dekho.
data warehouseAisa database jo kai OLTP systems ka data (neeche OLTP dekhein) ek jagah laata hai aur use analysis ke liye ready karta hai. Data warehousing ke liye Chapter 3 dekho.
declarativeYeh batana ki tumhe kaisa result ya kaunsi properties chahiye, bina exact steps likhe ki wahan tak kaise pahunchna hai. Queries ke case mein query optimizer (database ka woh hissa jo decide karta hai ki query kaise run hogi) steps decide karta hai. Query languages ke liye Chapter 2 dekho.
denormalizeNormalized dataset (jismein koi duplication nahi hota) mein thodi duplication jodna, aam taur par cache ya index ke roop mein, taaki reads fast hon. Denormalized value ek precomputed query result hoti hai, materialized view jaisi. Single-object aur multi-object operations ke liye Chapter 7 dekhein, aur ek hi event log se kai views derive karne ke liye Chapter 11.
derived dataAisa dataset jo kisi doosre data se ek repeatable process se banaya gaya ho, aur zaroorat padne par tum use dobara run kar sakte ho. Yeh aam taur par kisi ek tarah ki read ko fast karne ke liye banta hai. Indexes, caches aur materialized views isi ke examples hain. Part III ka introduction dekho.
deterministicAisa function jo same input par hamesha same output deta hai. Matlab woh random numbers, time of day, network communication ya kisi aur unpredictable cheez par depend nahi kar sakta.
distributedNetwork se jude kai nodes par run hona. Aise systems mein partial failures hoti hain: ek hissa toot sakta hai jabki baaki chalte rehte hain, aur software ko aksar exactly pata nahi chalta ki kya toota hai. Faults aur partial failures ke liye Chapter 8 dekho.
durableData ko aise store karna ki tumhe yakeen ho ki alag-alag faults hone par bhi woh lost nahi hoga. Durability ke liye Chapter 7 dekho.
ETLExtract–Transform–Load. Source database se data nikalna, use is tarah reshape karna ki analytic queries ke liye suit kare, aur phir data warehouse ya batch processing system mein load karna. Data warehousing ke liye Chapter 3 dekho.
failoverSingle leader wale system mein leader ka role ek node se doosre node ko dena, jaise jab current leader down ho jaaye. Node outages handle karne ke liye Chapter 5 dekho.
fault-tolerantKuch galat hone par, jaise machine crash ho jaana ya network link fail ho jaana, apne aap recover kar paana. Reliability ke liye Chapter 1 dekho.
flow controlBackpressure ka doosra naam. Upar backpressure dekho.
followerAisi replica (doosre node par data ki copy) jo clients se koi writes accept nahi karti. Woh sirf leader se mile data changes apply karti hai. Ise secondary, slave, read replica ya hot standby bhi kehte hain. Leaders aur followers ke liye Chapter 5 dekho.
full-text searchText ko kisi bhi keyword se search karna, aksar extras ke saath jaise milti-julti spellings ya synonyms match karna. Full-text index ek tarah ka secondary index hota hai jo in searches ko support karta hai. Full-text search aur fuzzy indexes ke liye Chapter 3 dekho.
graphAisa data structure jo vertices (woh cheezein jinhe refer kiya ja sake, inhe nodes ya entities bhi kehte hain) aur edges (ek vertex se doosre vertex tak connections, inhe relationships ya arcs bhi kehte hain) se bana hota hai. Yahan “node” ka matlab graph ka ek point hai, machine nahi. Graph-like data models ke liye Chapter 2 dekho.
hashAisa function jo input ko ek random dikhne wale number mein badal deta hai. Same input par hamesha same number aata hai.
